sql: select 1.0*sum(a.element='h')/count(*) as hydrogen_fraction, m.label from atom a join molecule m using(molecule_id) where molecule_id='TR006'
answer: TR006에는 원자가 47개 있고 그중 수소(h)가 17개여서 비율은 약 0.3617(36.2%)입니다. 이 분자의 발암성 레이블은 '+'입니다. 모든 원자 중 수소의 비율로 해석했고, 원소 기호는 소문자 'h'로 저장되어 있습니다.

sql: select d.nationality from qualifying q join races r on r.raceId=q.raceId join drivers d on d.driverId=q.driverId where r.year=2017 and r.name='Italian Grand Prix' and q.q3 = (select min(q2.q3) from qualifying q2 join races r2 on r2.raceId=q2.raceId where r2.year=2017 and r2.name='Italian Grand Prix' and q2.q3<>'')
answer: British. Lewis Hamilton had the fastest Q3 time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix (1:35.554), and no other driver shared that time. Q3 times are stored as text in the same m:ss.mmm format, so the minimum text value is also the fastest time. The query returns every driver tied at that time.

sql: SELECT e.event_name, e.location, COUNT(a.link_to_member) AS attendee_count FROM event e LEFT JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.type = 'Budget' GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name, e.location
answer:
Budget review events are the events with type 'Budget'. There are two, and both were held in Conference Room BA 452:
- Fall Budget Review: 5 members attended.
- Spring Budget Review: 0 attendance records. Its status is 'Open', so it may not have taken place yet.

I counted every event of type 'Budget' regardless of status. If you only want events that are finished, add `AND e.status = 'Closed'`, which leaves only Fall Budget Review. I counted attendees as rows in the attendance table, which has one row per member per event. The Event Term in the ontology is still a draft (not certified).

sql: with a as (select p.ID, cast((strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',Birthday)) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09')<strftime('%m-%d',Birthday)) as int) age from Patient p where Birthday is not null and p.ID in (select ID from Laboratory where RNP glob '[0-9]*' and cast(RNP as real)>=64)) select round(avg(age),1) as avg_age from a where age<70
answer: 61.1 years, averaged over 7 distinct patients. I counted each patient once, even if they had several RNP results of 64 or higher. Age is in completed years as of 2026-10-09. RNP is stored as text, so I cast the numeric values to numbers and ignored 'negative' and blank entries.

sql: select round(avg(n),2) from (select s.code, count(distinct t.language) n from sets s left join set_translations t on t.setCode=s.code and t.translation is not null and trim(t.translation)<>'' where s.releaseDate between '2016-01-01' and '2016-12-31' group by s.code)
answer: 2016년에 출시된 세트의 이름은 평균 4.74개 언어로 번역되었습니다. 2016년 출시 세트는 모두 포함했고, 번역이 없는 세트는 0개로 계산했습니다. 번역문(translation)이 NULL인 행은 해당 언어로 번역된 것으로 보지 않았습니다. set_translations에는 이런 행이 231건 있었습니다. 세트별 언어 수는 중복 없이 세었습니다.

sql: select count(*) as customers from (select y.CustomerID from yearmonth y join customers c using(CustomerID) where c.Segment='KAM' and c.Currency='CZK' and y.Date like '2013%' group by y.CustomerID having sum(y.Consumption)>1000000)
answer: 335 KAM-segment CZK customers had total 2013 consumption above 1,000,000. I summed each customer's monthly Consumption for 2013 and compared that total to 1,000,000. The data has no months after November 2013 (201311 is the last), so the total covers January to November. Negative consumption values were kept in the sums.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID JOIN Examination e ON e.ID=p.ID WHERE CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 0 AND e.Thrombosis = 0
answer: 4 patients. I counted distinct patients who have at least one laboratory RNP value above 0 and at least one examination with thrombosis degree 0. RNP is stored as text, so I cast it to a number, which treats 'negative' as 0. A patient with several examinations could be counted even if another of their examinations shows thrombosis. The Terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT f."Low Grade" FROM frpm f JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode=f.CDSCode WHERE s.NCESDist='0632640' AND f."Low Grade" IS NOT NULL ORDER BY CASE f."Low Grade" WHEN 'P' THEN -2 WHEN 'K' THEN 0 ELSE CAST(f."Low Grade" AS INTEGER) END LIMIT 1
answer:
The lowest grade level in district 0632640 is P (preschool). Redwood Consortium for Student Services has a Low Grade of P and a grade span of P-6. The other schools in the district start at K.

I read "lowest grade" as the Low Grade column in frpm. Because Low Grade is text, the query sorts it explicitly in the order P, then K, then 1 to 12. A plain text sort would not give that order. The Low Grade values for the district's nine schools are P (one school) and K (eight schools).

The Terms the query relies on (School, Free or Reduced Price Meal Record) are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.Tags LIKE '%<r>%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct FROM posts p INNER JOIN users u ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id WHERE u.DisplayName = 'Community'
answer: 0.00% of Community's posts use the R tag. Community owns 211 posts and none has any tags. Reading used: owner is the user with DisplayName 'Community', and the R tag is matched as '<r>' in posts.Tags. The Post and User terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(weight),1) AS avg_weight FROM Player WHERE player_api_id IN (SELECT player_api_id FROM Player_Attributes WHERE preferred_foot='left')
answer: 좌측 발 선호 선수의 평균 체중은 166.6입니다(Player.weight 단위 그대로, 파운드로 보임). 선수 한 명을 한 번만 세었고, Player_Attributes에 preferred_foot='left' 기록이 한 번이라도 있는 선수를 왼발 선수로 봤습니다. 사용한 Term(Player, Player Attributes)은 아직 draft 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS slow_q1_count FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE d.code IS NULL AND d.forename IN (SELECT forename FROM drivers GROUP BY forename HAVING COUNT(*)>1) AND q.q1 IS NOT NULL AND (CAST(substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60 + CAST(substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,':')+1) AS REAL))>120
answer: 23 qualifying Q1 times slower than 2:00.000 were set by drivers with no code (NULL) whose forename is shared with at least one other driver. Reading chosen: "slower than two minutes" means strictly more than 120 seconds, counted per qualifying row with a non-null q1. The Driver and Qualifying Result terms are draft (not certified).

sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(SEX='F') / COUNT(*), 1) AS female_pct
FROM Patient p
WHERE SEX IN ('F','M')
  AND Birthday >= '1936-01-01' AND Birthday < '1957-01-01'
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.CPK >= 250)
answer: 85.3% of the group's men and women are women. Group: patients born 1936-01-01 to 1956-12-31 with no CPK result of 250 or higher, including patients with no CPK results. Patients with a blank SEX value are excluded from the denominator. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms used are still drafts.

sql: select b.bond_type,count(*) from bond b join molecule m on m.molecule_id=b.molecule_id where m.label='+' and exists (select 1 from connected c where c.bond_id=b.bond_id) and not exists (select 1 from connected c join atom a on a.atom_id in (c.atom_id,c.atom_id2) where c.bond_id=b.bond_id and a.element<>'c') group by 1
answer: 탄소-탄소 결합만 세었습니다(두 원자가 모두 element='c'). 발암성 분자는 label='+'로 보았습니다. 결과는 단일결합('-') 843개, 이중결합('=') 478개입니다. 삼중결합('#')은 발암성 분자의 탄소-탄소 결합에는 없어서 결과에 나오지 않습니다.

sql: select count(*) from (select u.Id from users u join (select UserId,min(Date) d from badges where Name='Organizer' group by UserId) o on o.UserId=u.Id where u.Location like '%Germany%' and (select count(*) from badges b where b.UserId=u.Id and b.Date<o.d and b.Name<>'Organizer')>=5)
answer: 11 users. I counted a user as based in Germany if their Location contains "Germany" (case-insensitive), which includes entries like "Berlin, Germany" and "Germany". "Germantown, MD" is not matched. Each user's Organizer date is their earliest Organizer badge. A user qualifies if they have at least 5 non-Organizer badges dated strictly before that date. I read "had already earned 5 badges" as 5 or more.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(t.NumTstTakr,0)),2) AS avg_test_takers FROM schools s LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds=s.CDSCode WHERE s.CharterNum='0756' AND s.MailCity='San Diego'
answer: The average is 41.33 SAT test takers per school. Charter number 0756 has 6 schools with a San Diego mailing city, all Active. Two of them have SAT records: High Tech High Chula Vista with 136 test takers and High Tech High North County with 112. The other four have no SAT record and count as 0, so the total is 248 and 248 / 6 = 41.33. I read "charter number 756" as the stored value '0756'. I used an exact match so that '1756' (California Prep Sutter, mailing city Meridian) is excluded. The School and SAT Score Record terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
SELECT d.A2, CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) AS population
FROM district d
WHERE d.district_id IN (
  SELECT a.district_id FROM account a
  WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', a.date) = (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', MIN(date)) FROM account))
AND CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) = (
  SELECT MAX(CAST(d2.A4 AS INTEGER)) FROM district d2
  WHERE d2.district_id IN (
    SELECT a.district_id FROM account a
    WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', a.date) = (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', MIN(date)) FROM account)))
answer: Hl.m. Praha (Prague), with 1,204,953 inhabitants. No ties. I read "first month of operations" as the calendar month of the earliest account creation date (January 1993). Population is stored as text, so I cast it to an integer. The Account and District Terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: select (b.balance-a.balance)*100.0/a.balance from trans a, trans b where a.account_id=(select account_id from loan where date='1993-07-05') and b.account_id=a.account_id and a.date='1993-03-22' and b.date='1998-12-27'
answer: The loan dated 1993-07-05 belongs to account 1787. Its balance was 1100 on 1993-03-22 and 5835 on 1998-12-27, an increase of about 430.45%. Only one loan has that date, and each of the two dates has one transaction for the account.

sql: select round(avg(c),4) from (select m.molecule_id, (select count(*) from atom a where a.molecule_id=m.molecule_id and a.element='o') c from molecule m where exists (select 1 from bond b where b.molecule_id=m.molecule_id and b.bond_type='-'))
answer: 단일 결합('-')이 하나 이상 있는 분자의 분자당 평균 산소 원자 수는 2.1613입니다. 산소가 없는 분자는 0개로 계산해 평균에 넣었습니다.

sql: select (select bond_type from bond where molecule_id='TR010' group by bond_type order by count(*) desc limit 1) as bond_type, (select case label when '+' then 'YES' else 'NO' end from molecule where molecule_id='TR010') as carcinogenic
answer: TR010의 가장 흔한 결합 유형은 '-'(단일 결합, 16개)이고, 발암성은 NO입니다. 라벨 '-'를 비발암성으로 해석했습니다(라벨 '+'가 발암성).

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(d.A11),2) AS avg_salary, COUNT(*) AS n_districts FROM district d WHERE d.A3='east Bohemia' AND d.district_id IN (SELECT a.district_id FROM account a JOIN disp p ON p.account_id=a.account_id JOIN client c ON c.client_id=p.client_id WHERE c.birth_date >= '1980-01-01' AND c.birth_date < '1990-01-01')
answer: 10 East Bohemia districts serve at least one client born 1980-1989, and their average salaries average 8618.20. Reading used: a client is served by a district if they hold any disposition (OWNER or DISPONENT) on an account whose branch (account.district_id) is in that district. Each district counts once, and the salary is district.A11. The Account, Client and District terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(d.A11),2) AS avg_salary FROM district d WHERE d.A3='central Bohemia' AND d.district_id IN (SELECT c.district_id FROM client c JOIN disp o ON o.client_id=c.client_id AND o.type='OWNER' WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM disp x JOIN card k ON k.disp_id=x.disp_id WHERE x.account_id=o.account_id))
answer: 9357.25. This is the mean of each district's average salary (A11) over the distinct central Bohemia districts (client's own district) where OWNER clients live whose account has no card on any of its dispositions. Each district counts once (not weighted by client count). Terms used (Client, Disposition, District) are draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT SUM(SEX='M') AS male_patients, SUM(SEX='F') AS female_patients FROM Patient p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.GPT >= 60);
answer: 178 male patients and 956 female patients have never had an ALT (GPT) result above the normal range. I took "above normal" as GPT >= 60, because the docs give the normal range as GPT < 60. Patients with no lab rows, or only NULL GPT values, count as never abnormal. The 13 patients with an empty SEX value are excluded, since you asked for exactly male and female.

sql:
WITH c AS (
 SELECT DISTINCT cl.district_id FROM client cl
 JOIN disp d ON d.client_id=cl.client_id AND d.type='OWNER'
 WHERE cl.gender='F'
 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM card k WHERE k.disp_id=d.disp_id)
 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=d.account_id)
), r AS (
 SELECT di.* , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY A3 ORDER BY CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) DESC, A2) rn
 FROM district di JOIN c USING(district_id)
)
SELECT A3 AS region, ROUND(AVG(A11),2) AS avg_salary, ROUND(AVG(A13),2) AS avg_unemployment_1996,
 (SELECT A2 FROM r r2 WHERE r2.A3=r.A3 AND rn=1) AS most_populous_district
FROM r GROUP BY A3 ORDER BY A3;
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 8개 지역이 나왔습니다. 가장 인구가 많은 지구는 Prague는 Hl.m. Praha, central Bohemia는 Kladno, east Bohemia는 Pardubice, north Bohemia는 Liberec, north Moravia는 Ostrava - mesto, south Bohemia는 Ceske Budejovice, south Moravia는 Brno - mesto, west Bohemia는 Plzen - jih입니다.

모호한 부분은 다음과 같이 해석했습니다.
- 평균은 고객 수가 아니라 지역 안에서 해당 고객이 사는 지구를 한 번씩만 센 값입니다. 지구마다 한 번씩 계산하므로 고객이 많은 지구에 가중치가 붙지 않습니다.
- 고객이 사는 지구는 client.district_id 기준입니다. 계좌가 등록된 지구는 쓰지 않았습니다.
- 카드와 대출은 그 고객이 OWNER인 disp에 연결된 카드와, 같은 계좌의 대출로 판단했습니다.
- 인구(A4)는 텍스트로 저장되어 있어 정수로 바꿔 비교했습니다. 평균 급여는 A11, 1996년 실업률은 A13입니다.

sql: select bank, account, count(*) as payment_count, sum(amount) as total_paid from trans where account_id=(select account_id from loan where amount=98832 and date='1996-01-03') and type='VYDAJ' and date<'1996-01-03' and bank is not null and bank<>'' and account is not null group by bank, account order by total_paid desc
answer:
I read "98832" as the loan amount, since no loan has that ID. One loan matches that amount and the date 1996-01-03: loan 5999, account 4907. Counting only VYDAJ transactions before 1996-01-03 that have a bank and account number, the account paid three counterparties:
- YZ / 25638538: 18 payments, 70,884 total
- AB / 5604631: 18 payments, 22,554 total
- QR / 82890259: 19 payments, 6,175 total

Outgoing payments with no bank or account number (for example cash withdrawals) are left out, because they have no counterparty.

sql:
SELECT p.Admission AS Admission, COUNT(*) AS patient_count, ROUND(AVG(CAST(strftime('%Y','2026-10-09') AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y',p.Birthday) AS INTEGER) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09') < strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday))),1) AS avg_age
FROM Patient p
WHERE p.Admission IN ('+','-') AND p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RBC < 3.5)
GROUP BY p.Admission ORDER BY p.Admission DESC
answer: Among patients with at least one RBC result below 3.5, 41 were admitted (+) and 29 were outpatient (-). Average completed age on 2026-10-09 is 70.3 for admitted and 73.6 for outpatient. Assumptions: only Admission '+' and '-' are counted (blank and '+(' excluded), and each patient is counted once. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still drafts.

sql: SELECT c.name, (min(l.milliseconds)/60000) || ':' || printf('%02d.%03d', (min(l.milliseconds)%60000)/1000, min(l.milliseconds)%1000) AS fastest_lap_time FROM lapTimes l JOIN races r ON r.raceId=l.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId=r.circuitId WHERE c.country='Italy' GROUP BY c.circuitId, c.name
answer: Two Italian circuits have recorded laps. Autodromo Nazionale di Monza's fastest lap is 1:21.046, and Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari's is 1:20.411. I took "in Italy" to mean circuits.country = 'Italy', and "fastest" to be the minimum lapTimes.milliseconds across all races at that circuit. The ontology terms Circuit, Lap Time and Race are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superhero s LEFT JOIN race r ON s.race_id = r.id WHERE s.publisher_id = (SELECT publisher_id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = 'A-Bomb') AND (s.race_id IS NULL OR r.race = '-')
answer: 171 characters published by A-Bomb's publisher have no race listed. "No race listed" means race_id is NULL or the race is '-' (the placeholder for unknown). The count includes A-Bomb. The Superhero and Race terms are still draft.

sql:
SELECT AVG(s.weight_kg) AS avg_weight_kg
FROM superhero s
WHERE s.weight_kg IS NOT NULL AND s.weight_kg > 0
AND s.race_id IS NOT NULL
AND s.race_id NOT IN (SELECT s2.race_id FROM superhero s2 JOIN gender g ON g.id = s2.gender_id WHERE g.gender = 'Female' AND s2.race_id IS NOT NULL)
answer: The average weight is about 156,709.09 kg. One extreme recorded weight of 90,000,000 kg inflates it, and I did not remove it. Choices made: a weight of 0 or NULL counts as not recorded (matching the ontology's 'Weight Known' filter), heroes with no race are excluded, and the '-' (unknown) race is treated like any other race. The Superhero and Gender terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
SELECT e.type,
 (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) FROM attendance a JOIN event x ON x.event_id=a.link_to_event WHERE x.type=e.type AND x.event_date LIKE '2019%') AS members_attended,
 (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(b.amount),0) FROM budget b JOIN event x ON x.event_id=b.link_to_event WHERE x.type=e.type AND x.event_date LIKE '2019%') AS total_budgeted
FROM event e
WHERE e.event_date LIKE '2019%'
GROUP BY e.type
ORDER BY e.type
answer: 2019 has 8 event types. Result (type: distinct members attended, budgeted $): Budget 5, 0; Community Service 13, 0; Election 0, 0; Game 24, 0; Guest Speaker 29, 785; Meeting 30, 1175; Registration 30, 300; Social 24, 0. Reading I chose: "members who attended" counts each member once per type (distinct), not total attendance records (which would be 5/19/0/43/83/105/30/37). Budget uses budget.amount (planned, not spent), summed per type by joining budget to events dated in 2019; missing values show 0.

sql:
SELECT c.Currency, COUNT(*) AS customer_count
FROM customers c
WHERE c.CustomerID IN (
  SELECT CustomerID FROM yearmonth
  WHERE Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201311' AND Consumption > 0
  GROUP BY CustomerID
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT Date) = 11
)
GROUP BY c.Currency;
answer: CZK: 61 customers, EUR: 4 customers. I treated "bought fuel in a month" as a `yearmonth` row with Consumption > 0, and required all 11 months from 201301 to 201311. If any recorded row counted regardless of consumption, CZK would be 62 and EUR would stay at 4. I did not use `transactions_1k` because it is only a sample and the product list does not mark which products are fuel.

sql: SELECT SUM(Reputation) AS total_reputation FROM users WHERE Id IN (SELECT OwnerUserId FROM posts WHERE Score = 10 AND Tags LIKE '%<r>%')
answer: 50863. This is the combined reputation of the 43 distinct users who own at least one post with Score = 10 and the exact tag <r>. Tags are stored as "<r><ggplot2>…", so I matched "<r>" to exclude other tags that merely contain an r. I counted each user once. If a user's reputation were counted once per qualifying post (46 posts), the total would be 75563.

sql:
WITH c AS (SELECT uuid, COUNT(*) n FROM rulings GROUP BY uuid)
SELECT DISTINCT cards.name, cards.artist, cards.isPromo
FROM c JOIN cards ON cards.uuid = c.uuid
WHERE c.n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM c)
answer: Two combinations occur among the printings tied for the most rulings: Teferi's Protection by Chase Stone with isPromo = 0, and Teferi's Protection by Chase Stone with isPromo = 1. I read "printings" as individual card rows (one per uuid) and counted rulings per uuid. The Card Term used is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.name) FROM cards c WHERE c.types LIKE '%Creature%' AND CAST(c.power AS INTEGER) >= 10 AND c.setCode IN (SELECT setCode FROM set_translations WHERE language='French' AND translation IS NOT NULL)
answer: 33 distinct creature cards with power >= 10 have a printing in a set with a French set-name translation (non-null French translation in set_translations). Cards are counted by distinct name; power is cast to integer, so non-numeric values like '*' are excluded.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE borderColor='black' AND availability LIKE '%mtgo%' AND power GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(power AS INTEGER)>=10
answer: 83. I counted rows in `cards`, not unique card names. "Available on MTGO" means `availability` contains 'mtgo', and `power` is numeric and at least 10. Rows with non-numeric power such as '*' are excluded.

sql: select d.forename, d.surname, q.q3 from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) where d.nationality='Italian' and coalesce(q.q3,'')<>'' and q.q3=(select min(q2.q3) from qualifying q2 join drivers d2 using(driverId) where d2.nationality='Italian' and coalesce(q2.q3,'')<>'')
answer: Jarno Trulli, 1:11.328. Reading used: "Italian" means drivers.nationality = 'Italian'. Empty or NULL q3 values are ignored. The minimum was taken as text, which is valid because all times use the m:ss.mmm format. Only one driver has this time.

sql: with q as (select c.Currency cur, y.CustomerID, sum(y.Consumption) s from yearmonth y join customers c using(CustomerID) where y.Date between '201304' and '201306' group by 1,2) select round(avg(case when cur='EUR' then s end),2) as EUR, round(avg(case when cur='CZK' then s end),2) as CZK from q;
answer: EUR-paying customers consumed 3627.03 on average over Q2 2013, and CZK-paying customers consumed 44462.45. I summed each customer's April, May and June 2013 consumption from yearmonth, then averaged those per-customer totals by account currency. Only customers with at least one recorded month in the quarter are included. Negative consumption values were kept as recorded, and no currency conversion was applied because the values are consumption amounts.

sql: select frameVersion, count(*) from cards where frameVersion=(select max(frameVersion) from cards where convertedManaCost=0 and frameVersion glob '[0-9]*') group by frameVersion
answer: 가장 최신 프레임 버전은 2015이고, 데이터베이스 전체에서 이 프레임을 쓰는 카드는 25,500장입니다. 'future'는 연도가 아니라 Future Sight 프레임(2007년경)이라서 최신 후보에서 제외했습니다. 'future'를 가장 최신으로 본다면 결과는 93장입니다. 마나 비용 0 카드 중에는 'future'를 쓰는 카드가 8장 있습니다.

sql: select round(avg(l.ALB),4) from Laboratory l join Patient p on p.ID=l.ID where p.SEX='F' and p.Diagnosis='SLE' and l.PLT>400
answer: 평균 ALB는 3.9123입니다. 'SLE 진단'은 Diagnosis 값이 정확히 'SLE'인 환자로 해석했습니다. 'SLE susp'나 'SLE, SJS'처럼 다른 진단이 섞인 경우는 제외했습니다. 조건은 SEX='F'이고 검사 기록의 PLT가 400을 넘는 경우입니다.

sql: select d.driverRef, d.nationality, d.dob from qualifying q join races r on r.raceId=q.raceId join drivers d on d.driverId=q.driverId where r.year=2017 and r.name='Italian Grand Prix' and q.q2 is not null and q.q2<>'' and (q.q3 is null or q.q3='')
answer: 2017 이탈리아 그랑프리에서 Q2에 기록을 남기고 Q3에 오르지 못한 드라이버는 5명입니다. 이름, 국적, 생년월일 순으로 적습니다. perez(멕시코, 1990-01-26), hulkenberg(독일, 1987-08-19), alonso(스페인, 1981-07-29), kvyat(러시아, 1994-04-26), sainz(스페인, 1994-09-01). 이 데이터에서는 시간이 없는 칸이 빈 문자열이거나 NULL로 들어 있습니다. 그래서 'Q2 기록이 있고 Q3 기록이 없는 경우'를 Q2 탈락으로 보았습니다. Q2 기록이 없는 드라이버(magnussen, palmer, ericsson, wehrlein, grosjean)는 Q1에서 탈락했거나 Q2에 나가지 않은 것으로 보고 제외했습니다. 쿼리에 쓴 Driver, Qualifying Result, Race 용어는 아직 인증되지 않은(draft) 상태입니다.

sql: with a as (select p.ID, cast(strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',Birthday)-(strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09')<strftime('%m-%d',Birthday)) as int) age from Patient p where Birthday is not null and p.ID in (select ID from Laboratory where RNP glob '[0-9]*' and cast(RNP as real)>=64)) select round(avg(age),1) as average_age from a where age<70;
answer: The average age is 61.1 years, across 7 patients aged 51 to 67. I took 'at least one anti-RNP result of 64 or higher' to mean any Laboratory row where RNP is numeric and at least 64. Text values such as 'negative' are excluded. I computed age in completed years as of 2026-10-09 and kept only patients under 70. Patients with no birthday are excluded.

sql: SELECT artist, COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS creature_cards FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND artist IS NOT NULL GROUP BY artist HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT name) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) c FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND artist IS NOT NULL GROUP BY artist)) ORDER BY artist
answer: Kev Walker has illustrated the most different creature cards, 275, with no tie. I counted distinct card names, because the table has one row per printing. I treated any card whose types include Creature as a creature card, including Artifact Creature. The result relies on the Card Term, which is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: select round(1.0*(select count(*) from hero_power hp join superhero s on s.id=hp.hero_id join race r on r.id=s.race_id join gender g on g.id=s.gender_id where r.race='God / Eternal' and g.gender='Male')/(select count(*) from superhero s join race r on r.id=s.race_id join gender g on g.id=s.gender_id where r.race='God / Eternal' and g.gender='Male'),2) as avg_powers
answer: 16.18. 'God / Eternal' is the race value, and I limited it to male heroes. I counted every such hero in the denominator, including any with no powers listed, so they count as 0.

sql: SELECT ROUND(1.0*COUNT(c.atom_id)/COUNT(DISTINCT a.atom_id),2) AS avg_bonds_per_atom FROM atom a LEFT JOIN connected c ON c.atom_id=a.atom_id WHERE a.molecule_id='TR397'
answer: 2.02. An atom in TR397 has 2.02 bonds on average. Each atom's bonds are its rows in `connected` as atom_id, since every bond is stored in both directions. The average includes any atoms with no bonds. The Atom term used is still a draft.

sql: select count(distinct l.ID) from Laboratory l join Patient p on p.ID=l.ID where p.Description is null and (l.CRP='+' or l.CRP glob '[0-9]+' or (l.CRP glob '[0-9.]*' and cast(l.CRP as real)>=1.0));
answer: 42 patients. I counted a CRP result as positive when it is '+', '2+', '3+', '4+', '5+', or a number of 1.0 or higher. The wiki lists '-', '+-' and values below 1.0 as normal, so those are excluded. 'No recorded patient description' means Patient.Description is NULL. That column holds a date, and the wiki says its NULLs are real missing values.

sql: select s.School,s.Phone from schools s join satscores t on t.cds=s.CDSCode where s.DOC='03' and t.rtype='S' and t.NumGE1500=(select max(t2.NumGE1500) from schools s2 join satscores t2 on t2.cds=s2.CDSCode where s2.DOC='03' and t2.rtype='S')
answer: High Tech High North County, phone (619) 243-5014, with 56 SAT test takers scoring 1500 or above. I took "statewide benefit charter" to mean DOC code '03' (Statewide Benefit Charter). I counted only school-level rows (rtype 'S'). The district-level row (102) has no school name, so it isn't a school. No other school ties at 56.

sql: select sum(cr.points) as points, c.name, c.nationality from constructorResults cr join races r using(raceId) join constructors c using(constructorId) where r.name='Monaco Grand Prix' and r.year between 1980 and 2010 group by c.constructorId order by points desc limit 1
answer: McLaren (British) scored the most points at the Monaco Grand Prix from 1980 to 2010, with 218.5. I summed constructorResults points over the Monaco races in those years, including 1980 and 2010. Ferrari was second with 194.5.

sql: select round((select max(s) from (select sum(Consumption) s from yearmonth where Date like '2013%' group by Date)) - (select max(s) from (select sum(Consumption) s from yearmonth where Date like '2012%' group by Date))) as diff
answer: 2013년 최대 월 총소비량이 2012년 최대 월보다 338,745,665 단위 많습니다. yearmonth 테이블에서 월별로 전체 고객의 Consumption을 합산한 뒤, 연도별 최댓값의 차이를 반올림했습니다.

sql:
WITH l AS (SELECT s.School, s.DOCType, f.`Enrollment (K-12)`-f.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)` d
 FROM frpm f JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode=f.CDSCode
 WHERE f.`Charter Funding Type`='Locally funded' AND f.`Enrollment (K-12)` IS NOT NULL AND f.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)` IS NOT NULL)
SELECT School, DOCType FROM l WHERE d > (SELECT AVG(d) FROM l)
answer: The query returns 49 schools, each with its name from the schools directory and its DOCType. I read "locally funded" as frpm."Charter Funding Type" = 'Locally funded' (328 rows). The average difference (K-12 enrollment minus ages 5-17 enrollment) is taken over those rows that have both enrollment values. Schools with a difference above that average are listed.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c WHERE c.setCode IN (SELECT code FROM sets WHERE releaseDate = (SELECT MAX(releaseDate) FROM sets WHERE code IN (SELECT setCode FROM cards WHERE name = 'Ancestor''s Chosen'))) AND c.types LIKE '%Creature%' AND c.power GLOB '*[0-9]*' AND c.toughness GLOB '*[0-9]*' AND CAST(c.power AS REAL) > CAST(c.toughness AS REAL);
answer: 29. The most recent set containing Ancestor's Chosen is UMA (Ultimate Masters, released 2018-12-07). It has 29 creature cards with power greater than toughness. I excluded creatures whose power or toughness is '*' (e.g. '*/*', '*/1+*'), since those can't be compared numerically.

sql: SELECT d.nationality FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3<>'' AND q.q3=(SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying q2 WHERE q2.raceId=q.raceId AND q2.q3<>'')
answer: British. One driver set the fastest Q3 time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, so there was no tie. Fastest means the lowest Q3 time, and drivers with no Q3 time were excluded.

sql: select s.name, s.releaseDate from cards c join sets s on s.code=c.setCode where c.name='Aven Mindcensor' and c.frameVersion <> 'future' and c.frameVersion = (select max(frameVersion) from cards where name='Aven Mindcensor' and frameVersion <> 'future') and s.releaseDate = (select max(s2.releaseDate) from cards c2 join sets s2 on s2.code=c2.setCode where c2.name='Aven Mindcensor' and c2.frameVersion = (select max(frameVersion) from cards where name='Aven Mindcensor' and frameVersion <> 'future')) group by s.name, s.releaseDate
answer: Amonkhet Remastered, released 2020-08-13. Assumption: the 'future' frameVersion is the 2007 Future Sight frame, so 2015 is the newest frame (a text sort would wrongly rank 'future' last). Among the four 2015-frame printings, Amonkhet Remastered is the most recently released, with no tie.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_api_id) FROM Player_Attributes WHERE jumping >= 80 AND date >= '2007-02-22' AND date < '2007-08-31'
answer: 654 distinct players had a jumping score of 80 or higher in assessments from 2007-02-22 to 2007-08-30 inclusive. I counted each player once. Counting assessment rows instead gives 1049. I ran the query with an equivalent date filter and got 654.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(s.NumTstTakr,0)),2) AS avg_sat_test_takers FROM schools sc LEFT JOIN satscores s ON s.cds = sc.CDSCode WHERE sc.CharterNum = '0756' AND sc.MailCity = 'San Diego'
answer: 41.33. 헌장 번호 0756이고 우편 발송 도시가 San Diego인 6개교를 운영 상태와 관계없이 모두 포함했고, SAT 기록이 없는 학교는 응시자 0명으로 계산했습니다. 헌장 번호 1756(Meridian 소재 1개교)은 0756이 아니므로 제외했습니다. 쿼리가 쓴 'School'과 'SAT Score Record' 용어는 아직 검증되지 않은 draft 상태입니다.
