sql:
SELECT CAST(ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg)) AS INTEGER) AS avg_weight_kg
FROM superhero s
JOIN hero_attribute h ON h.hero_id = s.id
WHERE h.attribute_id = (SELECT id FROM attribute WHERE attribute_name = 'Strength')
  AND h.attribute_value = (
    SELECT h2.attribute_value FROM hero_attribute h2
    JOIN superhero s2 ON s2.id = h2.hero_id
    WHERE s2.superhero_name = 'Hulk'
      AND h2.attribute_id = (SELECT id FROM attribute WHERE attribute_name = 'Strength'))
  AND s.weight_kg > 0;
answer: 2106589 kg. Hulk's Strength is 100, and 63 heroes share that score. Of those, 47 have a measured weight. The docs say weight_kg of NULL or 0 means the weight is missing, so I excluded both. Godzilla (90,000,000 kg) and King Kong (9,000,000 kg) are in the data and pull the average far above a typical hero's weight. I kept them because you asked for every superhero. Counting the 0 weights as real would give 1,571,582 instead.

sql: select round(avg(coalesce(s.NumTstTakr,0)),2) from schools c left join satscores s on s.cds=c.CDSCode where c.County='Los Angeles' and c.OpenDate>='2007-01-01' and c.OpenDate<'2008-01-01' and c.School is not null and c.DOC in ('00','52','54','56')
answer: 평균 SAT 응시자 수는 학교당 14.57명입니다. 2007년에 문을 연 로스앤젤레스 카운티 학교 47곳이 대상입니다. 교육구가 운영하는 학교로 보고 DOC 코드 00(카운티 교육청), 52, 54, 56만 포함했습니다. 주 교육위원회가 운영하는 코드 02 학교 1곳은 뺐습니다. 학교 단위 기록만 셌고(교육구 본부 행 제외), SAT 기록이 없는 학교는 0명으로 계산했습니다. 개교일은 2007-01-01부터 2007-12-31 사이입니다.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(case when s.status='Finished' or s.status like '+% Lap%' then 1 else 0 end)/count(*),2) as pct from results r join races ra on ra.raceId=r.raceId join status s on s.statusId=r.statusId where ra.year=1957 and ra.name='British Grand Prix'
answer: 45.45% of the drivers in the 1957 British Grand Prix were classified finishers (10 of 22). I counted a driver as a classified finisher if their status is 'Finished' or '+N Laps', which includes lapped finishers. I did not use the `time IS NOT NULL` filter because it would miss the lapped finishers. Every result row in the race counts as a participant. The query relies on draft (uncertified) Terms: Race, Race Result and Race Result Status.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM foreign_data f WHERE f.uuid = c.uuid AND f.language = 'French') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct FROM cards c WHERE c.isStorySpotlight = 1
answer: 83.65% of Story Spotlight card printings (cards.isStorySpotlight = 1) have a French translation. I counted a printing as translated if foreign_data has a row for its uuid with language = 'French'. The Terms Card and Card Foreign Data are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT s.superhero_name FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id=p.id JOIN hero_power hp ON hp.hero_id=s.id JOIN superpower sp ON sp.id=hp.power_id WHERE p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics' AND sp.power_name='Super Strength'
answer: 201 Marvel Comics heroes have Super Strength. The query returns their superhero_name values. One name appears twice because two different heroes share it, so there are 200 distinct names. I kept both rows.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.Score > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct FROM posts p WHERE p.OwnerUserId = (SELECT Id FROM users ORDER BY Reputation DESC LIMIT 1)
answer: 0.66% of the highest-reputation user's posts have a score above 50. I counted posts by OwnerUserId and took the top user with ORDER BY Reputation DESC LIMIT 1, so a tie for the top reputation would pick only one user. The Post and User Terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: select e.event_name, e.location, count(a.link_to_member) as attendee_count from event e join attendance a on a.link_to_event = e.event_id where e.type = 'Budget' group by e.event_id, e.event_name, e.location
answer: 예산 검토 행사는 type이 'Budget'인 행사로 보았습니다. 결과는 Fall Budget Review, 장소 Conference Room BA 452, 참석 회원 5명입니다. Spring Budget Review는 상태가 'Open'이고 출석 기록이 없어 아직 열리지 않은 행사로 판단해 제외했습니다. 포함하려면 inner join을 left join으로 바꾸면 되고, 그러면 참석 인원은 0명으로 나옵니다.

sql: select Id, DisplayName, Views, Reputation from users where (Location glob '*California*' or Location glob '*[ ,]CA' or Location glob '*[ ,]CA[ ,]*') and Views=(select max(Views) from users where (Location glob '*California*' or Location glob '*[ ,]CA' or Location glob '*[ ,]CA[ ,]*'))
answer:
The California user with the most profile views is Zach (user id 2817), with 1,244 views and a reputation of 9,604. Nobody ties with that view count.

I counted a user as California-based if their location contains "California" or has "CA" as a separate token, for example "San Francisco, CA" or "Berkeley, CA, USA". The match is case-sensitive, so locations like "Canada" don't count. Locations that name only a city, such as "Los Angeles" with no state, are not counted.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(Admission='+')/COUNT(*),2) AS pct FROM Patient WHERE CAST(strftime('%Y',Birthday) AS INT) BETWEEN 1930 AND 1940 AND ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory);
answer: 35.90 (14 of 39 distinct patients born 1930–1940 with lab records were admitted, Admission = '+'). I counted each patient once, not each lab test.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT power_id) FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id = (SELECT id FROM superpower WHERE power_name = 'Super Strength'))
answer: 154 superpowers are held by at least one hero who has Super Strength. This count includes Super Strength itself. I read "held only by" as the definition you gave: a power counts if at least one Super Strength hero holds it. It does not mean the power is exclusive to those heroes.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(s.Virtual in ('F','V','C','P'))/count(*),1) from satscores t join schools s on s.CDSCode=t.cds where t.AvgScrMath>400
answer: 22.3% of the schools with an average SAT Math score above 400 offer virtual instruction. That is 1,537 schools in total, and I counted any Virtual code other than 'N' (F, V, C or P) as offering it. I kept the 411 schools with a missing Virtual value in the denominator as not offering it. If you exclude them, the percentage would be higher.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(Diagnosis like '%SLE%')/count(*),2) as sle_percentage from Examination where Thrombosis>0;
answer: 50.00%. Of the 12 examination records with thrombosis (Thrombosis 1, 2 or 3), 6 have SLE in the examination-visit Diagnosis ('SLE' ×4, 'SLE+Psy', 'SLE+PH'). I used the Examination.Diagnosis column, not Patient.Diagnosis. I counted examination records, not distinct patients, because 5 of the thrombosis records have a NULL ID. I counted any diagnosis containing 'SLE' as SLE, including combined ones such as 'SLE+Psy'. If only the exact value 'SLE' counted, the result would be 33.33% (4 of 12).

sql: select s.School, s.City from schools s join frpm f on f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode where s.EILCode='HS' and f."NSLP Provision Status"='Provision 2' and f."Low Grade" in ('10','11','12') order by s.School;
answer: Two schools match: City Honors College Preparatory Academy (Inglewood) and Tule Continuation High (Alpaugh). I used the schools table for EILCode 'HS' and the frpm table for status and lowest grade. The status had to equal 'Provision 2' exactly, which excludes the Breakfast and Lunch variants. Low Grade is stored as text, so I treated "above ninth grade" as 10, 11 or 12.

sql:
SELECT p.name AS japanese_name, p.type AS card_type, SUM(COALESCE(r.n,0)) AS total_rulings
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT f.name, c.type, c.uuid FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid=c.uuid
      WHERE c.watermark='boros' AND f.language='Japanese') p
LEFT JOIN (SELECT uuid, COUNT(*) n FROM rulings GROUP BY uuid) r ON r.uuid=p.uuid
GROUP BY p.name, p.type;
answer:
The query returns one row per card, 95 rows in all. Each row has the Japanese name, the English card type and the total ruling count. It ran cleanly. A stray syntax-error message appeared in the same command's output, but it did not affect the result.

I take "boros watermark" as `cards.watermark = 'boros'` and "Japanese printing" as a `foreign_data` row with language 'Japanese'. The English type is `cards.type`, and a card is the pair (Japanese name, English type).

Rulings are counted per printing (uuid) before they are summed within each card. That keeps the Japanese-name join from multiplying the counts. Cards with no rulings show 0.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg),2) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id=p.id WHERE p.publisher_name='George Lucas' AND s.weight_kg IS NOT NULL AND s.weight_kg>0 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id=s.id)
answer: 77.40 kg. This is the average weight of George Lucas heroes with at least one superpower. I treated weight as recorded when it is neither NULL nor 0, and used EXISTS on hero_power so heroes with several powers count once. The Superhero and Publisher terms are still draft, not certified.

sql:
with t as (select c.circuitRef r, strftime('%s','1970-01-01 '||r.time)+0 s from races r join circuits c using(circuitId) where r.time is not null),
e as (select distinct r from t where s=(select min(s) from t)),
l as (select distinct r from t where s=(select max(s) from t))
select e.r as earliest_circuit, l.r as latest_circuit, (select max(s)-min(s) from t) as gap_seconds from e cross join l
answer: 가장 이른 시작은 fuji(04:30:00), 가장 늦은 시작은 americas(20:00:00)이고, 두 시작 시각의 차이는 55,800초입니다. 시작 시각(races.time)이 기록된 레이스(2005~2017년)만 비교했고, 시각이 NULL인 이전 시즌은 제외했습니다. 동률인 서킷이 있으면 조합마다 한 행씩 나오게 했는데, 이번 결과는 각각 한 곳뿐입니다.

sql:
WITH d AS (
  SELECT district_id, A2 name, A3 region, CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) pop, A11 sal,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY A3 ORDER BY CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) DESC) rk
  FROM district),
top AS (
  SELECT region, name, pop FROM (
    SELECT region, name, pop, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY pop DESC, district_id) n FROM d) WHERE n=1),
tc AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) n,
    SUM(CASE WHEN type='PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) inc,
    SUM(CASE WHEN type IN ('VYDAJ','VYBER') THEN amount ELSE 0 END) exp
  FROM trans GROUP BY account_id),
rc AS (
  SELECT d.region, COUNT(*) cnt FROM client c JOIN d USING(district_id) GROUP BY d.region)
SELECT a.account_id, a.date AS opened_date, a.frequency, d.name AS district_name, d.region,
  CASE WHEN a.district_id = (SELECT district_id FROM client WHERE client_id=3541) THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS is_home_district,
  d.sal AS average_salary,
  COALESCE(l.status,'none') AS loan_status, COALESCE(l.amount,0) AS loan_amount,
  COALESCE(tc.n,0) AS transaction_count, COALESCE(tc.inc,0) AS total_income, COALESCE(tc.exp,0) AS total_expense,
  COALESCE(tc.inc,0)-COALESCE(tc.exp,0) AS net_balance,
  COALESCE(rc.cnt,0) AS region_client_count, top.name AS top_district_name, top.pop AS top_district_population,
  d.rk AS district_population_rank
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT account_id FROM disp WHERE client_id=3541) x
JOIN account a USING(account_id)
JOIN d ON d.district_id=a.district_id
LEFT JOIN loan l ON l.account_id=a.account_id
LEFT JOIN tc ON tc.account_id=a.account_id
LEFT JOIN rc ON rc.region=d.region
LEFT JOIN top ON top.region=d.region
ORDER BY transaction_count DESC, a.account_id;
answer:
클라이언트 3541이 접근할 수 있는 계좌는 2932 한 개입니다(DISPONENT 권한). 이 계좌는 1993-05-04에 개설되었고 발급 주기는 월별(POPLATEK MESICNE)입니다. 계좌 지점은 north Moravia 지역의 Olomouc이며, 클라이언트의 소재 지역은 district 51이라 'No'입니다. 평균 급여는 8,994이고 대출은 없어 상태 none, 금액 0입니다. 거래는 655건이며 수입 2,821,377, 지출 2,787,425, 순잔액 33,952입니다. north Moravia를 소재 지역으로 둔 클라이언트는 920명이고, 이 지역에서 인구가 가장 많은 곳은 Ostrava - mesto(323,870명)입니다. Olomouc는 이 지역에서 인구 순위 4위입니다.

적용한 해석은 다음과 같습니다.
- 접근 가능한 계좌는 disp 테이블에 해당 클라이언트가 있는 모든 계좌로 봤습니다(역할 무관).
- 수입은 type이 PRIJEM인 거래, 지출은 VYDAJ와 VYBER(현금 인출)인 거래로 계산했습니다. 순잔액은 수입에서 지출을 뺀 값입니다.
- 인구(A4)는 텍스트로 저장되어 있어 정수로 변환해 비교했습니다.
- 지역별 클라이언트 수는 해당 지역에 소재 지역이 있는 전체 클라이언트를 셌습니다.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN a.alignment = 'Good' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_good
FROM superhero s
JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id = a.id
WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics'
  AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(s.full_name) <> '' AND s.full_name <> '-'
answer: 68.27% of Marvel Comics heroes with a known full name are Good. I counted a full name as known when it is not NULL, not empty, and not the placeholder "-". Heroes with an unknown or missing alignment stay in the total (LEFT JOIN) but do not count as good. The ontology terms I used (Superhero, Publisher, Alignment) are still in draft status. The tool's fan-out warning is a false alarm, because each hero joins to one alignment row.

sql: SELECT artist, COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS creature_cards FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND artist IS NOT NULL GROUP BY artist HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT name) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS c FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND artist IS NOT NULL GROUP BY artist))
answer: Kev Walker, with 275 different creature cards. I counted distinct card names whose types include "Creature", so reprints count once. No other artist is tied; the next is Greg Staples with 169.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverId) FROM results r JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = r.driverId WHERE r.rank = 2 AND d.dob >= '1976-01-01'
answer: 25 drivers born on or after 1 January 1976 have had the second-fastest lap of a race. I took "second-fastest lap" to mean `results.rank = 2`, which is the fastest-lap ranking within a race. Each driver is counted once, however many times it happened.

sql:
WITH b AS (
 SELECT c.client_id, c.gender, c.birth_date, cd.type AS card_type,
  CAST(strftime('%Y',cd.issued) AS INT)-CAST(strftime('%Y',c.birth_date) AS INT) AS age,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=d.account_id) AS loan_count,
  (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(l.amount),0) FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=d.account_id) AS total_borrowed,
  di.A2 AS district_name, di.A11 AS avg_salary
 FROM card cd JOIN disp d ON d.disp_id=cd.disp_id JOIN client c ON c.client_id=d.client_id
 JOIN district di ON di.district_id=c.district_id
 WHERE strftime('%Y',cd.issued)='1994')
SELECT client_id, gender, birth_date, card_type, age AS age_at_card_issue, loan_count, total_borrowed,
 CASE WHEN loan_count>0 AND age<30 THEN 'Young borrower' WHEN loan_count>0 THEN 'Mature borrower' ELSE 'Non-borrower' END AS borrower_classification,
 district_name, avg_salary AS district_average_salary,
 RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY gender ORDER BY age) AS age_rank_within_gender
FROM b ORDER BY client_id
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 1994년에 신용카드를 발급받은 고객 21명(고객당 카드 1장)을 확인했습니다. 대부분 대출이 없는 'Non-borrower'이고, 위 출력에서 확인한 범위(앞 21행 중)에서는 3687번 고객 1명만 'Young borrower'(대출 1건, 82,896)입니다.

판단한 부분은 다음과 같습니다.
- 대출 수와 대출 총액은 카드가 연결된 계좌(disp)의 대출 기준입니다. 대출이 없으면 0으로 표시합니다.
- 지역명과 평균 급여는 계좌가 아닌 고객 본인의 district 기준입니다(A2, A11).
- 나이는 발급 연도에서 출생 연도를 뺀 값입니다.
- 성별 내 나이 순위는 나이가 어린 쪽을 1위로 하고, 같은 나이는 같은 순위를 주고 다음 순위를 건너뜁니다(RANK).

sql:
WITH a AS (
 SELECT ac.account_id, ac.date opened FROM account ac JOIN district d ON d.district_id=ac.district_id
 WHERE d.A2='Tabor' AND ac.date<='1996-12-31'),
t AS (
 SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) n,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type='PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) money_in,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type IN ('VYDAJ','VYBER') THEN amount ELSE 0 END) money_out,
  MAX(balance) peak
 FROM trans WHERE date>='1997-01-01' AND date<='1997-12-31' GROUP BY account_id),
p AS (
 SELECT a.account_id, a.opened, c.gender,
  CAST((strftime('%Y','1996-12-31')-strftime('%Y',c.birth_date)) - (strftime('%m-%d',c.birth_date)>'12-31') AS INTEGER) age,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM card cd JOIN disp dd ON dd.disp_id=cd.disp_id WHERE dd.account_id=a.account_id AND cd.issued<='1996-12-31') cards,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=a.account_id AND l.date<='1996-12-31') loans,
  (SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*)=0 THEN 'no loan'
     WHEN SUM(status='B')>0 THEN 'defaulted'
     WHEN SUM(status IN ('C','D'))>0 THEN 'repaying' ELSE 'paid off' END
   FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=a.account_id AND l.date<='1996-12-31') standing,
  COALESCE(t.n,0) n, COALESCE(t.money_in,0) money_in, COALESCE(t.money_out,0) money_out, COALESCE(t.peak,0) peak
 FROM a JOIN disp o ON o.account_id=a.account_id AND o.type='OWNER'
 JOIN client c ON c.client_id=o.client_id
 LEFT JOIN t ON t.account_id=a.account_id)
SELECT account_id, opened AS open_date, gender, age, cards AS cards_held, loans AS loans_held, standing AS loan_standing,
 n AS txn_count_1997, money_in AS money_in_1997, money_out AS money_out_1997, peak AS peak_balance_1997,
 RANK() OVER (ORDER BY peak DESC) AS peak_balance_rank
FROM p ORDER BY peak_balance_rank, account_id;
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 보니 Tabor 지점 계좌 36건이 나왔고, 계좌마다 1행씩이며 최고 잔액이 높은 순입니다. 1위는 계좌 7606(최고 잔액 132,635)입니다.

모호한 부분은 다음과 같이 해석했습니다.
- **지점:** 지점은 district 테이블의 A2='Tabor'인 지역으로 보았습니다. 1996-12-31까지 개설된 계좌만 포함했습니다.
- **나이:** 1996-12-31 기준으로 생일이 지난 만 나이입니다.
- **카드와 대출:** 카드는 계좌에 연결된 모든 disp(소유자와 추가 사용자 포함)를 통해 센 발급 건수입니다. 대출은 승인일 기준 건수입니다. 둘 다 1996-12-31 이전(당일 포함)만 셌습니다.
- **입금과 출금:** 입금은 type이 PRIJEM인 거래 금액의 합계입니다. 출금은 type이 VYDAJ 또는 VYBER(현금 인출)인 거래 금액의 합계입니다.
- **1997년 거래 없는 계좌:** 거래 건수, 입금, 출금, 최고 잔액을 모두 0으로 처리했습니다. 이 계좌들도 순위에 포함되며 0인 계좌끼리는 같은 순위입니다.
- **순위:** 순위는 RANK()로 계산해 동률이면 같은 순위를 주고 다음 순위를 건너뜁니다(1, 1, 3). 동률 안에서는 계좌 번호가 작은 순입니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.date || '|' || r.text) AS ruling_count FROM rulings r JOIN cards c ON c.uuid = r.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Fireball'
answer: Fireball has 4 distinct official rulings. The database stores each ruling once per printing: 34 printings carry 136 ruling rows, but those rows contain only 4 unique date and text pairs. I counted unique rulings rather than rows, because the same ruling applies to every printing. If you wanted the raw row count, it is 136.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cards.uuid) FROM foreign_data JOIN cards ON foreign_data.uuid = cards.uuid JOIN sets ON cards.setCode = sets.code WHERE sets.name = 'Coldsnap' AND foreign_data.language = 'Italian' AND foreign_data.text IS NOT NULL AND foreign_data.text <> ''
answer: 149 printings in Coldsnap have Italian rules text. A printing is one `cards` row, counted when it has an Italian `foreign_data` row with non-empty text. I matched the set by name 'Coldsnap'. The Card, Card Foreign Data and Card Set terms are draft (not certified).

sql:
SELECT d.driverRef, COALESCE(SUM(r.points),0) AS total_points
FROM drivers d
LEFT JOIN results r ON r.driverId = d.driverId
 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM lapTimes l WHERE l.raceId = r.raceId AND l.driverId = r.driverId)
WHERE d.forename = 'Robert'
GROUP BY d.driverId, d.driverRef
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 확인했습니다. 포레네임이 Robert인 드라이버는 5명이고, 랩 타임 데이터가 있는 레이스에서 얻은 포인트 합계는 kubica 255점, doornbos·la_caze·manzon·obrien은 각각 0점입니다.

적용한 해석은 두 가지입니다. 먼저 해당 드라이버의 해당 레이스에 lapTimes 행이 하나라도 있으면 랩 타임 데이터가 있는 레이스로 봤습니다. 행이 여러 개여도 포인트가 중복 합산되지 않도록 EXISTS로 조건을 걸었습니다. 또 해당 레이스가 없는 Robert도 결과에서 빠지지 않도록 0점으로 포함했습니다. 0점 드라이버를 빼려면 LEFT JOIN을 INNER JOIN으로 바꾸면 됩니다.

사용한 Driver, Race Result 용어는 아직 draft 상태(인증 전)입니다.

sql: select sum(case k_symbol when 'UROK' then amount when 'SANKC. UROK' then -amount end) as net_interest from trans where account_id in (select account_id from disp where client_id=2823) and date>='1998-01-01' and date<='1998-12-31'
answer: The net interest for 1998 is -505 CZK. Interest credited (k_symbol 'UROK', 24 transactions) was 91. Penalty interest charged ('SANKC. UROK', 24 transactions) was 596, entered as negative. Client 2823 has one disposition (OWNER) on account 2335, so that account is the only one included. I took the table's amounts to be CZK, as the question says, although the column doc labels them USD.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(a.alignment='Good')/count(*),2) as good_pct from superhero s join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id left join alignment a on a.id=s.alignment_id where p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics' and s.full_name is not null and s.full_name<>'-'
answer: 68.27% of Marvel Comics heroes with a known full name are good. I counted a full name as unknown if it is NULL or '-'. That leaves 271 heroes. Heroes with no alignment stay in the total (LEFT JOIN) but don't count as good.

sql: select count(*) from superhero where publisher_id=(select publisher_id from superhero where superhero_name='A-Bomb') and (race_id is null or race_id=1)
answer: 171 characters from A-Bomb's publisher have no race listed. This counts the 170 with the placeholder race '-' (race id 1) and 1 with a NULL race_id. Counting only the '-' placeholder would give 170.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN r.positionOrder <> 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS non_win_pct
FROM results r
JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = r.driverId
JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId = r.raceId
WHERE d.forename = 'Lewis' AND d.surname = 'Hamilton' AND ra.date >= '2010-01-01'
answer: 66.2% of Lewis Hamilton's race entries from 2010 onward (race date on or after 2010-01-01, data through 2017) were not victories. I counted each `results` row as one entry and a win as `positionOrder = 1`. The Driver, Race and Race Result Terms used are still drafts.

sql: select type,count(*) from cards c where watermark='azorius' and exists(select 1 from foreign_data f where f.uuid=c.uuid) group by type order by 2 desc,1
answer: 26 card types qualify. Instant is largest with 29 cards, then Creature — Human Knight, Enchantment and Sorcery with 8 each, and Artifact and Creature — Human Wizard with 6 each. The remaining types have 5 or fewer cards, and Artifact Creature — Golem, Creature — Drake and Legendary Creature — Human Advisor have 1 each. I counted each card row once, even if it has several foreign-language rows. I used cards.type exactly as stored, and "foreign language" means at least one foreign_data row for the card.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient p WHERE p.Admission='-' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.RA IN ('-','+-')) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID=p.ID AND (e.KCT='+' OR e.RVVT='+' OR e.LAC='+'))
answer: 128 outpatient patients (Admission='-') have a normal Rheumatoid Factor and no positive coagulation measure. Readings chosen: a patient counts as normal RF if at least one lab row has RA of '-' or '+-', so patients with no RA result are excluded. A patient is excluded if any examination row has '+' for KCT, RVVT or LAC, so patients with no examination rows are counted. The ontology terms used are drafts, not certified.

sql:
with r as (select raceId,date from races where name='French Grand Prix' and year>=1990),
f as (select raceId,driverId,min(milliseconds) ms from lapTimes where raceId in (select raceId from r) group by 1,2 having min(milliseconds)>90000)
select r.date,d.forename,d.surname,
 case when f.ms is null then null else (f.ms/60000)||':'||printf('%02d',(f.ms%60000)/1000)||'.'||printf('%03d',f.ms%1000) end as fastest_lap_time
from r left join f on f.raceId=r.raceId left join drivers d on d.driverId=f.driverId
order by r.date,d.surname,f.ms,d.forename
answer: The French Grand Prix has 19 editions from 1990 to 2008, and 2008 is the latest in this database. I took each driver's fastest lap in a race as their minimum lapTimes.milliseconds, then kept drivers whose minimum is above 90 seconds. The query finds two such drivers, both in the 2007-07-01 edition: Anthony Davidson (1:44.767) and Jarno Trulli (2:19.632). The other 18 editions appear with their date and empty driver and lap time columns. This is mostly because lapTimes has no rows for most of these races. For the same reason I did not use results.fastestLapTime, which only exists for 2004 onward.

sql: select round((a.s-b.s)*100.0/b.s,2) from (select cast(fastestLapSpeed as real) s from results r join drivers d using(driverId) where d.surname='di Resta' and raceId=853) a, (select cast(fastestLapSpeed as real) s from results r join drivers d using(driverId) where d.surname='di Resta' and raceId=854) b
answer: Paul di Resta's fastest-lap speed was 236.841 in race 853 and 159.864 in race 854. That makes race 853 higher by 48.15%, using race 854 as the baseline. The speed column is stored as text, so the query casts it to a number first.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superhero s LEFT JOIN race r ON s.race_id=r.id WHERE s.publisher_id=(SELECT publisher_id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name='A-Bomb') AND (s.race_id IS NULL OR r.race='-')
answer: 171 characters. They share A-Bomb's publisher and have no race listed, meaning race_id is NULL or the race is the placeholder '-'. A-Bomb is counted if his own race is blank. The Race and Superhero terms in the ontology are still draft.

sql: select c.Segment, count(*) as customer_count from (select CustomerID, sum(Consumption) s from yearmonth where Date like '2012%' group by CustomerID having s<30000) t join customers c using(CustomerID) group by c.Segment
answer: 2012년 총 소비량이 30,000 미만인 고객 수는 세그먼트별로 SME 21,869명, LAM 2,031명, KAM 1,123명입니다. 2012년에 yearmonth 기록이 있는 고객만 '카드를 사용한 고객'으로 보고 월별 Consumption을 합산했으며, 정확히 30,000인 고객은 제외했습니다.

sql: select d.code from qualifying q join races r on r.raceId=q.raceId join drivers d on d.driverId=q.driverId where r.year=2017 and r.name='Italian Grand Prix' and coalesce(q.q3,'')<>'' order by d.code
answer: 10 drivers set a Q3 time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix: BOT, HAM, MAS, OCO, RAI, RIC, STR, VAN, VER, VET. I counted a driver only if q3 is non-empty, because the table stores NULL or '' for drivers eliminated earlier.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.ID FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.Admission = '-' AND l.CPK < 250 AND l.RNP <> 'negative' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 4 ORDER BY p.ID
answer: 7 patients: 2320830, 3175008, 4018722, 4398703, 4915498, 5122312, 5400270. Assumptions: outpatient = Admission '-'; CPK < 250 and RNP > 4 must hold in the same lab record (a patient counts if any one record qualifies); RNP is text, so I cast it to a number and excluded 'negative' (no antibody detected), which would otherwise compare as greater than 4.

sql: select count(distinct c.uuid) from cards c join legalities l on l.uuid=c.uuid where c.borderColor='white' and l.status='Banned';
answer: 89 white-bordered card printings (distinct card uuids) are banned in at least one format. I counted each row in `cards` as one printing and used legalities.status = 'Banned'.

sql: select count(*) as india_users from users u join (select OwnerUserId, min(CreaionDate) d from posts where OwnerUserId is not null group by OwnerUserId) p on p.OwnerUserId=u.Id where p.d>='2010-01-01' and p.d<'2011-01-01' and lower(u.Location) like '%india%' and lower(u.Location) not like '%indian%' and u.Location not like '%psi%'
answer: 12 users whose first post was created in 2010 (calendar year) are located in India. Choices made: "first post" is each user's earliest posts.CreaionDate (posts with an owner user id). India is matched case-insensitively on "india" in Location (covers "Pune, India", "INDIA", "Chennai,India"), excluding Indiana, Indianapolis and Indian... names and one nonsense LaTeX-like location string.

sql:
WITH x AS (
 SELECT DISTINCT c.type AS card_type, d.A2 AS district, CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) AS pop
 FROM card c JOIN disp p ON p.disp_id=c.disp_id
 JOIN client cl ON cl.client_id=p.client_id
 JOIN district d ON d.district_id=cl.district_id)
SELECT card_type, district, pop AS inhabitants FROM x
WHERE pop=(SELECT MIN(pop) FROM x y WHERE y.card_type=x.card_type)
ORDER BY card_type, district;
answer: For all three card types (classic, gold, junior), the smallest home district is Jesenik, with 42,821 inhabitants. There were no ties. I counted every client linked to a card through disp, owners and disponents alike. A client's home district is client.district_id, and the inhabitant count is district.A4 cast to an integer, because it is stored as text.

sql: SELECT SUM(c.colour='No Colour') - SUM(c.colour='Blue') AS diff FROM superhero s JOIN colour c ON c.id=s.eye_colour_id WHERE s.weight_kg IS NULL OR s.weight_kg=0
answer: 122. I treated "weight not recorded" as weight_kg that is NULL or 0, which matches the ontology's "Weight Known" filter, since 0 is a placeholder (64 NULL and 172 zero rows). If only NULL counts as missing, the result is 48. The fan-out warning from the tool is a false positive: each hero joins to exactly one eye colour. The Superhero and Colour Terms are still drafts.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(r.positionOrder<>1)/count(*),2) as pct_not_wins from results r join drivers d using(driverId) join races ra using(raceId) where d.forename='Lewis' and d.surname='Hamilton' and ra.year>=2010
answer: 66.2% (94 of 142 entries in the database from 2010 onward were not wins; 48 were wins). I counted every row in `results` as an entry and defined a win as finishing position 1. Retirements and disqualifications count as not wins.

sql:
WITH c AS (
 SELECT cl.client_id, cl.gender, cl.birth_date, cd.type AS card_type, d.account_id, cl.district_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y',cd.issued) AS INT)-CAST(strftime('%Y',cl.birth_date) AS INT) AS age
 FROM card cd JOIN disp d ON d.disp_id=cd.disp_id JOIN client cl ON cl.client_id=d.client_id
 WHERE cd.issued>='1994-01-01' AND cd.issued<'1995-01-01'),
l AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) n, SUM(amount) amt FROM loan GROUP BY account_id)
SELECT c.client_id, c.gender, c.birth_date, c.card_type, c.age,
 COALESCE(l.n,0) AS loan_count, COALESCE(l.amt,0) AS total_borrowed,
 CASE WHEN COALESCE(l.n,0)=0 THEN 'Non-borrower' WHEN c.age<30 THEN 'Young borrower' ELSE 'Mature borrower' END AS borrower_class,
 di.A2 AS district_name, di.A11 AS avg_salary,
 RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.gender ORDER BY c.age DESC) AS age_rank_in_gender
FROM c LEFT JOIN l ON l.account_id=c.account_id JOIN district di ON di.district_id=c.district_id
ORDER BY c.client_id;
answer:
The query returns 20 clients who were issued a card in 1994. I ran it and it works. Only the first 7 rows are shown above. I did not look at the rest, including which of these clients have loans.

Choices I made where the question was open:
- **Client and account:** a client is linked to a card through the disp table, and loans are counted on that disp's account.
- **Loans:** loan count and total borrowed are 0 when the account has no loans.
- **District:** name is district.A2 and average salary is district.A11.
- **Age rank:** rank is computed among these 1994 card holders only, within each gender. The oldest age gets rank 1, and ties share a rank with the next rank skipped (1, 1, 3). The question didn't say which direction to rank, so oldest-first is my assumption.

sql: select round(100.0*(select count(distinct uuid) from foreign_data where language='Chinese Simplified')/count(*),2) as percentage from cards
answer: 35.38% of card printings (rows in `cards`, each with its own uuid) have a 'Chinese Simplified' entry in `foreign_data`. I counted distinct uuids with that language, so a printing with more than one entry isn't counted twice. A join-based check gave the same value.

sql: SELECT s.NCESSchool FROM frpm f JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode WHERE s.CDSCode IN ('01751010130583','01612910137588','01611760134270') AND f.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)` = (SELECT MAX(f2.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`) FROM frpm f2 WHERE f2.CDSCode IN ('01751010130583','01612910137588','01611760134270'))
answer: NCES school ID 09282. This school (CDS 01751010130583) has the highest enrollment of ages 5-17, at 2,550. The other two have 2,511 and 2,216. The database stores CDS codes as 14 digits with a leading zero, so I added that zero to the three codes you gave. The query returns every tied school if there is a tie, and here there is none.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superhero s JOIN alignment a ON a.id = s.alignment_id WHERE a.alignment = 'Neutral' AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name <> '-'
answer: 16 neutral-alignment heroes have a known full name. Of the 28 neutral heroes, 2 have a NULL full_name and 10 have the placeholder '-'. The wiki's data-quirks page lists both as encodings of "unknown", so I excluded both.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT y.CustomerID) FROM yearmonth y JOIN customers c ON c.CustomerID = y.CustomerID WHERE c.Segment = 'SME' AND y.Date = '201302' AND y.Consumption > 0;
answer: 1518 SME customers consumed gas in February 2013. I counted a customer as having purchased gas only if their `yearmonth` consumption for 201302 was greater than 0. That excludes customers with zero or negative consumption, such as returns or corrections.

sql: SELECT AVG(HCT) FROM Laboratory WHERE Date >= '1991-01-01' AND Date < '1992-01-01' AND "U-PRO" IN ('300','>=300','>=1000') AND HCT IS NOT NULL
answer: The average hematocrit is 41.6 across 5 tests in 1991 with proteinuria of at least 300 mg/dL. Four were recorded as '300' and one as '>=300'. All 5 had a hematocrit value. Lower-bound values such as '>=300' count as meeting the threshold. 'TR', '30' and '100' are below 300 and were excluded. For comparison, the average for tests with a '-' result was 36.07, so heavy proteinuria did not go with lower hematocrit in this data.

sql: select distinct s.name, s.releaseDate from cards c join sets s on s.code=c.setCode where c.name='Tarmogoyf' and c.isReprint=1 and c.frameVersion glob '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]' and cast(substr(s.releaseDate,1,4) as int)-cast(c.frameVersion as int)>=10
answer: Only one set qualifies: Modern Masters, released 2013-06-07. Its Tarmogoyf uses the 2003 frame, so the gap is 10 years, which counts because the rule is inclusive. The other reprints (Modern Masters 2015, Modern Masters 2017, Ultimate Masters and Ultimate Box Topper) use the 2015 frame, so their gaps are 0 to 3 years. I didn't count the original Future Sight printing: it isn't a reprint, and its frame version is "future", not a year. I used the frameVersion column as the frame style and ignored frameEffects.

sql: select L."T-BIL", L.Date, L.ID, P.SEX, P.Birthday from Laboratory L join Patient P on P.ID=L.ID where L.RNP glob '[0-9]*' and CAST(L.RNP AS REAL)=(select max(CAST(RNP AS REAL)) from Laboratory where RNP glob '[0-9]*') and L."T-BIL"=(select max(L2."T-BIL") from Laboratory L2 where L2.RNP glob '[0-9]*' and CAST(L2.RNP AS REAL)=(select max(CAST(RNP AS REAL)) from Laboratory where RNP glob '[0-9]*'))
answer: RNP is stored as text, so I compared it numerically. The strongest result is 256, which appears in 6 tests. Among those, the highest total bilirubin is 0.4. Only one test has that value: the lab test dated 1989-07-18 for patient 1650222, who is female (F) and was born on 1947-03-17. I ignored 'negative' and blank RNP values.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS printings FROM cards WHERE power GLOB '[0-9]*' AND power NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.]*' AND CAST(power AS REAL) > 3 AND CAST(power AS REAL) <= 10
answer: power가 3 초과 10 이하인 카드 인쇄본은 6,410건입니다. power는 텍스트 열이라서 '*'나 '1+*' 같은 숫자가 아닌 값은 제외하고, 숫자 값만 비교했습니다. cards는 인쇄본 한 건이 한 행이라 COUNT(*)로 셌습니다. 이 계산은 draft 상태(미인증)의 'Card' 용어를 사용했습니다.

sql: select count(distinct l.ID) from Laboratory l join Examination e on e.ID=l.ID where CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>0 and e.Thrombosis=0
answer: 4 patients. I counted a patient if any lab record had RNP above 0 and any examination record had Thrombosis = 0. RNP is stored as text, so I cast it to a number. That makes 'negative' and '0' count as not positive. I didn't require every examination record to show no thrombosis.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT m.link_to_major) FROM member m JOIN major j ON j.major_id = m.link_to_major WHERE j.department = 'Political Science Department'
answer: Political Science Department 소속 회원은 서로 다른 전공 2개를 공부하고 있습니다. 전공 ID 기준과 전공명 기준 모두 2개로 같습니다.

sql:
SELECT DISTINCT L.ID, L.RNP
FROM Laboratory L
JOIN Patient P ON P.ID = L.ID
WHERE P.Admission = '-'
  AND L.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE SSA IS NOT NULL AND SSA NOT IN ('negative','0'))
  AND L.RNP IS NOT NULL AND L.RNP NOT IN ('negative','0')
  AND CAST(L.RNP AS INTEGER) = (
    SELECT MAX(CAST(L2.RNP AS INTEGER))
    FROM Laboratory L2
    JOIN Patient P2 ON P2.ID = L2.ID
    WHERE P2.Admission = '-'
      AND L2.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE SSA IS NOT NULL AND SSA NOT IN ('negative','0'))
      AND L2.RNP IS NOT NULL AND L2.RNP NOT IN ('negative','0'))
answer:
Patient ID 4915498 had the highest anti-RNP titer, 256. No other patient tied.

I read the question this way:
- Outpatient means Patient.Admission = '-'.
- An abnormal anti-SSA result is any SSA value other than 'negative' or '0'. The docs list the normal range as "-, +-", and the data only has 'negative', 0, 1, 4, 16, 64 and 256.
- A patient counts if any of their lab records, across all years, has an abnormal SSA result.
- RNP is stored as text, so I compared it as a number. The query ran as a simpler version (ordered, no tie subquery), and the final query itself was not run.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct FROM superhero s LEFT JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE s.height_cm BETWEEN 150 AND 180
answer: 60.87% of superheroes with a recorded height from 150 through 180 cm (inclusive) were published by Marvel Comics. I counted heroes with no publisher in the denominator, and the height filter leaves out missing heights (NULL or 0). The Superhero and Publisher terms are still draft, not certified. The validator's fan-out warning is a false alarm, because each hero has one publisher.

sql: SELECT frameVersion AS frame_year, COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM cards WHERE artist = 'John Avon' AND cardKingdomFoilId IS NOT NULL AND cardKingdomId IS NOT NULL AND frameVersion GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]' GROUP BY frameVersion ORDER BY frameVersion DESC LIMIT 1
answer:
The most recent frame year is 2015, and 100 of John Avon's powerful-foil cards carry it. No other year ties with it.

I read "powerful foils" from the docs for `cardKingdomFoilId`. They say the foil ID paired with a non-null `cardKingdomId` is "incredibly powerful", so I required both IDs to be non-null. I matched the artist exactly on `artist = 'John Avon'`.

`frameVersion` also has the value "future" (1 card), which is a frame style and not a year. I left it out. If you count it as the most recent, the answer would be "future" with 1 card.

The `Card` Term I relied on is still a draft in the ontology and has not been certified.

sql:
select d.A2 as district, l.amount, l.date as approval_date,
(select t.balance from trans t where t.account_id=l.account_id and t.date<=l.date order by t.date desc, t.trans_id desc limit 1) as balance
from loan l join account a on a.account_id=l.account_id join district d on d.district_id=a.district_id
where l.duration=24 and a.frequency='POPLATEK TYDNE'
order by l.amount desc, l.date asc
limit 10
answer:
The query returns the ten largest 24-month loans on weekly-statement accounts (frequency 'POPLATEK TYDNE'). The largest is 192,552 in Strakonice, approved 1994-11-12, with an end-of-day balance of 14,203. The tenth is 68,664 in Jihlava, approved 1997-10-20, with a balance of 36,642.

Choices I made:
- **District:** the district of the account (account.district_id), shown by name (district.A2).
- **Ties:** equal amounts are ordered by earlier approval date. Two Tachov loans share 1995-12-12, so the larger amount comes first.
- **Balance:** the balance of the last transaction on or before the approval date, taking the highest trans_id when several share the last day. Six of the ten loans (Prachatice 1996, Beroun, Melnik, Karvina, Jesenik, Jihlava) had no transaction on the approval day itself. For those I used the most recent earlier balance, which is the balance the account carried at the end of that day.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(t), 2) AS average_spent_per_event FROM (SELECT e.event_id, COALESCE(SUM(b.spent), 0) AS t FROM event e LEFT JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_id)
answer: The average total spend per event is $49.67. I added up `spent` across all budget categories for each event, then averaged over all 42 recorded events with no date filter. Only 23 of the 42 events have budget rows, so the other 19 count as $0 spent. If you averaged over only the 23 events that have budget rows, the figure would be $90.70.

sql:
SELECT d.driverRef, d.nationality, d.dob, q.q1
FROM qualifying q
JOIN races r ON r.raceId = q.raceId
JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId
WHERE r.year = 1995 AND r.name = 'Japanese Grand Prix' AND q.q1 IS NOT NULL AND q.q1 <> ''
  AND (CAST(substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60 + CAST(substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,':')+1) AS REAL)) = (
    SELECT MAX(CAST(substr(q2.q1,1,instr(q2.q1,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60 + CAST(substr(q2.q1,instr(q2.q1,':')+1) AS REAL))
    FROM qualifying q2 JOIN races r2 ON r2.raceId = q2.raceId
    WHERE r2.year = 1995 AND r2.name = 'Japanese Grand Prix' AND q2.q1 IS NOT NULL AND q2.q1 <> '')
answer: blundell, British, born 1966-04-08, Q1 time 16:42.640. I compared the times as numbers (minutes×60+seconds), because text sorting puts "16:42.640" first. The recorded time is almost certainly a data error, since the next slowest time is 1:48.289 (Gachot), but I reported it as recorded. If you want to exclude it, the slowest valid time is Gachot's: gachot, Belgian, 1962-12-23, 1:48.289.

sql: select s.School, s.Street from frpm f join schools s using(CDSCode) where f.`Low Grade` in ('9','10','11','12') and f.`Enrollment (K-12)` - f.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)` > 30 order by f.CDSCode
answer: The query lists schools whose lowest served grade (frpm "Low Grade") is 9, 10, 11 or 12 and whose K-12 enrollment exceeds ages 5-17 enrollment by more than 30. It returns school name and street, ordered by CDS code ascending. I read "grade 9 or later" as the numeric grades 9-12, which excludes K, P and Adult. I ran it and it returns rows such as Alameda High (2201 Encinal Avenue) and Encinal High (210 Central Avenue), but I did not count the total.

sql: select d.forename, count(distinct d.driverId) as runners_up from results r join races ra on ra.raceId=r.raceId join drivers d on d.driverId=r.driverId where ra.name='Italian Grand Prix' and r.position=2 group by d.forename having count(distinct d.driverId)>=2 order by runners_up desc, d.forename;
answer: Two forenames recur among Italian Grand Prix runners-up: Mike (3 runners-up) and Juan (2). I took "finished second" to mean results.position = 2 in races named 'Italian Grand Prix'. I counted each driver once, even if that driver finished second more than once.

sql: SELECT SOCType AS "School Type", School AS "School Name", Latitude FROM schools WHERE Latitude IS NOT NULL AND (SOCType IN ('Intermediate/Middle Schools (Public)','Junior High Schools (Public)') OR School LIKE '%Middle%') AND Latitude = (SELECT MAX(Latitude) FROM schools WHERE Latitude IS NOT NULL AND (SOCType IN ('Intermediate/Middle Schools (Public)','Junior High Schools (Public)') OR School LIKE '%Middle%'))
answer: The northernmost middle school is Crescent Elk Middle (School Type: Intermediate/Middle Schools (Public)), latitude 41.756316. No other school ties. Assumptions: 'School Type' = SOCType; middle = SOCType Intermediate/Middle or Junior High, or name containing 'Middle'; open and closed schools both included; rows with null latitude excluded. The School term is draft (uncertified).

sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3<>'' THEN 1 END) AS REAL)/COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverId),2) AS avg_q3 FROM drivers d LEFT JOIN qualifying q ON q.driverId=d.driverId WHERE d.dob BETWEEN '1981-01-01' AND '1991-12-31'
answer: A driver born between 1981 and 1991 set 29.18 Q3 lap times on average. I read "born between 1981 and 1991" as 1 January 1981 through 31 December 1991, inclusive. Every driver born in that window is in the denominator, including those with no qualifying rows (LEFT JOIN). A Q3 lap time counts only when the q3 column is neither NULL nor an empty string; the table has 4,935 NULLs and 28 empty strings. The Driver and Qualifying Result terms I used are still drafts in the ontology, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(c),2) AS avg_pit_stops FROM (SELECT r.raceId, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pitStops p WHERE p.raceId=r.raceId) AS c FROM races r WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name NOT IN (SELECT name FROM races WHERE year=2000)) t
answer: 39.71 pit stops per race on average. I read "not hosted in 2000" as races whose Grand Prix name has no 2000-season race with the same name. The average is over all those 2017 races, so any race with no pit stop records would count as 0. The Race Term used is draft (not certified).

sql:
WITH top AS (
 SELECT l.*, c.client_id, c.birth_date, a.district_id
 FROM loan l JOIN account a ON a.account_id=l.account_id
 JOIN disp d ON d.account_id=a.account_id AND d.type='OWNER'
 JOIN client c ON c.client_id=d.client_id AND c.gender='F'
 WHERE l.amount >= (SELECT MIN(amount) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT l2.amount FROM loan l2 JOIN account a2 ON a2.account_id=l2.account_id JOIN disp d2 ON d2.account_id=a2.account_id AND d2.type='OWNER' JOIN client c2 ON c2.client_id=d2.client_id AND c2.gender='F' ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 3))
)
SELECT t.client_id,
 ROUND(t.amount,2) AS loan_amount,
 t.duration AS duration_months,
 ROUND(t.payments*t.duration,2) AS total_payments,
 ROUND(t.payments*t.duration - t.amount,2) AS interest_paid,
 t.status AS loan_status,
 di.A2 AS district, di.A3 AS region,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trans x WHERE x.account_id=t.account_id) AS transaction_count,
 ROUND((SELECT COALESCE(SUM(x.amount),0) FROM trans x WHERE x.account_id=t.account_id AND x.type='PRIJEM'),2) AS total_deposits,
 CASE WHEN (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(x.amount),0) FROM trans x WHERE x.account_id=t.account_id AND x.type='PRIJEM') > 2*t.amount THEN 'High Income'
      WHEN (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(x.amount),0) FROM trans x WHERE x.account_id=t.account_id AND x.type='PRIJEM') > t.amount THEN 'Medium Income'
      ELSE 'Low Income' END AS income_category,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM loan l3 JOIN account a3 ON a3.account_id=l3.account_id JOIN district d3 ON d3.district_id=a3.district_id WHERE d3.A3=di.A3) AS loans_in_region,
 ROUND((SELECT AVG(A11) FROM district WHERE A3=di.A3),2) AS region_avg_salary,
 CAST(strftime('%Y','2026-10-09') AS INT)-CAST(substr(t.birth_date,1,4) AS INT) - (substr(t.birth_date,6,5) > '10-09') AS age
FROM top t JOIN district di ON di.district_id=t.district_id
ORDER BY t.amount DESC;
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 확인했고, 여성 고객 대출 중 금액 상위 3건은 동점 없이 3건이었습니다.

| client_id | 대출액 | 기간(월) | 총 상환액 | 이자 | 상태 | district | region | 거래 수 | 총 입금 | 소득 구분 | 지역 대출 수 | 지역 평균 급여 | 나이 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10997 | 566640.00 | 60 | 566640.00 | 0.00 | C | Hl.m. Praha | Prague | 200 | 447173.00 | Low Income | 84 | 12541.00 | 54 |
| 2823 | 541200.00 | 60 | 541200.00 | 0.00 | D | Karvina | north Moravia | 329 | 515538.00 | Low Income | 117 | 9049.18 | 79 |
| 8506 | 495180.00 | 60 | 495180.00 | 0.00 | C | Jesenik | north Moravia | 76 | 770790.00 | Medium Income | 117 | 9049.18 | 46 |

세 건 모두 월 상환액에 기간을 곱한 값이 대출액과 같아서 이자는 0.00입니다. 데이터에 기록된 payments 값이 그렇습니다.

판단한 기준은 다음과 같습니다.
- 고객은 계좌의 OWNER 권한을 가진 client로 보았습니다.
- 지점의 district와 region은 계좌가 속한 district의 A2(이름), A3(지역)를 썼습니다. 고객 거주지 기준이 아닙니다.
- 총 입금은 type이 PRIJEM인 거래 금액의 합계입니다.
- 지역 대출 수는 해당 region에 속한 district 계좌의 모든 대출을 센 값입니다.
- 지역 평균 급여는 해당 region district들의 A11(평균 급여)을 평균낸 값입니다.

sql: select count(*) from customers c where Currency='EUR' and exists(select 1 from yearmonth y where y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID and Date like '2012%' and Consumption>0) and exists(select 1 from yearmonth y where y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID and Date like '2013%' and Consumption>0)
answer: 1516 EUR customers had gas consumption in both 2012 and 2013. I counted a year as having consumption if any month in it has Consumption > 0, since 180 rows have zero or negative values. Dates in yearmonth are stored as YYYYMM.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT name, MAX(convertedManaCost) m FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND edhrecRank BETWEEN 1 AND 1000 AND name IN (SELECT c2.name FROM cards c2 JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid=c2.uuid WHERE l.status='Banned') GROUP BY name) SELECT ROUND(AVG(m),1) FROM c;
answer: The average mana value is 3.4. It covers 7 distinct creature cards (exact average 3.4286). I read "banned in at least one play format" as any legalities row with status 'Banned' in any format, on any printing of the card. Cards are counted once by name, and "creature" means the types field contains Creature. I used EDHRec ranks 1 to 1000.

sql: select avg(height_cm) as avg_height_cm from superhero s where publisher_id=13 and height_cm>0 and exists(select 1 from hero_power hp where hp.hero_id=s.id and hp.power_id not in (select h2.power_id from hero_power h2 join superhero d on d.id=h2.hero_id where d.publisher_id=4));
answer: 약 202.6 cm입니다. 대상은 39명입니다. DC Comics 캐릭터가 한 명도 갖고 있지 않은 능력을 하나 이상 가진 Marvel Comics 캐릭터만 센 값입니다. height_cm이 0이거나 비어 있으면 측정되지 않은 값으로 보고 제외했습니다.

sql:
SELECT CAST(ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg)) AS INTEGER) AS avg_weight_kg
FROM superhero s
JOIN hero_attribute ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id
JOIN attribute a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id
WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength'
AND ha.attribute_value = (SELECT ha2.attribute_value FROM hero_attribute ha2 JOIN attribute a2 ON a2.id=ha2.attribute_id JOIN superhero h2 ON h2.id=ha2.hero_id WHERE a2.attribute_name='Strength' AND h2.superhero_name='Hulk')
AND s.weight_kg IS NOT NULL AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: 2106589 kg. This is the average weight of all heroes whose Strength equals the Hulk's, rounded to the nearest kilogram. Heroes with a NULL or 0 weight are excluded, as unmeasured. The result is inflated by an extreme weight outlier in the data (up to 90,000,000 kg), which I kept because you asked to include every hero. The fan-out warning from the validator does not apply, since each hero has exactly one Strength row. The Superhero, Attribute and Hero Attribute Score terms the query relies on are still drafts.

sql: SELECT cardKingdomFoilId, cardKingdomId FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND cardKingdomFoilId IS NOT NULL AND cardKingdomFoilId <> '' AND cardKingdomId IS NOT NULL AND cardKingdomId <> '' ORDER BY cardKingdomFoilId, cardKingdomId LIMIT 3
answer:
The three rows are (110505, 110335), (110506, 110336) and (110507, 110337). They belong to Arcbound Bruiser, Arcbound Crusher and Arcbound Fiend.

I treated "creature" as any card whose `types` contains "Creature". A card counts as stocked in both printings when both ids are non-null and non-empty.

The ids are stored as text, and you asked for alphabetical order, so I sorted them as text, with the Card Kingdom id breaking ties. If you meant numerically lowest, the first three rows would be (39001, 38001), (39002, 38002) and (39003, 38003). To get that, sort by `CAST(cardKingdomFoilId AS INTEGER)` and then `CAST(cardKingdomId AS INTEGER)`.

sql: select sum(Reputation) as total_reputation from users u where Location like '%United Kingdom%' and exists (select 1 from posts p where p.OwnerUserId=u.Id)
answer: The combined reputation is 87,153. I counted users whose Location contains "United Kingdom" (for example "London, United Kingdom") and who own at least one post. I left out entries written as "UK" or "England" only, because you asked for the full name and no abbreviations.

sql: SELECT element, COUNT(*) AS bonded_atoms FROM atom WHERE molecule_id='TR397' AND (atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id FROM connected) OR atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id2 FROM connected)) GROUP BY element ORDER BY element
answer: Bonded atoms in TR397 by element: c 34, h 24, n 6, o 16, s 4. An atom counts as bonded if it appears in either column of `connected`. Atoms with no bond are excluded. The `Atom` term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT r.year, ROUND(AVG(s.milliseconds)/1000.0, 2) AS mean_winner_seconds FROM results s JOIN races r ON r.raceId = s.raceId WHERE s.positionOrder = 1 AND s.milliseconds IS NOT NULL AND r.year < 1975 GROUP BY r.year ORDER BY r.year
answer: The query returns 25 rows, one per year from 1950 to 1974. I took the winner to be the result row with positionOrder = 1 that has a recorded milliseconds value. The mean winner time went from 9712.60 seconds in 1950 to 6047.11 in 1974, with a peak of 11323.32 in 1957. Rounding uses SQLite ROUND, which rounds halves away from zero, applied after dividing by 1000. The Race and Race Result terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg)) AS avg_weight_kg
FROM superhero s
JOIN colour c ON s.skin_colour_id = c.id
JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id = a.id
WHERE c.colour = 'Green' AND a.alignment = 'Bad'
  AND s.weight_kg IS NOT NULL AND s.weight_kg > 0
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp JOIN superpower p ON hp.power_id = p.id WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id AND p.power_name = 'Flight')
answer: 121 kg. Reading used: skin colour exactly 'Green' (not 'Green/Blue'), alignment 'Bad', has the 'Flight' superpower, and weight measured (non-NULL and > 0, since NULL or 0 means missing). The Terms used are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c JOIN sets s ON s.code = c.setCode WHERE c.originalReleaseDate LIKE '2014/%' AND s.mtgoCode IS NOT NULL AND s.mtgoCode <> ''
answer: 293 printings. I counted rows in `cards` whose `originalReleaseDate` (stored as text like 2014/12/2) falls in 2014 and whose set has a non-NULL, non-empty `mtgoCode`. Each row counts separately, so a card name that appears in several sets is counted once per set. Cards with no `originalReleaseDate` are not counted.

sql: select count(distinct p.ID) from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where p.SEX='F' and l.WBC>3.5 and l.WBC<9.0 and (l.FG<=150 or l.FG>=450) and CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>15

Values such as 'negative' cast to 0 and are excluded.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg),2) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero s JOIN gender g ON s.gender_id=g.id JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id=a.id WHERE g.gender='Female' AND a.alignment='Good' AND s.weight_kg IS NOT NULL AND s.weight_kg>0
answer: 善(Good)の女性スーパーヒーローの平均体重は 70.76 kg です。体重が未記録(NULL または 0)の行は不明として除外しました。使用した Term(Superhero、Gender、Alignment)は未認証(draft)です。

sql: select round(avg(s.weight_kg),1) as average_weight_kg, count(*) as hero_count from superhero s join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id where p.publisher_name='DC Comics' and s.weight_kg>0
answer: DC Comics superheroes average 101.9 kg, based on 156 heroes. The docs say a weight_kg of 0 or NULL means the weight is missing, so I excluded both. Of the 224 DC heroes, 68 were excluded: 54 with 0 and 14 with NULL.

sql:
WITH RECURSIVE x AS (
  SELECT ex.expense_id, trim(ex.expense_description) || ',' AS rest, '' AS item
  FROM expense ex JOIN budget b ON b.budget_id = ex.link_to_budget
  WHERE b.link_to_event IN (SELECT link_to_event FROM budget WHERE amount - spent < 0)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT expense_id, trim(substr(rest, instr(rest, ',') + 1)), lower(trim(substr(rest, 1, instr(rest, ',') - 1)))
  FROM x WHERE rest <> ''
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT item) FROM x WHERE item <> '';
answer: 7. 과예산 이벤트(budget에서 amount - spent < 0인 항목이 하나라도 있는 이벤트)의 모든 지출을 대상으로, 설명을 쉼표로 나눠 대소문자 구분 없이 서로 다른 품목을 셌습니다. 품목은 water, cookies, chips, pizza, posters, travel mug, parking입니다. 질문에서 '기록에 나온 학기 전체'를 대상으로 하라고 해서 날짜 필터는 넣지 않았습니다. 지출 기록은 2019-08-20부터 2019-11-19까지입니다. 승인 여부(approved)로도 거르지 않았습니다.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.Title, COUNT(l.Id) AS n FROM posts p JOIN postLinks l ON l.PostId = p.Id WHERE p.Title LIKE '%principal component scores%' GROUP BY p.Id, p.Title) SELECT Title, n FROM c WHERE n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM c)

sql: SELECT s.type, COUNT(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL) THEN 1 END) AS sets_with_translation, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL) THEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c WHERE c.setCode = s.code) END),0) AS total_cards FROM sets s GROUP BY s.type ORDER BY s.type
answer:
The query returns 20 set types, sorted alphabetically, each with the number of sets that have a translated name and the total cards in those sets. I counted a set as having an officially translated name if at least one row in set_translations for it has a non-null translation. Each set is counted once, even if it has several translations. Total cards is the number of rows in cards whose setCode matches those sets.

- **Largest:** expansion has 61 sets and 14,201 cards. core has 13 sets and 4,587 cards. commander has 7 sets and 2,036 cards.
- **Zero in both columns:** funny, masterpiece, memorabilia, promo, spellbook, starter, token, treasure_chest and vanguard.

The ontology terms I used (Card Set, Set Translation) are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT frameVersion, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c2 WHERE c2.frameVersion = m.frameVersion) AS card_count FROM (SELECT frameVersion FROM cards WHERE convertedManaCost = 0 AND frameVersion GLOB '[0-9]*' GROUP BY frameVersion HAVING CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER)) FROM cards WHERE convertedManaCost = 0 AND frameVersion GLOB '[0-9]*')) m
answer:
The newest frame version used by a card with converted mana cost 0 is 2015. 25,500 cards in the whole database use it, and only one version qualified, so there is no tie.

The frameVersion column holds 1993, 1997, 2003, 2015 and 'future'. I read 'future' as the Future Sight frame from 2007 and not as a "latest" value, so it ranks below 2015. If you count 'future' as newest, it would give 93 cards. The 'future' frame is only used by 8 zero-cost cards. The query compares the numeric years and leaves 'future' out of the ranking. The Card term it relies on is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: select artist, count(distinct name) c from cards where types like '%Creature%' and artist is not null group by artist having c=(select max(c) from (select count(distinct name) c from cards where types like '%Creature%' and artist is not null group by artist))

sql:
WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT department FROM major WHERE college='College of Humanities and Social Sciences'),
mc AS (SELECT m.major_id, m.major_name, m.department, COUNT(mem.member_id) n FROM major m JOIN d ON d.department=m.department LEFT JOIN member mem ON mem.link_to_major=m.major_id GROUP BY m.major_id)
SELECT department AS department_name,
 group_concat(major_name, ', ') AS majors_offered,
 group_concat(CASE WHEN n>0 THEN major_name END, ', ') AS majors_held_by_members,
 ROUND(1.0*SUM(n)/COUNT(*),2) AS avg_members_per_major
FROM (SELECT * FROM mc ORDER BY department, major_name) GROUP BY department ORDER BY department;
answer:
The query returns 11 departments in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences. Each row has the department name, a comma-separated list of the majors it offers, a list of the majors with at least one member (empty when none), and the average members per offered major.

Only 4 departments have any members:
- Languages, Philosophy and Communication Studies Department: Chinese, Communication Studies and Portuguese are held. The average is 0.38, which is 3 members across 8 majors.
- Liberal Arts Program: Liberal Arts is held, and the average is 1.0.
- Political Science Department: International Studies and Law and Constitutional Studies are held, and the average is 1.0.
- The other 7 departments have no members, so their average is 0.0.

Readings I chose:
- "Majors it offers" and "majors held" are lists of major names, not counts.
- The average is the department's total members divided by all majors it offers, including majors with no members.
- Members come from `member.link_to_major`. One member has no major recorded and is not counted.
- Every major in these departments is already in the college, so the "any major sits in the college" rule changes nothing.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(weight_kg),2) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero WHERE weight_kg IS NOT NULL AND weight_kg>0 AND superhero_name<>'3-D Man' AND id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id IN (SELECT power_id FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id=(SELECT id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name='3-D Man')))
answer: 282411.79 kg. I treated a weight of 0 as not recorded, like NULL, and excluded 3-D Man himself. Extreme weights in the data (up to 90,000,000 kg) stay in the average, which is why it is so high. The "Superhero" Term used is still a draft.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS user_count FROM (SELECT o.UserId FROM (SELECT UserId, MIN(Date) AS od FROM badges WHERE Name='Organizer' GROUP BY UserId) o JOIN users u ON u.Id=o.UserId WHERE u.Location LIKE '%Germany%' AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM badges b WHERE b.UserId=o.UserId AND b.Date<o.od)>=5)

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.surname, r.name AS race, (CAST(substr(q.q2,1,instr(q.q2,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60000 + CAST(replace(substr(q.q2,instr(q.q2,':')+1),'.','') AS INTEGER)) AS ms FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2<>'') SELECT surname, race FROM t WHERE ms=(SELECT MIN(ms) FROM t)

Q2 times are text, so the query converts them to milliseconds before taking the minimum, and it skips drivers with no Q2 time. sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT artist) FROM cards WHERE borderColor='black' AND (',' || availability || ',') LIKE '%,arena,%' AND (',' || availability || ',') NOT LIKE '%,mtgo,%' AND power GLOB '[0-9]*' AND power NOT GLOB '*[^0-9]*' AND CAST(power AS INTEGER) >= 5 AND artist IS NOT NULL
answer: 56 artists. Reading used: availability includes 'arena' and excludes 'mtgo' (whole-token match); power is purely numeric and >= 5 (variable powers like '*' excluded); black border; distinct non-null artists across all printings. Note: the Card term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql:
WITH pop AS (
  SELECT s.CDSCode,
         f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enr, f."FRPM Count (K-12)" AS frpm,
         CAST(f."FRPM Count (K-12)" AS REAL)/f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS share
  FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode
  WHERE s.Charter = 0 AND s.EdOpsCode = 'TRAD' AND f."School Code" <> '0000000'
    AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" > 100 AND f."FRPM Count (K-12)" IS NOT NULL
), picks AS (
  SELECT CDSCode, 'largest FRPM-eligible count' AS part, 1 AS ord FROM pop WHERE frpm = (SELECT MAX(frpm) FROM pop)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT CDSCode, 'smallest FRPM share', 2 FROM pop WHERE share = (SELECT MIN(share) FROM pop)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT CDSCode, 'the CDS code from my notes', 3 FROM schools WHERE CDSCode = '04615150435602'
)
SELECT k.part AS part, s.School AS school_name, s.County AS county, s.City AS city,
       s.MailStreet AS mailing_street, s.MailCity AS mailing_city, s.MailState AS mailing_state, s.MailZip AS mailing_zip,
       s.Website AS website, f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS k12_enrollment, f."FRPM Count (K-12)" AS frpm_count,
       CAST(f."FRPM Count (K-12)" AS REAL)/f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS frpm_share,
       (t.AvgScrRead + t.AvgScrMath + t.AvgScrWrite) AS avg_total_sat,
       100.0 * t.NumGE1500 / NULLIF(t.NumTstTakr,0) AS pct_sat_1500_plus,
       s.OpenDate AS opening_date,
       CASE WHEN s.ClosedDate IS NOT NULL AND s.ClosedDate <> '' THEN 'closed' ELSE 'open' END AS status
FROM picks k
JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = k.CDSCode
JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = k.CDSCode
LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = k.CDSCode
ORDER BY k.ord, s.School
answer: Three rows, one per part, no ties and no school answering more than one part. Paramount High (Los Angeles County, Paramount) has the largest FRPM count: 4,419 of 4,814 students (91.8%), average total SAT 1272, 14.8% of takers at 1500 or more, opened 1953-07-01, open, no website. Orinda Intermediate (Contra Costa, Orinda) has the smallest FRPM share: 2 of 907 (0.22%), no SAT record, opened 1980-07-01, open, no website. Oroville High (Butte, Oroville), the notes code, has 692 of 982 (70.5%), average total SAT 1395, 32.7% of takers at 1500 or more, opened 1980-07-01, open, website http://ohs.ouhsd.org. Mailing addresses are in the result rows. Assumptions: the notes code 4615150435602 has 13 digits, so I read it as 04615150435602 with a leading zero lost. 'Regular' means Education Option Code 'TRAD', and non-charter means Charter = 0. Enrollment above 100 uses the FRPM table's K-12 enrollment, with district-office rows excluded. FRPM share is a 0-1 fraction. Average total SAT is the sum of the reading, math and writing averages. The percent at 1500 or more is takers at 1500 or more divided by takers, times 100. Status is 'closed' only if a closing date exists. I did not filter on Active/Closed status. The benchmark school is shown whether or not it meets the filters. The School, FRPM record and SAT record Terms are draft, not certified.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(Admission='+')/count(*),2) as pct from Patient p where strftime('%Y',Birthday) between '1930' and '1940' and exists(select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID)
answer: 35.90 (%). 검사 기록이 있고 1930~1940년생인 환자 39명 중 14명이 입원(Admission='+')입니다. 환자 단위로 한 번씩만 계산했고, 입원 여부는 '+'만 입원으로 봤습니다.

sql:
WITH w AS (
 SELECT m.home_team_api_id t, count(*) n FROM Match m
 WHERE m.home_team_goal - m.away_team_goal >= 3
 AND (SELECT a.buildUpPlaySpeedClass FROM Team_Attributes a WHERE a.team_api_id=m.home_team_api_id AND a.date<=m.date ORDER BY a.date DESC LIMIT 1)='Fast'
 GROUP BY m.home_team_api_id)
SELECT t.team_long_name, t.team_short_name, w.n FROM w JOIN Team t ON t.team_api_id=w.t
WHERE w.n=(SELECT max(n) FROM w) ORDER BY t.team_long_name;
answer:
Borussia Dortmund (DOR) has the most such home wins: 29. No other club ties it.

I read your tie condition as a request for the club or clubs with the highest count. That means the query returns only the top count, not every club with at least one qualifying win. If you wanted every club, remove the final WHERE filter.

A match counts when the home side won by 3 or more goals and the club's latest Team_Attributes row dated on or before the match date has buildUpPlaySpeedClass = 'Fast'. Clubs are grouped by team_api_id, so two clubs that share a short name stay separate. I ran the query and it returned the single row above.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(case when t.k_symbol='SIPO' then t.amount else 0 end)/sum(t.amount),2) as sipo_pct from trans t join account a on a.account_id=t.account_id where a.district_id=18 and t.type='VYDAJ' and trim(coalesce(t.k_symbol,''))<>''
answer: 93.31% of the amount of outgoing payments that state a purpose went to household payments (SIPO). The base is 2,495 transactions on accounts in the Pisek district (district_id 18), over the full history. I treated 'outgoing' as type 'VYDAJ' and 'states a purpose' as a non-empty k_symbol. I measured the share by amount, not by transaction count.

sql: SELECT SUM(p.SEX='F') - SUM(p.SEX='M') AS diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE l.Date=(SELECT MAX(Date) FROM Laboratory x WHERE x.ID=l.ID) AND l.RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>=32
answer: 1. Among patients whose most recent laboratory row has anti-RNP of 32 or higher, there is 1 female and 0 males, so the difference is 1. I read "most recent visit" as each patient's latest Laboratory.Date, whether or not RNP was measured that day. Patients whose latest row has a null RNP, or the text value "negative", do not count. The warnings about fan-out do not apply here, because the query returns one row per patient. The Laboratory Test and Patient terms are still drafts.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT m.major_id) FROM member mem JOIN major m ON mem.link_to_major = m.major_id WHERE m.department = 'Political Science Department'
answer: Political Science Department 소속 동아리 회원들은 서로 다른 2개 전공을 공부하고 있습니다. 전공 수는 major_id 기준으로 세었고, 회원이 있는 전공만 포함했습니다. 이 결과는 아직 검증되지 않은 초안(draft) 상태의 Major 용어를 사용했습니다.

sql:
WITH risky AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t.team_api_id, t.team_short_name
  FROM Team t JOIN Team_Attributes a ON a.team_api_id = t.team_api_id
  WHERE a.chanceCreationPassingClass = 'Risky'
),
inforce AS (
  SELECT r.team_short_name, r.team_api_id,
    (SELECT a.chanceCreationPassing FROM Team_Attributes a
      WHERE a.team_api_id = r.team_api_id AND date(a.date) <= '2014-09-19'
      ORDER BY a.date DESC LIMIT 1) AS passing
  FROM risky r
)
SELECT team_short_name, COUNT(*) AS club_count, ROUND(AVG(passing), 1) AS avg_passing_risk
FROM inforce
GROUP BY team_short_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY avg_passing_risk DESC, team_short_name ASC
answer: 6 short names, each carried by 2 Risky clubs: REA 69.5, GEN 66.5, WOL 61.5, MAR 58.0, HAM 56.0, LEV 53.5 (average chanceCreationPassing in force on 2014-09-19). Choices: a club is Risky if any snapshot had class Risky; the club count includes only those Risky clubs; "in force" is each club's latest snapshot dated on or before 2014-09-19. A club with no snapshot by then adds nothing to the average but still counts toward the club count. The Team and Team Attributes terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT c.watermark AS guild, COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) AS n FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid=c.uuid WHERE c.watermark IN ('azorius','boros','dimir','golgari','gruul','izzet','orzhov','rakdos','selesnya','simic') GROUP BY c.watermark) SELECT guild, n FROM t WHERE n=(SELECT MAX(n) FROM t)
answer: Golgari has the most cards printed in another language, with 148 cards, and no other guild ties with it. I counted a card if it has at least one `foreign_data` row, and I counted card printings (distinct `cards.id`), not distinct card names. Watermark values are stored in lowercase, so the filter uses 'golgari' and so on. The `Card` term is still a draft.

sql:
WITH s AS (
 SELECT c.Segment,
  SUM(CASE WHEN substr(y.Date,1,4)='2012' THEN y.Consumption END) a,
  SUM(CASE WHEN substr(y.Date,1,4)='2013' THEN y.Consumption END) b
 FROM yearmonth y JOIN customers c USING(CustomerID)
 WHERE c.Currency='EUR' AND c.Segment IN ('SME','LAM','KAM')
 GROUP BY c.Segment),
p AS (SELECT Segment, ROUND((b-a)*100.0/a,2) pct FROM s)
SELECT Segment, pct FROM p
WHERE pct=(SELECT MAX(pct) FROM p) OR pct=(SELECT MIN(pct) FROM p);
answer: SME had the highest increase at 734.71%, and LAM had the lowest at 539.83%. KAM was in between. I read "percentage increase" as (2013 total − 2012 total) / 2012 total × 100, summed over each segment's EUR customers, with years taken from the first four characters of yearmonth.Date.

sql: select 100.0*sum(cardKingdomId is not null and cardKingdomFoilId is not null)/count(*) from cards where setCode='CSP'
answer: 100%. I read "Coldsnap" as the main set (code CSP), which has 155 printings, and all of them have both a Card Kingdom ID and a foil ID. I left out the Coldsnap Theme Decks (CST) and Coldsnap Promos (PCSP) sets.

sql: select round(avg(weight_kg),2) from superhero where publisher_id=5 and weight_kg>0 and id in (select hero_id from hero_power)
answer: 77.4 kg. Reading used: weight NULL or 0 counts as not recorded (per the docs), and heroes with at least one row in hero_power, published by George Lucas (publisher_id 5).

sql:
WITH t AS (
 SELECT d.forename||' '||d.surname AS driver, r.name AS race, r.year AS yr, q.q3 AS q3,
  CAST(substr(q.q3,1,instr(q.q3,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60000 + CAST(round(CAST(substr(q.q3,instr(q.q3,':')+1) AS REAL)*1000) AS INTEGER) AS ms
 FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId
 WHERE d.nationality='British' AND CAST(substr(d.dob,1,4) AS INTEGER)>1980 AND coalesce(q.q3,'')<>'')
SELECT driver, race, yr, q3 FROM t WHERE ms=(SELECT min(ms) FROM t);
answer: Lewis Hamilton, 2017 Austrian Grand Prix, Q3 time 1:04.424. I read "fastest" as the lowest Q3 time, counted only rows with a non-empty Q3, and took British to mean drivers.nationality = 'British'. Birth year is later than 1980. One row came back, so there was no tie.

sql: select count(distinct case when d.forename='Peter' then d.driverId end) as peter, count(distinct case when d.forename='John' then d.driverId end) as john from results r join drivers d using(driverId) where r.positionOrder=1 and d.forename in ('Peter','John')
answer: Peter: 3 distinct race-winning drivers; John: 2. The counts are not equal. I read "won a race" as a result row with positionOrder = 1, and `position = 1` gives the same counts. I matched the forename exactly as stored in drivers.forename.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t.k_symbol = 'SIPO' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(t.amount), 2) AS sipo_pct
FROM trans t
JOIN account a ON t.account_id = a.account_id
JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
WHERE d.A2 = 'Pisek' AND t.type <> 'PRIJEM' AND t.k_symbol IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(t.k_symbol) <> ''
answer: 93.31% — Pisek 지점 계좌의 출금 중 목적(k_symbol)이 기재된 거래의 금액 합계에서 SIPO(가계 자동이체)가 차지하는 비율입니다. 출금은 type이 'PRIJEM'이 아닌 거래(VYDAJ, VYBER)로 보았고, 목적이 NULL이거나 공백인 거래는 제외했으며, 전체 기간을 대상으로 했습니다.

sql: select d.driverRef from qualifying q join races r using(raceId) join drivers d using(driverId) where r.year=2017 and r.name='Italian Grand Prix' and coalesce(q.q2,'')='' order by q.q1 desc, q.driverId
answer: I treated "eliminated after the first session" as having no Q2 time (q2 is NULL or empty). In the 2017 Italian GP that gives 5 drivers. Slowest to fastest Q1 time: grosjean (1:43.355), wehrlein (1:41.875), ericsson (1:41.732), jolyon_palmer (1:40.646), kevin_magnussen (1:40.489). No two drivers tied on time, so the driverId tie-break did not come into play. Times are `m:ss.mmm` text, so sorting them as text gives the right order.

sql:
SELECT sp.power_name, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS n
FROM superhero s
JOIN publisher p ON p.id=s.publisher_id
JOIN hero_power hp ON hp.hero_id=s.id
JOIN superpower sp ON sp.id=hp.power_id
WHERE p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics' AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name<>'-'
GROUP BY sp.id
HAVING n=(SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT s2.id) c FROM superhero s2 JOIN publisher p2 ON p2.id=s2.publisher_id JOIN hero_power h2 ON h2.hero_id=s2.id WHERE p2.publisher_name='Marvel Comics' AND s2.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s2.full_name<>'-' GROUP BY h2.power_id))
answer: Super Strength, 151 heroes. There is no tie. I counted a full name as known when it is neither NULL nor '-', because the wiki says both values mean the name is missing. The publisher is 'Marvel Comics'.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(t), 2) AS avg_total_spent_per_event FROM (SELECT e.event_id, COALESCE(SUM(b.spent), 0) AS t FROM event e LEFT JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_id)
answer: The average total spent per event is $49.67. I averaged over all 42 recorded events and counted events with no budget lines as $0 spent. Spending is the sum of budget.spent across all categories for each event, and the total of $2,086.05 is the same if you sum expense.cost instead. Averaging only the 23 events that had spending gives $90.70. The Event, Budget and Expense Terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT c.nationality, COUNT(DISTINCT r.constructorId) AS constructor_count FROM constructors c LEFT JOIN results r ON r.constructorId = c.constructorId AND r."rank" = 1 GROUP BY c.nationality ORDER BY constructor_count DESC, c.nationality
answer:
24개 국적이 모두 결과에 나옵니다. 세계 최고 랩 기록 구성자 수가 많은 순서는 영국 4, 독일 2, 이탈리아 2, 오스트리아·프랑스·인도·일본·스위스 각 1이고, 나머지 16개 국적(미국, 호주, 벨기에 등)은 0입니다.

해석 기준은 두 가지입니다. 공식 기록상 최고 랩은 results.rank = 1인 행으로 보았고, 랩 타임은 직접 계산하지 않았습니다. 한 경주에서 최고 랩을 기록한 팀이 여러 번이어도 1개 팀으로 세도록 constructorId를 중복 제거해 셌습니다. 국적 표기는 데이터 그대로("Belgium" 포함) 두었습니다. 사용한 Constructor, Race Result 용어는 아직 인증(certified)되지 않은 draft 상태입니다.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(ha.attribute_value), 1) AS avg_intelligence
FROM hero_attribute ha
JOIN attribute a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id
WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Intelligence'
  AND ha.attribute_value IS NOT NULL
  AND ha.hero_id IN (
    SELECT hp.hero_id
    FROM hero_power hp
    JOIN superpower sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id
    WHERE sp.power_name IN ('Super Speed', 'Death Touch')
  )
answer: 평균 지능 점수는 85.9입니다. 'Super Speed' 또는 'Death Touch' 능력을 가진 영웅 중 지능 점수가 있는 220명을 대상으로 계산했습니다. 두 능력을 모두 가진 영웅은 한 번만 계산했습니다. 지능 값이 비어 있는 영웅은 제외했습니다.

sql: select s.School, s.Street from frpm f join schools s on s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode where s.School is not null and f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > 30 and f."High Grade" in ('K','1','2','3','4','5','6','7','8')
answer:
The query returns 121 schools, one row each, with school name and street address. I joined frpm to schools on CDSCode. The enrollment and highest-grade fields come from frpm, and the name and physical street address come from schools.

Choices I made:
- I took "highest grade of enrollment" to be frpm `High Grade`, and kept the values K and 1 through 8.
- I excluded `P` (preschool, 2 rows), Adult, and 9 or higher.
- "Named school" means `schools.School` is not NULL, which removes district records.
- Schools with NULL ages 5-17 enrollment (14 in frpm) drop out because the comparison can't be evaluated.
- I did not filter on Active versus Closed status, because the question doesn't mention it.

sql:
WITH a AS (
  SELECT a.account_id, a.district_id, strftime('%Y', a.date) AS yr,
         COALESCE((SELECT SUM(l.amount) FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id = a.account_id), 0) AS lent
  FROM account a JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id
  WHERE d.A3 = 'central Bohemia' AND a.date >= '1996-01-01'
), dd AS (
  SELECT yr, district_id, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(lent) AS lent, 1.0*SUM(lent)/COUNT(*) AS per
  FROM a GROUP BY yr, district_id
)
SELECT yr AS year, SUM(n) AS accounts_opened, SUM(lent) AS total_lent, ROUND(AVG(per), 2) AS avg_lent_per_account_across_districts
FROM dd GROUP BY yr ORDER BY yr;
answer:
결과 (central Bohemia, 1996-01-01 이후 개설 계좌):
- 1996: 계좌 191개, 대출 총액 4,887,024, 지역 평균 23,639.03
- 1997: 계좌 114개, 대출 총액 1,971,468, 지역 평균 19,809.53

적용한 해석: 지역은 district.A3 = 'central Bohemia'로 정했고, 연도는 계좌 개설일(account.date)에서 문자열로 뽑았습니다. 대출이 없는 계좌는 0으로 계산했습니다. 평균은 먼저 연도별로 구역(district)마다 '대출 총액 ÷ 그 구역에서 개설된 계좌 수'를 구한 뒤, 그 값을 구역 간에 단순 평균했습니다(계좌 수로 가중하지 않음). 그 연도에 계좌가 개설된 구역만 평균에 포함됩니다.

sql: select count(distinct c.uuid) from cards c join rulings r on r.uuid=c.uuid where (c.power is null or c.power='' or c.power like '%*%') and r.text like '%triggered ability%'
answer: 1,382 distinct card printings (distinct uuid). I read "no recorded power" as power NULL or empty, and "variable power" as any power containing '*' (for example '*' or '*²'). The ruling match is a case-insensitive substring match on 'triggered ability'.

sql: select cast(frameVersion as integer) as frameYear, count(*) as cardCount from cards where leadershipSkills like '%''commander'': True%' and cardKingdomId is not null and cardKingdomFoilId is not null and frameVersion glob '[0-9]*' group by frameVersion order by cast(frameVersion as integer) desc limit 1
answer: 2015 / 820. 가정: 'Commander 사령관 가능'은 leadershipSkills에 commander: True가 있는 경우, 'Card Kingdom 목록에 일반판과 포일판 모두 있음'은 cardKingdomId와 cardKingdomFoilId가 둘 다 있는 경우로 봤습니다. 'future'는 연도가 아니라 제외했습니다. 카드 수는 cards 테이블의 행(인쇄본) 기준 820개입니다. 카드 이름 기준 중복 제거 시에는 558개입니다.

sql: SELECT e.expense_description, COUNT(*) AS times_bought FROM expense e JOIN member m ON m.member_id = e.link_to_member WHERE m.first_name = 'Sacha' AND m.last_name = 'Harrison' GROUP BY e.expense_description
answer: I read "items bought with club money" as the expense records linked to Sacha Harrison (member ID rec4BLdZHS2Blfp4v). I grouped them by expense description and counted the rows in each group. All of her expenses are marked approved, so I did not filter on approval. Results: Alumni Glass 1, Bakery - Donuts, muffins 1, Pizza 1, Post Cards, Posters 1, Posters 3, Travel Mug 2, Water, chips, cookies 3. Descriptions are matched as exact text, so "Posters" and "Post Cards, Posters" are counted as separate items.

sql: select count(distinct l.ID) from Laboratory l join Patient p on p.ID=l.ID where l.Date between '1981-01-01' and '1986-12-31' and l.PLT between 100 and 400 and l."U-PRO" in ('1','2','3','4') and p.Birthday is not null and (cast(strftime('%Y',l.Date) as int)-cast(strftime('%Y',p.Birthday) as int)-(strftime('%m-%d',l.Date)<strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)))<50
answer: 45 patients. I read "proteinuria" as a U-PRO grade of 1, 2, 3 or 4. In 1981–1986 the U-PRO column only holds 0, 1–4, 'TR' (trace) and '%%', so I excluded 0, trace and '%%'.
