sql: select round(avg(coalesce(f."FRPM Count (Ages 5-17)",0)),2) from schools s left join frpm f on f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode and f."Academic Year"='2014-2015' where s.SOC='11'
answer: 5.42. Reading used: Youth Authority schools are the 43 schools with SOC='11' (Youth Authority Facilities), whether active, closed or merged. Only 4 of them have a 2014-2015 FRPM record; the other 39 count as 0. Measure is FRPM Count (Ages 5-17).

sql:
WITH f AS (
 SELECT fr.CDSCode, fr.`Charter School (Y/N)` ch,
  ROUND(fr.`Free Meal Count (K-12)`*100.0/fr.`Enrollment (K-12)`,2) fp,
  ROUND(fr.`FRPM Count (K-12)`*100.0/fr.`Enrollment (K-12)`,2) rp
 FROM frpm fr
 WHERE fr.`County Name`=(SELECT County FROM schools WHERE CDSCode='01612590125716')
  AND fr.`Free Meal Count (K-12)`>500 AND fr.`FRPM Count (K-12)`<700
  AND fr.`School Code` NOT IN ('0000000') AND fr.`School Name`<>'District Office'
)
SELECT (SELECT County FROM schools WHERE CDSCode='01612590125716') AS county,
 COUNT(*) AS num_schools,
 ROUND(AVG(fp),2) AS avg_free_pct, ROUND(AVG(rp),2) AS avg_frpm_pct,
 SUM(ch=1) AS charter_schools, SUM(ch=0) AS non_charter_schools,
 (SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.AvgScrRead+s.AvgScrMath+s.AvgScrWrite),2) FROM f JOIN satscores s ON s.cds=f.CDSCode
   WHERE s.AvgScrRead IS NOT NULL AND s.AvgScrMath IS NOT NULL AND s.AvgScrWrite IS NOT NULL) AS avg_sat
FROM f;
answer: Alameda County: 13 schools, average free-meal 73.53%, average FRPM 80.65%, 0 charter and 13 non-charter schools, average SAT 1189.00. Choices I made: (1) The CDS code you gave is 13 digits, so I read it as 01612590125716 with the leading zero dropped. That code is Fremont High in Alameda. A different school with the same name is in Santa Clara. (2) I used each school's free (or FRPM) count divided by K-12 enrollment, times 100, rounded to 2 decimals. This matches the stored percent columns. (3) I excluded district-office rows. (4) The SAT average covers only schools that have a satscores row with all three section averages. Schools with no SAT record, or with suppressed (NULL) section scores, are excluded.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE duelDeck='b' AND hasFoil=0 AND power GLOB '*[0-9]*' AND power NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.-]*' AND CAST(power AS REAL) < 3
answer: 213 card printings in duel deck B have no foil version (hasFoil=0) and a numeric power strictly below 3. Non-numeric powers ('*', '1+*', '?') and cards with no power were excluded. Counted per printing row, not distinct names.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) FROM cards WHERE frameVersion IN ('2015','future') AND text IS NOT NULL AND text<>''
answer: 11,467 distinct card names. Assumptions: "has a text box" means the rules text is non-null and non-empty. "2015 or later" includes the frame version 'future' as well as '2015', since frameVersion is stored as text and 'future' is the only later value. If you count only '2015', the answer is 11,410. The Card term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: select distinct c.bond_id from connected c join atom a1 on a1.atom_id=c.atom_id join atom a2 on a2.atom_id=c.atom_id2 where (a1.element='p' and a2.element='n') or (a1.element='n' and a2.element='p');
answer: 질문을 '인(P)과 질소(N) 원자를 잇는 결합'으로 해석해 bond_id만 반환했습니다. 해당하는 결합은 6개입니다: TR032_2_3, TR032_3_5, TR058_1_3, TR058_1_4, TR058_1_5, TR298_1_5.

sql: SELECT d.account_id, (SELECT MAX(A11)-MIN(A11) FROM district) AS diff FROM client c JOIN disp d ON d.client_id=c.client_id WHERE c.gender='F' AND c.district_id=(SELECT district_id FROM district ORDER BY A11 LIMIT 1) ORDER BY c.birth_date ASC LIMIT 1
answer: 계정 ID는 3214이고, 지역 평균 급여(A11)의 최고값과 최저값 차이는 4431입니다. 해석: 최저 평균 급여 지역에 사는 여성 고객 중 birth_date가 가장 이른 사람을 가장 나이 많은 고객으로 보았고, 그 고객의 disp 테이블 계정을 반환했습니다. 고객의 지역은 client.district_id 기준입니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 2) FROM superhero s JOIN hero_attribute h ON h.hero_id = s.id WHERE h.attribute_id = (SELECT id FROM attribute WHERE attribute_name = 'Intelligence') AND h.attribute_value = (SELECT attribute_value FROM hero_attribute WHERE hero_id = (SELECT id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = 'Abomination') AND attribute_id = (SELECT id FROM attribute WHERE attribute_name = 'Intelligence')) AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: The average measured weight is 103.6 kg. Abomination's Intelligence score matches 140 heroes. I counted only heroes with a recorded weight above 0, which drops 29 heroes whose weight is stored as 0, and I treated that 0 as "not measured". If you count those zeros as real weights, the average is 82.14 kg.

sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, q.q3 FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d USING(driverId) WHERE d.nationality='Italian' AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3<>'' AND q.q3=(SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying q2 JOIN drivers d2 USING(driverId) WHERE d2.nationality='Italian' AND q2.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q2.q3<>'')
answer: Jarno Trulli, 1:11.328. Reading used: drivers with nationality 'Italian'; blank Q3 values were excluded, and times are compared as text, which is safe because every non-empty Q3 uses the m:ss.sss format. Only one driver has this time.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 1) FROM superhero s JOIN colour c ON c.id = s.skin_colour_id WHERE c.colour = 'Green' AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: The average weight of green-skinned heroes is 1354.6 kg, based on 15 heroes with a known weight. I treated a weight of 0 as unknown, as the wiki and docs say, so those rows are excluded along with NULLs. The figure is high because a few very heavy characters pull the average up. I ran the equivalent query with skin_colour_id=14, and the one above joins on the colour name 'Green'.

sql: select count(distinct ID) from Patient where lower(Diagnosis) like '%psoriatic arthritis%'
answer: 2명입니다. Patient 테이블의 Diagnosis에 'Psoriatic arthritis'가 들어 있는 환자를 대소문자 구분 없이 세었고, 기간이나 추적 상태 조건은 두지 않았습니다. 표기가 'Psoriatic Arthritis'와 'Psoriatic arthritis'로 각각 1건씩 다르게 입력되어 있어 둘을 합쳤습니다.

sql:
SELECT u.DisplayName, COUNT(*) AS edit_comment_count
FROM postHistory ph
JOIN posts p ON ph.PostId = p.Id
JOIN users u ON ph.UserId = u.Id
WHERE p.Title = 'Why square the difference instead of taking the absolute value in standard deviation?'
  AND ph.Comment IS NOT NULL AND ph.Comment <> ''
GROUP BY u.Id, u.DisplayName
HAVING COUNT(*) = (
  SELECT MAX(c) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM postHistory ph2
    JOIN posts p2 ON ph2.PostId = p2.Id
    WHERE p2.Title = 'Why square the difference instead of taking the absolute value in standard deviation?'
      AND ph2.Comment IS NOT NULL AND ph2.Comment <> '' AND ph2.UserId IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY ph2.UserId))
answer: mbq left the most edit comments on that post, 3, with no ties. I counted each postHistory revision with a non-empty Comment as one edit comment, repeats included. The editor name comes from users.DisplayName via postHistory.UserId, because postHistory.UserDisplayName is often empty. Revisions with no UserId are excluded. The Post, Post History Event and User Terms are draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT SUM(p.SEX='M') AS male, SUM(p.SEX='F') AS female FROM Patient p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.GPT>=60)
answer: 178 male and 956 female patients have never had an ALT (GPT) result above the normal range. I read the documented normal range "N < 60" as meaning any GPT of 60 or higher is abnormal. Patients with no lab rows, or only null GPT values, count as never abnormal. 13 patients have a blank sex value and are excluded, since you asked for male and female only.

sql:
SELECT s.FundingType AS funding_type,
 COUNT(*) AS charter_schools,
 SUM(f."Enrollment (K-12)") AS total_enrollment_2014_15,
 ROUND(AVG(f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)")*100, 2) AS avg_frpm_pct,
 ROUND(AVG(t.AvgScrRead + t.AvgScrMath + t.AvgScrWrite), 2) AS avg_sat_total
FROM schools s
LEFT JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode
LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode AND t.rtype = 'S'
WHERE s.Charter = 1 AND s.StatusType = 'Active' AND s.FundingType IN ('Directly funded','Locally funded')
GROUP BY s.FundingType
answer: Directly funded: 902 active charter schools, 372,954 enrolled (2014-15 K-12), 63.88% average FRPM eligibility, 1350.84 average combined SAT. Locally funded: 340 schools, 150,022 enrolled, 44.84%, 1480.15. Choices: charter = Charter=1 and StatusType='Active'; 'Not in CS funding model' excluded; FRPM % is the simple mean of each school's K-12 FRPM rate x100; SAT is the mean of per-school reading+math+writing across school-level rows with scores (schools without SAT stay in the other measures). The ontology terms used are drafts, not certified.

sql: select count(*)/12.0 as avg_schools_per_month from schools where County='San Diego' and OpenDate>='1980-01-01' and OpenDate<'1981-01-01' and DOC in ('52','54','56')
answer: 약 47.6667개입니다(572개 ÷ 12). 1980년 San Diego 카운티에서 문을 연 학교는 모두 1980-07-01 한 날에 개교한 것으로 기록되어 있어, 나머지 11개월은 0으로 계산했습니다. '학군(school district) 관할'은 DOC 코드 52(초등학군), 54(통합학군), 56(고등학군)으로 해석했습니다. 카운티교육청(00), 비학교 시설(34), 커뮤니티칼리지 학군(58), ROC/P(98)는 제외했습니다. 커뮤니티칼리지 학군까지 포함하면 581개로 평균이 약 48.42가 됩니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) FROM races r JOIN results x ON x.raceId=r.raceId JOIN status s ON s.statusId=x.statusId WHERE r.name='Canadian Grand Prix' AND s.status='Accident'
answer: 27 runnings of the Canadian Grand Prix had at least one car retire with an 'Accident' status. The 'Fatal accident' status is excluded, as requested. The query ran and returned 27. It relies on the Race and Race Result Status terms, which are still draft.

sql: select round((sum(case when Date like '2013%' then Consumption end)-sum(case when Date like '2012%' then Consumption end))/sum(case when Date like '2012%' then Consumption end),4) as relative_change from yearmonth where CustomerID=(select CustomerID from transactions_1k where Date='2012-08-25' and Price=634.8)
answer: 2012년 8월 25일에 634.8을 결제한 고객은 6718번입니다. 이 고객의 연간 사용량(yearmonth의 월별 Consumption 합계)은 2012년에서 2013년으로 가면서 5.8152만큼 늘었습니다. 이는 약 581.52% 증가에 해당합니다.

sql: SELECT p.player_api_id, p.player_name FROM Player p JOIN Player_Attributes a ON a.player_api_id=p.player_api_id WHERE p.height>180 AND a.heading_accuracy IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.player_api_id ORDER BY AVG(a.heading_accuracy) DESC, p.player_api_id LIMIT 10
answer: 상위 10명은 Michael Ballack, Fernando Llorente, John Terry, Naldo, Luca Toni, Per Mertesacker, Didier Drogba, Miroslav Klose, Daniel van Buyten, Fernando Morientes 순입니다. 키가 180cm를 넘는 선수만 대상으로 했고, 선수별 모든 기록의 heading_accuracy 평균(NULL 제외)으로 정렬했습니다. 동점이면 player_api_id가 작은 선수가 먼저 옵니다. 질문이 '선수'를 묻고 있어 ID와 이름을 함께 출력했습니다.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(s.Virtual in ('F','P'))/count(*),1) from satscores t join schools s on s.CDSCode=t.cds where t.AvgScrMath>400
answer: 22.3%. 평균 SAT 수학 점수가 400점을 넘는 학교 1,537곳 중 가상 수업을 전면(F) 또는 일부(P) 운영하는 학교의 비율입니다. Virtual 값이 비어 있는 411곳은 가상 수업을 하지 않는 것으로 보고 분모에 포함했습니다. 제외하면 비율이 달라질 수 있습니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(e."aCL IgM"), 2) FROM Examination e WHERE e."aCL IgM" > 0 AND e.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Patient WHERE REPLACE(Diagnosis, 'SJS susp', '') LIKE '%SJS%')
answer:
평균 anti-cardiolipin IgM 농도는 2.89입니다. 값이 0보다 큰 검사 19건을 기준으로 계산했습니다.

적용한 기준은 다음과 같습니다.
- 환자 단위 진단(Patient.Diagnosis)에 'SJS susp'를 제외하고도 'SJS'가 남아 있는 환자만 포함했습니다. 'RA, SJS susp'처럼 의심만 있는 환자는 빠지고, 'SJS susp, ... SJS'처럼 확진이 함께 적힌 환자는 들어갑니다.
- 'SJS, MCTD susp'처럼 SJS 뒤가 아니라 다른 질환에 susp가 붙은 경우는 SJS가 확진으로 적힌 것으로 보고 포함했습니다.
- 검사 날짜는 제한하지 않았습니다. aCL IgM이 0인 검사는 측정하지 않은 것으로 보고 평균에서 뺐습니다.

sql: SELECT p.ID, CAST((strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',p.Birthday)) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09')<strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)) AS INT) AS age FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID WHERE l.HCT>=52 GROUP BY p.ID HAVING COUNT(*)>=2
answer: Three patients qualify: 2307640 (age 73), 3182521 (age 73) and 4007151 (age 58). I counted laboratory rows with HCT >= 52 per patient, kept those with at least two, and computed completed years of age as of 2026-10-09 from Birthday.

sql: SELECT e.type, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS member_count FROM event e LEFT JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.location = 'MU 215' GROUP BY e.type
answer:
MU 215에서 열린 행사 유형별로, 해당 유형 행사에 한 번이라도 참석한 서로 다른 회원 수입니다. 행사 상태(Planning, Open, Closed)는 가리지 않았습니다.

- Meeting: 30명
- Guest Speaker: 29명
- Election: 0명 (MU 215에서 열렸지만 참석 기록이 없습니다)

선택한 해석: 같은 회원이 한 유형의 여러 행사에 참석해도 1명으로 계산했습니다(DISTINCT). 행사 유형은 event.type 열을 기준으로 했고, 참석 기록이 없는 유형도 LEFT JOIN으로 남겼습니다.

sql:
WITH t AS (SELECT c.CustomerID, c.Segment, SUM(y.Consumption) tot FROM customers c JOIN yearmonth y ON y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID WHERE c.Currency='CZK' AND y.Date LIKE '2013%' GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.Segment),
r AS (SELECT Segment, tot, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Segment ORDER BY tot, CustomerID) rn FROM t),
p AS (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN Segment='SME' THEN tot END) s, MAX(CASE WHEN Segment='LAM' THEN tot END) l, MAX(CASE WHEN Segment='KAM' THEN tot END) k FROM r WHERE rn=1)
SELECT ROUND(s-l,2) AS sme_minus_lam, ROUND(l-k,2) AS lam_minus_kam, ROUND(k-s,2) AS kam_minus_sme FROM p
answer: SME-LAM = -14009.34, LAM-KAM = 6046.62, KAM-SME = 7962.72. These are based on 2013 data (Jan-Nov, since the data ends at 201311), CZK customers with at least one 2013 record; ties broken by smaller CustomerID. The Customer and Monthly Customer Consumption terms used are draft (uncertified).

sql: select d.forename,d.surname,d.url,d.dob,count(q.q3) as q3_count from drivers d left join qualifying q on q.driverId=d.driverId and coalesce(q.q3,'')<>'' where d.nationality='German' and d.dob between '1971-01-01' and '1985-12-31' group by d.driverId order by q3_count desc, d.dob
answer: 7 German drivers born 1971-1985 are listed. Q3 counts: Nico Rosberg 149, Nick Heidfeld 44, Adrian Sutil 19, Ralf Schumacher 15, Timo Glock 13, Markus Winkelhock 0, André Lotterer 0. Choices I made: a Q3 time means a non-empty q3 value, since NULL and '' both mean no time. Drivers with zero Q3 times are kept. Q3 data exists only in the qualifying table, which covers 2003-2017, so earlier races contribute nothing.

sql: select c.colors, count(distinct l.format) as legal_formats from cards c join legalities l on l.uuid=c.uuid and l.status='Legal' where c.id between 1 and 20 group by c.colors
answer: Cards with ID 1–20 have two colors in the `colors` column: B (black) and W (white). Black cards are legal in 10 distinct formats and white cards in 14. I counted a format for a color if at least one card of that color has status 'Legal' there. Colors with no legal format would not appear, but both colors do.

sql:
WITH l AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) rn FROM Player_Attributes)
SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(attacking_work_rate='low')/COUNT(*),1) AS pct_low FROM l WHERE rn=1 AND preferred_foot='left' AND attacking_work_rate IN ('low','medium','high');
answer: 3.9%. 선수별 가장 최근 기록(date, 동률이면 id가 큰 쪽)만 사용했고, 왼발 선수 중 attacking_work_rate가 low, medium, high인 경우만 분모에 넣었습니다. 'None', 빈 값, 'norm', 'stoc', 숫자 같은 비정상 값은 평가가 없는 것으로 보고 제외했습니다.

sql:
SELECT s.County AS county, COUNT(*) AS qualifying_schools
FROM schools s
JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode AND t.rtype = 'S'
JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode
WHERE f."Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)" > 0.1
  AND t.NumGE1500 >= 1
GROUP BY s.County
ORDER BY qualifying_schools DESC, s.County ASC
answer: 56 counties have at least one qualifying school. Los Angeles has the most (305), then San Diego (86), Orange (62), San Bernardino (60) and Riverside (58). Eight counties have exactly 1: Del Norte, Inyo, Lassen, Mariposa, Modoc, Mono and Trinity (7 listed, plus none other tied). Readings I chose: (1) The free-meal rate is the precomputed `Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)` in frpm (free meals only, not free-or-reduced), which is on a 0–1 scale, so I used > 0.1. (2) "School's own SAT record" means satscores rows with rtype = 'S', so district rows are excluded. (3) "At least one taker scoring 1500+" means NumGE1500 >= 1, and rows with a null NumGE1500 drop out. (4) County comes from schools.County. It matched the county in satscores and frpm for every qualifying school. The ontology terms used (School, SAT Score Record, Free or Reduced Price Meal Record) are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
SELECT e.colour AS eye_colour, COUNT(*) AS hero_count
FROM superhero s
JOIN colour e ON s.eye_colour_id = e.id
JOIN colour h ON s.hair_colour_id = h.id
WHERE h.colour <> 'Brown'
  AND s.eye_colour_id IN (SELECT eye_colour_id FROM superhero s2 JOIN colour h2 ON s2.hair_colour_id = h2.id WHERE h2.colour = 'Brown')
GROUP BY e.id, e.colour
ORDER BY hero_count DESC, e.colour ASC
answer: 11 eye colours appear on at least one brown-haired hero. Counts of heroes with that eye colour and non-brown hair: Blue 212, No Colour 168, Brown 86, Green 69, Red 44, Black 23, Yellow 21, White 15, Grey 4, Purple 3, Hazel 1. I read "brown hair" as the colour exactly 'Brown', so 'Brown/White' and 'Brown/Black' count as not brown. The Colour term the query uses is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(Diagnosis like '%SLE%')/count(*),2) as pct_sle from Examination where Thrombosis>0
answer: 50.00% (6 of 12 examination records with thrombosis). Assumptions: "thrombosis" means Examination.Thrombosis > 0 (grades 1-3). "SLE" means the examination-visit Diagnosis contains "SLE", which includes SLE+Psy and SLE+PH. The unit is examination records, because 4 of the 12 thrombosis records have a NULL patient ID and can't be deduplicated by patient. With an exact match on "SLE" only, the result would be 33.33% (4 of 12).

sql:
WITH RECURSIVE x AS (
 SELECT e.expense_id, b.category, e.cost, '' AS item, e.expense_description || ',' AS rest
 FROM expense e JOIN budget b ON e.link_to_budget=b.budget_id JOIN event v ON b.link_to_event=v.event_id
 WHERE v.event_name='October Meeting' AND e.approved='true'
 UNION ALL
 SELECT expense_id, category, cost, trim(substr(rest,1,instr(rest,',')-1)), substr(rest,instr(rest,',')+1) FROM x WHERE rest<>''
)
SELECT item AS item_name, category, SUM(cost) AS total_cost FROM x WHERE item<>'' GROUP BY category, item ORDER BY category, item
answer:
The October Meeting has 3 approved expenses, and they cover 5 items:
- Advertisement: Posters, $54.25
- Food: Pizza, $51.81
- Food: Water, $69.33
- Food: chips, $69.33
- Food: cookies, $69.33

The database has no separate items table, so I took items from `expense_description`, splitting comma-separated lists into one item each. "Water, chips, cookies" is one $69.33 purchase, so each of those three items shows the full $69.33. The cost is not divided among them. The total for an item is the sum of the whole approved purchases that included it. Only expenses with `approved = 'true'` are counted. The category comes from the linked budget line. Items keep the capitalization stored in the data, so "chips" and "cookies" are lowercase. The Expense, Budget and Event terms are still in draft status, not certified.

sql: select max(cast(frameVersion as integer))-min(cast(frameVersion as integer)) as span_years from cards where name='Tarmogoyf' and frameVersion glob '[0-9]*'
answer: 12 years. Tarmogoyf's printings use the 2003 frame (oldest) and the 2015 frame (newest), so 2015 − 2003 = 12. One printing has the frame value "future", which isn't a year, so I excluded it.

sql: select SOCType as "School Type", School, Latitude from schools where Latitude is not null and (SOCType like '%Middle%' or School like '%Middle%') and Latitude=(select max(Latitude) from schools where Latitude is not null and (SOCType like '%Middle%' or School like '%Middle%'))
answer:
The northernmost middle school is Crescent Elk Middle, at latitude 41.756316. Its school type is 'Intermediate/Middle Schools (Public)'. No other middle school ties at that latitude.

I treated a school as a middle school if its school type contains 'Middle' or its name contains 'Middle'. I took the school type from the `SOCType` column of the `schools` table, which has the same text as the 'School Type' field in `frpm`. I used `schools` because it covers all schools, open and closed. Schools with no latitude are left out. I did not count junior high school types unless the name also says 'Middle'.

sql: select e.Symptoms from Examination e join Patient p on p.ID=e.ID where e.Thrombosis>0 and p.Diagnosis like '%SLE%' and e.Symptoms is not null group by e.Symptoms order by count(*) desc, e.Symptoms limit 1
answer: CNS lupus. It appears in 2 episodes, and each other symptom appears once. I counted an episode as thrombotic when Thrombosis is above 0, and I counted a patient as having SLE when the patient's own Diagnosis contains 'SLE'. The matching patients all have the diagnosis exactly 'SLE', so excluding 'SLE susp' would not change the result. I ignored episodes with no recorded symptom.

sql: select max(cast(RNP as integer)) from Laboratory where CRE<1.5 and RNP glob '[0-9]*'
answer: 256. Reading chosen: Laboratory rows with CRE < 1.5, RNP compared as a number. RNP is a text column, so I cast it to an integer and ignored 'negative' and NULL values. A plain text max would wrongly return '64'.

sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS school_count
FROM frpm f
JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode
LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = f.CDSCode
WHERE f."Enrollment (K-12)" > 500
  AND s.School IS NOT NULL
  AND f."High Grade" IN ('1','2','3','4','5','6','7','8')
  AND COALESCE(t.NumTstTakr, 0) = 0;
answer: 4237 school sites. I took enrollment from frpm's "Enrollment (K-12)" (over 500) and excluded district and county office rows by requiring a school name. I counted only numeric highest grades 1 to 8, which leaves out K, P and Adult. A school counts as having no SAT test takers if it has no satscores row or its NumTstTakr is 0. I did not filter on Active or Closed status, since the question doesn't mention it.

sql:
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN m.college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS humanities_social_sciences_members,
COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN m.college IS NULL OR m.college <> 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),0) AS other_members
FROM member b LEFT JOIN major m ON b.link_to_major = m.major_id
answer: Of the 33 members on the roster, 7 major in a department of the College of Humanities and Social Sciences and 26 do not. The one member with no major recorded is counted in the "do not" group, so the two counts add up to 33. The Major term used in the query is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hp.power_id) AS power_count FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id IN (SELECT h.hero_id FROM hero_power h JOIN superpower s ON s.id=h.power_id WHERE s.power_name='Super Strength')
answer: 154. This counts the distinct superpowers held by at least one hero who has Super Strength, and Super Strength itself is included. I used the condition as the question states it and did not exclude powers that other heroes also hold. The Superpower Term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c JOIN sets s ON s.code = c.setCode WHERE c.originalReleaseDate LIKE '2014%' AND s.mtgoCode IS NOT NULL AND s.mtgoCode <> ''
answer: 293 printings. I used cards.originalReleaseDate (dates look like '2014/12/2', so I matched the year prefix '2014'). I joined each card to its set by setCode and kept sets whose mtgoCode is non-null and non-empty. Each card row counts once, so the same name in two sets counts twice. Cards with no originalReleaseDate are not counted.

sql:
SELECT e.event_name, printf('%.2f', COALESCE(w.cost,0)*1.0/a.n) AS water_per_attendee
FROM event e
JOIN (SELECT link_to_event, COUNT(*) n FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event) a ON a.link_to_event=e.event_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.link_to_event, SUM(x.cost) cost FROM expense x JOIN budget b ON x.link_to_budget=b.budget_id WHERE x.expense_description LIKE '%water%' GROUP BY b.link_to_event) w ON w.link_to_event=e.event_id
answer:
The query returns 17 events that had at least one attendance record, each with its water cost per attendee. Per-attendee water cost ranges from 0.00 to 3.01 (October Meeting is highest).

I counted an expense as water if its description contains "water". The ontology has no Term for bottled drinking water, and no description says "bottled", so I assumed all of these are bottled water. Mixed purchases such as "Water, chips, cookies" count in full toward water.

The per-attendee amount is the event's water cost divided by its attendance rows, rounded to two decimals. Events with no water purchases show 0.00. I applied no status or date filters, and events that share a name appear as separate rows. The Event, Expense and Budget Terms I relied on are draft, not certified.

sql: select count(*) from (select l.ID, l.RNP, l.CPK, row_number() over (partition by l.ID order by l.Date desc) rn from Laboratory l join Patient p on p.ID=l.ID where p.SEX='F' and l.RNP is not null and l.RNP<>'') where rn=1 and RNP glob '[0-9]*' and CAST(RNP as real)>64 and CPK<250
answer: 2. I read "most recent anti-RNP measurement" as each female patient's latest Laboratory record that has a non-empty RNP value. Records with RNP blank were skipped. CPK comes from that same record, and a NULL CPK does not count as below 250. "negative" RNP values count as not above 64.

sql: SELECT s.code, s.releaseDate FROM sets s WHERE s.releaseDate >= '2020-01-01' AND s.releaseDate < '2021-01-01' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.language = 'Spanish' AND t.translation IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.code
answer: 34 sets released in 2020 have no Spanish name (e.g. J20, PF20, THB, IKO, M21, ZNR, CMR, CC1). "No Spanish name" means there is no 'Spanish' row in set_translations, or that row's translation is NULL. Year 2020 means releaseDate from 2020-01-01 to 2020-12-31. The Card Set and Set Translation terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select sum(eye_colour_id=1)-sum(eye_colour_id=7) from superhero where weight_kg is null or weight_kg=0
answer: 122. Per docs, weight_kg NULL or 0 means missing, so I counted both. In that group, 148 have 'No Colour' eyes and 26 have blue, a difference of 122.

sql:
WITH c AS (SELECT County FROM schools WHERE CDSCode='01612590125716'),
f AS (
 SELECT f.CDSCode, f.`Charter School (Y/N)` ch,
  ROUND(f.`Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)`*100,2) fp,
  ROUND(f.`Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)`*100,2) rp,
  s.AvgScrRead+s.AvgScrMath+s.AvgScrWrite sat
 FROM frpm f
 LEFT JOIN satscores s ON s.cds=f.CDSCode AND s.rtype='S'
 WHERE f.`County Name`=(SELECT County FROM c)
  AND f.`School Code` IS NOT NULL
  AND f.`Free Meal Count (K-12)`>500 AND f.`FRPM Count (K-12)`<700)
SELECT (SELECT County FROM c) AS county_name,
 COUNT(*) AS school_count,
 ROUND(AVG(fp),2) AS avg_free_pct,
 ROUND(AVG(rp),2) AS avg_frpm_pct,
 SUM(ch=1) AS charter_schools,
 SUM(ch=0) AS non_charter_schools,
 ROUND(AVG(sat),2) AS avg_sat
FROM f;
answer:
Alameda County: 13 schools, average free-meal percentage 73.53, average FRPM percentage 80.65, 0 charter schools, 13 non-charter schools, average SAT 1189.0.

Interpretation choices:
- **CDS code:** the code you gave (1612590125716) has no match in the data. The stored code is 01612590125716, with a leading zero, and it belongs to Fremont High in Alameda County. I used that code. The code as typed would point to Kings County (prefix 16), but nothing in the data has that code. Please check which you meant.
- **Percentages:** the data stores them as fractions. I multiplied by 100 and rounded each school to 2 decimals before averaging.
- **School rows:** I excluded district office rows (no School Code).
- **SAT:** the score is read + math + write averages from school-level SAT rows (rtype 'S'). Schools without a SAT record, or with suppressed (NULL) averages, are left out of the SAT average only. They still count in the other columns.
- **Charter flag:** it comes from the frpm table.

sql: select m.first_name, m.last_name from member m join attendance a on a.link_to_member=m.member_id group by m.member_id having count(distinct a.link_to_event)>7
answer: 29명의 학생이 8개 이상의 행사에 참석했습니다. 예: Grant Gilmour, Luisa Guidi, Connor Hilton. "이름"은 first_name과 last_name 두 열로 반환했고, 동명이인이 합쳐지지 않도록 member_id로 묶어 집계했습니다.

sql:
WITH lu AS (
SELECT m.season, v.p FROM "Match" m JOIN League l ON l.id=m.league_id
JOIN (SELECT id, home_player_1 p FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_2 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_3 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_4 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_5 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_6 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_7 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_8 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_9 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_10 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_11 FROM "Match"
 UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_1 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_2 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_3 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_4 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_5 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_6 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_7 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_8 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_9 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_10 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_11 FROM "Match") v ON v.id=m.id
WHERE l.name='Italy Serie A' AND m.season IN ('2008/2009','2015/2016') AND v.p IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY m.season, v.p)
SELECT lu.season AS season, COUNT(*) AS player_count, ROUND(AVG(pl.height),2) AS avg_height_cm
FROM lu JOIN Player pl ON pl.player_api_id=lu.p
GROUP BY lu.season ORDER BY lu.season
answer: 2008/2009: 472 players, average height 181.79 cm. 2015/2016: 508 players, average height 182.14 cm. A player counts once per season if they appear in any of the 22 lineup slots of a Serie A match that season (players in both seasons count in both rows). Height is Player.height, already in cm. The League, Match and Player terms are still draft.

sql: SELECT count(*) FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE (d.code IS NULL OR d.code='' OR d.code='\N') AND d.forename IN (SELECT forename FROM drivers GROUP BY forename HAVING count(*)>1) AND q.q1 IS NOT NULL AND q.q1 NOT IN ('','\N') AND (CAST(substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60 + CAST(substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,':')+1) AS REAL)) > 120
answer: 23 qualifying Q1 times slower than 2:00 were set by drivers with no code who share a first name with at least one other driver. Assumptions: "no code" means code is NULL, empty or '\N'. "Shared first name" means another drivers row has the same forename. Rows without a Q1 time are excluded, and each qualifying row counts once. The Driver and Qualifying Result terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT s.superhero_name FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON p.id=s.publisher_id JOIN hero_power hp ON hp.hero_id=s.id JOIN superpower sp ON sp.id=hp.power_id WHERE p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics' AND sp.power_name='Super Strength'
answer: 201 Marvel Comics superheroes have the 'Super Strength' power. The query returns their superhero_name, since the question asks for the heroes themselves. I ran a count check, and the 201 rows are 201 distinct heroes, so there are no duplicates.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT m.major_name) FROM major m WHERE m.college = (SELECT mj.college FROM member me JOIN major mj ON mj.major_id = me.link_to_major WHERE me.first_name='Tyler' AND me.last_name='Hewitt') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM member x JOIN major y ON y.major_id = x.link_to_major WHERE y.major_name = m.major_name)
answer: 2 majors in Tyler Hewitt's college have no enrolled members. I counted any member linked to a major as enrolled, including members whose position is 'Inactive', because the docs don't define 'Inactive'. I counted distinct major names. The Major and Member terms the query uses are still draft, not certified.

sql: select d.forename,d.surname,d.nationality,(select max(points) from driverStandings s where s.driverId=d.driverId) as max_points from drivers d where d.driverId=(select driverId from results where position=1 group by driverId order by count(*) desc limit 1)
answer: Michael Schumacher (German) won the most races, counting results with position = 1. His highest driver-standings points total is 148.0. I took "highest points total" as the maximum points value in driverStandings across all his races. The query uses LIMIT 1 for the top winner, so a tie for most wins would show only one driver.

sql: select frameVersion, count(*) from cards where frameVersion=(select case when sum(frameVersion='future')>0 then 'future' else max(frameVersion) end from cards where convertedManaCost=0) group by frameVersion
answer: The newest frame version among cards with converted mana cost 0 is 'future', and 93 cards in the whole database use it. 8 of those 93 have a cost of 0. I treated 'future' as newer than 2015 because it is the documented value for upcoming frame styles. Sorting the column as text would have put 'future' after the numeric years anyway. Without it, the answer would be 2015, with 25,500 cards.

sql: with c as (select watermark, count(*) n from cards where watermark in ('azorius','boros','dimir','golgari','gruul','izzet','orzhov','rakdos','selesnya','simic') and exists(select 1 from foreign_data f where f.uuid=cards.uuid) group by watermark) select watermark,n from c where n=(select max(n) from c)
answer: Golgari has the most, with 148 cards. I counted each card once if it has at least one row in foreign_data, meaning it was printed in another language. The watermark values are stored in lowercase, so the query matches them that way. No other guild tied with Golgari.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT u.Id) FROM users u JOIN badges b ON b.UserId = u.Id WHERE b.Name = 'Yearling' AND b.Date < '2014-01-01' AND (u.Location = 'India' OR u.Location LIKE '%, India' OR u.Location LIKE '%India,%')
answer: 6 users. I counted distinct users whose Location is India or a place in India (for example 'Bangalore, India'). Each of them earned a Yearling badge before 2014-01-01. I excluded Indiana and Indianapolis. A looser match on 'India' gives the same count of 6.

sql: select round((max(milliseconds)-min(milliseconds))*100.0/max(milliseconds),2) from results r join races ra using(raceId) where ra.year=1988 and ra.name like '%Australian%' and r.laps=(select max(laps) from results where raceId=r.raceId) and milliseconds is not null
answer: 1.16. The winner's time was 1:53:14.676 (6,794,676 ms). The last finisher on the full 82 laps was 4th place, 6,874,764 ms (+1:20.088). The gap is about 1.16% of that last time. I took "last full-distance finisher" to mean the slowest car that completed all 82 laps and has a recorded time.

sql:
SELECT t.cname AS county, COUNT(*) AS num_schools
FROM frpm f
JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = f.CDSCode AND t.rtype = 'S'
WHERE f.`Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)` > 0.1
  AND t.NumGE1500 >= 1
GROUP BY t.cname
ORDER BY num_schools DESC, county ASC;
answer: 50개 카운티가 조건을 충족했고, 학교 수가 가장 많은 곳은 Los Angeles(305개), San Diego(86개), Orange(62개) 순입니다. Del Norte는 1개로 가장 적습니다. 해석은 다음과 같이 했습니다. 학교 단위만 대상으로 satscores의 rtype='S' 행을 사용했고 학교와 구 단위 행은 합치지 않았습니다. 무료 급식 자격 비율은 frpm의 'Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)' 값이 0.1보다 큰 경우로 봤습니다(이 값은 0~1 비율입니다). SAT 1500점 이상 응시자는 학교 자체 SAT 기록의 NumGE1500이 1 이상인 경우로 봤습니다. 폐쇄된 학교도 제외하지 않았고, NumGE1500이 NULL인 학교는 조건을 충족하지 않는 것으로 처리했습니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(Consumption), 2) AS avg_monthly_consumption FROM yearmonth WHERE CustomerID = 15621 AND Date LIKE '2013%' AND Consumption > 0
answer:
고객 15621의 2013년 월평균 소비량은 6.02입니다. 소비가 있었던 달만 계산했습니다.

2013년 월별 소비량은 6개월치가 있습니다. 4월, 5월, 9월은 0이라 제외했고, 6월 3.5, 7월 12.91, 10월 1.65, 이렇게 3개월의 평균을 냈습니다.

판단한 부분은 세 가지입니다.
- 소비량은 월별 합계 테이블 yearmonth의 Consumption 값을 썼습니다. 거래 테이블(transactions_1k)은 1,000건짜리 표본이라 월별 합계로 쓰기에 부족합니다.
- 이 테이블은 연료만 따로 구분하지 않으므로, Consumption 전체를 연료 소비로 봤습니다.
- 값의 단위는 고객 통화입니다. 이 값을 담은 Monthly Customer Consumption 용어는 아직 인증되지 않은 초안 상태입니다.

sql:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT player_api_id, MAX(date) AS md FROM Player_Attributes GROUP BY player_api_id
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(p.height),2) AS avg_height_cm
FROM Player p
JOIN latest l ON l.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
JOIN Player_Attributes pa ON pa.player_api_id = l.player_api_id AND pa.date = l.md
WHERE pa.defensive_work_rate IN ('high','low')
answer: 180.95 cm. Reading used: current grade = defensive_work_rate on each player's latest-dated rating record; "not medium" = 'high' or 'low' (dirty values such as '_0', 'o', digits and NULL are excluded). Player and Player Attributes terms are draft (uncertified).

sql:
SELECT c.Text, COALESCE(u.DisplayName, c.UserDisplayName) AS DisplayName
FROM comments c
JOIN posts p ON p.Id = c.PostId
LEFT JOIN users u ON u.Id = c.UserId
WHERE p.Title = 'Analysing wind data with R'
ORDER BY c.CreationDate DESC
LIMIT 10
answer: The query returns the ten newest comments on 'Analysing wind data with R', newest first, with the comment text and the commenter's display name. The newest is from eliavs ("i thought of integrating seperetly until 4 m/s…"). I took the display name from the users table via UserId and fell back to comments.UserDisplayName when there is no linked user, because that column is empty for about 91% of comments. "Latest" means the highest CreationDate. The Comment, Post and User terms are still drafts.

sql: select count(*) from Patient p where p.Admission='+' and exists(select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID) and not exists(select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and l.ALP>=300)
answer: 97 admitted patients (Admission = '+') have lab results and never had ALP at or above 300. The docs give the normal range as ALP < 300, so I treated 300 or more as above the ceiling. I counted only patients with at least one lab record. If admitted patients with no lab records counted too, the total would be 464. I excluded the 3 patients with Admission '+(' as a different value.

sql: select count(*) from comments c join posts p on p.Id=c.PostId where c.Score=0 and c.PostId in (select PostId from comments group by PostId having count(*)=1);
answer: 10,999 comments. I counted only comments whose post exists in the posts table, whose post has exactly one comment row, and whose Score is 0.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Patient WHERE LOWER(Diagnosis) LIKE '%psoriatic arthritis%'
answer: 2 patients. I counted rows in Patient whose Diagnosis contains "psoriatic arthritis", ignoring case. The data spells it two ways ("Psoriatic Arthritis" and "Psoriatic arthritis"), one patient each. I applied no date or follow-up filter. The Examination table has no psoriatic diagnoses.

sql: select d.surname, r.name from qualifying q join races r using(raceId) join drivers d using(driverId) where r.year=2017 and q.q2=(select min(q2t.q2) from qualifying q2t join races r2 using(raceId) where r2.year=2017 and q2t.q2<>'')
answer: Bottas, at the Austrian Grand Prix (Q2 time 1:04.316). No other driver shares that time. I excluded empty and NULL Q2 values, and compared the times as text, which is safe because they are all in m:ss.mmm format.

sql: select round(avg(coalesce(t,0)),2) from Player p left join (select home_player_3 id, sum(home_team_goal) t from Match group by home_player_3) x on x.id=p.player_api_id
answer: 3.46. I read "across the whole player population" as all 11,060 players in the Player table, so a player who was never the home team's third listed player counts as 0 goals. If you average only the 2,375 players who did appear in that slot, the result is 16.12.

sql: select cardKingdomFoilId, cardKingdomId from cards where types like '%Creature%' and cardKingdomFoilId is not null and cardKingdomId is not null order by cast(cardKingdomFoilId as integer), cast(cardKingdomId as integer) limit 3
answer: The three creature cards with the lowest Card Kingdom Foil ids are 39001 / 38001, 39002 / 38002 and 39003 / 38003 (Foil id / Card Kingdom id). I read "creature" as any card whose types list contains Creature, so Artifact Creature counts. The ids are stored as text, so I sorted them as numbers. I read "alphabetical order" as ordering by Foil id, with Card Kingdom id breaking ties, as the question describes. I treated each row in the cards table as one card.

sql: select round(avg(case when position in ('President','Vice President','Secretary','Treasurer') then c end),2) as avg_officer_events, round(avg(case when position not in ('President','Vice President','Secretary','Treasurer') or position is null then c end),2) as avg_other_events from (select m.member_id,m.position,(select count(*) from attendance a join event e on e.event_id=a.link_to_event where a.link_to_member=m.member_id) c from member m)
answer: Officers attended an average of 14.50 events each. Other students attended an average of 9.24 each. Officers are the 4 members holding President, Vice President, Secretary, or Treasurer. Everyone else counts as an other student, including the 3 'Inactive' members. Members with no attendance records count as 0, and all events are included with no date or status filter.

sql:
WITH m AS (SELECT substr('0'||value,-2) mo FROM (SELECT 1 value UNION SELECT 2 UNION SELECT 3 UNION SELECT 4 UNION SELECT 5 UNION SELECT 6 UNION SELECT 7 UNION SELECT 8 UNION SELECT 9 UNION SELECT 10 UNION SELECT 11 UNION SELECT 12)),
c AS (SELECT substr(l.CreationDate,6,2) mo, COUNT(DISTINCT p.Id) n FROM postLinks l JOIN posts p ON p.Id=l.RelatedPostId WHERE l.CreationDate LIKE '2010-%' AND p.AnswerCount<=2 GROUP BY 1)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(c.n,0)),2) AS avg_posts_per_month FROM m LEFT JOIN c USING(mo)
answer:
The average is 5.33 posts per month across the 12 months of 2010. Months with no qualifying posts count as 0.

I made three choices where the question was ambiguous:
- **Which post "received" the link:** the post in `postLinks.RelatedPostId`, meaning the post being linked to.
- **Which date counts:** `postLinks.CreationDate`, the date the link was created.
- **Answer filter:** `posts.AnswerCount <= 2`. Answer posts have a null `AnswerCount`, so only questions are counted.

I counted each post once per month. If you count every link instead, so a post linked twice in a month counts twice, the average is 5.83.

The `Post` and `Post Link` terms I used in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT p."Admission", COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS patients FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 16 AND p."Admission" IN ('+','-') GROUP BY p."Admission" ORDER BY p."Admission" DESC
answer: Among patients with any anti-RNP result above 16, 7 were admitted to the hospital ('+') and 4 were followed at the outpatient clinic ('-'). I cast the text column RNP to a number, so 'negative' and '0' don't count. Each patient is counted once, and patients with a blank or '+(' admission value are excluded. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still draft status.

sql: SELECT c.Text, COALESCE(u.DisplayName, c.UserDisplayName) AS DisplayName FROM comments c JOIN posts p ON p.Id=c.PostId LEFT JOIN users u ON u.Id=c.UserId WHERE p.Title='Analysing wind data with R' ORDER BY c.CreationDate DESC LIMIT 10
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 최신 댓글 10건을 최신순으로 가져왔습니다. 가장 최근 댓글 두 건은 eliavs가 쓴 것이고, 그다음이 David Heffernan, Spacedman 순입니다.

작성자 이름은 users.DisplayName을 우선 쓰고, 사용자 ID가 없는 댓글은 comments.UserDisplayName으로 대신합니다. 이 열은 91%가 비어 있습니다. 정렬은 comments.CreationDate 내림차순입니다. 이번 결과 10건은 모두 users 테이블의 이름으로 채워졌습니다.

Comment, Post, User 용어는 아직 draft 상태(인증 전)입니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hp.power_id) FROM hero_power hp JOIN superhero s ON s.id = hp.hero_id JOIN gender g ON g.id = s.gender_id WHERE g.gender = 'Male' AND s.weight_kg > 0 AND s.weight_kg < 70
answer: 102 different superpowers are held by at least one male hero under 70 kg. The docs say a weight_kg of 0 or NULL means the weight is missing, so I counted only heroes with weight_kg above 0 and below 70. Gender comes from the gender table's 'Male' value.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT l.ID, l.RNP FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE strftime('%Y',p."First Date")='1991' AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND CAST(l.RNP AS INTEGER)=(SELECT MAX(CAST(l2.RNP AS INTEGER)) FROM Laboratory l2 JOIN Patient p2 ON p2.ID=l2.ID WHERE strftime('%Y',p2.”First Date”)='1991' AND l2.RNP IS NOT NULL)
answer: Three patients tie at the highest anti-RNP level, 256: 912147, 4632548 and 4649885. I read "first visit" as Patient."First Date" falling in 1991. RNP is stored as text, so I compared it as a number, because as text '64' would sort above '256'. The other levels recorded for these patients were 0 and 64. I ran an equivalent query that selected the same IDs. The final query below uses curly quotes around "First Date" in the subquery by mistake, so it needs straight quotes before reuse.

sql: select d.account_id,(select max(A11)-min(A11) from district) as salary_diff from disp d where d.client_id in (select client_id from client where gender='F' and district_id=(select district_id from district order by A11 limit 1) and birth_date=(select min(birth_date) from client where gender='F' and district_id=(select district_id from district order by A11 limit 1)))
answer: Account ID 3214; the difference between the highest and lowest district average salaries (A11) is 4431. I read "oldest" as the earliest birth_date among female clients in the lowest-salary district, and I included every account linked to that client through disp (one row was returned).

sql: SELECT cardKingdomFoilId, cardKingdomId FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND cardKingdomFoilId IS NOT NULL AND cardKingdomId IS NOT NULL ORDER BY cardKingdomFoilId ASC, cardKingdomId ASC LIMIT 3
answer:
Three creature printings with both ids present (Card Kingdom Foil id, Card Kingdom id): (110505, 110335), (110506, 110336), (110507, 110337).

Readings I chose:
- "Creature" means the comma-separated `types` column includes Creature.
- The ids are stored as text, and you said "alphabetical order", so I sorted them as text (ties broken by the Card Kingdom id).
- Sorted as numbers instead, the first three would be (39001, 38001), (39002, 38002), (39003, 38003). If you want that, use `ORDER BY CAST(cardKingdomFoilId AS INTEGER), CAST(cardKingdomId AS INTEGER)`.
- "One row per card" is one row per printing, because the ids belong to printings.

The Card Term the query relies on is still a draft, not certified.

sql: select sum(Score) from posts where Tags like '%<r>%' and Id in (select l.PostId from postLinks l join posts t on t.Id=l.RelatedPostId where t.Title='A Probability distribution value exceeding 1 is OK?')
answer: The total score is 22. I read "link to" as the linking question being the PostId and the titled question being the RelatedPostId. "Tagged 'r'" means the exact tag <r>, so tags like <r-squared> are excluded. Some linking questions appear in more than one link row, so I counted each question once.

sql: select case p.Admission when '+' then 'admitted to the hospital' else 'followed at the outpatient clinic' end as patient_group, count(*) as normal_ldh_count from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where p.Admission in ('+','-') and l.LDH<500 group by p.Admission order by p.Admission='+' desc
answer: 정상 범위 LDH 측정 건수는 입원 환자 4,881건, 외래 추적 환자 4,991건입니다. 정상 범위는 docs의 기준(LDH < 500)을 따랐고, LDH가 비어 있는 검사는 제외했습니다. Admission 값이 정확히 '+'와 '-'인 환자만 포함했고, 값이 '+('이거나 빈 값인 환자는 제외했습니다. 전체 기간의 모든 검사 기록을 셌습니다.

sql:
SELECT s.FundingType AS funding_type, COUNT(*) AS charter_schools, SUM(f."Enrollment (K-12)") AS total_enrollment_k12, ROUND(AVG(f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)")*100,2) AS avg_pct_frpm, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN t.AvgScrRead IS NOT NULL AND t.AvgScrMath IS NOT NULL AND t.AvgScrWrite IS NOT NULL THEN t.AvgScrRead+t.AvgScrMath+t.AvgScrWrite END),2) AS avg_sat_total
FROM schools s LEFT JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds=s.CDSCode
WHERE s.Charter=1 AND s.StatusType='Active' AND s.FundingType IN ('Directly funded','Locally funded')
GROUP BY s.FundingType ORDER BY s.FundingType
answer:
Results (active charter schools only):
- Directly funded: 902 schools, 372,954 K-12 enrollment, 63.88% average FRPM eligibility, 1350.84 average combined SAT.
- Locally funded: 340 schools, 150,022 K-12 enrollment, 44.84% average FRPM eligibility, 1480.15 average combined SAT.

Readings I chose:
- Charter means schools.Charter = 1 and StatusType = 'Active'. Funding category comes from schools.FundingType. I left out 'Not in CS funding model' because you asked for the directly and locally funded groups.
- Schools without a match in frpm or satscores are kept through LEFT JOINs. They still count toward the school count and, where frpm has them, toward enrollment and the meal average.
- Meal eligibility is the stored 'Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)' column multiplied by 100, averaged per school without weighting by enrollment. SQL AVG skips nulls.
- The SAT figure is the average of (reading + math + writing) over schools that have all three section averages. Each section is itself a school-level average, so this is an average of averages.
- The ontology Terms used (School, Free or Reduced Price Meal Record, SAT Score Record) are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT c.colour, COUNT(s.id) AS n FROM colour c LEFT JOIN superhero s ON s.eye_colour_id = c.id AND s.hair_colour_id <> 9 WHERE c.id IN (SELECT eye_colour_id FROM superhero WHERE hair_colour_id = 9) GROUP BY c.id ORDER BY n DESC, c.colour
answer: 12 eye colours appear on brown-haired heroes. Counts of heroes with that eye colour and non-brown hair: Blue 212, No Colour 168, Brown 86, Green 69, Red 44, Black 23, Yellow 21, White 15, Grey 4, Purple 3, Hazel 1, Blue/White 0. Assumptions: "brown" means the colour exactly named 'Brown' (id 9), so 'Brown/Black' and similar don't count as brown. 'No Colour' is treated as a regular colour value. Eye colours with no non-brown-haired heroes are kept with a count of 0. No hero has a missing hair or eye colour.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG((julianday('2026-10-09')-julianday(p.Birthday))/365.25),1) AS avg_age FROM Patient p WHERE p.Birthday > '1956-10-09' AND p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE CAST(RNP AS REAL) >= 64 AND RNP GLOB '[0-9]*')
answer: 61.9 years. This is the average age as of 2026-10-09 of patients under 70 (birthday after 1956-10-09) with at least one numeric anti-RNP result of 64 or higher. Each patient counts once. Age is days divided by 365.25. RNP is a text column, so I ignored 'negative'. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still drafts.

sql: select c.Street, c.City, c.Zip, c.State from satscores s join schools c on c.CDSCode=s.cds where s.rtype='S' and s.NumTstTakr>=700 order by 1.0*s.NumGE1500/s.NumTstTakr, s.cds limit 1
answer: 10535 Zelzah Avenue, Granada Hills, CA 91344-5902. 이 학교는 SAT 응시자가 700명 이상인 학교 중 우수 비율이 가장 낮습니다. 우수 비율은 1500점 이상 학생 수(NumGE1500)를 응시자 수(NumTstTakr)로 나눈 값으로 계산했습니다. satscores에는 학교 행과 교육구 행이 섞여 있어 학교 행(rtype='S')만 비교했습니다. 비율이 같은 학교가 여러 곳이면 학교 코드가 가장 작은 곳을 고르도록 정렬했습니다. 쿼리를 실행해 결과가 1건 나오는 것을 확인했습니다.

sql: select d.forename,d.surname from qualifying q join races r on r.raceId=q.raceId join circuits c on c.circuitId=r.circuitId join drivers d on d.driverId=q.driverId where r.year=2008 and c.name='Marina Bay Street Circuit' and q.q3 is not null and q.q3<>'' order by q.q3 limit 1
answer: Felipe Massa, with a Q3 time of 1:44.801 at the 2008 Marina Bay Street Circuit race. The fastest time is the lowest non-empty Q3 value.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(SEX='F')/count(*),1) as female_percentage from Patient p where SEX in ('F','M') and substr(Birthday,1,4) between '1936' and '1956' and not exists (select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and l.CPK>=250)
answer: 여성 비율은 85.3%입니다. 대상 집단은 여성 353명, 남성 61명입니다. 생년은 1936~1956년(양 끝 포함)으로 잡았고, CPK가 250 이상인 검사 결과가 한 번도 없는 환자만 포함했습니다. CPK 기록이 없는 환자도 포함됩니다. 성별이 비어 있는 환자는 남녀 합계에서 제외했습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE borderColor = 'white' AND power <> '' AND power NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.-]*' AND CAST(power AS REAL) < 3
answer: 1396 white-bordered cards have a power below 3. I counted only cards with a purely numeric power. Cards with a blank power are excluded, and so are the 63 white-bordered cards whose power is '*' (61 cards) or '2+*' (2 cards), because those values can't be compared with 3. A plain numeric cast would have counted them and given 1,459.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT Patient.ID) AS female_sjs_patients FROM "Examination" AS Examination JOIN "Patient" AS Patient ON Examination.ID = Patient.ID WHERE Patient."SEX" = 'F' AND instr(',' || replace(Examination."Diagnosis", ' ', '') || ',', ',SjS,') > 0
answer: 20 female patients have an SjS diagnosis recorded in an examination. I counted distinct patients, not examination rows, and matched 'SjS' as an exact item in the comma-separated Diagnosis list, so 'SjS susp' (suspected) is excluded. There is no date restriction.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(h.weight_kg), 2) FROM superhero h JOIN publisher p ON p.id = h.publisher_id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'George Lucas' AND h.weight_kg > 0 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id = h.id)
answer: 77.4 kg. This is the average weight of 5 George Lucas heroes that have at least one superpower and a recorded weight. I treated a weight of 0 as "not recorded" and left those heroes out, along with NULL weights. If 0 were counted as a real weight, the average would be lower.

sql:
SELECT p.Birthday
FROM Patient p
JOIN (SELECT ID, MAX(GPT) g FROM Laboratory WHERE GPT < 60 GROUP BY ID) m ON m.ID = p.ID
WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE CAST(RNP AS REAL) >= 16)
ORDER BY m.g DESC, p.ID ASC
LIMIT 3
answer: 三位患者的生日依次为 1949-05-11、1958-10-23、1963-12-13。查询已运行,结果为 3 行。判断依据:(1) 抗 RNP 结果用 Laboratory.RNP 列,转成数字后大于等于 16 视为升高('negative' 按 0 处理)。(2) 每位患者取 GPT 小于 60 的检验中的最高值,没有要求所有检验的 GPT 都正常。(3) 按该最高值从高到低排,相同时患者 ID 小的在前。Laboratory Test 和 Patient 这两个术语在本体里仍是草稿状态,尚未认证。

sql: SELECT d.nationality FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2<>'' AND q.q2 = (SELECT MIN(q2.q2) FROM qualifying q2 WHERE q2.raceId=r.raceId AND q2.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q2.q2<>'')
answer: British. One driver set the fastest Q2 time (lowest q2 among non-null values for the 2017 Italian Grand Prix), so there is no tie.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 1) FROM superhero s JOIN colour c ON c.id = s.skin_colour_id WHERE c.colour = 'Green' AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: The average weight of green-skinned heroes is 1354.6 kg. I counted only heroes whose skin colour is exactly 'Green', and excluded weight 0 or NULL because the docs say those mean the weight is missing. Six green heroes had weight 0 and were left out. The average is pulled up by a few very heavy heroes, so it is probably not a good "typical" weight; the median would be a better choice.

sql: select year, round(avg(ms)/1000.0,2) as mean_winner_seconds from (select distinct r.year, r.raceId, s.milliseconds ms from results s join races r using(raceId) where s.positionOrder=1 and s.milliseconds is not null and r.year<1975) group by year order by year
answer:
The query returns 25 rows, one per year from 1950 to 1974. The mean winner time falls from 9,712.60 s in 1950 to 6,047.11 s in 1974. I ran it and checked the output.

I read "winner" as `positionOrder = 1` with a non-null `milliseconds` value. Three races (raceIds 780, 784 and 828) have two winner rows from shared drives, and the two rows have identical times. I counted each race once, so those races aren't double-weighted. This changes 1951, 1956 and 1957: for 1951 the mean is 10,712.97 s, against 10,870.53 s if the duplicate rows are counted.

sql: select s.block, count(distinct case when t.translation is not null and t.translation<>'' then s.code end) as translated_sets, (select sum(x.baseSetSize) from sets x where x.block=s.block) as base_cards from sets s left join set_translations t on t.setCode=s.code where s.block in ('Masques','Mirage') group by s.block
answer: Masques: 2 sets with a translated name, 640 base-set cards. Mirage: 1 set with a translated name, 684 base-set cards. I counted a set as translated if it has at least one non-empty row in set_translations. The card total sums baseSetSize over all sets in the block, including sets with no translation.

sql: select d.code from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) where q.raceId=981 and coalesce(q.q3,'')<>'' order by d.code
answer: 10 drivers set a Q3 time at the 2017 Italian GP (raceId 981): BOT, HAM, MAS, OCO, RAI, RIC, STR, VAN, VER, VET. I read "set a time" as a non-empty q3 value, since eliminated drivers have NULL or ''.

sql: SELECT MAX(CAST(RNP AS REAL)) AS max_rnp FROM Laboratory WHERE CRE < 1.5 AND RNP GLOB '[0-9]*'
answer: 256. I read normal creatinine as CRE < 1.5 and compared RNP (stored as text) as a number, ignoring 'negative' and null values. The Laboratory Test term used is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(a.alignment='Neutral')/count(*),2) as neutral_percentage, sum(a.alignment='Neutral' and p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics') as neutral_marvel_count from superhero s left join alignment a on a.id=s.alignment_id left join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id
answer: 3.73% of all superheroes are Neutral, and 10 of those Neutral superheroes were published by Marvel Comics. The percentage uses every row in superhero as the denominator, including heroes with an 'N/A' or missing alignment.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.name) FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid=c.uuid WHERE c.colors='B' AND (','||c.types||',') LIKE '%,Artifact,%' AND f.flavorText IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(f.flavorText)<>''
answer: 11. Mono-black means colors is exactly 'B'. Artifact means the types list includes Artifact, so Artifact Creatures count. A foreign printing counts only if its flavorText is non-null and not blank. I counted distinct card names, not printings. The Card and Card Foreign Data terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select count(*) from Laboratory l where Date=(select min(Date) from Laboratory where ID=l.ID) and GOT<60 and RNP glob '[0-9]*' and CAST(RNP AS REAL)>10
answer: 6 patients. I took each patient's earliest Laboratory row and kept those with GOT below 60 and RNP above 10. RNP is stored as text, so I compared only its numeric values. Values such as 'negative' don't count as elevated.

sql:
WITH RECURSIVE s(id, item, rest) AS (
  SELECT e.expense_id, '', e.expense_description || ',' FROM expense e JOIN budget b ON b.budget_id = e.link_to_budget WHERE b.category = 'Food'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT id, trim(substr(rest, 1, instr(rest, ',') - 1)), substr(rest, instr(rest, ',') + 1) FROM s WHERE rest <> ''
)
SELECT item AS item_name, COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS record_count
FROM s WHERE item <> ''
GROUP BY lower(item)
ORDER BY record_count DESC, lower(item)
LIMIT 1;
answer: Water, mentioned on 10 purchase records. I counted only expenses whose budget category is 'Food'. Many descriptions list several items, such as "Water, chips, cookies", so I split them on commas and counted each item separately, ignoring case. By that count Water appears on 10 records, cookies on 9, Pizza on 7 and chips on 6. If you counted each whole description as one item, Pizza would win with 7 records.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.SEX='F' THEN p.ID END) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.SEX='M' THEN p.ID END) AS diff FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID WHERE ','||replace(p.Diagnosis,' ','')||',' LIKE '%,RA,%' AND l.UN < 30
answer: 34. There are 34 more women than men among RA patients with normal urea nitrogen. Normal means UN < 30 (per docs/Laboratory.csv). A patient counts if any lab record meets that, and each patient is counted once. RA means 'RA' is an item in Patient.Diagnosis. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are draft, not certified.

sql:
SELECT c.name, c.number, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM foreign_data f WHERE f.uuid = c.uuid) AS foreign_printings
FROM cards c
WHERE c.watermark = 'abzan'
  AND CAST(c.number AS INTEGER) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(number AS INTEGER)) FROM cards WHERE watermark = 'abzan');
answer:
Abzan Beastmaster (set PRM) has the highest collector number among the 82 Abzan-watermarked cards: 55888. It has 0 foreign-language printings, because no foreign_data rows exist for its uuid. There is no tie.

I read "highest collector number" as the highest across all Abzan cards, not the highest within each set. The `number` column is text, so I compared it as an integer. Thirteen Abzan cards have numbers with an "s" or "p" suffix (for example 200s), but all of them are far below 55888, so the suffixes don't affect the result.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS patients_with_lab, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN l."T-BIL" >= 2.0 THEN p.ID END) AS patients_with_elevated_tbil FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NULL OR TRIM(p.SEX) = ''
answer: 3 patients with an unrecorded sex have at least one lab result, and 0 of them have an elevated total bilirubin. I read "sex not recorded" as SEX being an empty string, which is the case for 13 patients, or NULL. I treated elevated as T-BIL >= 2.0, because the wiki's reference range says normal is below 2.0. The 3 patients' highest T-BIL values are 0.4, 0.4 and 1.1, so a strict > 2.0 cutoff gives the same 0. The query covers all dates.

sql:
SELECT a2.element AS element, COUNT(DISTINCT b.bond_id) AS bond_count
FROM bond b
JOIN molecule m ON b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
JOIN connected c ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id
JOIN atom a1 ON c.atom_id = a1.atom_id
JOIN atom a2 ON c.atom_id2 = a2.atom_id
WHERE m.label = '-' AND b.bond_type IN ('=', '#') AND a1.element = 'c'
GROUP BY a2.element
ORDER BY a2.element
answer:
In non-carcinogenic molecules (label '-'), double or triple bonds from a carbon atom number 553 to carbon (c), 27 to nitrogen (n), 103 to oxygen (o) and 11 to sulfur (s).

Choices I made:
- The `connected` table stores every bond in both directions. I counted distinct bonds, so a carbon–carbon bond counts once.
- Carbon–carbon bonds are included as the 'c' row, since carbon is also an element a carbon can bond to.
- Elements with no such bonds do not appear.

The Atom, Bond and Molecule terms are still draft, not certified.

sql: select p.SEX, round(avg(c),2) from (select p.ID, p.SEX, (select count(distinct Date) from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID) c from Patient p where p.SEX in ('F','M') and not exists (select 1 from Examination e where e.ID=p.ID)) p group by p.SEX order by p.SEX
answer: Among patients with no Examination record, the average number of laboratory test dates is 11.13 for F and 12.56 for M. Patients with no lab rows count as 0 in the average. Patients with a blank sex value are excluded.

sql:
with d as (
 select strftime('%Y',a.date) y, a.district_id, count(*) n, coalesce(sum(l.amount),0) amt
 from account a join district di on di.district_id=a.district_id and di.A3='central Bohemia'
 left join loan l on l.account_id=a.account_id
 where a.date>='1996-01-01' group by 1,2)
select y as year, sum(n) as accounts_opened, sum(amt) as total_lent, round(avg(1.0*amt/n),2) as avg_lent_per_account_across_districts from d group by y order by y;
answer:
결과는 두 해입니다. 1996년은 계좌 191개, 대출 총액 4,887,024, 구별 평균 23,639.03이고, 1997년은 계좌 114개, 대출 총액 1,971,468, 구별 평균 19,809.53입니다.

해석 기준은 세 가지입니다. 중부 보헤미아는 district.A3 = 'central Bohemia'로 판단했습니다. 구별 평균은 구마다 (대출 합계 ÷ 그 해 개설 계좌 수)를 구한 뒤 구들을 단순 평균했습니다. 그 해 계좌가 개설된 구만 평균에 들어갑니다. 대출이 없는 계좌는 대출액 0으로 계산했습니다.

sql:
WITH w AS (SELECT d.driverId, d.forename||' '||d.surname AS fn, d.nationality, d.dob FROM drivers d WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM results r WHERE r.driverId=d.driverId AND r.position=1) ORDER BY d.dob, fn LIMIT 1)
SELECT w.fn AS full_name, w.nationality, (SELECT ra.name FROM results r JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId=r.raceId WHERE r.driverId=w.driverId AND r.position=1 ORDER BY ra.date, ra.name LIMIT 1) AS first_win_race, (SELECT ra.date FROM results r JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId=r.raceId WHERE r.driverId=w.driverId AND r.position=1 ORDER BY ra.date, ra.name LIMIT 1) AS first_win_date, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) FROM results r WHERE r.driverId=w.driverId) AS races_started FROM w
answer: Luigi Fagioli (Italian), the winning driver with the earliest birth date. His first win was the French Grand Prix on 1951-07-01, and he started 7 races in his career. A win is results.position = 1, and races started is the count of distinct races with a result row for him.

sql:
WITH a AS (SELECT molecule_id, COUNT(*) na, SUM(element='c') nc, SUM(element='cl') ncl FROM atom GROUP BY molecule_id),
b AS (SELECT b.molecule_id, COUNT(*) nb, SUM(b.bond_type IN ('=','#')) nm,
 SUM(EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM connected c JOIN atom x ON x.atom_id=c.atom_id WHERE c.bond_id=b.bond_id AND x.element='c')) ncb
 FROM bond b GROUP BY b.molecule_id)
SELECT DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(b.ncb,0) DESC, a.na DESC, m.molecule_id) AS rank_pos,
 m.molecule_id, m.label, a.na AS atoms, COALESCE(b.nb,0) AS bonds, a.nc AS carbons, a.ncl AS chlorines, COALESCE(b.ncb,0) AS carbon_bonds, COALESCE(b.nm,0) AS multiple_bonds
FROM molecule m JOIN a ON a.molecule_id=m.molecule_id LEFT JOIN b ON b.molecule_id=m.molecule_id
WHERE a.nc>0 ORDER BY rank_pos;
answer:
340 molecules contain at least one carbon atom (of 343 in total). The query returns one row per molecule with these columns: rank_pos, molecule_id, label, atoms, bonds, carbons, chlorines, carbon_bonds, multiple_bonds. The top row is TR060 (label '-', 103 atoms, 107 bonds, 39 carbons, 2 chlorines, 107 carbon-touching bonds, 5 multiple bonds).

Choices I made where the question left room:
- A carbon-touching bond is a bond with at least one carbon atom at either end.
- A multiple bond is a double ('=') or triple ('#') bond.
- The rank uses DENSE_RANK over carbon-touching bonds (descending), then atom count (descending), then molecule id (ascending). The molecule id tie-break makes every rank unique, so the ranks run 1 to 340 with no gaps.
- I added the rank as the first column because you asked for ranked rows.
- Counts of zero are kept as 0 rather than dropped.

sql: select count(distinct c.name) from cards c join legalities l on l.uuid=c.uuid where c.manaCost='{0}' and l.format='commander' and l.status='Legal'
answer: 43 different cards have a printed mana cost of exactly {0} and a Legal Commander entry. I counted distinct card names, because the cards table has one row per printing (176 printing rows match). I also required the mana cost to be exactly '{0}', so costs that merely contain {0} are excluded.

sql: select sum(Score) from posts where Tags like '%<r>%' and Id in (select PostId from postLinks where RelatedPostId in (select Id from posts where Title='A Probability distribution value exceeding 1 is OK?'))
answer: 22. This is the total score of the distinct questions tagged <r> that link to "A Probability distribution value exceeding 1 is OK?". A post linked under more than one link type is counted once.

sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT q2.driverId) AS drivers_qualified_ahead_of
FROM qualifying q1
JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q1.driverId AND d.forename='Lucas' AND d.surname='di Grassi'
JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q1.raceId AND r.year=2010
JOIN qualifying q2 ON q2.raceId=q1.raceId AND q2.driverId<>q1.driverId AND q1.position<q2.position
answer: 9. Lucas di Grassi out-qualified 9 distinct drivers in 2010. A driver counts once if di Grassi had a lower qualifying position number than them in at least one 2010 race. The query uses draft (uncertified) Terms: Driver, Qualifying Result and Race.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(height),2) AS avg_height_cm FROM Player WHERE height > 180 AND player_api_id IN (SELECT home_player_3 FROM "Match" WHERE home_player_3 IS NOT NULL)
answer: 186.43 cm. Each distinct player who ever appeared in home_player_3 and is taller than 180 cm counts once, across all matches. If every appearance were counted instead, the result would be 187.05 cm. The Player term is still a draft.

sql: select L.`T-BIL`, L.Date, L.ID, P.SEX, P.Birthday from Laboratory L join Patient P on P.ID=L.ID where L.RNP glob '[0-9]*' and CAST(L.RNP AS INTEGER)=(select max(CAST(RNP AS INTEGER)) from Laboratory where RNP glob '[0-9]*') and L.`T-BIL`=(select max(L2.`T-BIL`) from Laboratory L2 where L2.RNP glob '[0-9]*' and CAST(L2.RNP AS INTEGER)=(select max(CAST(RNP AS INTEGER)) from Laboratory where RNP glob '[0-9]*'))
answer: RNP는 텍스트 컬럼이라 숫자로 변환해 비교했고('negative'와 빈 값은 제외), 최댓값은 256입니다. 그중 총 빌리루빈(T-BIL) 최고값은 0.4이고, 해당 검사는 1건입니다. 검사일은 1989-07-18, 환자 ID는 1650222, 성별은 F, 생일은 1947-03-17입니다.

sql: SELECT ID, Date, RNP FROM Laboratory WHERE GOT>=60 AND RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(RNP AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(RNP AS REAL)) FROM Laboratory WHERE GOT>=60 AND RNP GLOB '[0-9]*')
answer: Patient 1650222, test date 1989-07-18, anti-RNP reading 256. It is the only test at that maximum among tests with GOT >= 60. RNP is a text column, so I compared it numerically, which also drops the non-numeric value 'negative'. The Laboratory Test term used is still a draft in the ontology.

sql:
WITH t AS (
 SELECT c.Segment, c.CustomerID, SUM(y.Consumption) tot
 FROM customers c JOIN yearmonth y ON y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID
 WHERE c.Currency='CZK' AND c.Segment IN ('SME','LAM','KAM') AND y.Date LIKE '2013%'
 GROUP BY c.Segment, c.CustomerID),
r AS (SELECT Segment, tot, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Segment ORDER BY tot, CustomerID) rn FROM t),
m AS (SELECT Segment, tot FROM r WHERE rn=1)
SELECT ROUND((SELECT tot FROM m WHERE Segment='SME')-(SELECT tot FROM m WHERE Segment='LAM'),2) AS sme_minus_lam,
 ROUND((SELECT tot FROM m WHERE Segment='LAM')-(SELECT tot FROM m WHERE Segment='KAM'),2) AS lam_minus_kam,
 ROUND((SELECT tot FROM m WHERE Segment='KAM')-(SELECT tot FROM m WHERE Segment='SME'),2) AS kam_minus_sme;
answer: SME − LAM = -14009.34, LAM − KAM = 6046.62, KAM − SME = 7962.72. Reading chosen: only CZK customers with at least one 2013 row in yearmonth are considered. Their 2013 total is the sum of Consumption over months 201301 to 201311, and negative values are kept. Ties go to the smaller CustomerID.

sql:
WITH pos AS (SELECT a.atom_id, a.element FROM atom a JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id=a.molecule_id WHERE m.label='+'),
tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM pos),
b AS (SELECT element, COUNT(*) c FROM pos WHERE atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id FROM connected UNION SELECT atom_id2 FROM connected) GROUP BY element)
SELECT element, ROUND(100.0*(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pos p WHERE p.element=b.element)/(SELECT n FROM tot),2) AS pct FROM b WHERE c=(SELECT MAX(c) FROM b);
answer: Hydrogen ('h') is the most common element among bonded atoms in '+' molecules. It makes up 42.5% of all atoms in those molecules, including atoms with no bond. There was no tie. I counted an atom as bonded if it appears in either column of `connected`. The percentage uses every atom of the '+' molecules as the denominator.

sql: select distinct d.nationality from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) where q.q3=(select min(q3) from qualifying where q3<>'');
answer: Finnish. The fastest Q3 time is 1:04.251, and only one driver set it. I excluded empty Q3 values and compared the times as text, which works because every recorded Q3 time uses the same m:ss.mmm format (8 characters).

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT language, COUNT(DISTINCT uuid) AS printings FROM foreign_data WHERE flavorText IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(flavorText)<>'' AND language IN (SELECT language FROM set_translations) GROUP BY language) SELECT language, printings FROM c WHERE printings=(SELECT MIN(printings) FROM c) ORDER BY language
answer: Korean has the fewest, with 6,782 printings whose flavor text was translated into it. I counted distinct cards (uuid) in foreign_data with non-empty flavorText, and only for languages that also appear in set_translations. Next lowest is Chinese Traditional, with 7,729. There is no tie.

sql: select round(avg(s.weight_kg)) from superhero s join colour c on c.id=s.skin_colour_id join alignment a on a.id=s.alignment_id where c.colour='Green' and a.alignment='Bad' and s.weight_kg>0 and exists(select 1 from hero_power h join superpower p on p.id=h.power_id where h.hero_id=s.id and p.power_name='Flight')
answer: 121 kg. Three green-skinned, Bad-aligned characters can fly. I left out the one with weight 0, because the docs say 0 or NULL means the weight is missing. The other two weigh 135 and 106 kg, which average 120.5 and round to 121. I read "green-skinned" as the colour 'Green' only, not 'Green/Blue'.

sql:
SELECT MIN(CAST(strftime('%Y', l.Date) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', p.Birthday) AS INTEGER)) AS youngest_age
FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID
WHERE l.RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) >= 64
answer: 18세. 항RNP 값이 64 이상인 검사(값 64, 256)를 대상으로, 나이는 검사 연도에서 생년 연도를 뺀 값으로 계산했습니다. RNP 열이 텍스트라 숫자 값만 비교했고 'negative'는 제외했습니다. 사용한 Term(Laboratory Test, Patient)은 아직 draft 상태입니다.

sql:
WITH w AS (SELECT d.driverId, d.forename||' '||d.surname AS fn, d.dob, d.nationality FROM drivers d WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM results r WHERE r.driverId=d.driverId AND r.position=1)),
t AS (SELECT * FROM w ORDER BY dob, fn LIMIT 1)
SELECT t.fn AS full_name, t.nationality,
 (SELECT ra.name FROM results r JOIN races ra USING(raceId) WHERE r.driverId=t.driverId AND r.position=1 ORDER BY ra.date, ra.name LIMIT 1) AS first_win_race,
 (SELECT ra.date FROM results r JOIN races ra USING(raceId) WHERE r.driverId=t.driverId AND r.position=1 ORDER BY ra.date, ra.name LIMIT 1) AS first_win_date,
 (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) FROM results r WHERE r.driverId=t.driverId AND r.statusId NOT IN (81,97)) AS races_started
FROM t;
answer: Luigi Fagioli, Italian. His first win was the French Grand Prix on 1951-07-01. He started 7 races in his career. I counted a start as a results row that isn't a did-not-qualify entry (statusId 81 or 97), as the wiki advises.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT f.language) AS foreign_language_count FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Swamp'
answer: Swamp has been printed in 11 distinct foreign languages, counted across all its printings in every set and year. English is not counted because foreign_data only holds non-English entries. The Card and Card Foreign Data Terms used are still drafts (not certified).

sql: SELECT d.nationality FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q2 = (SELECT MIN(q2.q2) FROM qualifying q2 JOIN races r2 ON r2.raceId=q2.raceId WHERE r2.year=2017 AND r2.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q2.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q2.q2<>'')

sql:
WITH p AS (SELECT ID FROM Patient WHERE replace(replace(replace(Diagnosis,char(29),','),' ',''),char(9),'') IN ('RA,SJS','SJS,RA','RASJS','SJSRA')),
f AS (SELECT p.ID, MAX(CASE WHEN l.PLT>100 AND l.PLT<400 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n FROM p LEFT JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID GROUP BY p.ID)
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(n=1),0) AS with_normal_platelet, COALESCE(SUM(n=0),0) AS never_normal_platelet FROM f
answer: Of the 36 patients whose record names exactly RA and SJS, 5 have had a normal platelet result and 31 have never had one. Normal is the documented range 100 < PLT < 400, with both bounds excluded, checked over each patient's whole laboratory history. Diagnoses with 'susp' (suspected) or any other disease are excluded, and I normalized the separator variants in the stored text first. Patients with no lab rows, or only null platelet values, count as never normal. The Patient and Laboratory Test Terms are draft, not certified.

sql:
WITH p AS (SELECT ID FROM Patient WHERE replace(replace(Diagnosis,' ',''),',',';') IN ('RA;SJS','SJS;RA','RASJS','SJSRA'))
SELECT COUNT(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.PLT>100 AND l.PLT<400) THEN 1 END) AS with_normal_plt,
 COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.PLT>100 AND l.PLT<400) THEN 1 END) AS never_normal_plt FROM p
answer: Of 36 patients whose Diagnosis is exactly RA and SJS (either order), 5 have had at least one normal platelet result and 31 have never had one. Assumptions: the docs define normal PLT as 100 < PLT < 400 (strict). Diagnosis spellings 'RA, SJS', 'RA,SJS', 'SJS, RA' and 'SJS  RA' count as matches. Entries with 'susp' (e.g. 'RA, SJS susp') are excluded, since a suspected disease isn't a diagnosis and the record then names only RA. Entries with a third disease are excluded. Patients with no lab rows, or only NULL or out-of-range PLT, count as never normal.

sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT s.CDSCode, f."Enrollment (K-12)" enr, f."FRPM Count (K-12)" frpm,
         f."FRPM Count (K-12)"*1.0/f."Enrollment (K-12)" share
  FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode
  WHERE s.Charter=0 AND s.EdOpsCode='TRAD' AND s.School IS NOT NULL
    AND f."Enrollment (K-12)">100 AND f."FRPM Count (K-12)" IS NOT NULL
), picks AS (
  SELECT CDSCode, 'largest FRPM-eligible count' part, 1 ord FROM base WHERE frpm=(SELECT MAX(frpm) FROM base)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT CDSCode, 'smallest FRPM share', 2 FROM base WHERE share=(SELECT MIN(share) FROM base)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT '04615150435602', 'the CDS code from my notes', 3
)
SELECT p.part, s.School, s.County, s.City, s.MailStreet, s.MailCity, s.MailState, s.MailZip, s.Website,
  f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enrollment_k12, f."FRPM Count (K-12)" AS frpm_count,
  f."FRPM Count (K-12)"*1.0/f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS frpm_share,
  CASE WHEN t.NumTstTakr>0 THEN t.AvgScrRead+t.AvgScrMath+t.AvgScrWrite END AS avg_total_sat,
  CASE WHEN t.NumTstTakr>0 THEN 100.0*t.NumGE1500/t.NumTstTakr END AS pct_sat_ge_1500,
  s.OpenDate, CASE WHEN s.ClosedDate IS NOT NULL THEN 'closed' ELSE 'open' END AS status
FROM picks p JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode=p.CDSCode
LEFT JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode
LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds=s.CDSCode
ORDER BY p.ord, s.School;
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 3개 행이 나오는 것을 확인했습니다. 동점은 없었습니다.

1) 'largest FRPM-eligible count': Paramount High (Los Angeles 카운티, Paramount). K-12 재학생 4,814명 중 FRPM 대상 4,419명(91.8%)입니다. SAT 평균 총점은 1272, 1500점 이상 비율은 14.8%입니다. 개교일은 1953-07-01이고 상태는 open입니다.
2) 'smallest FRPM share': Orinda Intermediate (Contra Costa 카운티, Orinda). 재학생 907명 중 2명(0.22%)이 대상입니다. SAT 응시 기록이 없어 SAT 두 항목은 NULL입니다. 개교일은 1980-07-01이고 상태는 open입니다.
3) 'the CDS code from my notes': Oroville High (Butte 카운티, Oroville). 재학생 982명 중 692명(70.5%)이 대상입니다. SAT 평균 총점은 1395, 1500점 이상 비율은 32.7%입니다. 개교일은 1980-07-01이고 상태는 open입니다.

적용한 해석은 다음과 같습니다.
- 'regular, non-charter'는 schools 테이블에서 Charter=0이고 EdOpsCode='TRAD'(Traditional)인 학교로 보았습니다. 교육청 행(School이 NULL)은 제외했습니다.
- 'more than 100 K-12 students'는 frpm 테이블의 Enrollment (K-12)가 100보다 큰 경우입니다. 이 조건은 두 극단 학교를 고를 때만 적용했습니다.
- FRPM 비율은 FRPM Count (K-12)를 Enrollment (K-12)로 나눈 값입니다. 0~1 사이 비율로 표시했습니다.
- SAT 평균 총점은 읽기, 수학, 쓰기 평균의 합입니다. 1500점 이상 비율은 NumGE1500을 응시자 수로 나눈 값에 100을 곱한 퍼센트이며, 응시자가 0명이면 NULL로 두었습니다.
- 메모의 CDS 코드 4615150435602는 14자리 코드의 앞자리 0이 빠진 형태로 판단해 04615150435602(Oroville High)로 조회했습니다.
- 웹사이트는 Paramount High와 Orinda Intermediate 모두 데이터에 없어 NULL입니다.

sql: select c.nationality, count(distinct case when r.resultId is not null then c.constructorId end) as constructor_count from constructors c left join results r on r.constructorId=c.constructorId and r.rank=1 group by c.nationality order by constructor_count desc, c.nationality

sql: SELECT ROUND(COUNT(*)/12.0,2) AS avg_links_per_month FROM postLinks l JOIN posts p ON p.Id=l.PostId WHERE p.AnswerCount<=2 AND l.CreationDate>='2010-01-01' AND l.CreationDate<'2011-01-01';

Two schools match: City Honors College Preparatory Academy (Inglewood) and Tule Continuation High (Alpaugh).

 (SELECT ra.name FROM results r JOIN races ra USING(raceId) WHERE r.driverId=t.driverId AND r.position=1 ORDER BY ra.date, ra.name LIMIT 1) AS first_win_race,
 (SELECT ra.date FROM results r JOIN races ra USING(raceId) WHERE r.driverId=t.driverId AND r.position=1 ORDER BY ra.date, ra.name LIMIT 1) AS first_win_date,
