sql: select ID, Date, RNP from Laboratory where GOT>=60 and RNP glob '[0-9]*' and CAST(RNP as REAL)=(select max(CAST(RNP as REAL)) from Laboratory where GOT>=60 and RNP glob '[0-9]*')
answer: GOT가 60 이상인 검사 중 항-RNP 값이 가장 높은 검사는 1건입니다. 환자 ID 1650222, 검사일 1989-07-18, RNP 256입니다. RNP 열이 텍스트(문자열)라서 숫자로 바꿔 비교했습니다. 'negative'와 빈 값은 제외했습니다. 날짜는 Laboratory.Date(검사 시행일)를 썼습니다.

sql: select round(avg(weight_kg),2) from superhero s join gender g on g.id=s.gender_id where g.gender='Female' and weight_kg>0
answer: 78.51 kg. Weights of NULL or 0 are treated as unknown, because the docs say 0 means missing. This excludes 17 NULL and 42 zero-weight Female heroes. If zeros were counted as real weights, the result would be lower.

sql: select count(distinct r.raceId) from races r join results s on s.raceId=r.raceId where r.name='Canadian Grand Prix' and s.statusId=3
answer: 27 runnings of the Canadian Grand Prix had at least one retirement with status 'Accident' (statusId 3). I excluded 'Fatal accident' (statusId 104).

sql:
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE LOWER(p.Diagnosis) LIKE '%psoriatic arthritis%') AS total_lab_tests,
(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient p WHERE LOWER(p.Diagnosis) LIKE '%psoriatic arthritis%' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID)) AS patients_without_lab_tests

The Patient term used is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT u.DisplayName FROM posts p JOIN users u ON u.Id = p.LastEditorUserId WHERE p.Title = 'Examples for teaching: Correlation does not mean causation'
answer: 마지막으로 글을 수정한 사용자의 표시 이름은 Abhilash입니다. 제목이 정확히 일치하는 글은 1건이었고, posts.LastEditorUserId를 users.Id와 연결해 이름을 가져왔습니다. 이 결과에 쓴 Post와 User 용어는 아직 확정(certified)되지 않은 초안 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT notes FROM income WHERE source='Fundraising' AND date_received='2019-09-14'
answer: The note is "Secured donations to help pay for speaker gifts." I read "fundraising proceeds" as income rows with source = 'Fundraising'. Exactly one row matched. The Income term the query relies on is still a draft.

sql: select count(*) from cards where borderColor='black' and availability like '%mtgo%' and cast(power as integer)>=10
answer: 83. I took "available on MTGO" to mean `availability` contains 'mtgo', and compared `power` as a number (it is stored as text).

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(UpVotes),2) AS avg_upvotes, ROUND(AVG(Age),2) AS avg_age FROM users WHERE Id IN (SELECT OwnerUserId FROM posts WHERE CreaionDate >= '2012-01-01' AND CreaionDate < '2013-01-01' GROUP BY OwnerUserId HAVING COUNT(*) > 10)
answer: 268명의 사용자가 2012년에 게시글을 10개보다 많이 작성했습니다. 이들의 평균 UpVotes는 505.63, 평균 나이는 36.14입니다. 게시글 작성일 컬럼은 원본 스키마에 `CreaionDate`로 오타가 나 있어 그대로 사용했습니다. 모든 게시글 유형(질문과 답변)을 포함했고, 나이가 비어 있는 사용자는 평균 나이 계산에서 제외했습니다.

sql: SELECT p.ViewCount, u.DisplayName FROM posts p LEFT JOIN users u ON u.Id = p.LastEditorUserId WHERE p.Title = 'Computer game datasets'
answer: The post 'Computer game datasets' has 1708 views, and its last editor is 'mbq'. I took the editor's display name from users.DisplayName through posts.LastEditorUserId, because posts.LastEditorDisplayName is almost always empty. The Post and User terms the query relies on are still draft in the ontology.

sql:
WITH c AS (SELECT s.School, s.District, s.County, t.AvgScrWrite w FROM satscores t JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode=t.cds WHERE s.StatusType='Closed' AND t.rtype='S' AND s.School IS NOT NULL AND t.AvgScrWrite IS NOT NULL)
SELECT School, District, County, w AS AvgScrWrite FROM c WHERE w=(SELECT MAX(w) FROM c WHERE w<(SELECT MAX(w) FROM c));
answer: FAME Public Charter (district: Alameda County Office of Education, county: Alameda), average SAT writing score 505. It is the only school at that score. I counted only school-level records (rtype 'S'). A district-level record (rtype 'D') for a closed district, Livermore Valley Charter Preparatory High, has 515, but it has no school name, so I left it out. If you count it, the runner-up changes to that record.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(e."aCL IgM"), 2) AS avg_aCL_IgM FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID WHERE REPLACE(p.diagnosis, 'SJS susp', '') LIKE '%SJS%' AND e."aCL IgM" > 0;
answer: The average aCL IgM is 2.89, over 19 examinations from 18 patients. I kept a patient if 'SJS' remained in the diagnosis after removing 'SJS susp', so 'SJS, RA susp' counts and 'SJS susp' alone does not. All dates are included, and values of 0 are excluded.

sql:
select d.department,
 group_concat(distinct m.major_name) as majors_offered,
 (select group_concat(major_name) from (select distinct m2.major_name from major m2 join member b on b.link_to_major=m2.major_id where m2.department=d.department order by 1)) as majors_held,
 round(1.0*(select count(*) from member b join major m3 on b.link_to_major=m3.major_id where m3.department=d.department)/count(*),2) as avg_members_per_major
from (select distinct department from major where college='College of Humanities and Social Sciences') d
join major m on m.department=d.department
group by d.department order by d.department;
answer:
The query returns 11 departments in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences. The columns are department, majors offered, majors held by members, and average members per major offered. No department has majors in more than one college, so the "any major in the college" rule changes nothing here.

Readings I chose:
- Majors offered means every major in the department.
- Average members per major offered is the members whose current `link_to_major` falls in the department, divided by the number of majors the department offers (not just the held ones). A member with no major is not counted.
- Departments with no held majors show NULL in the held column and 0.0 as the average.

Departments with members:
- Languages, Philosophy and Communication Studies: 3 of 8 majors held (Chinese, Communication Studies, Portuguese), average 0.38.
- Political Science: 2 of 3 majors held (International Studies, Law and Constitutional Studies), average 1.0.
- Liberal Arts Program: its one major is held, average 1.0.

The other 8 departments have no members.

sql: select d.account_id, (select max(A11)-min(A11) from district) as salary_diff from disp d where d.client_id=(select client_id from client where gender='F' and district_id=(select district_id from district order by A11 limit 1) order by birth_date limit 1);
answer: 계좌 ID는 3214이고, 지역 평균 급여의 최고값과 최저값 차이는 4431입니다. 평균 급여(A11)가 가장 낮은 district의 여성 고객 중 생년월일이 가장 빠른 고객을 가장 나이 많은 고객으로 보았습니다. 계좌는 disp 테이블로 연결했고 disp 유형은 구분하지 않았습니다.

sql: with c as (select m.major_name, count(distinct a.link_to_member) n from attendance a join event e on e.event_id=a.link_to_event join member b on b.member_id=a.link_to_member join major m on m.major_id=b.link_to_major where e.event_name='Football game' group by m.major_id, m.major_name) select major_name, n from c where n=(select max(n) from c) order by major_name
answer: Three majors tie for the most football-game attendees, with 2 each: Elementary Education, Environmental Engineering, and Human Development and Family Studies. The database has two events named "Football game" (2019-09-12 and 2019-10-10). I counted distinct members across both, so a member who went to both counts once. Members with no major recorded are not counted.

sql: select count(*) from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) where (d.code is null or d.code='') and d.forename in (select forename from drivers group by forename having count(*)>1) and q.q1 like '%:%' and cast(substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1) as int)>=2
answer: 23 Q1 times of two minutes or slower were set by drivers who have no code and share a first name with at least one other driver. I read "slower than two minutes" as a Q1 time with 2 or more minutes. Q1 is stored as text, so I compared the minutes part as a number. That also catches an odd value like "16:42.640". Empty or NULL Q1 values are excluded. "No code" means a NULL code (an empty string would count too, but there are none).

sql: select r.year, round(avg(s.milliseconds)/1000.0,2) as mean_winner_seconds from results s join races r using(raceId) where s.positionOrder=1 and s.milliseconds is not null and r.year<1975 group by r.year order by r.year
answer:
The query returns 25 rows, one for each year from 1950 to 1974. The mean winner time falls from 9712.60 s in 1950 to 6047.11 s in 1974. 1957 was the slowest year at 11323.32 s.

I took the winner as the result with positionOrder = 1. I counted only winners that have a recorded milliseconds value, and divided by 1000 to get seconds. I rounded with SQLite's round(), which rounds halves away from zero.

sql:
WITH q AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT c.district_id FROM client c
  JOIN disp d ON d.client_id=c.client_id AND d.type='OWNER'
  WHERE c.gender='F'
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM card k WHERE k.disp_id=d.disp_id)
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=d.account_id)
), r AS (
  SELECT di.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY A3 ORDER BY CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) DESC, A2) rn
  FROM district di JOIN q ON q.district_id=di.district_id
)
SELECT A3 AS region, ROUND(AVG(A11),2) AS avg_salary, ROUND(AVG(A13),2) AS avg_unemployment_1996,
       MAX(CASE WHEN rn=1 THEN A2 END) AS most_populous_district
FROM r GROUP BY A3 ORDER BY A3;
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 8개 지역이 모두 나왔습니다. 지역별 (평균 급여 / 1996 실업률 / 최다 인구 district):
Prague 12541.0 / 0.43 / Hl.m. Praha
central Bohemia 9318.3 / 3.18 / Kladno
east Bohemia 8614.25 / 3.27 / Pardubice
north Bohemia 9386.11 / 6.37 / Liberec
north Moravia 9179.11 / 5.61 / Ostrava - mesto
south Bohemia 8989.2 / 2.53 / Ceske Budejovice
south Moravia 9001.0 / 2.83 / Brno - mesto
west Bohemia 8745.5 / 2.75 / Plzen - jih

선택한 해석: 대상은 OWNER disposition의 여성 고객 중 그 disposition에 카드가 있고 같은 계좌에 대출이 있는 사람입니다. 고객 거주 district(client.district_id)를 기준으로 했습니다. 평균은 고객 수 가중이 아니라 해당 지역의 서로 다른 district마다 한 번씩 계산했습니다. 인구(A4)는 텍스트라 정수로 변환해 비교했고, 동률이면 district 이름 알파벳 순으로 골랐습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient p WHERE p.Admission = '+' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.ALP >= 300)
answer: 464 admitted patients never had an ALP result above the normal ceiling. The docs give the ALP normal range as N < 300, so I counted a result of 300 or more as above the ceiling. 'Admitted' means Patient.Admission = '+'. This count includes admitted patients with no lab rows at all, since they never had a high ALP either. If you only want patients who have at least one lab record, the count is 97. The ontology Terms used (Patient, Laboratory Test) are still drafts.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT s.code) FROM sets s JOIN set_translations t ON t.setCode = s.code WHERE s.block = 'Ice Age' AND t.language = 'Italian' AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND t.translation <> ''
answer: 1. Of the 5 sets in the Ice Age block, only Coldsnap (CSP) has an Italian translation, 'Ondata Glaciale'. Ice Age (ICE) has an Italian row with an empty translation, which I did not count. If you count that row, the answer would be 2.

sql: select round(avg(TP-8.5),3) from Laboratory l where TP>8.5 and exists(select 1 from Patient p where p.ID=l.ID and p.SEX='F') and exists(select 1 from Examination e where e.ID=l.ID and e.Diagnosis like '%SLE%' and e.Diagnosis not like '%susp%');
answer:
평균 편차는 0.156입니다. 조건에 맞는 검사 기록은 9건입니다.

적용한 해석은 세 가지입니다.
- 진단에 'SLE'가 들어간 검진 기록을 SLE 진단으로 봤습니다. 'SLE'만 있는 경우와 다른 병명이 함께 있는 경우를 모두 포함합니다.
- 'SLE susp'(의심) 1건은 확진이 아니라서 제외했습니다.
- 환자 한 명의 검진 기록이 여러 건이어도 검사 기록이 중복 계산되지 않도록, 환자 단위로 SLE 진단 여부를 확인했습니다.

sql:
WITH g AS (
SELECT c.Segment s,
 SUM(CASE WHEN substr(y.Date,1,4)='2012' THEN y.Consumption END) a,
 SUM(CASE WHEN substr(y.Date,1,4)='2013' THEN y.Consumption END) b
FROM yearmonth y JOIN customers c ON c.CustomerID=y.CustomerID
WHERE c.Currency='EUR' AND c.Segment IN ('SME','LAM','KAM')
GROUP BY c.Segment),
p AS (SELECT s, ROUND((b-a)*100.0/a,2) pct FROM g)
SELECT s AS Segment, pct FROM p
WHERE pct=(SELECT MAX(pct) FROM p) OR pct=(SELECT MIN(pct) FROM p)
ORDER BY pct DESC;
answer: SME 의 증가율이 734.71%로 가장 높고, LAM 이 539.83%로 가장 낮습니다. 증가율은 EUR 고객의 연간 총 소비량을 2012년과 2013년으로 합산해 (2013-2012)/2012 로 계산했습니다. KAM 은 두 값 사이에 있어 결과에 나오지 않습니다. 동률은 없었습니다.

sql: SELECT u.DisplayName FROM posts p JOIN users u ON u.Id = p.LastEditorUserId WHERE p.Title = 'Examples for teaching: Correlation does not mean causation'
answer: Abhilash. 제목이 정확히 일치하는 게시글 1건의 LastEditorUserId를 users.Id와 연결해 DisplayName을 가져왔습니다. 'Post'와 'User' 용어는 아직 인증되지 않은 초안 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superhero WHERE alignment_id = 1 AND (publisher_id IS NULL OR publisher_id <> 4)
answer: 358 superheroes have alignment Good and are not published by DC Comics. I counted heroes with no publisher (NULL publisher_id) as "not DC", and 3 of the 358 are in that group. Excluding them would give 355.

sql: with t as (select e.type, count(distinct a.link_to_member) as n from event e join attendance a on a.link_to_event=e.event_id where e.event_date>='2019-09-01' and e.event_date<'2020-06-01' group by e.type) select type, n as members from t where n=(select max(n) from t)
answer: Meeting and Registration tie, with 30 distinct members each. I counted each member once per event type, even if they attended several events of that type. I included every event dated September 2019 through May 2020 regardless of status (Closed, Open or Planning). All events fall in that range anyway.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.driverId) AS drivers_outqualified FROM qualifying g JOIN races r ON r.raceId=g.raceId AND r.year=2010 JOIN qualifying o ON o.raceId=g.raceId AND o.driverId<>g.driverId WHERE g.driverId=(SELECT driverId FROM drivers WHERE forename='Lucas' AND surname='di Grassi') AND g.position<o.position
answer: 9. Lucas di Grassi (driverId 810) out-qualified 9 distinct drivers in 2010. I counted each driver once, however many races he beat them in. Counting every driver-and-race pairing instead gives 34.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) FROM cards c JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid=c.uuid WHERE c.borderColor='white' AND l.status='Banned'
answer: 89 distinct white-bordered card printings (cards rows, by uuid) are banned in at least one format. Restricted status is not counted as banned. The Card and Card Legality terms are still drafts in the ontology.

sql: SELECT SUM(p.SEX='F') AS F, SUM(p.SEX='M') AS M FROM Patient p WHERE p.SEX IN ('F','M') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.Date BETWEEN '1994-01-01' AND '1994-12-31' AND l.GOT < 60)
answer: F: 80, M: 16. Normal GOT is defined as GOT < 60 (per docs). A patient is counted once if at least one 1994 lab test had GOT < 60; tests with null GOT and patients with blank SEX are excluded. Patient and Laboratory Test Terms are draft (uncertified).

sql:
WITH c AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.event_name, e.event_date, COUNT(a.link_to_member) n FROM event e LEFT JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event=e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_id),
s AS (SELECT n FROM c WHERE event_name='Women''s Soccer'),
f AS (SELECT ROUND(AVG(n),1) avg FROM c WHERE event_date >= '2019-09-01' AND event_date < '2019-12-01')
SELECT s.n AS womens_soccer_attendees, f.avg AS fall_2019_avg_attendees,
CASE WHEN s.n>f.avg THEN 'more' WHEN s.n<f.avg THEN 'fewer' ELSE 'equal' END AS verdict FROM s, f;
answer: 17 students attended the Women's Soccer game (2019-10-05). The average attendance across all fall 2019 events (1 Sep to 30 Nov 2019) is 16.1, so the verdict is 'more'. Choices: events with no attendance rows count as 0 in the average (LEFT JOIN), and attendance is counted as one row per member per event.

sql: select distinct s.name, s.releaseDate from cards c join sets s on s.code=c.setCode where c.name='Aven Mindcensor' and c.frameVersion='2015' and s.releaseDate=(select max(s2.releaseDate) from cards c2 join sets s2 on s2.code=c2.setCode where c2.name='Aven Mindcensor' and c2.frameVersion='2015')
answer: Amonkhet Remastered, released 2020-08-13. Aven Mindcensor has 6 printings. Five use the 2015 frame (Amonkhet, Amonkhet Remastered, Amonkhet Invocations, and Amonkhet Promos twice). Future Sight uses the "future" frame. I treated "future" as the 2007 Future Sight frame, which is older than 2015, not as the newest. Among the 2015-frame printings, Amonkhet Remastered has the latest release date.

sql: SELECT s.Street, s.City, s.Zip, s.State FROM satscores AS t INNER JOIN schools AS s ON t.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE t.rtype = 'S' AND t.NumTstTakr >= 700 AND t.NumGE1500 IS NOT NULL ORDER BY CAST(t.NumGE1500 AS REAL) / t.NumTstTakr ASC, t.cds ASC LIMIT 1
answer: 10535 Zelzah Avenue, Granada Hills, CA 91344-5902. Excellence rate is read as NumGE1500 / NumTstTakr (share of test takers scoring 1500 or higher), using school-level rows only (rtype = 'S') with at least 700 test takers and a non-null NumGE1500. Ties go to the smallest school code. The ontology terms used (SAT Score Record, School) are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT d.A2 FROM client c JOIN disp ON c.client_id=disp.client_id JOIN account a ON disp.account_id=a.account_id JOIN district d ON a.district_id=d.district_id WHERE c.gender='F' AND c.birth_date='1976-01-29'
answer: Tachov. I read "district where she opened her account" as the account's district (account.district_id), reached through disp, not the client's own district. The query returned one row. The Account, Client and District terms are still draft (not certified).

sql: select f."County Name" AS county, count(*) AS school_count from frpm f join satscores s on s.cds=f.CDSCode where s.rtype='S' and f."Academic Year"='2014-2015' and f."Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)">0.1 and s.NumGE1500>=1 group by f."County Name" order by school_count desc, county asc
answer: I joined frpm to satscores on the CDS code. I kept only school-level SAT rows (rtype='S'), so district rows aren't counted. The filters were academic year 2014-2015, free-meal rate above 0.1 and NumGE1500 of at least 1. County comes from the frpm county name. The query ran and the top counties are Los Angeles (305), San Diego (86), Orange (62), San Bernardino (60) and Riverside (58). I only checked the first 8 rows of the result, not the full list.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(height_cm), 1) FROM superhero WHERE publisher_id = (SELECT publisher_id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = 'A-Bomb') AND height_cm > 0
answer: 389.5 cm. I read "A-Bomb's group" as heroes with the same publisher (Marvel Comics). The average covers 327 heroes, including A-Bomb. Heroes whose height is NULL or 0 are excluded, because the docs say those mean the height is missing.

sql: select (100.0*(e.balance-s.balance))/s.balance as pct_increase from trans s, trans e where s.account_id=e.account_id and s.date='1993-03-22' and e.date='1998-12-27' and s.account_id=(select account_id from loan where date='1993-07-05')
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) FROM cards WHERE frameVersion = '2015' AND text IS NOT NULL AND text <> ''
answer: 11,410 distinct cards. I counted only frameVersion = '2015', because 'future' is a frame style label and not a year. A card counts as having a text box when its rules text is neither NULL nor empty. Cards are counted by distinct name, since the table has one row per printing. The Card term used is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 2) FROM superhero s JOIN gender g ON g.id = s.gender_id WHERE g.gender = 'Female' AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: 78.51 kg (144 female heroes). The docs say a weight_kg of NULL or 0 means unknown, so I excluded both. If 0 were counted as a real weight, the average would be 60.78.

sql: select round(avg(case when height_cm>0 then height_cm end),1) as avg_height_cm, round(avg(case when weight_kg>0 then weight_kg end),1) as avg_weight_kg from superhero s join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id where p.publisher_name='George Lucas'
answer:
George Lucas's heroes average 187.2 cm in height and 83.0 kg in weight.

I read "heroes he created" as the heroes whose publisher is 'George Lucas', which is how the data records it. The data stores unknown height and weight as 0 or NULL, so I left out both values. Height is averaged over 12 heroes and weight over 5.

sql:
SELECT s.type AS type, COUNT(DISTINCT t.setCode) AS japanese_name_set_count
FROM sets s
LEFT JOIN set_translations t
  ON t.setCode = s.code
 AND t.language = 'Japanese'
 AND t.translation IS NOT NULL
 AND TRIM(t.translation) <> ''
GROUP BY s.type
ORDER BY s.type;
answer:
The query returns all 20 expansion types, sorted alphabetically, each with the number of its sets that have a Japanese entry in set_translations. I ran it and it works.

Counts above 0: expansion 41, duel_deck 16, from_the_vault 8, commander 7, core 7, masters 5, box 3, draft_innovation 2, planechase 2, archenemy 1, premium_deck 1. Nine types show 0: funny, masterpiece, memorabilia, promo, spellbook, starter, token, treasure_chest and vanguard.

I counted a set only if its Japanese entry has a non-empty translation. 28 Japanese rows have a blank or null translation, and I judged that those don't actually give the name in Japanese. Each set is counted once, even if it had more than one Japanese row.

sql: select avg(height_cm) from superhero s where publisher_id=13 and height_cm>0 and exists(select 1 from hero_power hp where hp.hero_id=s.id and hp.power_id not in (select hp2.power_id from hero_power hp2 join superhero d on d.id=hp2.hero_id where d.publisher_id=4))
answer: The average height is about 202.6 cm. This covers Marvel Comics characters with at least one power that no DC Comics character has. I treated a height of 0 or NULL as not measured and excluded those characters.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(weight),1) FROM Player WHERE player_api_id IN (SELECT player_api_id FROM Player_Attributes WHERE preferred_foot='left')
answer: 166.6 (weight units as stored in Player.weight, which I did not check against docs/). I counted each player once if any of their Player_Attributes rows has preferred_foot='left'. Some players may also have right-footed rows in other seasons.

sql: select sum(p.SEX='F')-sum(p.SEX='M') as diff from Laboratory l join Patient p using(ID) where l.Date=(select max(Date) from Laboratory where ID=l.ID) and l.RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' and CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>=32
answer: 1. Reading used: each patient's most recent Laboratory row (latest Date), since RNP is recorded there. Only numeric RNP values of 32 or higher count. A patient whose latest row has a NULL or 'negative' RNP is not counted, and earlier tests are not carried forward. Result: 1 female and 0 male patients, so the difference is 1.

sql:
SELECT b.bond_type, COUNT(DISTINCT b.bond_id) AS bond_count
FROM bond b
JOIN molecule m ON b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
JOIN connected c ON c.bond_id = b.bond_id
JOIN atom a1 ON c.atom_id = a1.atom_id
JOIN atom a2 ON c.atom_id2 = a2.atom_id
WHERE m.label = '+' AND a1.element = 'c' AND a2.element = 'c'
GROUP BY b.bond_type
answer: In carcinogenic molecules (label '+'), carbon-carbon bonds (both atoms are carbon) are: single '-' = 843, double '=' = 478. There are no triple '#' carbon-carbon bonds, so that type does not appear. Each bond is stored twice in `connected`, so I counted distinct bond_id. The Atom, Bond and Molecule terms are still draft in the ontology.

sql: select p.Id, u.DisplayName from posts p left join users u on u.Id=p.OwnerUserId where p.CreaionDate like '2010%' order by p.FavoriteCount desc limit 1
answer: Post 1595, owned by Fabian Fagerholm (233 favorites). I used the users table's DisplayName for the owner. I also used the posts column CreaionDate, which is misspelled in the schema, to filter for 2010.

sql: select count(distinct u.DisplayName) from users u join badges b on b.UserId=u.Id where b.Name='Supporter' and u.Age between 19 and 65
answer: 2940 distinct display names. I counted users aged 19–65 inclusive who have a badge named 'Supporter', at any time. 3,024 such users share 2,940 distinct names, so some names repeat.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) FROM cards WHERE type LIKE '%Creature%' AND power GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(power AS INTEGER) >= 10 AND setCode IN (SELECT setCode FROM set_translations WHERE language='French' AND translation IS NOT NULL AND translation<>'')
answer: 33 distinct creature cards (by name) with power ≥ 10 have a printing in a set that has a French name translation. I counted each card name once, and treated a card as a creature if its type contains "Creature".

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE SEX='F' AND Admission='+' AND "First Date" >= '1998-01-01' AND "First Date" <= '1998-12-31'
answer: 13 female patients had their first hospital visit in 1998 and were admitted. I used `First Date` as the first-visit date (not `Description`, the date the patient's data was first recorded), `Admission = '+'` for admitted, and `SEX = 'F'` for female. Blank-sex patients are excluded. The `Patient` Term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(A11), 2) FROM district WHERE district_id IN (SELECT district_id FROM client WHERE gender = 'F' AND birth_date < '1950-01-01')
answer: 9031.68. I counted each home district once, then averaged their average salaries (A11). If you weight by client, so that districts with more such clients count more, the figure is 9518.51.

sql:
SELECT
 SUM(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bond b WHERE b.molecule_id=m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type<>'-') THEN CASE m.label WHEN '+' THEN 1 WHEN '-' THEN -1 ELSE 0 END ELSE 0 END) AS all_single_diff,
 SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bond b WHERE b.molecule_id=m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type<>'-') THEN CASE m.label WHEN '+' THEN 1 WHEN '-' THEN -1 ELSE 0 END ELSE 0 END) AS other_diff
FROM molecule m
answer: Molecules with only single bonds: carcinogenic minus non-carcinogenic = 9. All other molecules: -48. So fully saturated molecules lean carcinogenic, and the rest lean non-carcinogenic. I ran the two groups as separate queries and got these values. The final single-row query is the same logic, but I didn't run it as one statement. Assumptions: every molecule has at least one bond, so none fall in the "all single" group by default. Five molecules have label '#', which is neither '+' nor '-', so they count as 0 in both differences.

sql: select count(*) as school_count from frpm f join schools s on s.CDSCode=f.CDSCode where f."Enrollment (K-12)">500 and f."High Grade" in ('1','2','3','4','5','6','7','8') and s.School is not null and trim(s.School)<>'' and not exists (select 1 from satscores t where t.cds=f.CDSCode and t.NumTstTakr>0);
answer: 4,237 school sites. I counted a school only if it has a name in schools.School, which excludes district and county offices. Highest grade had to be numeric 1 to 8, so 'K', 'P' and 'Adult' were left out. A school with no SAT row, or an SAT row showing 0 test takers, counts as having no test takers.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(e.m) - julianday(p."First Date"))) AS avg_delay_days
FROM Patient p
JOIN (SELECT ID, MIN("Examination Date") AS m FROM Examination GROUP BY ID) e ON e.ID = p.ID
WHERE p.Admission LIKE '+%' AND p."First Date" IS NOT NULL AND e.m IS NOT NULL
answer: The average delay is 1616 days (about 4.4 years), based on 20 admitted patients. Readings I chose: "admitted" means Admission starts with '+', which includes the 3 malformed '+(' rows. Each patient's first visit is Patient."First Date" and the first examination is the earliest Examination."Examination Date". Patients missing either date (NULL First Date, or no examination) are left out. Only 20 patients had both dates, so the figure rests on a small sample.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT mj.college AS college_name, COUNT(DISTINCT mj.major_id) AS num_majors FROM member m JOIN major mj ON mj.major_id=m.link_to_major GROUP BY mj.college) SELECT college_name, num_majors FROM c WHERE num_majors=(SELECT MAX(num_majors) FROM c) ORDER BY college_name
answer: Two colleges tie for the most majors on the roster, with 6 majors each: College of Agriculture and Applied Sciences and College of Humanities and Social Sciences. I counted distinct majors held by any member, whatever their position, and grouped them by the college stored on the major table. One member has no major listed, so that member is not counted. The Major term is still a draft in the ontology, not certified.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT c.types, COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) n FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid=c.uuid WHERE c.watermark='boros' GROUP BY c.types) SELECT types, n FROM t WHERE n=(SELECT MAX(n) FROM t)
answer: Creature is the most common type among boros-watermark cards with foreign-language data, with 71 cards and no ties. I read "printed in a foreign language" as having at least one row in foreign_data, and "card type" as cards.types. Each card is counted once. The Card Term is still a draft.

sql:
SELECT t.team_long_name, t.team_short_name, COUNT(*) AS home_wins
FROM "Match" m
JOIN "Team" t ON t.team_api_id = m.home_team_api_id
WHERE m.home_team_goal - m.away_team_goal >= 3
AND (SELECT ta.buildUpPlaySpeedClass FROM "Team_Attributes" ta
     WHERE ta.team_api_id = m.home_team_api_id AND ta.date <= m.date
     ORDER BY ta.date DESC, ta.id DESC LIMIT 1) = 'Fast'
GROUP BY t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name, t.team_short_name
ORDER BY home_wins DESC, t.team_long_name
answer:
65개 클럽이 조건에 맞았습니다. 가장 많은 클럽은 Borussia Dortmund(DOR) 29경기, Celtic(CEL) 26경기, SL Benfica(BEN) 17경기, Manchester City(MCI) 14경기, Legia Warszawa(LEG) 13경기 순입니다. 마지막 11개 클럽은 1경기입니다.

적용한 해석: (1) 속도 등급은 경기일 이전(경기일 포함)의 가장 최근 Team_Attributes 기록의 buildUpPlaySpeedClass가 'Fast'인 경우입니다. 경기일 이전 기록이 없으면 제외했습니다. (2) team_api_id로 묶어서 약칭이 같은 클럽(예: HAM)도 따로 나옵니다. (3) 동률 문장은 '해당하는 모든 클럽, 클럽당 한 행'으로 읽어 65개 전체를 냈습니다. 최다 승 클럽만 원한다면 Dortmund 한 곳입니다. Match, Team, Team_Attributes는 아직 인증되지 않은 draft 항목입니다.

sql:
select round(1.0*sum(case when g.gender='Male' then c end)/sum(g.gender='Male'),2) as male_avg, round(1.0*sum(case when g.gender='Female' then c end)/sum(g.gender='Female'),2) as female_avg
from (select s.id, s.gender_id, (select count(*) from hero_power hp where hp.hero_id=s.id) c from superhero s where s.full_name is not null and s.full_name<>'-') s join gender g on g.id=s.gender_id
answer: Male 8.49, Female 6.83. A hero has a documented full name when full_name is neither NULL nor the placeholder '-'. Heroes with no power records count as 0 powers, so each average covers every named hero of that gender.

sql: select distinct c.bond_id from connected c join atom a1 on a1.atom_id=c.atom_id join atom a2 on a2.atom_id=c.atom_id2 where (a1.element='p' and a2.element='n') or (a1.element='n' and a2.element='p')
answer: 질문을 '인(p)과 질소(n) 원자를 잇는 결합의 bond_id'로 해석했습니다. 결합은 6개입니다: TR032_2_3, TR032_3_5, TR058_1_3, TR058_1_4, TR058_1_5, TR298_1_5. 원소 값은 데이터에 소문자로 저장되어 있어 소문자로 비교했습니다.

sql: select e.event_name, printf('%.2f', coalesce((select sum(x.cost) from budget b join expense x on x.link_to_budget=b.budget_id where b.link_to_event=e.event_id and lower(x.expense_description) like '%water%'),0)*1.0/(select count(*) from attendance a where a.link_to_event=e.event_id)) as water_cost_per_attendee from event e where exists(select 1 from attendance a where a.link_to_event=e.event_id)
answer:
The query returns 17 events that had attendees, one row per event, so the two 'Football game' events appear separately. Events with no water purchases show 0.00. Water cost per attendee ranges from 0.94 (Yearly Kickoff) to 3.01 (October Meeting).

I made three choices:
- **Water purchases:** I counted any expense whose description contains 'water'. The four descriptions that match are 'Water, Cookies', 'Water, chips, cookies', 'Water, Veggie tray, supplies' and 'Water, cookies, chips'. Each counts at its full cost.
- **Linking expenses to events:** I linked expenses to events through the budget table.
- **Per-attendee amount:** I divided the water total by the number of attendance records for the event.

All event statuses are included. The amount is a text value formatted to two decimals.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers c WHERE c.Currency='EUR' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM yearmonth y WHERE y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID AND y.Date LIKE '2012%' AND y.Consumption>0) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM yearmonth y WHERE y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID AND y.Date LIKE '2013%' AND y.Consumption>0)
answer: 1516 EUR customers had gas consumption in both 2012 and 2013. I counted a year only if some month in it had consumption above 0. If any recorded row counts, including zero or negative values, the count is 1517.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(c), 2) AS avg_powers FROM (SELECT s.id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id) AS c FROM superhero s INNER JOIN race r ON s.race_id = r.id INNER JOIN gender g ON s.gender_id = g.id WHERE r.race = 'God / Eternal' AND g.gender = 'Male')
answer: 16.18. I took "God / Eternal" to be the race value of that name, and heroes with no powers count as 0 in the average. Superhero, Race and Gender are draft (uncertified) terms.

sql: select s.School, s.Street from frpm f join schools s using(CDSCode) where s.School is not null and trim(s.School)<>'' and f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > 30 and f."High Grade" in ('K','1','2','3','4','5','6','7','8')
answer: The query returns 121 schools, one row each (frpm has one row per CDSCode). Columns are school name and street address, taken from the schools table. I kept schools where Enrollment (K-12) minus Enrollment (Ages 5-17) is greater than 30. I counted a high grade of K or 1 through 8 as "grade 8 or below". I left out P (preschool), Adult, Post Secondary and grades 9-13. Schools with a blank name are excluded as unnamed. Rows with a null enrollment value drop out of the comparison.

sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS patient_count
FROM Laboratory l
JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID
WHERE l.Date BETWEEN '1981-01-01' AND '1986-12-31'
  AND l.PLT BETWEEN 100 AND 400
  AND l."U-PRO" IN ('1','2','3','4','30','100','300','>=300','>=1000','+1(30)','+2(100)')
  AND p.Birthday IS NOT NULL
  AND CAST(strftime('%Y', l.Date) AS INT) - CAST(strftime('%Y', p.Birthday) AS INT)
      - (strftime('%m-%d', l.Date) < strftime('%m-%d', p.Birthday)) < 50
answer: 45 patients. Proteinuria is read as a positive U-PRO grade (1-4) or a value of 30 or higher (30, 100, 300, >=300, >=1000, +1(30), +2(100)). '-', '0' and 'TR' (trace) are treated as negative. A strict "30 or higher" rule gives 0 patients, because 1981-1986 tests only use the graded scale. Age is completed years on the test date. The date and platelet ranges are inclusive, and each patient is counted once. The Laboratory Test and Patient terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT d.A2 FROM client c JOIN disp ON disp.client_id=c.client_id JOIN account a ON a.account_id=disp.account_id JOIN district d ON d.district_id=a.district_id WHERE c.gender='F' AND c.birth_date='1976-01-29'
answer: Tachov. I used the district of the account (account.district_id, reached through disp), not the client's own district_id. Exactly one client matches, a female client (client 3339) who owns account 2766.

sql: select bank, account, count(*) as payments, sum(amount) as total_paid from trans where account_id=(select account_id from loan where amount=98832 and date='1996-01-03') and type='VYDAJ' and date<'1996-01-03' and bank is not null and bank<>'' and account is not null group by bank,account order by total_paid desc
answer:
The loan (loan_id 5999) belongs to account 4907. Before 1996-01-03 it paid three counterparties, listed largest total first:
- YZ / 25638538: 18 payments, 70,884
- AB / 5604631: 18 payments, 22,554
- QR / 82890259: 19 payments, 6,175

I left out debits with no bank or account recorded, since they can't be tied to a specific counterparty. The date filter is strictly before 1996-01-03.

sql: SELECT d.driverRef, COALESCE(SUM(r.points),0) AS total_points FROM drivers d LEFT JOIN results r ON r.driverId=d.driverId AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM lapTimes l WHERE l.raceId=r.raceId AND l.driverId=r.driverId) WHERE d.forename='Robert' GROUP BY d.driverId, d.driverRef;
answer: The query returns five drivers with the forename Robert. Only kubica has points in races that have lap timing data for him: 255.0. doornbos, la_caze, manzon and obrien show 0. Points come from results.points, which holds the points scored in each race. A race counts only if lapTimes has at least one lap for that driver in that race. I kept Roberts with no matching races and showed them as 0, rather than dropping them, because the question asks for every Robert. Two of these, doornbos and la_caze, did score points in some races, but those races have no lap timing for them.

sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname FROM drivers d JOIN results r ON r.driverId = d.driverId WHERE d.dob >= '1980-01-01' AND d.dob < '1991-01-01' AND r.fastestLapSpeed IS NOT NULL GROUP BY d.driverId ORDER BY MAX(CAST(r.fastestLapSpeed AS REAL)) DESC, d.dob ASC, d.surname ASC LIMIT 3
answer: Fernando Alonso, Antônio Pizzonia, Jenson Button (in that order). I read "between 1980 and 1990" as born from 1980-01-01 through 1990-12-31, and I cast the text column fastestLapSpeed to a number. Ties are broken by earlier birth date, then by surname. The Driver and Race Result terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(Diagnosis = 'SLE') / COUNT(*), 2) AS sle_percentage FROM Examination WHERE Thrombosis > 0;
answer: 33.33. Of the 12 examination records with thrombosis (Thrombosis > 0, any grade), 4 have the examination-visit Diagnosis exactly 'SLE'. I used Examination.Diagnosis, not Patient.Diagnosis. I counted examination records, including 5 with a NULL ID, so the figure is a share of records and not of distinct patients. I counted only the exact value 'SLE'. If combined labels such as 'SLE+Psy' and 'SLE+PH' also count, the result is 50.00.

sql:
WITH bu AS (SELECT DISTINCT uuid FROM legalities WHERE status='Banned'),
b AS (SELECT c.name, MIN(c.edhrecRank) AS r, MIN(c.convertedManaCost) AS m
      FROM cards c JOIN bu ON bu.uuid=c.uuid
      WHERE c.types LIKE '%Creature%'
      GROUP BY c.name)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(m),1) AS avg_mana_value FROM b WHERE r BETWEEN 1 AND 1000;
answer: 평균 마나 가치는 3.4입니다(정확한 값 3.4286, 카드 7장). 같은 카드의 여러 인쇄본은 이름 기준으로 한 장으로 합쳤고, 인쇄본 사이에 마나 가치가 다른 경우는 없었습니다. 'Creature'가 types에 들어간 카드(아티팩트 크리처 포함)를 크리처로 보았습니다. 금지 여부는 legalities에서 어느 포맷이든 status가 'Banned'이면 해당하는 것으로 보았습니다.

sql: select sum(cr.points) as score, c.name, c.nationality from constructorResults cr join races r on r.raceId=cr.raceId join constructors c on c.constructorId=cr.constructorId where r.name='Monaco Grand Prix' and r.year between 1980 and 2010 group by c.constructorId order by score desc limit 1
answer: McLaren (British) scored the most points at the Monaco Grand Prix from 1980 to 2010: 218.5. I read "between 1980 and 2010" as inclusive of both years and summed the constructorResults points. Ferrari was second with 194.5.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(d.A11),2) AS avg_salary, COUNT(*) AS n_districts FROM district d WHERE d.A3='east Bohemia' AND d.district_id IN (SELECT a.district_id FROM disp JOIN client c ON c.client_id=disp.client_id JOIN account a ON a.account_id=disp.account_id WHERE c.birth_date >= '1980-01-01' AND c.birth_date < '1990-01-01')
answer: The average of the districts' average salaries is 8618.20, across 10 East Bohemia districts. A district counts as serving a client when the client is on an account (owner or disponent) whose branch district is that district, not the client's home district. Birth years 1980 through 1989 are matched on birth_date, and each district is counted once. The Account, Client and District Terms are draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT SUM(totalSetSize) FROM sets WHERE releaseDate BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2017-12-31' AND code IN (SELECT setCode FROM set_translations WHERE translation IS NOT NULL AND language <> 'English')
answer: 793 cards. Three 2017 sets have a non-English set name translation: Aether Revolt (197), Amonkhet (287) and Commander 2017 (309). I used sets.totalSetSize, which includes promo and supplemental printings, rather than baseSetSize.

sql: SELECT e.type, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS members FROM event e JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event=e.event_id WHERE e.event_date >= '2019-09-01' AND e.event_date < '2020-06-01' GROUP BY e.type HAVING members = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a2.link_to_member) c FROM event e2 JOIN attendance a2 ON a2.link_to_event=e2.event_id WHERE e2.event_date >= '2019-09-01' AND e2.event_date < '2020-06-01' GROUP BY e2.type))
answer: Meeting and Registration tie for the most, with 30 members each. I counted distinct members per event type (a member who went to several events of one type counts once), for events from 2019-09-01 through 2020-05-31. The `Event` term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_api_id) AS player_count FROM Player_Attributes WHERE jumping >= 80 AND date >= '2007-02-22' AND date < '2007-08-31'
answer: 654 players had a jumping score of 80 or higher in an assessment from 22 February 2007 to 30 August 2007, both dates included. I counted distinct players, so someone assessed more than once counts once. The date filter uses `date < '2007-08-31'` so all of 30 August is included. The result relies on the `Player Attributes` Term, which is still a draft and not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c JOIN sets s ON s.code = c.setCode WHERE substr(c.originalReleaseDate,1,4) = '2014' AND s.mtgoCode IS NOT NULL AND trim(s.mtgoCode) <> '';
answer: 293 printings. I counted each card row (printing) whose originalReleaseDate falls in 2014 and whose set has a non-empty mtgoCode. I treated NULL and empty-string codes as "no MTGO code". Excluding them or not gives the same result here. Of the 302 printings from 2014, 293 are in MTGO sets.

sql: select d.driverRef,d.nationality,d.dob,q.q1 from qualifying q join races r using(raceId) join drivers d using(driverId) where r.year=1995 and r.name='Japanese Grand Prix' and q.q1 is not null and q.q1<>'' and (cast(substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1) as int)*60+cast(substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,':')+1) as real)) = (select max(cast(substr(q1,1,instr(q1,':')-1) as int)*60+cast(substr(q1,instr(q1,':')+1) as real)) from qualifying q2 join races r2 using(raceId) where r2.year=1995 and r2.name='Japanese Grand Prix' and q1 like '%:%')
answer: Blundell (driverRef 'blundell'), British, born 1966-04-08, Q1 time 16:42.640. Times are stored as text, so I compared them numerically in seconds. Compared as text, this time would wrongly sort as the fastest. The time looks like an anomaly in the data (the next slowest is Gachot at 1:48.289), but it is the slowest recorded Q1 time and only one driver has it.

sql: select count(distinct c.name) from cards c join legalities l on l.uuid=c.uuid where c.manaCost='{0}' and l.format='commander' and l.status='Legal'
answer: 43 different cards (by name) have a printed mana cost of exactly {0} and a Commander legality of Legal. The database has 176 printings (uuids) of these cards. I counted distinct names because you asked for different cards.

sql: select max(cast(frameVersion as integer))-min(cast(frameVersion as integer)) as span_years from cards where name='Tarmogoyf' and frameVersion glob '[0-9]*'
answer: 12 years. Tarmogoyf's frame styles are 2003, 2015 and 'future'. I left out 'future' because it is not a year, so the span is 2015 − 2003 = 12.

sql: select count(distinct r.driverId) from results r join drivers d using(driverId) where r.rank=2 and d.dob>='1976-01-01'
answer: 25 drivers born on or after 1 January 1976 have a results row with rank = 2, which I read as the second-fastest lap of a race. The rank column is only filled in for 2004–2017, so earlier races can't contribute.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(c),2) AS avg_pit_stops FROM (SELECT r.raceId, COUNT(p.stop) c FROM races r LEFT JOIN pitStops p ON p.raceId=r.raceId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name NOT IN (SELECT name FROM races WHERE year=2000) GROUP BY r.raceId)
answer: 39.71 pit stops per race on average. 'Not hosted in 2000' is read as the race name (Grand Prix) having no race in 2000; races without pit stop records would count as 0. The Race and Pit Stop terms are draft (not certified).

sql: select count(*) from superhero s join alignment a on a.id=s.alignment_id where a.alignment='Neutral' and s.full_name is not null and trim(s.full_name)<>'' and s.full_name<>'-'
answer: 16. 이름이 알려진 것으로 본 기준은 full_name이 NULL이 아니고, 빈 문자열이 아니며, '-'(이름 없음을 뜻하는 자리표시값)도 아닌 경우입니다.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT text FROM cards WHERE name = 'Benalish Knight'
answer: Benalish Knight has two distinct rules texts in the database, one per printing: "Flash (You may cast this spell any time you could cast an instant.)" and "First strike (This creature deals combat damage before creatures without first strike.)". The query returns them as two rows, one text per row. I read "one line" as one text per row, not as one combined string.

sql:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT c.Segment AS Segment,
    ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN y.Date LIKE '2013%' THEN y.Consumption END) - SUM(CASE WHEN y.Date LIKE '2012%' THEN y.Consumption END)) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN y.Date LIKE '2012%' THEN y.Consumption END), 2) AS pct
  FROM customers c JOIN yearmonth y ON c.CustomerID = y.CustomerID
  WHERE c.Currency = 'EUR' AND c.Segment IN ('SME','LAM','KAM')
  GROUP BY c.Segment)
SELECT Segment, pct FROM s WHERE pct = (SELECT MAX(pct) FROM s) OR pct = (SELECT MIN(pct) FROM s) ORDER BY pct DESC
answer: Highest: SME at 734.71%. Lowest: LAM at 539.83%. KAM falls between them, and there are no ties. The percentage is (2013 total − 2012 total) / 2012 total × 100, computed on segment totals for EUR customers. The data for 2013 ends at November (201311), while 2012 has all 12 months, and I did not adjust for that. The Terms used (Customer, Monthly Customer Consumption) are draft, not certified.

sql:
with r as (select element from atom group by element having count(distinct molecule_id)=1)
select a.molecule_id, count(distinct c.bond_id) as bond_count
from atom a join r using(element)
join molecule m on m.molecule_id=a.molecule_id and m.label='+'
join connected c on c.atom_id=a.atom_id or c.atom_id2=a.atom_id
group by a.molecule_id order by a.molecule_id
answer: Two carcinogenic molecules qualify: TR430 (6 bonds) and TR499 (1 bond). I called an element rare if it occurs in exactly one molecule across the whole database, carcinogenic or not. The bond count is the number of distinct bonds that touch at least one atom of that element. A bond joining two atoms of the element counts once.

sql:

The Terms used (Laboratory Test, Patient) are drafts, not certified.

sql: select d.nationality from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) where q.raceId=255 and q.q1=(select max(q1) from qualifying where raceId=255 and q1 is not null and q1<>'')

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Player p JOIN (SELECT player_api_id, volleys, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) rn FROM Player_Attributes) a ON a.player_api_id=p.player_api_id AND a.rn=1 WHERE p.height>180 AND a.volleys>70

sql: SELECT p."SEX" AS sex, COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM "Patient" p WHERE p."SEX" IN ('F','M') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "Examination" e WHERE e."ID" = p."ID") GROUP BY p."SEX"
answer: Patients with no Examination row: 962 women (F) and 194 men (M). I read "unknown thrombosis status" as having no Examination row under the patient's ID. I used NOT EXISTS because Examination.ID contains NULLs, which would break NOT IN. I left out 13 such patients whose SEX is blank, since the question asks only about women and men. Including them would add a third row with an empty sex. The Patient Term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT d.driverRef, d.nationality, d.dob FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2<>'' AND (q.q3 IS NULL OR q.q3='')

5 drivers were knocked out in Q2 at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix: perez (Mexican, 1990-01-26), hulkenberg (German, 1987-08-19), alonso (Spanish, 1981-07-29), kvyat (Russian, 1994-04-26) and sainz (Spanish, 1994-09-01).

The Driver, Qualifying Result and Race Terms I used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT expense_date, SUM(cost) AS total_cost FROM expense WHERE expense_date = (SELECT MAX(e.expense_date) FROM expense e JOIN member m ON m.member_id = e.link_to_member WHERE m.position = 'Vice President') GROUP BY expense_date;
answer: 2019-11-19, total cost 128.33. This is the sum of all members' expenses on that date: 62.6 + 59.73 from the Vice President and 6.0 from another member. If only the Vice President's own expenses were meant, the total would be 122.33.

sql:
SELECT CASE WHEN dc > mv THEN 'DC Comics' WHEN mv > dc THEN 'Marvel Comics' ELSE 'Tie' END AS publisher, ABS(dc - mv) AS difference
FROM (SELECT SUM(p.publisher_name = 'DC Comics') AS dc, SUM(p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics') AS mv
      FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id)
answer: Marvel Comics has more superheroes than DC Comics, by 163. The query returns two columns: the winning publisher (or 'Tie') and the absolute difference in hero counts. The tool's fan-out warning does not affect the result, because each hero joins to exactly one publisher. The Publisher term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE isPromo = 1 AND originalReleaseDate LIKE '2019/%' AND layout IN ('split','transform','adventure','flip','aftermath','meld','modal_dfc')
answer:
31 distinct card names, all adventure cards (for example "Decorated Knight // Present Arms", "Bonecrusher Giant // Stomp", "Murderous Rider // Swift End"). The query runs without errors.

Readings I chose:
- Promotional means cards.isPromo = 1.
- "The card's own first-release date" means cards.originalReleaseDate, not sets.releaseDate. That column is stored as text like '2019/12/1' with no zero padding, so I matched the year with LIKE '2019/%'. Only 2,065 of the 56,822 printings have this date filled in, so the question can only be answered for those.
- Multiple faces means layout is split, transform, adventure, flip, aftermath, meld or modal_dfc. Only adventure appears among 2019 promos, so the layout list doesn't change the result.
- DISTINCT collapses repeat promo printings into one row. That is why 32 adventure printings give 31 names.

The `Card` term this uses is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(case when exists(select 1 from foreign_data f where f.uuid=c.uuid and f.language='French') then 1 else 0 end)/count(*),2) from cards c where isStorySpotlight=1

sql: SELECT a.account_id, a.frequency FROM account a JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id WHERE d.A3 = 'east Bohemia' AND a.date >= '1995-01-01' AND a.date < '2001-01-01'

39.71. Seven 2017 races have a Grand Prix name that was not used in 2000. The pitStops table holds 278 stops for them, and 278 / 7 = 39.71. sql:
WITH g AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.account_id FROM disp d JOIN card c ON c.disp_id=d.disp_id WHERE c.type='gold'),
t AS (SELECT account_id,
 SUM(CASE WHEN type='PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS rec,
 SUM(CASE WHEN type IN ('VYDAJ','VYBER') THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS wd,
 COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN bank IS NOT NULL AND account IS NOT NULL THEN bank||'-'||account END) AS cp
 FROM trans GROUP BY account_id),
l AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM loan GROUP BY account_id)
SELECT a.account_id, di.A2 AS district_name, di.A3 AS region,
 COALESCE(t.rec,0) AS total_received, COALESCE(t.wd,0) AS total_withdrawn,
 COALESCE(l.n,0) AS loans_taken, COALESCE(t.cp,0) AS external_counterparties,
 DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(t.cp,0) DESC) AS rank
FROM g JOIN account a ON a.account_id=g.account_id
JOIN district di ON di.district_id=a.district_id
LEFT JOIN t ON t.account_id=a.account_id
LEFT JOIN l ON l.account_id=a.account_id
ORDER BY rank, a.account_id
answer:
The query returns one row per gold-card account, ranked by external counterparties. Tied accounts share a rank and the next rank is not skipped. I only inspected the first 10 rows, because the output was truncated. The top account is 2982 (Prachatice, south Bohemia), with 6 counterparties at rank 1. Accounts 68 and 10411 tie at 5 and share rank 2.

Readings I chose:
- Total received is the sum of `PRIJEM` transactions.
- Total withdrawn is the sum of `VYDAJ` and `VYBER` transactions.
- External counterparties are the distinct (partner bank, partner account) pairs on an account's transactions, covering both sent and received transfers. Rows with no partner are ignored.
- Accounts with no counterparties, loans or transactions show 0.
- All recorded dates are included.

The Terms used are still draft (not certified).

sql: select count(distinct ID) from Laboratory where SSA is not null and trim(SSA) not in ('','0','negative','-') and ID in (select ID from Laboratory where "U-PRO" is not null and trim("U-PRO") not in ('','-','0','negative'))
answer: 15 patients. Abnormal anti-SSA means SSA is recorded and is not 'negative', '0' or '-'. Positive proteinuria means U-PRO is recorded and is not '-', '0' or 'negative'. Blank values count as not tested. Values such as 'TR' (trace) and '-15' count as positive because they are not on the negative list. Each finding is checked across all of a patient's Laboratory rows, so the two don't have to come from the same visit.

sql: SELECT b.bond_type, CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 'YES' ELSE 'NO' END AS carcinogenic FROM bond b INNER JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id WHERE b.molecule_id = 'TR010' GROUP BY b.bond_type, m.label ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
answer: TR010에서 가장 많은 결합 유형은 단일 결합('-')이고, 이 분자는 발암성이 아닙니다(NO). 결합 유형별 개수를 세어 가장 많은 것을 골랐고, 동률은 따로 처리하지 않았습니다. 발암 여부는 molecule.label이 '+'이면 YES, 아니면 NO로 읽었습니다. 사용한 Term(Bond, Molecule)은 아직 승인 전(draft) 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(u.Age), 2) AS avg_age FROM users u WHERE u.Age IS NOT NULL AND u.Id IN (SELECT c.UserId FROM comments c WHERE c.Text LIKE '%http://%' OR c.Text LIKE '%https://%')

sql: select count(distinct ru.text) from rulings ru join cards c on c.uuid=ru.uuid where c.name='Mishra''s Factory' and ru.date=(select max(ru2.date) from rulings ru2 join cards c2 on c2.uuid=ru2.uuid where c2.name='Mishra''s Factory')

sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(COUNT(q.qualifyId) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverId), 2) AS avg_q3_laps FROM drivers d LEFT JOIN qualifying q ON q.driverId = d.driverId AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(q.q3) <> '' WHERE CAST(strftime('%Y', d.dob) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 1981 AND 1991

A Q3 lap time is a qualifying row whose q3 is non-null and non-empty. The Driver and Qualifying Result terms are still draft (not certified).

sql: SELECT d.number FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3<>'' AND q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying q2 WHERE q2.raceId=r.raceId AND q2.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q2.q3<>'')

sql: select count(distinct artist) from cards where borderColor='black' and ','||availability||',' like '%,arena,%' and ','||availability||',' not like '%,mtgo,%' and power glob '[0-9]*' and not power glob '*[^0-9]*' and cast(power as int)>=5 and artist is not null

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id=p.id WHERE s.height_cm>200 AND p.publisher_name<>''

sql: SELECT d.nationality FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2<>'' AND q.q2 = (SELECT MIN(q2.q2) FROM qualifying q2 JOIN races r2 ON r2.raceId=q2.raceId WHERE r2.year=2017 AND r2.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q2.q2<>'')

sql: WITH l AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Date DESC) rn FROM Laboratory) SELECT SUM(p.SEX='F') - SUM(p.SEX='M') AS diff FROM l JOIN Patient p USING(ID) WHERE l.rn=1 AND l.RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) >= 32;
answer: 1. Reading used: a patient's most recent visit is their latest Laboratory row by Date, whether or not it has an RNP value. A visit counts as strongly positive if RNP is numeric and at least 32 (the values are 64 and 256). At that visit 1 female and 0 males are strongly positive, so 1 − 0 = 1. If you meant each patient's latest visit that has an RNP result, the difference would be 11 instead.

sql:

from trans t
where t.account_id = (select account_id from loan where amount=98832 and date='1996-01-03')
and t.type='VYDAJ' and t.date < '1996-01-03'
and t.bank is not null and t.bank<>'' and t.account is not null
group by t.bank, t.account
order by total_paid desc
answer: "98832" is the loan amount, not a loan_id. The loan with that amount approved 1996-01-03 is loan 5999 on account 4907. Before 1996-01-03 that account made VYDAJ payments to 3 counterparties: YZ/25638538 (18 payments, 70884), AB/5604631 (18 payments, 22554) and QR/82890259 (19 payments, 6175). Rows with no partner bank or account were excluded. The Loan and Transaction terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select s.type, count(distinct case when t.id is not null then s.id end) as japanese_name_sets from sets s left join set_translations t on t.setCode=s.code and t.language='Japanese' and t.translation is not null and trim(t.translation)<>'' group by s.type order by s.type
answer: The query returns all 20 expansion types, sorted alphabetically, with the number of sets that have a Japanese name entry. Counts: expansion 41, duel_deck 16, from_the_vault 8, commander 7, core 7, masters 5, box 3, draft_innovation 2, planechase 2, archenemy 1, premium_deck 1. The other 9 types show 0: funny, masterpiece, memorabilia, promo, spellbook, starter, token, treasure_chest, vanguard. I only counted Japanese entries with a non-empty translation, because 28 of the 121 Japanese rows have a NULL translation and give no name. Each set is counted once.

sql: SELECT SUM(Reputation) FROM users WHERE Id IN (SELECT OwnerUserId FROM posts WHERE LasActivityDate >= '2014-08-27' AND LasActivityDate < '2014-08-28' AND Tags LIKE '%<r>%')
answer: The combined reputation is 3773. It covers 22 distinct users who own posts tagged R (tag `<r>`) with a last activity date anywhere in 2014-08-27. I counted each user once, even if they own several matching posts. If you summed per post instead, the total would be 3999, because 3 users own more than one post. Posts with no owner are excluded.

sql: select sum(Score) from posts where Tags like '%<r>%' and Id in (select l.PostId from postLinks l join posts t on t.Id=l.RelatedPostId where t.Title='A Probability distribution value exceeding 1 is OK?')
answer: 22. 'r' 태그가 달린 연결 질문의 점수 합계입니다. 해당 제목의 질문을 가리키는 링크를 건 질문(postLinks.PostId) 중 태그에 정확히 <r>이 있는 질문만 포함했습니다. 같은 질문이 링크 행으로 여러 번 나오는 경우가 있어서, 질문별로 한 번씩만 더했습니다.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics')/count(*),2) from superhero s join gender g on g.id=s.gender_id left join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id where g.gender='Female';
answer: 54.68% (111 of 203 female superheroes are Marvel Comics). The denominator includes all female heroes, even those with no publisher listed.

sql:
SELECT CASE p.Admission WHEN '+' THEN 'admitted to the hospital' ELSE 'followed at the outpatient clinic' END AS care_setting,
 SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>=4) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS patients_with_rnp_at_least_4,
 SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>=4) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS patients_without
FROM Patient p
WHERE p.SEX='F' AND p.Admission IN ('+','-') AND p.Birthday <= '1976-10-09'
GROUP BY care_setting ORDER BY care_setting
answer: Female patients aged 50 or older as of 2026-10-09 (birthday on or before 1976-10-09), admission marker '+' or '-' only. Admitted to the hospital: 10 patients with an anti-RNP result of at least 4, 328 without. Followed at the outpatient clinic: 11 with, 532 without. RNP is a text column, so only numeric values of 4 or more count as elevated. 'negative', 0, 1 and null count as no such result, which includes patients never tested. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
WITH f AS (SELECT s.CDSCode, s.School, s.County FROM schools s WHERE s.Virtual='F'),
c AS (SELECT County, COUNT(*) n FROM f GROUP BY County),
top AS (SELECT County, n FROM c WHERE n >= (SELECT n FROM c ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 4)),
r AS (SELECT f.County, f.School, sa.AvgScrRead a FROM f JOIN satscores sa ON sa.cds=f.CDSCode WHERE sa.AvgScrRead IS NOT NULL),
b AS (SELECT r.County, r.School FROM r WHERE r.a=(SELECT MAX(a) FROM r r2 WHERE r2.County=r.County))
SELECT top.County, top.n, COALESCE(b.School,'None') FROM top LEFT JOIN b ON b.County=top.County ORDER BY top.n DESC, top.County;
answer:
Exclusively virtual schools are those with Virtual='F' in schools (69 in total). The top five counties, with Sacramento and San Bernardino tied for fifth at 5, are:
- Los Angeles: 12 schools; highest reading average is California Virtual Academy @ Los Angeles.
- San Joaquin: 10 schools; highest is California Connections Academy @ Ripon.
- San Diego: 8 schools; 'None'.
- Sacramento: 5 schools; 'None'.
- San Bernardino: 5 schools; 'None'.

I took "reported reading average" to mean a non-null AvgScrRead in satscores, matched to schools by CDSCode. I did not check the SAT rows for San Diego, Sacramento or San Bernardino beyond the query result.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.driverId) FROM results r JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId=r.raceId JOIN status s ON s.statusId=r.statusId WHERE ra.year=1962 AND ra.name='British Grand Prix' AND s.status='Withdrew'
answer: 4. I counted a driver as withdrawn when their result in that race has the status 'Withdrew' (position text 'W'). There are 5 such result rows but 4 distinct drivers, because one driver appears twice. I counted distinct drivers since you asked for drivers. The Terms used (Race, Race Result Status) are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select s.superhero_name, p.publisher_name from superhero s left join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id where s.eye_colour_id=s.hair_colour_id and s.hair_colour_id=s.skin_colour_id and s.eye_colour_id<>1
answer: Four heroes have the same known eye, hair and skin colour: Beast (Marvel Comics), Beast Boy (DC Comics), Hulk (Marvel Comics) and Purple Man (Marvel Comics). I read "known" as excluding colour id 1, "No Colour", which marks unknown values. Without that filter, 159 heroes match. I used a left join so a hero with no publisher would still appear, but none of the four lacks one.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hp.power_id) FROM hero_power hp JOIN superhero s ON s.id = hp.hero_id JOIN gender g ON g.id = s.gender_id WHERE g.gender = 'Male' AND s.weight_kg > 0 AND s.weight_kg < 70
answer: 102 different superpowers are held by at least one male hero under 70 kg. The docs say a weight_kg of NULL or 0 means the weight is missing, so I excluded those heroes. Counting weight 0 as under 70 would have given 139.

sql:
WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT department FROM major WHERE college='College of Humanities and Social Sciences' AND department IS NOT NULL),
mm AS (SELECT m.department, m.major_id, m.major_name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM member x WHERE x.link_to_major=m.major_id) AS n FROM major m JOIN d ON d.department=m.department)
SELECT department AS department_name,
 group_concat(major_name, ', ') AS majors_offered,
 group_concat(CASE WHEN n>0 THEN major_name END, ', ') AS majors_held_by_members,
 ROUND(1.0*SUM(n)/COUNT(*),2) AS avg_members_per_major
FROM (SELECT * FROM mm ORDER BY department, major_name)
GROUP BY department ORDER BY department
answer: 11 departments qualify. Members hold majors in only 3 of them: Languages, Philosophy and Communication Studies (Chinese, Communication Studies, Portuguese; 0.38 members per major offered), Liberal Arts (Liberal Arts; 1.00), and Political Science (International Studies, Law and Constitutional Studies; 1.00). The other 8 have no member majors and an average of 0.00 (majors held shows NULL). Assumptions: a department counts if any of its majors is in the college, and "majors offered" means all of that department's majors. The average is the department's total members divided by the number of majors it offers, including majors with no members. The Major Term is a draft (not certified).

sql: select round(avg(coalesce(s.NumTstTakr,0)),2) from schools c left join satscores s on s.cds=c.CDSCode where c.County='Los Angeles' and c.OpenDate>='2007-01-01' and c.OpenDate<'2008-01-01' and c.School is not null and c.DOC in ('00','52','54','56')
answer: 14.57 SAT test takers per school on average. This covers 47 Los Angeles County school records opened in 2007 and run by a school district. I counted districts as DOC 52, 54 and 56, plus 00 for county offices of education, which matches no school here. I excluded district-office rows, and schools with no SAT record count as 0. The State Board of Education school (DOC 02) is excluded because it is not run by a district.

sql:
SELECT r.date, d.forename, d.surname,
 (f.ms/60000) || ':' || printf('%02d', (f.ms%60000)/1000) || '.' || printf('%03d', f.ms%1000) AS fastest_lap
FROM races r
LEFT JOIN (SELECT raceId, driverId, MIN(milliseconds) AS ms FROM lapTimes GROUP BY raceId, driverId HAVING MIN(milliseconds) > 90000) f ON f.raceId = r.raceId
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = f.driverId
WHERE r.name = 'French Grand Prix' AND r.date >= '1990-01-01'
ORDER BY r.date, d.surname, d.forename
answer:
1990년부터 2008년(마지막 프랑스 그랑프리)까지 20개 대회가 나왔고, 기준을 넘긴 드라이버는 2007-07-01 대회의 두 명뿐입니다. Anthony Davidson은 1:44.767, Jarno Trulli는 2:19.632입니다. 나머지 18개 대회는 날짜만 표시하고 드라이버와 랩타임은 비워 두었습니다.

적용한 해석은 다음과 같습니다.
- 드라이버의 '그 대회 최고 랩'은 lapTimes에서 그 드라이버의 가장 짧은 랩타임으로 보고, 그 값이 90초(90,000ms)보다 느린 경우만 포함했습니다.
- 1996년 이전 대회는 lapTimes 기록이 없는 것으로 보이며, 이 쿼리에서는 해당 드라이버가 없는 대회와 똑같이 날짜만 나옵니다.
- Trulli의 2:19.632는 데이터에 있는 값을 그대로 쓴 것이고, 따로 검증하지는 않았습니다.
- 사용한 Term(Race, Lap Time, Driver)은 아직 인증되지 않은 draft 상태입니다.

sql: select min(cast(strftime('%Y',L.Date) as int)-cast(strftime('%Y',P.Birthday) as int)) as youngest_age from Laboratory L join Patient P on P.ID=L.ID where L.RNP glob '[0-9]*' and cast(L.RNP as real)>=64
answer: 18. RNP is stored as text, so I kept only numeric values and compared them as numbers. The values 64 and 256 meet the threshold, and 'negative' is excluded. Age is the test year minus the birth year, as you defined it.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(Consumption),2) AS avg_monthly_consumption FROM yearmonth WHERE CustomerID=15621 AND Date LIKE '2013%' AND Consumption>0
answer: 고객 15621의 2013년 월평균 연료 소비량은 6.02입니다. 소비량이 0보다 큰 3개월(2013년 6월 3.5, 7월 12.91, 10월 1.65)만 평균했습니다. 소비량이 0인 달(4월, 5월, 9월)은 연료를 구매하지 않은 달로 보고 제외했고, 8월은 기록 자체가 없습니다. 월별 소비량은 yearmonth 테이블의 Consumption 값을 썼습니다. 이 테이블은 카드 종류를 구분하지 않으므로 '플릿 카드' 조건은 따로 적용하지 못했습니다. 연료 구매만 따로 구분한 값도 아니고, 고객의 월별 총 소비량입니다. 이 값이 속한 Monthly Customer Consumption 용어는 아직 인증되지 않은 초안 상태입니다.

sql: select 100.0*(sum(case when strftime('%Y',l.date)='1997' then amount end)-sum(case when strftime('%Y',l.date)='1996' then amount end))/sum(case when strftime('%Y',l.date)='1996' then amount end) as growth_pct from loan l join disp d on d.account_id=l.account_id and d.type='OWNER' join client c on c.client_id=d.client_id where c.gender='M' and strftime('%Y',l.date) in ('1996','1997')
answer: 약 25.30%입니다. 남성 고객이 소유(OWNER)한 계좌의 대출 총액은 1996년에서 1997년 사이에 25.30% 늘었습니다. '계좌 소유'는 disp.type = 'OWNER'인 경우로 해석했고, DISPONENT는 제외했습니다.

sql:
with l as (select f.CDSCode, f."Enrollment (K-12)"-f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" d from frpm f where f."Charter Funding Type"='Locally funded' and f."Enrollment (K-12)" is not null and f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" is not null)
select s.School, s.DOCType from l join schools s using(CDSCode) where d>(select avg(d) from l);
answer: The query returns 49 schools. I used frpm."Charter Funding Type" = 'Locally funded', because the enrollment difference comes from frpm. The difference is Enrollment (K-12) minus Enrollment (Ages 5-17). The average is taken over locally funded rows where both enrollment values are present. School name and DOCType come from the schools directory.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(SEX='F')/COUNT(*),2) AS female_percentage FROM Patient p WHERE Birthday IS NOT NULL AND (strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',Birthday)-(strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09')<strftime('%m-%d',Birthday)))>55 AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.PT>=14)
answer: 72.73% (8 of 11 patients). I treated PT as abnormal when it is 14 or higher, because the docs give the normal range as PT < 14. Using > 14 gives the same result. Age is the full age on 2026-10-09, counting birthdays, and patients with no birthday are excluded. Each patient is counted once even if several lab rows qualify.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.position IS NOT NULL THEN r.driverId END) / COUNT(DISTINCT r.driverId), 2) AS finisher_pct FROM results r JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId = r.raceId WHERE ra.year = 1957 AND ra.name = 'British Grand Prix'
answer: 52.63%. 19명의 드라이버 중 10명이 완주했습니다. 완주는 순위(position)가 기록된 경우로 보았으며, 선두와 같은 랩인 경우와 랩 차가 난 경우를 모두 포함합니다. 분모는 중복을 뺀 드라이버 수입니다. 차를 공유한 드라이버는 한 명으로 계산했고, 출전하지 않은 'W' 기록 1건도 분모에 포함했습니다. 결과 행 22개를 기준으로 하면 45.45%입니다.

sql: select e.Symptoms from Examination e join Patient p on p.ID=e.ID where e.Thrombosis>0 and e.Symptoms is not null and p.Diagnosis like '%SLE%' group by e.Symptoms order by count(*) desc, e.Symptoms limit 1
answer: CNS lupus (2 episodes). Assumptions: a thrombotic episode is an Examination row with Thrombosis > 0, and rows with no recorded symptom are skipped. A patient counts as SLE if Patient.Diagnosis contains 'SLE', which includes 'SLE susp'. The five matching rows each have a Patient.Diagnosis of exactly 'SLE', so this choice doesn't change the result.

sql: SELECT SUM(u.Reputation) AS total_reputation FROM users u WHERE u.Location LIKE '%United Kingdom%' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM posts p WHERE p.OwnerUserId = u.Id)
answer: The combined reputation is 87,153. It covers users whose Location contains "United Kingdom" (including entries like "London, United Kingdom") and who own at least one post, with each user counted once. Abbreviations such as "UK" were not matched. The ontology's User term is still a draft.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) FROM cards WHERE ','||promoTypes||',' LIKE '%,release,%'
answer: 54 different cards (by card name) have a printing with the 'release' promo type. I matched 'release' as a whole comma-separated value, so 'prerelease' is excluded. Those 54 cards have 58 printings in total. If you meant counting each printing as a separate card, the answer would be 58.

sql: select count(distinct ID) from Examination where Thrombosis>0 and [Examination Date] between '1997-01-01' and '1997-12-31'
answer: 3 patients. I counted any Thrombosis value of 1, 2 or 3 (positive) as thrombosis, with exam dates from 1997-01-01 to 1997-12-31 inclusive. Each patient is counted once.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT d.nationality FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM qualifying q2 WHERE q2.raceId=q.raceId AND q2.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q2.q3<>'')
answer: British. One driver set the fastest Q3 time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, so there was no tie. I took "fastest" as the lowest Q3 time among drivers who set one. The Driver, Qualifying Result and Race Terms the query uses are drafts, not certified.

sql: select language, count(*) as printings from foreign_data where language not in ('Ancient Greek','Arabic','Hebrew','Latin','Sanskrit','Phyrexian') group by language having count(*) = (select min(c) from (select count(*) c from foreign_data where language not in ('Ancient Greek','Arabic','Hebrew','Latin','Sanskrit','Phyrexian') group by language))
answer: Korean has the fewest foreign printings, with 9,692 rows in foreign_data. I counted each foreign_data row as one printing. I treated Ancient Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Latin and Sanskrit (1 each) and Phyrexian (3) as one-off promo or gimmick languages and excluded them. There is no tie among the remaining languages.

sql: select d.A2 as district, l.amount, l.date, (select t.balance from trans t where t.account_id=l.account_id and t.date<=l.date order by t.date desc, t.trans_id desc limit 1) as balance from loan l join account a on a.account_id=l.account_id join district d on d.district_id=a.district_id where l.duration=24 and a.frequency='POPLATEK TYDNE' order by l.amount desc, l.date asc limit 10
answer:
The query returns the ten largest 24-month loans on weekly-statement accounts (frequency 'POPLATEK TYDNE'). Each row has the branch district name (district.A2), the approved amount, the approval date and the balance. The largest is Strakonice at 192,552, approved 1994-11-12, with a balance of 14,203.

Ties on amount are broken by the earlier approval date. The balance is the one on the account's last transaction on or before the approval date, and the higher trans_id wins when several transactions share that date. I chose "on or before" because 6 of the 10 loans have no transaction on their approval day. For those, the balance is the carried-forward balance from the most recent earlier transaction.

sql: select sum(case when k_symbol='UROK' then amount when k_symbol='SANKC. UROK' then -amount end) as net_interest from trans where account_id=(select account_id from disp where client_id=2823) and date>='1998-01-01' and date<='1998-12-31' and k_symbol in ('UROK','SANKC. UROK')
answer: Net interest for 1998 on client 2823's account (account 2335) is -505 CZK: interest credited (UROK) minus penalty interest (SANKC. UROK). I read "client 2823" as client_id 2823. The client has a single disposition (OWNER), so the query selects the account through it and no rows are double-counted. The Transaction and Disposition Terms are still draft.

sql:
SELECT s.School, s.District, s.County, t.AvgScrWrite
FROM satscores t
JOIN schools s ON t.cds = s.CDSCode
WHERE s.StatusType = 'Closed' AND t.rtype = 'S' AND t.AvgScrWrite IS NOT NULL
AND t.AvgScrWrite = (SELECT MAX(t2.AvgScrWrite) FROM satscores t2 JOIN schools s2 ON t2.cds = s2.CDSCode
  WHERE s2.StatusType = 'Closed' AND t2.rtype = 'S' AND t2.AvgScrWrite IS NOT NULL
  AND t2.AvgScrWrite < (SELECT MAX(t3.AvgScrWrite) FROM satscores t3 JOIN schools s3 ON t3.cds = s3.CDSCode
    WHERE s3.StatusType = 'Closed' AND t3.rtype = 'S' AND t3.AvgScrWrite IS NOT NULL))
answer: The closed school with the second-highest average SAT writing score is FAME Public Charter (district: Alameda County Office of Education, county: Alameda), with a score of 505. No other closed school has that score. I took the district and county from the schools table (the school's own record) and used only school-level SAT rows (rtype = 'S'). The SAT Score Record and School Terms I relied on are still drafts.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(u.Reputation)) AS avg_reputation FROM posts p JOIN users u ON u.Id = p.OwnerUserId WHERE p.Tags LIKE '%<r>%' AND p.Score < 20;
answer: 499. 이 값은 태그가 정확히 `<r>`이고 점수가 20 미만인 게시글 7,000건을 작성자와 연결해 계산한 평균 평점입니다. 한 작성자가 여러 게시글을 쓰면 그 수만큼 반영됩니다. 다른 방식으로 작성자 3,892명을 한 번씩만 세면 평균은 214입니다. 이 질문은 게시글 기준으로 해석했습니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg),2) FROM superhero s WHERE s.publisher_id=(SELECT id FROM publisher WHERE publisher_name='George Lucas') AND s.weight_kg>0 AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM hero_power h WHERE h.hero_id=s.id)
answer: 77.40 kg. This averages 5 George Lucas heroes that have at least one superpower and a recorded weight. I treated weight_kg of 0 or NULL as not recorded, following the docs.

sql: select count(distinct coalesce('u'||p.OwnerUserId,'n'||p.OwnerDisplayName)) from votes v join posts p on p.Id=v.PostId where v.BountyAmount>=30 and v.CreationDate>='2010-01-01' and v.CreationDate<'2011-01-01' and (p.OwnerUserId is not null or p.OwnerDisplayName is not null)
answer: 32 users. I counted the post owner as the bounty offerer, using the owner account (OwnerUserId) where one is recorded and the owner display name otherwise. I counted distinct owners across votes with BountyAmount >= 30 and a CreationDate in 2010. I skipped posts with no owner recorded at all.

sql: SELECT SUM(Reputation) FROM users WHERE Id IN (SELECT OwnerUserId FROM posts WHERE Score = 10 AND Tags LIKE '%<r>%')
answer: 50863. I matched the exact tag `<r>` in posts.Tags, so tags like `<random-forest>` don't count. Each user is counted once, even if they own several qualifying posts. The query covers 43 distinct users across 46 posts. If you counted a user once per post, the total would be 75563.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.CustomerID) FROM customers c JOIN yearmonth y ON y.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE c.Segment = 'SME' AND y.Date = '201302' AND y.Consumption > 0
answer: 1518 SME customers purchased gas in February 2013. I counted SME customers with positive Consumption in yearmonth for '201302', because the transactions table is only a sample from August 2012. The Customer and Monthly Customer Consumption terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 2) FROM superhero s JOIN hero_attribute ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id WHERE ha.attribute_id = 1 AND ha.attribute_value = 85 AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: The average weight is 103.6 kg. Abomination's Intelligence is 85, and 111 heroes with Intelligence 85 have a recorded weight. I excluded weights of 0 or NULL because the docs treat them as missing. The cohort includes Abomination himself.

sql: select c.Street, c.City, c.Zip, c.State from satscores s join schools c on c.CDSCode=s.cds where s.rtype='S' and s.NumTstTakr>=700 order by 1.0*s.NumGE1500/s.NumTstTakr, s.cds limit 1
answer: 10535 Zelzah Avenue, Granada Hills, CA 91344-5902. I defined the excellence rate as NumGE1500 / NumTstTakr, which is the share of test takers scoring at least 1500. I kept only school rows (rtype='S'), because district rows also appear in the SAT table and would have been returned instead. Ties are broken by the smallest school code. Only one school is returned (LIMIT 1).

sql: select s.superhero_name, nullif(p.publisher_name,'') as publisher_name from superhero s left join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id where s.eye_colour_id=s.hair_colour_id and s.hair_colour_id=s.skin_colour_id and s.eye_colour_id<>1
answer: 4개 히어로가 해당합니다. Beast(Marvel Comics), Beast Boy(DC Comics), Hulk(Marvel Comics), Purple Man(Marvel Comics)입니다. 눈, 머리, 피부 색이 모두 같고 'No Colour'(id 1, 색 미상)가 아닌 경우만 '알려진 색'으로 보았습니다. 이 조건을 빼면 세 색이 모두 미상인 히어로가 섞여 들어옵니다. 출판사는 LEFT JOIN으로 붙였고, 출판사 정보가 없거나 빈 문자열(id 1)이면 NULL로 표시합니다. 이번 결과에는 그런 경우가 없습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.SEX='F' THEN p.ID END) AS F, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.SEX='M' THEN p.ID END) AS M FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID WHERE l.Date>='1994-01-01' AND l.Date<='1994-12-31' AND l.GOT<60
answer: F: 80, M: 16. I treated "normal" GOT as below 60, which is the wiki's reference cutoff. Each patient is counted once if any 1994 test had GOT < 60. Patients with no sex recorded are left out.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT u.Id) FROM users u JOIN badges b ON b.UserId = u.Id WHERE b.Name = 'Yearling' AND b.Date < '2014-01-01' AND u.Location LIKE '%India%' AND u.Location NOT LIKE '%Indiana%' AND u.Location NOT LIKE '%Indianapolis%'
