sql: select round(avg(weight_kg),2) from superhero where id != (select id from superhero where superhero_name='3-D Man') and weight_kg > 0 and id in (select hero_id from hero_power where power_id in (select power_id from hero_power where hero_id=(select id from superhero where superhero_name='3-D Man')));
answer: 282411.79 kg. I treated weight 0 as missing, because docs/superhero.csv says NULL or 0 both mean the weight is missing. I excluded those heroes along with NULLs. The average is pulled up by a few extreme weights recorded in the data, such as Godzilla at 90,000,000 kg. I left them in.

sql:
WITH s AS (SELECT CDSCode, substr(CDSCode,1,7) dc, AdmFName1 a1, AdmFName2 a2, AdmFName3 a3 FROM schools WHERE County IN ('Amador','Madera') AND School IS NOT NULL),
n AS (SELECT CDSCode, a1 fn FROM s UNION SELECT CDSCode, a2 FROM s UNION SELECT CDSCode, a3 FROM s),
top AS (SELECT fn, COUNT(DISTINCT CDSCode) c FROM n WHERE fn IS NOT NULL GROUP BY fn ORDER BY c DESC, fn LIMIT 2),
d AS (SELECT substr(CDSCode,1,7) dc, MIN(District) District FROM schools WHERE County IN ('Amador','Madera') AND DOC IN ('00','52','54','56') GROUP BY 1)
SELECT d.District, top.fn, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT n.CDSCode) FROM n JOIN s ON s.CDSCode=n.CDSCode WHERE s.dc=d.dc AND n.fn=top.fn) cnt
FROM d CROSS JOIN top ORDER BY d.District, top.fn;
answer:
The two names are Stacy (8 schools) and Avetik (4 schools). Avetik, Gary and Kuljeet each run 4 schools, so the alphabetical tiebreak puts Avetik second. The query returns 50 rows, one for each of 25 public districts and each of the two names. Nearly all counts are 0. Stacy runs 8 schools in Yosemite Unified, and Avetik runs 4 in Madera County Office of Education.

How I read the question:
- Schools are `schools` rows with a non-null `School` in Amador or Madera. This includes closed schools, though only active schools have administrator names.
- All three administrator first-name slots count, and each school counts once per name.
- A public district is a district whose `DOC` code is 00 (county office), 52 (elementary), 54 (unified) or 56 (high school). Schools are assigned to districts by the first 7 digits of `CDSCode`.

sql: select count(distinct c.uuid) from cards c join foreign_data f on f.uuid=c.uuid where c.setCode='CSP' and f.language='Italian' and f.text is not null and trim(f.text)<>''
answer: 149 printings in Coldsnap (set code CSP) have Italian rules text. I read "Coldsnap" as the main set only, so Theme Decks and Promos are excluded. A printing counts only if its Italian entry has non-empty text.

sql: select cast(frameVersion as int) as frame_year, count(*) as card_count from cards where leadershipSkills like '%''commander'': True%' and cardKingdomFoilId is not null and cardKingdomId is not null and frameVersion glob '[0-9]*' and frameVersion=(select max(frameVersion) from cards where leadershipSkills like '%''commander'': True%' and cardKingdomFoilId is not null and cardKingdomId is not null and frameVersion glob '[0-9]*') group by 1
answer: 2015 | 820. Choices I made: "Commander-leadable" means leadershipSkills has commander: True. "Listed for both foil and non-foil" means both cardKingdomFoilId and cardKingdomId are non-null. The frameVersion value 'future' isn't a calendar year, so I excluded it. A "card" is one row (one printing) in cards.

sql: SELECT p.publisher_name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p1 ON s.publisher_id=p1.id WHERE p1.publisher_name='Marvel Comics') - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p2 ON s.publisher_id=p2.id WHERE p2.publisher_name='DC Comics') AS difference FROM publisher p WHERE p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics'
answer: Marvel Comics has more superheroes than DC Comics, by 163. I counted rows in superhero joined to publisher by name. The query hardcodes Marvel as the leader; the positive difference confirms it.

sql: SELECT SUM(cr.points) AS points, c.name, c.nationality FROM constructorResults cr JOIN races r ON r.raceId=cr.raceId JOIN constructors c ON c.constructorId=cr.constructorId WHERE r.name='Monaco Grand Prix' AND r.year BETWEEN 1980 AND 2010 GROUP BY c.constructorId ORDER BY points DESC LIMIT 1
answer: McLaren (British) scored the most points at the Monaco Grand Prix between 1980 and 2010, with 218.5 points. I counted 1980 and 2010 as included and summed the constructors' race points over all Monaco Grand Prix races in those years. The Terms used (Constructor, Constructor Race Result, Race) are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(c), 2) AS avg_attendance FROM (SELECT e.event_id, COUNT(a.link_to_member) AS c FROM event e LEFT JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.event_id IN (SELECT link_to_event FROM budget WHERE category = 'Advertisement') GROUP BY e.event_id)
answer: 12.53. The 15 events with an 'Advertisement' budget line averaged 12.53 attending members per event, across all dates. I counted events with no attendance rows as 0 attendees, because the question covers every such event. If you only count events that have at least one attendance record, the average is 26.86.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT m.first_name, m.last_name, m.phone FROM expense e INNER JOIN member m ON e.link_to_member = m.member_id WHERE e.cost > (SELECT AVG(cost) FROM expense)
answer: Three members have at least one expense above the overall average expense cost: Sacha Harrison (840-555-4781), Phillip Cullen (905-555-5035) and Elijah Allen (724-555-5721). The average is taken over all rows in the expense table, including the one unapproved expense. Each member appears once. The Expense and Member Terms used are drafts, not certified.

sql: select CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name='Yearly Kickoff' THEN b.amount END) AS REAL)/SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name='October Meeting' THEN b.amount END) from budget b join event e on e.event_id=b.link_to_event where b.category='Advertisement'
answer: The ratio is about 2.727. The Yearly Kickoff Advertisement budget is 150 and the October Meeting's is 55. I matched the event names exactly, so 'October Speaker' is not counted as the October Meeting.

sql: select distinct m.first_name, m.last_name, m.phone from member m join expense e on e.link_to_member=m.member_id where e.cost > (select avg(cost) from expense)
answer: Three members have at least one expense above the average cost across all 32 expense rows: Sacha Harrison (840-555-4781), Phillip Cullen (905-555-5035) and Elijah Allen (724-555-5721). I took "overall average" to mean the average over every expense, approved or not. The query uses DISTINCT so each member appears once.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(u.UpVotes),2) AS avg_upvotes, ROUND(AVG(u.Age),2) AS avg_age FROM users u JOIN (SELECT OwnerUserId FROM posts WHERE CreaionDate >= '2012-01-01' AND CreaionDate < '2013-01-01' GROUP BY OwnerUserId HAVING COUNT(*) > 10) p ON u.Id = p.OwnerUserId
answer: Users with more than ten posts created in 2012 cast an average of 505.63 up-votes and have an average age of 36.14. Posts of all types (questions and answers) were counted by OwnerUserId, using the post creation date. AVG(Age) skips users whose age is null. The User and Post Terms are still draft (not certified).

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(weight_kg), 2) FROM superhero WHERE gender_id = 2 AND alignment_id = 1 AND weight_kg > 0
answer: 좋은 성향의 여성 슈퍼히어로 평균 체중은 70.76kg입니다. 체중이 기록된 116명 기준입니다. docs에 weight_kg가 NULL 또는 0이면 체중이 없는 것으로 적혀 있어서 0도 제외했습니다. 0을 포함하면 평균이 55.46kg으로 낮아집니다.

sql: select count(*) from Laboratory l where Date=(select min(Date) from Laboratory where ID=l.ID) and GOT<60 and RNP glob '[0-9]*' and CAST(RNP AS REAL)>10
answer: 6 patients. For each patient I took the laboratory record with the earliest Date and kept it if GOT < 60 and RNP > 10. RNP is stored as text, so I compared only numeric values. Non-numeric values such as "negative" do not count as elevated. A patient whose first record has a null GOT or RNP is not counted.

sql: SELECT s.code, s.releaseDate FROM sets s WHERE s.releaseDate >= '2020-01-01' AND s.releaseDate < '2021-01-01' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.language = 'Spanish' AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND t.translation <> '') ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.code
answer: 34 sets released in 2020 have no Spanish name, for example THB (2020-01-24), M21 (2020-07-03), ZNR (2020-09-25) and CC1 (2020-12-04). I read "no Spanish name" as no Spanish translation row, or one whose translation is null or empty. I counted 2020 as release dates from 2020-01-01 up to, but not including, 2021-01-01. The Card Set and Set Translation terms used are drafts, not certified.

sql: select c.name, count(distinct r.date||'|'||r.text) n from cards c join rulings r on r.uuid=c.uuid where c.originalType='Creature - Elf' group by c.name having n=(select max(n) from (select count(distinct r.date||'|'||r.text) n from cards c join rulings r on r.uuid=c.uuid where c.originalType='Creature - Elf' group by c.name))
answer: Gempalm Strider has the most rulings of any card with original type 'Creature - Elf', with 4. I grouped printings by card name. The same ruling is stored once per printing, so I counted distinct (date, text) pairs. Counting raw rows would give 8 for Gempalm Strider. No other card ties: the next ones have 2.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) FROM cards c INNER JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.borderColor = 'white' AND l.status = 'Banned'
answer: 89 distinct white-bordered card printings (distinct cards.uuid) are banned in at least one format. I read "printing" as one row in cards, and "banned" as legalities.status = 'Banned' (Restricted is not counted). The Card and Card Legality terms used are still drafts in the ontology.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(a.alignment='Good')/count(*),2) as good_percentage from superhero s join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id left join alignment a on a.id=s.alignment_id where p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics' and s.full_name is not null;
answer: 64.20% of Marvel Comics superheroes with a known full name are Good. Heroes with a NULL full_name are excluded. Heroes whose alignment is unknown stay in the total but don't count as good. 324 heroes have a full name, out of 387 Marvel heroes in all.

sql:
WITH s AS (
SELECT c.Segment seg,
 SUM(CASE WHEN substr(y.Date,1,4)='2012' THEN y.Consumption END) a,
 SUM(CASE WHEN substr(y.Date,1,4)='2013' THEN y.Consumption END) b
FROM yearmonth y JOIN customers c USING(CustomerID)
WHERE c.Currency='EUR' AND c.Segment IN ('SME','LAM','KAM') GROUP BY c.Segment),
p AS (SELECT seg, ROUND((b-a)*100.0/a,2) pct FROM s)
SELECT seg AS Segment, pct AS IncreasePct FROM p
WHERE pct=(SELECT MAX(pct) FROM p) OR pct=(SELECT MIN(pct) FROM p);
answer: SME had the highest increase at 734.71%, and LAM had the lowest at 539.83%. KAM fell in between. I summed Consumption per calendar year (2012 vs 2013) over EUR customers and computed (2013−2012)/2012×100. The yearmonth table has no rows for 201210–201212, and 2013 only runs through November, so 2012 and 2013 do not cover the same months. That likely inflates the percentages.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(alignment_id = 1) / COUNT(*), 2) AS good_pct FROM superhero WHERE publisher_id = (SELECT id FROM publisher WHERE publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics') AND full_name IS NOT NULL AND full_name <> '-'
answer: 68.27% of Marvel Comics heroes with a known full name are good. I treated NULL and the placeholder '-' (53 Marvel rows) as "not documented" and excluded them, which leaves 271 heroes. Heroes with unknown (N/A) alignment stay in the total but don't count as good. If '-' counted as a known name, the base would be 324 heroes and the figure would change.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_api_id) FROM Player_Attributes WHERE jumping >= 80 AND date >= '2007-02-22' AND date < '2007-08-31'
answer: 654 distinct players had a jumping score of 80 or higher in assessments from 2007-02-22 to 2007-08-30 inclusive. I counted distinct players, since the question asks how many players. Counting assessment rows instead gives 1049. Dates are stored as timestamps, so the query uses `date < '2007-08-31'` to include all of 30 August.

sql:
SELECT ROUND((MAX(CASE WHEN r.raceId=853 THEN CAST(r.fastestLapSpeed AS REAL) END) - MAX(CASE WHEN r.raceId=854 THEN CAST(r.fastestLapSpeed AS REAL) END)) * 100.0 / MAX(CASE WHEN r.raceId=854 THEN CAST(r.fastestLapSpeed AS REAL) END), 2) AS pct_higher
FROM results r JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=r.driverId
WHERE d.forename='Paul' AND d.surname='di Resta' AND r.raceId IN (853,854)
answer: Paul di Resta's fastest-lap speed in race 853 was 48.15% higher than in race 854, with race 854 as the baseline. I read "race 853" and "race 854" as raceId values and cast the text column fastestLapSpeed to a number. The Driver and Race Result terms used are still drafts in the ontology, not certified.

sql:
WITH d AS (
  SELECT di.district_id, di.A3 AS region, CAST(di.A4 AS INTEGER) AS pop, COUNT(*) AS n_acc
  FROM loan l
  JOIN account a ON l.account_id = a.account_id
  JOIN district di ON a.district_id = di.district_id
  WHERE l.duration > 24 AND l.date < '1997-01-01'
  GROUP BY di.district_id, di.A3, di.A4
)
SELECT region, COUNT(*) AS num_districts, SUM(pop) AS total_inhabitants, SUM(n_acc) AS num_accounts
FROM d GROUP BY region
ORDER BY total_inhabitants DESC, region ASC
LIMIT 1
answer: South Moravia has the largest combined population among regions with qualifying districts: 13 districts, 1,947,078 inhabitants, 40 accounts. I read "opened before 1997" as loan approval date < 1997-01-01 and "long-term" as duration > 24 months. Each account has at most one loan, so accounts are counted once each. District population is stored as text and is cast to integer. Ties would go to the alphabetically first region. The Loan, Account and District terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT cardKingdomFoilId, cardKingdomId FROM cards WHERE cardKingdomFoilId IS NOT NULL AND cardKingdomId IS NOT NULL AND types LIKE '%Creature%' ORDER BY CAST(cardKingdomFoilId AS INTEGER), CAST(cardKingdomId AS INTEGER) LIMIT 3
answer: The three creature cards with the lowest Card Kingdom Foil ids are 39001/38001, 39002/38002 and 39003/38003 (foil id/Card Kingdom id). I counted a card as a creature if its types include "Creature", which also covers Artifact Creature. "Present" means the id is not NULL, and no id is an empty string. The ids are stored as text with 5 or 6 digits, so I sorted them as numbers, which keeps the lowest ids first. I read "alphabetical order" as ordering by id, with the Card Kingdom id breaking ties, and I did not sort by card name.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT superhero.superhero_name FROM superhero INNER JOIN hero_power ON superhero.id = hero_power.hero_id INNER JOIN superpower ON hero_power.power_id = superpower.id INNER JOIN publisher ON superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id WHERE publisher.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND superpower.power_name = 'Super Strength'
answer: Marvel Comics has 200 superheroes with the 'Super Strength' power, for example 3-D Man, A-Bomb, Abomination, Hulk, Thor and Wolverine. The query returns only superhero_name, one row per hero (DISTINCT). I read "from Marvel Comics" as publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics'. The Superhero, Superpower and Publisher terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT pa.player_api_id, pa.preferred_foot, pa.attacking_work_rate, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pa.player_api_id ORDER BY pa.date DESC, pa.id DESC) rn FROM Player_Attributes pa WHERE pa.date <= '2015-01-01 23:59:59') t WHERE rn=1 AND preferred_foot='left' AND attacking_work_rate IN ('low','medium')
answer: 1,795 players. I took each player's most recent rating snapshot dated on or before 1 January 2015, then counted those whose preferred_foot is 'left' and whose attacking_work_rate is 'low' or 'medium'. Players with no snapshot by that date are left out, and so are rows with dirty or NULL work-rate values. The Player Attributes Term is still a draft, not certified.

sql: with m as (select player_api_id, max(date) d from Player_Attributes group by 1) select round(avg(p.height),2) from Player p join m on m.player_api_id=p.player_api_id join Player_Attributes a on a.player_api_id=m.player_api_id and a.date=m.d where a.defensive_work_rate in ('low','high')
answer: 180.95 cm (2,596 players). I took each player's latest rating by max date. I read "not medium" as a grade of low or high, so I left out junk values (digits, 'o', 'ormal') and nulls, which aren't valid grades.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "Laboratory" l WHERE l."Date" = (SELECT MIN("Date") FROM "Laboratory" WHERE "ID"=l."ID") AND l."GOT" < 60 AND CAST(l."RNP" AS REAL) > 10
answer: 6명입니다. 환자별로 검사일이 가장 이른 검사 기록에서 GOT가 60 미만이고 RNP가 10 초과인 환자를 셌습니다. RNP는 텍스트 열이라 숫자로 바꿔 비교했고, 'negative'나 빈 값은 제외됩니다.

sql:
WITH r AS (SELECT element FROM atom GROUP BY element HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id)=1)
SELECT a.molecule_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS bond_count
FROM atom a JOIN r ON r.element=a.element
JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id=a.molecule_id AND m.label='+'
JOIN connected c ON c.atom_id=a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2=a.atom_id
GROUP BY a.molecule_id ORDER BY a.molecule_id;
answer: 두 분자가 해당합니다: TR430은 결합 6개, TR499는 결합 1개입니다. 희귀 원소는 데이터베이스 전체(발암 여부와 무관)에서 원자가 단 하나의 분자에만 나타나는 원소로 보았습니다. 발암 분자는 label='+'로 판단했습니다. 결합 수는 그 원소 원자가 참여한 서로 다른 bond_id의 개수이며, 한 분자에서 같은 결합을 두 번 세지 않습니다.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT l.ID, l.RNP FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE strftime('%Y',p.`First Date`)='1991' AND l.RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(l.RNP AS INT)=(SELECT MAX(CAST(l2.RNP AS INT)) FROM Laboratory l2 JOIN Patient p2 ON p2.ID=l2.ID WHERE strftime('%Y',p2.`First Date`)='1991' AND l2.RNP GLOB '[0-9]*')
answer: Three patients tied at the highest anti-RNP level of 256: 912147, 4632548 and 4649885. I read "first visit" as Patient.`First Date` falling in 1991. RNP is stored as text, so I compared it as a number and left out 'negative' and null values, since no level was recorded for those. A patient's highest level can come from any of their lab dates, including after 1991.

sql:
SELECT (SELECT p.publisher_name FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name IN ('Marvel Comics','DC Comics') GROUP BY p.publisher_name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1) AS publisher_name,
(SELECT ABS(SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name='DC Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id) AS difference
answer: Marvel Comics has more superheroes than DC Comics, by 163. Each row of `superhero` counts as one hero, and publishers are matched by the exact names 'Marvel Comics' and 'DC Comics'. The Publisher term in the ontology is still a draft.

sql: SELECT d.driverRef FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3<>'' AND q.q3=(SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying q2 WHERE q2.raceId=r.raceId AND q2.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q2.q3<>'')
answer: hamilton (Q3 time 1:35.554, no tie). I compared Q3 times as text, which sorts correctly because they all use the same M:SS.mmm format.

sql:
WITH q AS (SELECT DISTINCT ds.raceId FROM driverStandings ds JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=ds.driverId WHERE d.nationality='Australian' AND ds.position<20)
SELECT r.year, COUNT(p.raceId) AS total_pit_stops FROM q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId LEFT JOIN pitStops p ON p.raceId=q.raceId WHERE r.year BETWEEN 2002 AND 2013 GROUP BY r.year ORDER BY r.year
answer:
I read "better than 20th" as standings position < 20, so 1st through 19th. 20th itself is excluded. Qualifying races are those where at least one Australian driver had a post-race standing in that range. Pit stops are counted for all drivers at those races.

Totals by season: 2011 had 1069 stops, 2012 had 905 and 2013 had 898. Seasons 2002 to 2010 show 0 because the pitStops table has no data before 2011. That is a data gap, not evidence that no stops happened. I ran the query with the extra clause, which does not change the result, but I did not re-run this final version. The Driver, Driver Standing and Race terms are draft, not certified.

sql: select sum(case when substr(e.event_date,1,4)='2019' then b.spent else 0 end)-sum(case when substr(e.event_date,1,4)='2020' then b.spent else 0 end) as difference from budget b join event e on b.link_to_event=e.event_id
answer: The difference is 2086.05. Events dated in 2019 have 2,086.05 in spending and events dated in 2020 have 0. I read "spent on events" as budget.spent for each event, grouped by the year of event_date. This matches the sum of expense.cost linked to those events through budget.

sql: select round(avg(case when height_cm>0 then height_cm end),2) as avg_height_cm, round(avg(case when weight_kg>0 then weight_kg end),2) as avg_weight_kg from superhero where skin_colour_id=14 and alignment_id=2
answer: 초록 피부 악당(skin colour = Green, alignment = Bad) 5명 기준 평균 키는 194.2cm, 평균 몸무게는 161.75kg입니다. 이 데이터에서는 값이 없는 키와 몸무게를 NULL이 아니라 0으로 저장해 두었기 때문에, 0은 기록 없음으로 보고 각 평균에서 제외했습니다. 그래서 키 평균은 4명(0cm인 1명 제외), 몸무게 평균은 4명(0kg인 1명 제외)으로 계산했습니다. 악당은 alignment가 'Bad'인 캐릭터로 해석했습니다.

sql: SELECT c.name, c.number, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM foreign_data f WHERE f.uuid=c.uuid) AS foreign_printings FROM cards c WHERE c.watermark='abzan' AND CAST(c.number AS INTEGER)=(SELECT MAX(CAST(number AS INTEGER)) FROM cards WHERE watermark='abzan')
answer:
Abzan Beastmaster (PRM set), collector number 55888, with 0 foreign-language printings. No other Abzan card ties for that number.

Assumptions:
- I compared collector numbers across all 82 Abzan-watermarked cards, not set by set. `cards.number` is text, so I compared it as an integer. 13 of the 82 numbers contain non-digit characters. They cast to their leading digits, and the maximum of 55888 is far above any of them, so they don't change the result.
- A printing is one `foreign_data` row for the card's uuid. Abzan Beastmaster has none, so the count is 0.
- The `Card` term in the ontology is still a draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(c),2) AS avg_powers FROM (SELECT s.id, COUNT(hp.power_id) AS c FROM superhero s JOIN race r ON s.race_id=r.id JOIN gender g ON s.gender_id=g.id LEFT JOIN hero_power hp ON hp.hero_id=s.id WHERE r.race='God / Eternal' AND g.gender='Male' GROUP BY s.id)
answer: 16.18. This is the average number of superpowers across the 17 male heroes whose race is 'God / Eternal'. I counted heroes with no powers as 0. If you only want heroes who have at least one power, the average is 19.64. The Race, Gender and Superhero terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select ID, Date, RNP from Laboratory where GOT>=60 and cast(RNP as real)=(select max(cast(RNP as real)) from Laboratory where GOT>=60 and RNP is not null)
answer: 환자 ID 1650222, 검사일 1989-07-18, 항RNP 수치 256입니다. 동률인 검사는 없습니다. RNP 열이 텍스트('negative', '16', '256' 등)라서 숫자로 바꿔 비교했고, 'negative'는 0으로 계산했습니다. GOT는 60 이상을 기준으로 했습니다.

sql: select (b.balance-a.balance)*100.0/a.balance from trans a, trans b where a.account_id=(select account_id from loan where date='1993-07-05') and b.account_id=a.account_id and a.date='1993-03-22' and b.date='1998-12-27'
answer: The loan dated 1993-07-05 belongs to account 1787. Its balance was 1100 on 1993-03-22 and 5835 on 1998-12-27, an increase of about 430.45%. There is one transaction on each of those dates, so no tie-break was needed.

sql: select count(distinct s.code) from sets s join set_translations t on t.setCode=s.code where s.block='Ice Age' and t.language='Italian' and t.translation is not null
answer: 1 of the 5 sets in the "Ice Age" block has an Italian translation. I counted sets that have a set_translations row with language 'Italian' and a non-null translation.

sql: select count(distinct case when P.SEX='F' then P.ID end)-count(distinct case when P.SEX='M' then P.ID end) as diff from Patient P join Laboratory L on L.ID=P.ID where P.Diagnosis='RA' and L.UN<30;
answer: 23. 해석 기준: RA는 Diagnosis가 정확히 'RA'인 환자만 포함했습니다. 'RA susp', 'RA, SJS' 같은 값은 제외했습니다. 요소질소(UN)는 정상 범위를 UN < 30으로 보고, 검사 기록이 한 번이라도 있으면 해당 환자로 세었습니다. 환자는 중복 없이 계산했습니다.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(s.status='Finished' or s.status like '+% Lap%')/count(*),2) as pct from results r join status s using(statusId) join races ra using(raceId) where ra.year=1957 and ra.name='British Grand Prix'
answer: 45.45%. In the 1957 British Grand Prix, 10 of the 22 drivers were classified finishers. Four have status 'Finished' and six are '+N Laps' (2, 2, 2, 5, 8 and 8 laps down, 19 laps down for one). The other 12 retired. I counted every row in results as a participant.

sql: SELECT s.School, s.Phone FROM schools s JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE s.DOC = '03' AND s.School IS NOT NULL AND t.NumGE1500 = (SELECT MAX(t2.NumGE1500) FROM satscores t2 JOIN schools s2 ON t2.cds = s2.CDSCode WHERE s2.DOC = '03' AND s2.School IS NOT NULL)
answer: High Tech High North County, phone (619) 243-5014 (56 test takers with SAT 1500+; no ties). I read "statewide benefit charter network" as District Ownership Code '03' (Statewide Benefit Charter, per docs/schools.csv); the ontology has no Term for it. I excluded the district-level aggregate row (no school name, 102) so only individual schools are compared. The School and SAT Score Record Terms are still drafts.

sql: SELECT c.colour AS eye_colour, COUNT(*) AS hero_count, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank FROM superhero s JOIN colour c ON c.id = s.eye_colour_id JOIN publisher p ON p.id = s.publisher_id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND c.colour <> 'No Colour' GROUP BY c.colour ORDER BY hero_count DESC, c.colour
answer: Blue is the most common eye colour among Marvel Comics heroes (126), then Brown (89), Green (40), Red (31), Yellow (13), White (12), Black (11), Grey (4), Hazel (3), and Gold and Purple (2 each, tied at rank 10). Seven colours have 1 hero each, tied at rank 12: Amber, Blue/White, Green/Blue, Silver, Violet, White/Red, Yellow/Blue. I treated 'No Colour' and NULL eye colours as unknown and excluded them. Tied counts share a rank (RANK), listed alphabetically.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT l.format, c.name FROM legalities l JOIN cards c ON c.uuid = l.uuid WHERE l.status = 'Banned' AND l.format = (SELECT format FROM legalities WHERE status = 'Banned' GROUP BY format ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1) ORDER BY c.name
answer: The format with the most banned records is legacy, with 546 banned printing records. The query returns the format and each distinct banned card name, 102 names in all. I read "banned card-printing records" as legalities rows with status 'Banned'. I did not print the 102 names here.

sql: select cast(round(avg(weight_kg)) as integer) from superhero where publisher_id=(select id from publisher where publisher_name='DC Comics') and weight_kg>0 and eye_colour_id in (select eye_colour_id from superhero where publisher_id=(select id from publisher where publisher_name='Marvel Comics') and eye_colour_id is not null)
answer: 102 kg. I treated weight_kg of NULL or 0 as unknown, which the docs define as missing, and excluded those heroes. 'No Colour' was matched like any other eye colour.

sql:
WITH a AS (SELECT molecule_id, COUNT(*) n_atoms, SUM(element='c') n_c, SUM(element='cl') n_cl FROM atom GROUP BY molecule_id),
b AS (SELECT molecule_id, COUNT(*) n_bonds, SUM(bond_type IN ('=','#')) n_multi FROM bond GROUP BY molecule_id),
cb AS (SELECT bond.molecule_id, COUNT(DISTINCT bond.bond_id) n_cbonds FROM bond JOIN connected ON connected.bond_id=bond.bond_id JOIN atom ON atom.atom_id=connected.atom_id WHERE atom.element='c' GROUP BY bond.molecule_id),
r AS (SELECT m.molecule_id, m.label, a.n_atoms, COALESCE(b.n_bonds,0) n_bonds, a.n_c, a.n_cl, COALESCE(cb.n_cbonds,0) n_cbonds, COALESCE(b.n_multi,0) n_multi FROM molecule m JOIN a ON a.molecule_id=m.molecule_id LEFT JOIN b ON b.molecule_id=m.molecule_id LEFT JOIN cb ON cb.molecule_id=m.molecule_id WHERE a.n_c>0)
SELECT molecule_id, label, n_atoms, n_bonds, n_c, n_cl, n_cbonds, n_multi, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY n_cbonds DESC, n_atoms DESC, molecule_id) AS rank FROM r ORDER BY rank
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 확인했습니다. 탄소 원자가 1개 이상인 분자마다 1행씩 나오고, 순위 1위는 TR060입니다(탄소 결합 107개, 원자 103개). 2위는 TR059(탄소 결합 107개, 원자 102개), 3위는 TR496(탄소 결합 99개)입니다. 결과 전체 행 수는 확인하지 않았고 상위 5행만 봤습니다.

선택한 해석은 다음과 같습니다.
- 탄소 접촉 결합은 양 끝 원자 중 하나라도 탄소(c)인 결합을 말하며, 결합 id 기준으로 중복 없이 셉니다.
- 다중 결합은 이중 결합('=')과 삼중 결합('#')을 합한 수입니다.
- 순위는 요청하신 대로 탄소 접촉 결합 수 내림차순, 원자 수 내림차순, 분자 id 오름차순으로 정렬해 1, 2, 3...으로 매겼습니다. 정렬 기준이 모두 같은 분자는 없다고 보고 ROW_NUMBER를 썼습니다.
- 요청하신 열(분자 id, 라벨, 원자 수, 결합 수, 탄소 수, 염소 수, 탄소 접촉 결합 수, 다중 결합 수) 뒤에 rank 열을 추가했습니다. 순위를 함께 달라는 요청으로 보았기 때문입니다.
- 사용한 Molecule, Atom, Bond 용어는 아직 draft 상태(인증 전)입니다.

sql:
SELECT e.location, COUNT(DISTINCT x.expense_description) AS n
FROM event e
JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
JOIN expense x ON x.link_to_budget = b.budget_id
WHERE e.location IS NOT NULL
  AND e.event_id IN (SELECT link_to_event FROM budget WHERE amount > 40)
GROUP BY e.location
answer: Two locations have qualifying events with recorded expenses: MU 215 (10 different items) and Campus Common (1 item). I read "different things bought" as distinct expense descriptions. An event qualifies if any of its budget lines has an amount over 40, and I counted every expense on those events, not only those on the over-40 lines. Events with no location are excluded. The Budget, Event and Expense ontology terms are still drafts.

sql: SELECT language, COUNT(*) AS printings FROM foreign_data WHERE language NOT IN ('Ancient Greek','Arabic','Hebrew','Latin','Sanskrit','Phyrexian') GROUP BY language HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MIN(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM foreign_data WHERE language NOT IN ('Ancient Greek','Arabic','Hebrew','Latin','Sanskrit','Phyrexian') GROUP BY language)) ORDER BY language
answer: Korean has the fewest printings, with 9,692. I counted rows in foreign_data (one per card and foreign language) as printings. I excluded Ancient Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Latin, Sanskrit and Phyrexian as promotional gimmick languages, since each has only 1 to 3 rows. The next-lowest count is Chinese Traditional at 11,106, so there is no tie. The query uses the final tie-safe form (HAVING = MIN); I ran the LIMIT 1 version, which returned the same row. The Card Foreign Data term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: select 100.0*(sum(case when strftime('%Y',l.date)='1997' then l.amount end)-sum(case when strftime('%Y',l.date)='1996' then l.amount end))/sum(case when strftime('%Y',l.date)='1996' then l.amount end) as growth_pct from loan l join disp d on d.account_id=l.account_id and d.type='OWNER' join client c on c.client_id=d.client_id and c.gender='M' where strftime('%Y',l.date) in ('1996','1997')
answer: 1996년에서 1997년으로 가면서 남성 고객이 소유한 계좌의 대출 총액은 약 25.30% 늘었습니다. 계좌 소유자는 disp 테이블에서 type이 'OWNER'인 행으로 판단했고, 그 고객의 gender가 'M'인 경우만 계산했습니다.

sql: select avg(1999-cast(strftime('%Y',Birthday) as int)) from Patient where ID in (select ID from Laboratory where "U-PRO" in ('3','4','300','>=300','>=1000','1000'))
answer: 약 42.41세입니다. U-PRO 값이 '3', '4', '300', '>=300', '>=1000'인 검사 기록이 한 번이라도 있는 환자를 환자당 1번씩 계산했습니다. 이 값들은 질문에서 말한 3~4등급과 300 이상 기준에 해당합니다. 이 조건에 맞는 값 중 '1000'만 표기된 행은 없었습니다. 나이는 1999에서 출생 연도를 뺀 값이고, 생년월일이 없는 환자는 평균에서 제외됩니다. 'TR', '1', '2', '30', '100', '+1(30)', '+2(100)'은 제외했습니다.

sql: select 100.0*sum(d.dob<'1985-01-01' and r.laps>50)/count(*) as percentage from results r join races ra on ra.raceId=r.raceId join drivers d on d.driverId=r.driverId where ra.year between 2000 and 2005
answer: 약 64.88%입니다. 2000~2005년 전체 레이스 결과 중, 1985년 이전에 태어난 드라이버가 50랩을 초과해 완주한 결과의 비율입니다. 분모는 해당 기간의 모든 결과 행이고, 분자는 dob < 1985-01-01 이면서 laps > 50인 행입니다.

sql:
SELECT m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT e.expense_description) AS kinds, SUM(e.cost) AS total_spent
FROM expense e JOIN member m ON e.link_to_member = m.member_id
WHERE e.expense_date >= '2019-10-01' AND e.expense_date < '2019-12-01'
GROUP BY m.member_id
HAVING kinds = (SELECT MAX(k) FROM (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT e2.expense_description) AS k FROM expense e2 WHERE e2.expense_date >= '2019-10-01' AND e2.expense_date < '2019-12-01' GROUP BY e2.link_to_member))
answer: Two members tie with 5 kinds of items each in Oct–Nov 2019: Sacha Harrison (total $407.90) and Phillip Cullen (total $464.99). Kinds = distinct expense_description values; all expenses counted (approved or not), dates 2019-10-01 to 2019-11-30. Expense and Member ontology terms are draft (uncertified).

sql:
WITH v AS (SELECT s.CDSCode, s.County, s.School, sa.AvgScrRead AS r FROM schools s LEFT JOIN satscores sa ON sa.cds=s.CDSCode AND sa.rtype='S' WHERE s.Virtual='F'),
c AS (SELECT County, COUNT(*) n FROM v GROUP BY County),
top AS (SELECT County, n FROM c WHERE n >= (SELECT n FROM c ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 4)),
m AS (SELECT County, MAX(r) mr FROM v GROUP BY County)
SELECT top.County, top.n AS num_virtual_schools, COALESCE(v.School,'None') AS school
FROM top JOIN m USING(County)
LEFT JOIN v ON v.County=top.County AND m.mr IS NOT NULL AND v.r=m.mr
ORDER BY top.n DESC, top.County, school;
answer:
"Exclusively virtual" means schools.Virtual = 'F' (69 schools). I took reading averages from satscores rows with rtype='S' (school level). The top five counties, with 5th place tied, give these rows:
- Los Angeles, 12 schools, top reading average: California Virtual Academy @ Los Angeles
- San Joaquin, 10, California Connections Academy @ Ripon
- San Diego, 8, None
- Sacramento, 5, None
- San Bernardino, 5, None
Sacramento and San Bernardino tie for fifth. San Diego, Sacramento and San Bernardino have no reported reading average for any of their exclusively virtual schools, so they show 'None'.

sql: select s.superhero_name from superhero s join colour c on c.id=s.eye_colour_id where c.colour='No Colour' and s.height_cm between 170 and 190
answer: 15개 이름이 나옵니다. 눈 색 '알 수 없음'은 colour 테이블의 'No Colour'(id 1)로 해석했고, 키 범위 170~190cm는 양 끝을 포함했습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c JOIN sets s ON s.code = c.setCode WHERE c.originalReleaseDate LIKE '2014%' AND s.mtgoCode IS NOT NULL AND s.mtgoCode <> ''
answer: 293 printings. I counted each card row once and matched it to its set. I treated a set as MTGO-available when its mtgoCode is neither NULL nor empty. The 2014 filter reads the year from originalReleaseDate, which is stored as text like '2014/5/2'. Of the 302 printings with a 2014 original release date, 293 are in sets that have an MTGO code.

sql: SELECT a.date FROM Player_Attributes a JOIN Player p ON p.player_api_id=a.player_api_id WHERE p.player_name='Kevin Constant' ORDER BY a.crossing DESC, a.date ASC LIMIT 1
answer: Kevin Constant first reached his highest crossing score (82) on 2013-02-15. The same score of 82 also appears on 2013-03-08 and 2013-03-28, and I took the earliest of the three.

sql:
WITH l AS (SELECT account_id, SUM(amount) total FROM loan GROUP BY account_id),
cp AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(DISTINCT account) n FROM trans WHERE bank IS NOT NULL AND bank<>'' AND account IS NOT NULL GROUP BY account_id),
b AS (
SELECT a.account_id, a.date opened, l.total, COALESCE(cp.n,0) n, d.A2 district, CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) pop
FROM account a JOIN l ON l.account_id=a.account_id
JOIN disp s ON s.account_id=a.account_id AND s.type='OWNER'
JOIN client c ON c.client_id=s.client_id
JOIN district d ON d.district_id=c.district_id
LEFT JOIN cp ON cp.account_id=a.account_id
WHERE a.district_id=19)
SELECT account_id, opened AS account_opening_date, total AS total_borrowed, n AS outside_counterparties, district AS home_district, pop AS district_population,
RANK() OVER (ORDER BY pop DESC) AS population_rank
FROM b ORDER BY population_rank, account_id;
answer:
14 Prachatice-branch accounts have loans. Trutnov (population 121,947) ranks 1 for account 8489, with 2 outside counterparties. Praha - zapad (75,637) ranks 2 for account 2762, with 3. The other 12 accounts have owners in Prachatice (51,428) and share rank 3, listed by account number.

Readings I chose:
- Branch means account.district_id = 19.
- The owner is the disp row with type OWNER.
- Total borrowed is the sum of all loan amounts on the account.
- Outside counterparties is the number of distinct trans.account values on rows where trans.bank is filled in. Cash rows have no bank, so they are excluded.
- Population is district.A4 cast to a number.
- RANK() gives ties the same rank and skips the next one.

sql: select distinct l."T-CHO" as max_tcho, p.Admission, p.ID from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where p.Admission in ('+','-') and l."T-CHO" = (select max(l2."T-CHO") from Laboratory l2 join Patient p2 on p2.ID=l2.ID where p2.Admission=p.Admission) order by p.Admission asc, p.ID
answer: 입원 환자 중 T-CHO 최고치는 568이며 환자 ID는 1185720입니다. 외래 환자 중 최고치는 443이며 환자 ID는 3380563입니다. 두 그룹 모두 동점자는 없었습니다. 결과 열 순서는 T-CHO, Admission, ID이고, '+' 행이 먼저 나옵니다. Admission 값이 정확히 '+' 또는 '-'인 환자만 포함했습니다. 값이 '+('인 3명과 값이 비어 있는 34명은 어느 그룹인지 불분명해 제외했습니다. 검사 기록 전체(모든 검사일)에서 그룹별 최고값을 찾았습니다.

sql: SELECT SUM(Admission='+') AS inpatients, SUM(Admission='-') AS outpatients, ROUND(100.0*SUM(Admission='+')/SUM(Admission IN ('+','-')),2) AS inpatient_pct FROM Patient WHERE REPLACE(Diagnosis,'SLE susp','') LIKE '%SLE%'
answer: 확진 SLE 환자 중 입원 164명, 외래 113명이고, 두 진료 형태 중 입원 비율은 59.21%입니다. 'SLE susp'(의심)만 있는 환자는 제외했고, 다른 진단과 함께 SLE가 확진으로 적힌 환자는 포함했습니다. Admission이 비어 있거나 '+('인 환자는 어느 쪽에도 넣지 않았고 분모에서도 뺐습니다. 쿼리가 쓴 Patient Term은 아직 draft 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT member.first_name, member.last_name FROM member INNER JOIN attendance ON attendance.link_to_member = member.member_id GROUP BY member.member_id, member.first_name, member.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT attendance.link_to_event) > 7
answer: 29명의 회원이 7개를 넘는 행사에 참석했습니다. 예: Grant Gilmour, Luisa Guidi, Connor Hilton. 결과는 first_name, last_name 두 열입니다. 'students'는 member 테이블의 회원으로, 참석 횟수는 회원별 중복 없는 행사 수로 계산했습니다. Member 용어는 아직 인증되지 않은 초안 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.bond_id FROM connected c JOIN atom a1 ON c.atom_id=a1.atom_id JOIN atom a2 ON c.atom_id2=a2.atom_id WHERE a1.element='p' AND a2.element='n' ORDER BY c.bond_id
answer: 6 bonds join a phosphorus atom and a nitrogen atom: TR032_2_3, TR032_3_5, TR058_1_3, TR058_1_4, TR058_1_5 and TR298_1_5. I read the question as asking for bond IDs where one end is phosphorus and the other is nitrogen. The `connected` table lists each bond in both directions, so filtering on phosphorus first and nitrogen second returns each bond once. The result relies on the `Atom` term, which is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: with p as (select ID, ','||replace(replace(replace(replace(replace(Diagnosis,char(29),','),char(11),','),char(30),','),'  ',','),' ','')||',' d from Patient) select round(avg(e.[aCL IgM]),2) from Examination e join p on p.ID=e.ID where (d like '%,SJS,%' or d like '%,SJSRA,%') and e.[aCL IgM]>0
answer:
SJS 환자의 항카디올리핀 IgM 평균 농도는 2.89입니다.

기준은 다음과 같이 적용했습니다. Patient.Diagnosis에는 'RA, SJS susp^K^]SJS'처럼 여러 진단이 구분 기호로 붙어 있어서, 진단을 항목별로 나눈 뒤 'SJS'가 'susp' 없이 단독으로 있는 환자만 포함했습니다. 'SJS susp'만 있는 환자는 제외했고, 'SJS, MCTD susp'처럼 SJS는 확정이고 다른 진단만 의심인 환자는 포함했습니다. 'SJS  RA'는 구분 기호가 빠진 입력으로 보고 SJS 확정으로 처리했습니다. 검사 날짜는 제한하지 않았고, aCL IgM이 0인 검사는 평균에서 뺐습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) FROM cards c JOIN rulings r ON r.uuid = c.uuid WHERE (c.power IS NULL OR c.power = '*') AND r.text LIKE '%triggered ability%'
answer: 1,382 distinct card printings. I counted distinct cards.uuid, because each row in cards is one printing. "No recorded power or variable power" is power IS NULL or power = '*', which matches docs/cards.csv ("null or * refers to unknown power"). Adding the one '*²' printing does not change the count. A ruling matches if its text contains 'triggered ability' (SQLite LIKE ignores case for ASCII text). The cards and rulings Terms are still in draft status.

sql: SELECT SUM(amount) AS total_dues FROM income WHERE source='Dues' AND link_to_member IN (SELECT a.link_to_member FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON e.event_id=a.link_to_event WHERE e.event_name='Football game');
answer: The Football game attendees paid $1,100 in total membership dues (income rows with source 'Dues'). Two events are named 'Football game', so I included attendees of both. A member who went to both is counted once, so their dues are not doubled.

sql:
SELECT frameVersion AS frame_year, COUNT(*) AS card_count
FROM cards
WHERE leadershipSkills LIKE '%''commander'': True%'
  AND cardKingdomId IS NOT NULL AND cardKingdomId <> ''
  AND cardKingdomFoilId IS NOT NULL AND cardKingdomFoilId <> ''
  AND frameVersion GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]'
GROUP BY frameVersion
ORDER BY CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER) DESC
LIMIT 1;
answer:
The latest frame year is 2015, and 820 cards in the group have that frame version.

I read the conditions this way:
- Commander-leadable: `leadershipSkills` contains `'commander': True`.
- Listed for both printings at Card Kingdom: both `cardKingdomId` (non-foil) and `cardKingdomFoilId` (foil) are present.
- Frame year: `frameVersion` values that are four-digit years. The value 'future' is not a calendar year, so I excluded it.
- Counting: each row in `cards` counts as one card, so a card printed in several sets counts once per printing.

sql: SELECT p.ID, p.Diagnosis, l.DNA FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' AND l.DNA IS NOT NULL AND CAST(l.DNA AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(l2.DNA AS REAL)) FROM Laboratory l2 JOIN Patient p2 ON p2.ID = l2.ID WHERE p2.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' AND l2.DNA IS NOT NULL)
answer: Patient 2933261, diagnosis SLE, highest anti-DNA result 185. The DNA column is stored as text, so I cast it to a number for the comparison and returned the original text value. I counted any diagnosis containing 'SLE' as lupus. Restricting to the exact diagnosis 'SLE' gives the same patient, with no tie.

sql: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.cardKingdomId IS NOT NULL AND c.cardKingdomFoilId IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS percentage FROM cards c JOIN sets s ON s.code = c.setCode WHERE s.name = 'Coldsnap'
answer: 100% of Coldsnap printings have both a Card Kingdom ID and a Card Kingdom foil ID. I used the set named exactly 'Coldsnap', so 'Coldsnap Theme Decks' and 'Coldsnap Promos' are excluded. An ID counts as recorded when it is not NULL, and I did not check for empty strings. The Card and Card Set terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select max(cast(frameVersion as int))-min(cast(frameVersion as int)) as years from cards where name='Tarmogoyf' and frameVersion glob '[0-9]*'
answer: 12 years (2015 − 2003). Tarmogoyf's printings use frame versions 2003, 2015 and "future". I left out "future" because it isn't a year.

sql: select count(distinct q.driverId) from qualifying q join races r using(raceId) where r.year=1995 and q.q1 glob '[0-9]:*' and (cast(substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1) as int)*60+cast(substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,':')+1) as real))>120
answer: 9 drivers set a Q1 time slower than 2:00.000 in 1995 races. I counted distinct drivers across all 1995 races, converting the m:ss.xxx text to seconds and keeping times above 120.

sql: SELECT element, COUNT(*) AS bonded_atoms FROM atom WHERE molecule_id='TR397' AND (atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id FROM connected) OR atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id2 FROM connected)) GROUP BY element ORDER BY element
answer: TR397 has 84 bonded atoms: c 34, h 24, n 6, o 16, s 4. I counted each atom once, even if it has several bonds, and counted it as bonded if it appears on either side of a `connected` row. The `Atom` term is still a draft in the ontology, not certified.

sql: select r.year, d.forename, d.surname, s.time from races r join results s on s.raceId=r.raceId and s.positionOrder=1 join drivers d on d.driverId=s.driverId where r.name like '%Canadian%' and r.year between 2007 and 2017 and r.time<='17:00:00' order by r.year
answer: 네 개 대회가 해당합니다. 2007년 Lewis Hamilton 1:44:11.292, 2008년 Robert Kubica 1:36:24.227, 2010년 Lewis Hamilton 1:33:53.456, 2011년 Jenson Button 4:04:39.537입니다. races.time은 현지 시각으로 보고 17:00:00 이하를 기준으로 삼았습니다. 2009년은 캐나다 GP가 열리지 않았고, 2012년 이후는 모두 18:00에 시작해 제외했습니다. 우승자는 positionOrder가 1인 드라이버로 정했습니다.

sql: select count(*) from Patient p where p.Admission='-' and exists(select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and (l.HCT<=29 or l.HCT>=52)) and exists(select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and l.RNP glob '[0-9]*' and CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>16);
answer: 2 patients. I read the question as follows. Outpatient means Admission = '-'. Non-normal hematocrit means HCT of 29 or below, or 52 or above, because the docs give the normal range as 29 < N < 52. RNP above 16 means a numeric RNP value over 16. The only values that qualify are 64 and 256. Text values such as '-', '+-', '+' and 'negative' are not counted. Each condition is checked across all of a patient's lab dates, and the count is of distinct patients, not only those with a thrombosis event.

sql: select count(*) from cards where (','||replace(keywords,', ',',')||',') glob '*,Flying,*' and (','||replace(keywords,', ',',')||',') glob '*,Cycling,*'
answer: 32 cards (printings) have both the Flying and Cycling keywords. I matched each keyword exactly, so variants such as Islandcycling or Landcycling don't count as Cycling. A plain substring match would have given 45.

sql: select p.Admission, count(distinct p.ID) as patients from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where l.RNP glob '[0-9]*' and cast(l.RNP as real)>16 and p.Admission in ('+','-') group by p.Admission
answer: 7명이 입원('+')했고, 4명이 외래 추적('-')입니다. RNP는 텍스트 열이라 숫자 값만 골라 숫자로 비교했습니다. 'negative'와 빈 값은 제외했습니다. 16 초과 값은 64와 256이었고, 한 환자가 여러 번 검사받았어도 1명으로 계산했습니다. Admission이 '+(' 형태이거나 비어 있는 환자는 질문의 '+', '-' 구분에 맞지 않아 뺐습니다.

sql: select d.code,q.q3 from qualifying q join races r using(raceId) join drivers d using(driverId) where r.year=2017 and r.name='Italian Grand Prix' and q.q3 = (select min(q2.q3) from qualifying q2 join races r2 using(raceId) where r2.year=2017 and r2.name='Italian Grand Prix' and q2.q3<>'')
answer: HAM (Lewis Hamilton) set the fastest Q3 time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix: 1:35.554. No other driver tied. The query compares the times as text, which orders them correctly because they all use the m:ss.mmm format, and it ignores empty Q3 values.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT s.code) FROM sets s JOIN set_translations t ON t.setCode = s.code WHERE s.block = 'Ice Age' AND t.language = 'Italian' AND t.translation IS NOT NULL
answer: 1 set in the "Ice Age" block has an Italian translation. I counted only rows where the translated name is not null, because a null name means no translation exists. If rows with a null name also counted, the result would be 2. The Card Set and Set Translation terms the query relies on are still draft, not certified.

sql: select type, count(*) as card_count from cards c where watermark='azorius' and exists(select 1 from foreign_data f where f.uuid=c.uuid) group by type order by card_count desc, type
answer: 26 card types qualify. Instant is the largest with 29 cards. Next come Creature — Human Knight, Enchantment and Sorcery with 8 each. Artifact, Creature — Human Wizard and Enchantment — Aura follow with 6 each. The smallest groups have 1 card each: Artifact Creature — Golem, Creature — Drake and Legendary Creature — Human Advisor. I used the `type` column as printed. I counted each card row once if it has at least one `foreign_data` row, matched by uuid. I matched the watermark as 'azorius'.

sql: select count(distinct p.ID) from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where p.SEX='F' and l.SC170 in ('negative','-','+-') and not exists (select 1 from Examination e where e.ID=p.ID and e.Symptoms is not null);
answer: 10 distinct female patients. I treated 'negative', '-' and '+-' as normal anti-Scl-70 (SC170) values. The docs give the normal range as '-' or '+-', and the data actually contains 'negative'. I excluded the numeric values 0, 1, 4 and 16 because they are ambiguous. 'No symptom' means no Examination row for the patient has a non-null Symptoms value, which includes patients with no examinations at all.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.name) FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid=c.uuid WHERE c.colors='B' AND c.types LIKE '%Artifact%' AND TRIM(COALESCE(f.flavorText,''))<>''
answer: 11 cards. I read mono-black as cards.colors being exactly 'B'. I read Artifact as cards.types containing 'Artifact', which includes Artifact Creature. A foreign printing counts when its foreign_data.flavorText is non-empty. foreign_data has no English rows, so every row is a foreign-language printing. Cards are counted by distinct name, and the count by oracle id gives the same 11.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(a.alignment='Neutral')/count(*),2) as neutral_pct, sum(a.alignment='Neutral' and p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics') as neutral_marvel from superhero s left join alignment a on s.alignment_id=a.id left join publisher p on s.publisher_id=p.id
answer: Neutral heroes are 3.73% of all superheroes, and 10 of them were published by Marvel Comics. I used every row in the superhero table as the denominator, including heroes whose alignment is N/A.

sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId=r.circuitId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE c.name='Marina Bay Street Circuit' AND r.year=2008 AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3<>'' ORDER BY q.q3 ASC LIMIT 1
answer: Felipe Massa recorded the fastest Q3 time at Marina Bay Street Circuit in 2008. I read "fastest" as the lowest non-empty q3 value, which sorts correctly as text in m:ss.mmm format. A tie for the fastest time would show only one driver. The ontology terms used are drafts, not certified.

sql:
SELECT s.AdmFName1, s.AdmLName1
FROM schools s
JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode AND t.rtype = 'S'
WHERE s.County = (SELECT County FROM schools WHERE CDSCode = '01611430131177')
ORDER BY t.NumGE1500 DESC, s.CDSCode ASC
LIMIT 1;
answer: Zachary Larsen (school 01611760135244, 421 students with SAT ≥1500). Assumptions: your code 1611430131177 is stored as 01611430131177 (leading zero dropped); that is Berkeley High in Alameda County. I counted only school-level SAT rows (rtype 'S'), not district roll-ups, and I included Berkeley High itself in the comparison (it has 335, so it doesn't win). I used the first administrator listed (AdmFName1/AdmLName1).

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT y.CustomerID) FROM yearmonth y JOIN customers c ON c.CustomerID=y.CustomerID WHERE c.Segment='SME' AND y.Date='201302' AND y.Consumption>0
answer: 1518 SME customers had consumption above 0 in February 2013. I used the yearmonth table (month 201302) and counted a customer as having purchased gas if Consumption > 0.

sql: SELECT ROUND(1.0 * (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pitStops p JOIN races r ON r.raceId = p.raceId WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name NOT IN (SELECT name FROM races WHERE year = 2000)) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM races r WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name NOT IN (SELECT name FROM races WHERE year = 2000)), 2) AS avg_pit_stops_per_race
answer: 39.71. I read "not hosted in 2000" as a race name (Grand Prix) that did not appear in the 2000 season. That leaves 7 races in 2017. Only 5 of them have pit stop records, so I counted the other 2 as 0 stops, as you asked for the average of all those races. The total is 278 stops across 7 races. If you averaged only the 5 races that have pit stop data, the result would be higher.

sql: SELECT SUM(totalSetSize) FROM sets s WHERE (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT translation) FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode=s.code AND translation IS NOT NULL) < 5;
answer: The total is 45,452 cards across 504 sets that have fewer than five distinct translated names. I used totalSetSize, which includes promotional and supplemental printings. Sets with no translations at all count as fewer than five. Identical translation strings are counted once.

sql: SELECT p.SEX, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS patient_count FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.ALB < 3.5 AND p.SEX IN ('F','M') GROUP BY p.SEX
answer: F: 64 patients, M: 14 patients. I counted each patient once if any of their lab records has ALB below 3.5. Two other patients with low albumin have a blank sex value, so I left them out of the F/M rows.

sql:
WITH fl AS (
  SELECT c.client_id, c.birth_date, l.account_id, l.amount, l.duration, l.payments, l.status
  FROM loan l
  JOIN disp d ON d.account_id = l.account_id AND d.type = 'OWNER'
  JOIN client c ON c.client_id = d.client_id AND c.gender = 'F'
), top AS (
  SELECT *, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY amount DESC) rk FROM fl
), tx AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) n, SUM(CASE WHEN type='PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) dep
  FROM trans GROUP BY account_id
), reg AS (
  SELECT d.A3 region, COUNT(l.loan_id) loans
  FROM district d JOIN account a ON a.district_id = d.district_id JOIN loan l ON l.account_id = a.account_id
  GROUP BY d.A3
), ra AS (
  SELECT A3 region, ROUND(AVG(A11),2) avg_sal FROM district GROUP BY A3
)
SELECT t.client_id AS client_id, t.amount AS loan_amount, t.duration AS duration_months,
  ROUND(t.payments*t.duration,2) AS total_payments,
  ROUND(t.payments*t.duration - t.amount,2) AS interest_paid,
  t.status AS loan_status, d.A2 AS district, d.A3 AS region,
  tx.n AS transaction_count, ROUND(tx.dep,2) AS total_deposits,
  CASE WHEN tx.dep > 2*t.amount THEN 'High Income' WHEN tx.dep > t.amount THEN 'Medium Income' ELSE 'Low Income' END AS income_category,
  reg.loans AS loans_in_region, ra.avg_sal AS region_avg_salary,
  CAST(strftime('%Y','2026-10-09') AS INT) - CAST(strftime('%Y',t.birth_date) AS INT)
   - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09') < strftime('%m-%d',t.birth_date)) AS age
FROM top t
JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id
JOIN tx ON tx.account_id = t.account_id
JOIN reg ON reg.region = d.A3
JOIN ra ON ra.region = d.A3
WHERE t.rk <= 3
ORDER BY t.amount DESC
answer:
The three largest loans held by female clients are 566,640 (client 10997, Prague, Low Income, age 54), 541,200 (client 2823, north Moravia, Low Income, age 79) and 495,180 (client 8506, north Moravia, Medium Income, age 46). There are no ties, so exactly three loans are returned. All three run 60 months, and total payments equal the loan amount, so interest paid is 0.00 for each. Transaction counts are 200, 329 and 76; total deposits are 447,173, 515,538 and 770,790. Prague has 84 loans and an average salary of 12,541; north Moravia has 117 loans and an average of 9,049.18.

Readings I chose: the client is the OWNER of the loan's account (disponents excluded); total deposits are credit ('PRIJEM') transactions only; transaction count is all transactions on the account; region and district come from the account's branch district. The ontology terms used are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient p WHERE trim(p.Diagnosis)='MCTD' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.PLT>100 AND l.PLT<400) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>5)
answer: 1 patient. Readings: MCTD alone means Diagnosis is exactly 'MCTD'; normal platelets means 100 < PLT < 400 (the ontology's documented range); anti-RNP above 5 uses numeric RNP values only (text such as 'negative' is ignored). The platelet and RNP readings may come from different test dates. Terms used (Patient, Laboratory Test) are draft, not certified.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT scryfallOracleId, MIN(edhrecRank) r, MIN(convertedManaCost) m FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND edhrecRank IS NOT NULL AND scryfallOracleId IN (SELECT c2.scryfallOracleId FROM cards c2 JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid=c2.uuid WHERE l.status='Banned') GROUP BY scryfallOracleId) SELECT ROUND(AVG(m),1) AS avg_mana_value FROM c WHERE r<=1000
answer:
The average mana value is 3.4. It covers 7 distinct creature cards that are banned in at least one format and have an EDHRec rank of 1000 or better.

I counted each card once, grouped by scryfallOracleId. Across printings, each of these cards has the same EDHRec rank and the same mana value. "Banned" means a legalities row with status 'Banned' in any format. "Creature" means the types column contains Creature. Mana value is convertedManaCost. The Card and Card Legality terms I relied on are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select 100.0*(sum(case when substr(l.date,1,4)='1997' then amount end)-sum(case when substr(l.date,1,4)='1996' then amount end))/sum(case when substr(l.date,1,4)='1996' then amount end) as growth_pct from loan l where l.account_id in (select d.account_id from disp d join client c using(client_id) where c.gender='M' and d.type='OWNER') and substr(l.date,1,4) in ('1996','1997')
answer: 약 25.30% 증가했습니다. 계좌 소유자(disp.type='OWNER')가 남성(gender='M')인 계좌의 대출을 기준으로 1996년 대비 1997년 총 대출 금액의 증가율을 계산했습니다. 'owned by'를 OWNER 유형으로 해석했고, DISPONENT는 제외했습니다.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p."Admission" = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_inpatients
FROM "Patient" p
WHERE p."Birthday" >= '1930-01-01' AND p."Birthday" < '1941-01-01'
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "Laboratory" l WHERE l."ID" = p."ID")
answer: 35.90. Distinct patients born 1930-01-01 to 1940-12-31 with at least one Laboratory row. Inpatient means Admission = '+'. The denominator is all patients in that group. The Patient Term is a draft, not certified.

sql: select count(*) from satscores where cname='Contra Costa' and rtype='S' and NumTstTakr > (select NumTstTakr from satscores where cds='07618040730051')
answer: 1 school (Dougherty Valley High, 528 test takers) had more SAT test takers than California High (435). I matched the CDS code as stored, with a leading zero (07618040730051). I counted only school rows (rtype 'S') and left out district totals, which would have added more rows.

sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, l.Date, l."U-PRO" AS proteinuria FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l."U-PRO" IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(l."U-PRO") <> '' AND l.Date = (SELECT MAX(l2.Date) FROM Laboratory l2 WHERE l2.ID = p.ID AND l2."U-PRO" IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(l2."U-PRO") <> '') ORDER BY p.ID
answer: The query returns one row per patient with a proteinuria result: patient ID, sex, date of the latest proteinuria test, and the proteinuria value from that test. I ran it and checked only the first 5 rows, so I haven't counted the full result. sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT s.CDSCode, f."FRPM Count (K-12)" AS frpm_cnt, f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enr,
         f."FRPM Count (K-12)" / f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS share
  FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode
  WHERE s.Charter = 0 AND s.EdOpsCode = 'TRAD' AND f."School Code" <> '0000000'
    AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" > 100 AND f."FRPM Count (K-12)" IS NOT NULL
), picks AS (
  SELECT CDSCode, 'largest FRPM-eligible count' AS part, 1 AS ord FROM base WHERE frpm_cnt = (SELECT MAX(frpm_cnt) FROM base)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT CDSCode, 'smallest FRPM share', 2 FROM base WHERE share = (SELECT MIN(share) FROM base)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT CDSCode, 'the CDS code from my notes', 3 FROM schools WHERE CDSCode = '04615150435602'
)
SELECT p.part AS part, s.School AS school_name, s.County AS county, s.City AS city,
  s.MailStreet AS mailing_street, s.MailCity AS mailing_city, s.MailState AS mailing_state, s.MailZip AS mailing_zip,
  s.Website AS website, f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enrollment_k12, f."FRPM Count (K-12)" AS frpm_eligible_count,
  f."FRPM Count (K-12)" / f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS frpm_share,
  CASE WHEN t.NumTstTakr > 0 THEN t.AvgScrRead + t.AvgScrMath + t.AvgScrWrite END AS avg_total_sat,
  CASE WHEN t.NumTstTakr > 0 THEN 100.0 * t.NumGE1500 / t.NumTstTakr END AS pct_sat_1500_plus,
  s.OpenDate AS opening_date,
  CASE WHEN s.ClosedDate IS NOT NULL THEN 'closed' ELSE 'open' END AS status
FROM picks p JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = p.CDSCode
LEFT JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode
LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode
ORDER BY p.ord, s.School
answer:
The query returns three rows, one per part, with no ties in either extreme.

- **Largest FRPM-eligible count:** Paramount High (Paramount, Los Angeles). 4,419 of 4,814 students are FRPM-eligible, a share of 0.918. Its average total SAT is 1272, and 14.8% of its SAT takers scored 1500 or more. It has no website on record and is open.
- **Smallest FRPM share:** Orinda Intermediate (Orinda, Contra Costa). 2 of 907 students are FRPM-eligible, a share of 0.0022. It has no SAT record and no website, so those fields are NULL. It is open.
- **The CDS code from my notes:** Oroville High (Oroville, Butte). 692 of 982 students are FRPM-eligible, a share of 0.705. Its average total SAT is 1395, and 32.7% of its SAT takers scored 1500 or more. Its website is http://ohs.ouhsd.org and it is open.

Each row also carries the school's mailing street, city, state and ZIP, plus its opening date. Opening dates are 1953-07-01 for Paramount High and 1980-07-01 for both Orinda Intermediate and Oroville High.

Choices I made where the question was ambiguous:
- **Your CDS code:** The code 4615150435602 has 13 digits, so I read it as 04615150435602 with the leading zero dropped. That matches Oroville High.
- **"Regular, non-charter":** I used Charter = 0 and the Traditional education option (EdOpsCode = 'TRAD'). I excluded district-office rows and kept schools with more than 100 K-12 students. This population is used only for the two extremes. The benchmark school is included by its code alone.
- **FRPM share:** FRPM count divided by K-12 enrollment, both from the frpm table.
- **SAT figures:** The average total is the average reading, math and writing scores added together. The 1500+ percentage is NumGE1500 divided by test takers, shown as 0–100. Schools with no SAT record, or zero test takers, get NULL.
- **Part label:** I added a `part` column at the front for the label you asked for. The other 15 columns follow in the order you listed.

The School, FRPM and SAT Terms the query relies on are still draft, not certified.

sql:
SELECT d.forename, d.surname, d.url, d.dob, COUNT(q.qualifyId) AS q3_count
FROM drivers d
LEFT JOIN qualifying q ON q.driverId = d.driverId AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(q.q3) <> ''
WHERE d.nationality = 'German' AND CAST(strftime('%Y', d.dob) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 1971 AND 1985
GROUP BY d.driverId
ORDER BY q3_count DESC, d.dob ASC
answer:
독일 국적 드라이버 중 1971~1985년생은 7명이고, Q3 기록 횟수 순으로 Nico Rosberg 149회, Nick Heidfeld 44회, Adrian Sutil 19회, Ralf Schumacher 15회, Timo Glock 13회입니다. Markus Winkelhock과 André Lotterer는 0회입니다. 결과에는 이름, 성, Wikipedia 링크, 생년월일, Q3 횟수가 순서대로 나옵니다.

적용한 해석은 세 가지입니다.
- Q3 횟수는 qualifying 테이블에서 q3 값이 비어 있지 않은 행의 수로 계산했습니다.
- Q3 기록이 한 번도 없는 드라이버도 0회로 포함했습니다.
- 국적은 nationality = 'German'으로 거르고, 생년은 dob의 연도로 판단했습니다.

동률이면 생년월일이 빠른 드라이버를 먼저 두었으며, 이번 결과에서는 동률이 0회인 두 명뿐입니다. 쿼리에 쓴 Driver와 Qualifying Result 용어는 아직 인증되지 않은(draft) 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.name) FROM cards c WHERE c.hasContentWarning = 1 AND ','||c.availability||',' LIKE '%,paper,%' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cards d WHERE d.name = c.name AND ','||d.availability||',' LIKE '%,mtgo,%')

sql: SELECT d.driverRef, COALESCE(SUM(r.points),0) AS total_points FROM drivers d LEFT JOIN results r ON r.driverId=d.driverId AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM lapTimes l WHERE l.raceId=r.raceId AND l.driverId=r.driverId) WHERE d.forename='Robert' GROUP BY d.driverId, d.driverRef;

sql: select count(distinct r.driverId) from results r join races ra on ra.raceId=r.raceId join status s on s.statusId=r.statusId where ra.year=1962 and ra.name='British Grand Prix' and s.status='Withdrew'

sql: select forename, surname from results join drivers using(driverId) where dob between '1980-01-01' and '1990-12-31' and fastestLapSpeed is not null group by driverId order by max(cast(fastestLapSpeed as real)) desc, dob asc, surname asc limit 3
answer: Fernando Alonso (253.874 km/h), Antônio Pizzonia (253.566), Jenson Button (252.262). I read "between 1980 and 1990" as inclusive of both years (dob 1980-01-01 to 1990-12-31); that choice doesn't change the top three.

sql:
WITH t AS (SELECT DISTINCT c.circuitRef, r.time FROM races r JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId=r.circuitId WHERE r.time IS NOT NULL AND r.time<>''),
e AS (SELECT circuitRef, time FROM t WHERE time=(SELECT MIN(time) FROM t)),
l AS (SELECT circuitRef, time FROM t WHERE time=(SELECT MAX(time) FROM t))
SELECT e.circuitRef AS earliest_circuitRef, l.circuitRef AS latest_circuitRef,
 (strftime('%s','2000-01-01 '||l.time)-strftime('%s','2000-01-01 '||e.time)) AS gap_seconds
FROM e CROSS JOIN l ORDER BY 1,2
answer: Earliest start: fuji. Latest start: americas. Gap: 55,800 seconds (15.5 hours). Only races with a recorded start time (races.time, about 24% of races) are included. Ties would be listed as separate rows, but there are none here. The Circuit and Race terms are still drafts in the ontology.

sql: select c.colour from superhero s join race r on r.id=s.race_id left join colour c on c.id=s.hair_colour_id where r.race='Human' and s.height_cm>0 order by s.height_cm limit 1
answer: Brown. The shortest human superhero is Jack-Jack, at 71 cm. I counted a hero as human if their race is 'Human'. I treated both NULL and 0 heights as unmeasured, because the docs say both mean missing. There are no ties at 71 cm.

sql: SELECT c.originalType AS card_type, COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM cards c WHERE c.watermark = 'azorius' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM foreign_data f WHERE f.uuid = c.uuid) GROUP BY c.originalType ORDER BY card_count DESC, card_type ASC
answer:
The query returns 38 card types. Instant has the most cards (29), followed by Enchantment (8), Sorcery (8) and Artifact (6). Several types are listed twice because the printed type line uses a hyphen in some printings and an em-dash in others, for example 'Creature — Human Knight' (6) and 'Creature - Human Knight' (2).

Choices I made where the question was ambiguous:
- **Card type:** I used `cards.originalType`, the type line as originally printed with supertypes and subtypes. I did not use the normalized `type` column.
- **Hyphen and em-dash variants:** I kept them as separate card types, because you asked for the type exactly as printed. Merging them would need a normalization step that I did not apply.
- **Unit counted:** I counted card rows in `cards`, which is one row per printing (uuid), not distinct card names.
- **Foreign-language filter:** A card qualifies if it has at least one row in `foreign_data`, regardless of language. I used EXISTS so that cards with several translations are not counted twice.
- **Watermark:** I filtered on `watermark = 'azorius'`, which matches 156 cards before the foreign-language filter.

The `Card` term in the ontology is still a draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE SSA IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(LOWER(SSA)) NOT IN ('negative','0','') INTERSECT SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE "U-PRO" IS NOT NULL AND TRIM("U-PRO") NOT IN ('-','0',''))
answer: 15 patients have both an abnormal anti-SSA result and a positive proteinuria finding somewhere in their record. Abnormal anti-SSA means any non-null SSA value other than 'negative' or '0'. Positive proteinuria means any non-null U-PRO value other than '-' or '0', so trace ('TR') counts as positive. The two findings are matched per patient across all visits, not within one visit. The Laboratory Test term used is still in draft status.

sql: select round(avg(height_cm),1) from superhero where publisher_id=(select publisher_id from superhero where superhero_name='A-Bomb') and height_cm>0

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE SEX='F' AND Admission='+' AND "First Date">='1998-01-01' AND "First Date"<'1999-01-01'

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT l.ID) FROM Laboratory l JOIN Examination e ON e.ID = l.ID WHERE l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND l.RNP NOT IN ('0','negative') AND e.Thrombosis = 0

Thrombosis comes from the Examination table. Only 4 patients have a positive RNP and an Examination record, and all 4 have thrombosis 0. The result is the same whichever way the question is read.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(c),1) FROM (SELECT hero_id, COUNT(DISTINCT power_id) c FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id IN (SELECT power_id FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id=19))) GROUP BY hero_id)

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT u.Id) AS user_count FROM users u JOIN badges b ON b.UserId = u.Id WHERE b.Name = 'Yearling' AND b.Date < '2014-01-01' AND (u.Location LIKE '%India' OR u.Location LIKE '%India,%')
answer: 6 users located in India earned a Yearling badge before 1 January 2014. Location matches "India" at the end or followed by a comma (case-insensitive), which excludes Indiana and Indianapolis. Each user is counted once. The ontology terms used (Badge, User) are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(Reputation)) FROM users WHERE Id IN (SELECT OwnerUserId FROM posts WHERE Tags LIKE '%<r>%' AND Score < 20)
answer: 214. This is the average reputation of the distinct users who own posts tagged <r> with Score < 20, rounded to a whole number. Each user is counted once. Averaging per post instead would give 499, because prolific high-reputation users would be counted several times. The R tag was matched with Tags LIKE '%<r>%', which excludes other tags such as <r-faq>. The Post and User terms are draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Examination e ON e.ID=p.ID WHERE p.SEX='F' AND e.Diagnosis LIKE '%SjS%' AND e.Diagnosis NOT LIKE '%SjS susp%'
answer: 20 female patients. I counted distinct patients whose Examination.Diagnosis contains 'SjS', including combinations such as 'SLE, SjS', and excluded any diagnosis containing 'SjS susp' (suspected). The count covers all examination dates.

sql: select artist, count(*) n from cards where borderColor='black' and availability like '%arena%' and power glob '[0-9]*' and cast(power as real)>=10 group by artist having n=(select max(c) from (select count(*) c from cards where borderColor='black' and availability like '%arena%' and power glob '[0-9]*' and cast(power as real)>=10 group by artist))
answer: Three artists tie with 2 cards each: Chase Stone, Jonathan Kuo and Zoltan Boros. I counted each card row (printing) in the database once. I kept only black-bordered rows whose availability includes "arena" and whose printed power is a number of 10 or more. Non-numeric powers such as ∞ and * were excluded. Counted by distinct card name, each of these artists has 1 card, and every artist in the results would then tie at 1.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2 <> '' AND q.q2 < '1:40.000'
answer: 15 drivers set a Q2 time faster than 1:40.000. Every recorded Q2 time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix was under that mark, with the slowest at 1:38.526. I counted only drivers who have a Q2 time recorded.

sql: SELECT notes FROM income WHERE source='Fundraising' AND date_received='2019-09-14'
answer: The note is "Secured donations to help pay for speaker gifts." I read "fundraising proceeds" as income with source 'Fundraising'. That date has exactly one such row, for $200.

sql: SELECT s.superhero_name FROM superhero s INNER JOIN colour c ON s.eye_colour_id = c.id WHERE c.colour = 'No Colour' AND s.height_cm BETWEEN 170 AND 190
answer:
키가 170cm 이상 190cm 이하이고 눈 색 분류가 '알 수 없음'인 히어로는 15명입니다. Chuck Norris, Destroyer, Flash III, Goku, Green Goblin III, Indiana Jones, Judge Dredd, Mister Freeze, One Punch Man, Paul Blart, Robocop, Space Ghost, Stormtrooper, T-1000, Two-Face입니다.

해석한 기준은 두 가지입니다. colour 테이블에는 'Unknown'이라는 값이 없습니다. 그래서 눈 색 정보가 없는 경우를 나타내는 값은 'No Colour'(1건)라고 보고 이 값으로 걸렀습니다. 이 해석은 데이터와 docs에서 직접 확인하지 못한 추정입니다. 키 범위는 170과 190을 모두 포함했습니다. 키가 NULL이거나 0인 히어로는 이 범위에 들어가지 않아 자동으로 빠집니다. 사용한 Term인 Superhero와 Colour는 아직 certified 되지 않은 draft 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT SUM(b.amount) AS total_budgeted FROM budget b WHERE b.link_to_event IN (SELECT e.event_id FROM event e JOIN budget b2 ON b2.link_to_event = e.event_id JOIN expense x ON x.link_to_budget = b2.budget_id WHERE e.event_date >= '2019-09-01' AND e.event_date < '2019-10-01' AND lower(x.expense_description) LIKE '%pizza%');
answer: $965. I counted an event as serving pizza if any expense booked to one of its budget lines has "pizza" in the description. I then summed the amount of all budget lines for those events, in every category. Each event is counted once, so several pizza expenses on one event don't double-count its budget.

sql:
SELECT SUM(n) AS accounts, COUNT(*) AS districts, ROUND(AVG(sal),2) AS avg_salary
FROM (SELECT d.district_id, d.A11 AS sal, COUNT(*) AS n
      FROM account a JOIN district d ON d.district_id=a.district_id
      WHERE a.frequency='POPLATEK MESICNE' AND a.date>='1997-01-01' AND a.date<'1998-01-01'
        AND CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER)>=100000
      GROUP BY d.district_id);
answer: 1997년에 월별 명세서(POPLATEK MESICNE) 계좌가 개설된 인구 10만 명 이상 지구는 46개이고, 개설된 계좌는 모두 569개입니다. 이 46개 지구의 평균 급여(A11)는 9,189.52입니다. 평균은 계좌 수로 가중하지 않고 지구별로 한 번씩만 계산했습니다. 계좌 단위로 평균을 내면 9,829.91로 달라집니다. 인구(A4)는 텍스트로 저장되어 있어 정수로 변환해 비교했습니다.

sql: select 1.0*(select sum(b.amount) from budget b join event e on b.link_to_event=e.event_id where e.event_name='Yearly Kickoff' and b.category='Advertisement')/(select sum(b.amount) from budget b join event e on b.link_to_event=e.event_id where e.event_name='October Meeting' and b.category='Advertisement') as ratio

sql: with c as (select sum(p.publisher_name='DC Comics') dc, sum(p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics') m from superhero s join publisher p on s.publisher_id=p.id) select case when dc=m then 'Tie' when dc>m then 'DC Comics' else 'Marvel Comics' end as publisher, abs(dc-m) as difference from c
