sql: SELECT e.event_name FROM event e JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event=e.event_id WHERE e.status='Closed' GROUP BY e.event_id HAVING ROUND(SUM(b.spent)*1.0/SUM(b.amount),9) = (SELECT MAX(r) FROM (SELECT ROUND(SUM(b2.spent)*1.0/SUM(b2.amount),9) r FROM event e2 JOIN budget b2 ON b2.link_to_event=e2.event_id WHERE e2.status='Closed' GROUP BY e2.event_id))
answer: Three closed events tie at the highest spending-to-budget ratio of 1.01 (spent $20.20 of a $20 budget): Officers meeting - October, Officers meeting - September and Officers meeting - November. I computed each event's total spent divided by its total budget amount, using events with status 'Closed'. The query returns only the event names. I rounded the ratio to 9 decimals so floating-point error doesn't break the tie.

18.67. Landon Donovan's overall rating on 12 July 2013 was 18.67% above the average for that date. For each player I took the latest rating record dated on or before 12 July 2013, so players not updated that day still count. I then kept only players whose defensive work rate in that record was low, medium or high, which drops the malformed values in the data. The same filter applies to Donovan's own record.

sql: SELECT c.name, c.location, c.country, r.year, p.duration FROM pitStops p JOIN races r ON r.raceId = p.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId WHERE p.milliseconds = (SELECT MAX(milliseconds) FROM pitStops)
answer: The longest single pit stop was at Autódromo José Carlos Pace in São Paulo, Brazil, in the 2016 season. It lasted 33:31.266 (33 minutes 31.266 seconds). The query returned one row, so there was no tie. I read "longest" as the maximum milliseconds value with no outlier filtering, so this stop is probably a red-flag stoppage rather than a normal service. The Circuit, Pit Stop and Race terms the query uses are still draft, not certified.

sql: select element, sum(atom_id in (select atom_id from connected) or atom_id in (select atom_id2 from connected)) as bonded_atoms from atom where molecule_id='TR397' group by element order by element
answer: TR397에서 결합에 참여하는 원자 수는 c 34, h 24, n 6, na 0, o 16, s 4입니다. 원자가 `connected` 테이블의 어느 쪽 열에든 나오면 결합에 참여한 것으로 보았습니다. 나트륨(na) 원자 4개는 결합이 없지만 분자에 존재하는 원소라서 0으로 표시했습니다. 0인 행이 필요 없다면 na 행을 빼면 됩니다.

sql:
WITH t AS (
  SELECT m.member_id, m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS full_name,
         COUNT(DISTINCT e.expense_description) AS kinds, SUM(e.cost) AS total
  FROM expense e JOIN member m ON m.member_id = e.link_to_member
  WHERE e.expense_date >= '2019-10-01' AND e.expense_date < '2019-12-01'
  GROUP BY m.member_id
)
SELECT full_name, kinds, total FROM t WHERE kinds = (SELECT MAX(kinds) FROM t);
answer: 두 명이 5종류로 공동 1위입니다. Sacha Harrison은 5종류에 $407.90, Phillip Cullen은 5종류에 $464.99를 썼습니다. 2019년 10월 1일부터 11월 30일까지의 지출을 기준으로 했습니다. 품목 종류는 서로 다른 expense_description 값의 개수로 계산했고, 승인 여부와 관계없이 모든 지출을 포함했습니다. 해당 기간 지출 중 승인 값이 비어 있는 건은 1건입니다. 다만 그 건이 이 기간에 속하는지는 따로 확인하지 않았습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.atom_id2) FROM connected c JOIN atom a ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id WHERE a.element = 'cl'
answer: 271 distinct atoms are bonded to chlorine ('cl') atoms across all molecules. The `connected` table stores each bond in both directions, so I started from the chlorine side and counted distinct neighbour atoms. I read the question as counting atoms, not bonds. Counting chlorine bonds instead gives 314. Some chlorine atoms share a neighbour, which is why the atom count is lower.

sql: select count(distinct l.ID) as patient_count from Laboratory l join Patient p on p.ID=l.ID where l.Date between '1981-01-01' and '1986-12-31' and l.PLT between 100 and 400 and l."U-PRO" in ('1','2','3','4') and p.Birthday is not null and (cast(strftime('%Y',l.Date) as int)-cast(strftime('%Y',p.Birthday) as int)-(strftime('%m-%d',l.Date)<strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)))<50
answer: 45 patients. Assumptions: (1) Age is completed years on the test date, so a birthday later in the year is subtracted. (2) The U-PRO column is text, and the documented normal range is 0 < N < 30. In the 1981–1986 window it only holds grades 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, TR (trace), '%%' and NULL. The numeric values of 30 or more never occur there, so a "30 or more" rule would give 0. I counted proteinuria as grades 1–4 and excluded 0, trace (TR), '%%' and NULL. If trace should count as positive, the number would be higher. (3) A patient is counted once if any one test meets all the conditions at the same time.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(A11),2) AS avg_salary FROM district WHERE district_id IN (SELECT c.district_id FROM disp d JOIN client c ON c.client_id=d.client_id JOIN district dc ON dc.district_id=c.district_id WHERE d.type='OWNER' AND dc.A3='central Bohemia' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM disp d2 JOIN card k ON k.disp_id=d2.disp_id WHERE d2.account_id=d.account_id))
answer: 9357.25. This is the average of the average salary (district.A11) over the distinct districts where the target clients live. The clients are account owners whose own district (client.district_id) is in central Bohemia and whose account has no card on any of its dispositions (owner or disponent). Each district counts once, not once per client. The Client, Disposition and District Terms in the ontology are still drafts.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT e.type, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS members FROM event e JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.event_date >= '2019-09-01' AND e.event_date < '2020-06-01' GROUP BY e.type) SELECT type, members FROM t WHERE members = (SELECT MAX(members) FROM t)
answer: Two event types tie for the most members: Meeting (30) and Registration (30). I counted distinct members per event type, so a member who attended several events of one type counts once. The date filter covers Sept 2019 through May 2020, which is every event in the data. The Event term used is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: select round(avg(l.ALB),4) from Laboratory l join Patient p on p.ID=l.ID where p.SEX='F' and p.Diagnosis='SLE' and l.PLT>400
answer: 평균 ALB는 3.9123입니다. 진단명이 정확히 'SLE'인 여성 환자의 PLT 400 초과 검사 기록을 대상으로 계산했습니다. 'SLE susp'나 'SLE, SJS'처럼 SLE가 일부로 들어간 진단까지 포함하면 4.0이 나옵니다. 질문은 SLE 진단이 기재된 환자를 묻는 것이라 보고, 진단명이 정확히 일치하는 쪽을 택했습니다.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT u.DisplayName AS name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM postHistory h JOIN posts p ON p.Id=h.PostId JOIN users u ON u.Id=h.UserId WHERE p.Title='Why square the difference instead of taking the absolute value in standard deviation?' AND h.Comment IS NOT NULL AND h.Comment<>'' GROUP BY u.Id, u.DisplayName) SELECT name, n FROM c WHERE n=(SELECT MAX(n) FROM c)
answer: mbq left the most edit comments on that post: 3. No one else tied. I counted each revision with a non-empty Comment as its own event, and took the editor name from users.DisplayName via postHistory.UserId, since postHistory.UserDisplayName is often empty. The Post, Post History Event and User terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select s.cname as county, count(*) as qualifying_schools from satscores s join frpm f on f.CDSCode=s.cds where s.rtype='S' and f."Academic Year"='2014-2015' and f."Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)">0.1 and s.NumGE1500>=1 group by s.cname order by 2 desc, 1
answer: 49 counties qualify. Los Angeles has the most qualifying schools (305), then San Diego (86), Orange (62), San Bernardino (60) and Riverside (58). Del Norte has the fewest (1). I counted only school-level SAT rows (rtype='S'), joined to frpm on CDSCode. Each school needed "Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)" above 0.1 and NumGE1500 of at least 1. I used the free-meal rate, not the FRPM rate, and included closed schools because the question doesn't exclude them. Schools with suppressed (NULL) NumGE1500 are not counted. The only academic year in frpm is 2014-2015.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 1) FROM superhero s JOIN colour c ON c.id = s.skin_colour_id WHERE c.colour = 'Green' AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: The average weight of green-skinned heroes is 1354.6 kg. It is based on 15 heroes. The docs say a weight of 0 or NULL means "missing", so I excluded those (6 green heroes have 0). The average is pulled up by one 18,000 kg outlier. The query includes that hero because the value is real, not an error.

sql: select ROUND(AVG(julianday(e.d)-julianday(p."First Date"))) as avg_delay_days from Patient p join (select ID, MIN("Examination Date") d from Examination group by ID) e on e.ID=p.ID where p.Admission like '%+%' and p."First Date" is not null;
answer: 입원 환자의 첫 방문(First Date)부터 첫 검사(Examination Date 최솟값)까지 평균 지연은 약 1616일입니다. 입원 여부는 Admission 값에 '+'가 들어 있으면 입원으로 봤습니다('+', '+(' 모두 포함). 검사 기록이 없는 환자와 첫 방문일이 없는 환자는 평균에서 제외했습니다. 첫 방문일은 Description이 아니라 First Date 컬럼으로 해석했습니다.

sql: select e.type, count(distinct a.link_to_member) as attendee_count from event e left join attendance a on a.link_to_event=e.event_id where e.location='MU 215' group by e.type
answer: MU 215 행사 유형별 참석 회원 수: Election 0명, Guest Speaker 29명, Meeting 30명. 이벤트 상태(planning/open/closed)는 구분하지 않았습니다. 카테고리는 event.type으로 보았고, 같은 회원이 한 유형의 여러 행사에 참석해도 1명으로 계산했습니다(중복 제거). 참석자가 없는 Election도 결과에 포함됩니다.

sql: SELECT s.name, s.releaseDate FROM sets s WHERE s.code IN (SELECT setCode FROM cards WHERE name='Aven Mindcensor' AND frameVersion='2015') ORDER BY s.releaseDate DESC LIMIT 1
answer: Amonkhet Remastered, released 2020-08-13. Aven Mindcensor has printings in frames 'future' (Future Sight) and '2015'. I treated 'future' as an older frame, since it dates from 2007, so 2015 is the newest. Four sets use the 2015 frame: Amonkhet Remastered (2020-08-13), Amonkhet, Amonkhet Invocations and Amonkhet Promos (all 2017-04-28). The most recent release is Amonkhet Remastered, so there is no tie.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(weight_kg),2) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero WHERE weight_kg IS NOT NULL AND weight_kg > 0 AND superhero_name <> '3-D Man' AND id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id IN (SELECT power_id FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id = (SELECT id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name='3-D Man')))
answer: 282411.79 kg. I treated NULL and 0 weights as not recorded, and I excluded 3-D Man himself. A hero counts if they share at least one power with him. Extreme weights (up to 90,000,000 kg) are left in, which makes the average very large. The query relies on the Superhero Term, which is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: select c.name, c.location, c.country, r.year, p.duration from pitStops p join races r on r.raceId=p.raceId join circuits c on c.circuitId=r.circuitId where p.milliseconds=(select max(milliseconds) from pitStops)
answer: The longest single pit stop was at Autódromo José Carlos Pace in São Paulo, Brazil, in the 2016 season. It lasted 33:31.266 (2,011,266 ms), about 33.5 minutes. I compared stops by the milliseconds column, because the duration column is text. Only one stop has that maximum, so the result is one row. The duration column is returned as the stop length.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN P.SEX='F' THEN P.ID END) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN P.SEX='M' THEN P.ID END) AS diff FROM Patient P JOIN Laboratory L ON L.ID=P.ID WHERE P.Diagnosis='RA' AND L.UN < 30
answer: 23. RA 환자 중 요소질소(UN)가 정상(N < 30)이었던 여성은 남성보다 23명 많습니다. 적용한 해석: RA 환자는 Diagnosis가 정확히 'RA'인 환자만 포함했고, 검사 기록 중 한 번이라도 UN < 30인 환자를 한 명으로 셌습니다(중복 제거).

sql: select count(distinct a.account_id) from account a join loan l on l.account_id=a.account_id where a.district_id=1 and a.date<='1995-12-31' and l.status in ('C','D')
answer: 13. I read "belonged to the branch" as district_id = 1 and created on or before 1995-12-31. "Active" means loan status C or D. Accounts are counted once even if they have several loans.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.account_id) FROM account a JOIN loan l ON l.account_id=a.account_id WHERE a.district_id=1 AND a.date<='1995-12-31' AND l.status IN ('C','D')
answer: 13. Readings: branch location 1 = account.district_id = 1; on the books at 31 Dec 1995 = account created on or before 1995-12-31 (no branch-transfer history exists); active loan = status C or D.

sql: SELECT SUM(totalSetSize) FROM sets s WHERE (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT translation) FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode=s.code) < 5;
answer: 45,452 cards in total across 504 sets. Choices I made: a set's size is `totalSetSize`, which includes promos and supplemental printings. Translations are counted as distinct name strings per set. Sets with no translations count as having 0, so they are included. I did not check whether any of these sets have a NULL `totalSetSize`. SUM would skip them.

sql: select r.year, count(*) as total_pit_stops from pitStops p join races r on r.raceId=p.raceId where r.year between 2002 and 2013 and p.raceId in (select s.raceId from driverStandings s join drivers d on d.driverId=s.driverId where d.nationality='Australian' and s.position<20) group by r.year order by r.year
answer: 2011: 1069, 2012: 905, 2013: 898 pit stops. The pitStops table only has data from 2011, so 2002–2010 have no rows and don't appear. I read "better than 20th" as standings position < 20 (strictly, so 20th itself doesn't count). I used the post-race driverStandings row of drivers with nationality 'Australian'. Pit stops are counted for all drivers at the qualifying races.

sql:
WITH cp AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(DISTINCT account) n FROM trans WHERE operation IN ('PREVOD NA UCET','PREVOD Z UCTU') AND account IS NOT NULL GROUP BY account_id)
SELECT a.account_id AS account_number, a.date AS account_opening_date, l.amount AS total_borrowed, COALESCE(cp.n,0) AS counterparty_count, d.A2 AS home_district, CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) AS home_district_population,
RANK() OVER (ORDER BY CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) DESC) AS population_rank
FROM account a
JOIN district bd ON bd.district_id=a.district_id AND bd.A2='Prachatice'
JOIN loan l ON l.account_id=a.account_id
JOIN disp ds ON ds.account_id=a.account_id AND ds.type='OWNER'
JOIN client c ON c.client_id=ds.client_id
JOIN district d ON d.district_id=c.district_id
LEFT JOIN cp ON cp.account_id=a.account_id
ORDER BY population_rank, a.account_id
answer: 14 Prachatice-branch accounts have a loan. Only 2 have owners from other districts: account 8489 (Trutnov, population 121,947, rank 1, 2 counterparties) and account 2762 (Praha - zapad, 75,637, rank 2, 3 counterparties). The other 12 owners live in Prachatice (51,428) and tie at rank 3, ordered by account number. Their counterparty counts run from 1 to 6, and the two cross-district accounts fall within that range, so this small sample shows no clear difference. Choices: total borrowed is the account's single loan amount; a counterparty is a distinct partner account number on transfers to or from another bank (`PREVOD NA UCET`, `PREVOD Z UCTU`) over all dates; the owner is the `OWNER` disposition; population is `district.A4` cast to an integer; ranking uses `RANK()`. The ontology Terms used are all drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT SUM(p.Score) AS total_score FROM postLinks l JOIN posts p ON p.Id = l.PostId JOIN posts t ON t.Id = l.RelatedPostId WHERE t.Title = 'A Probability distribution value exceeding 1 is OK?' AND p.PostTypeId = 1 AND p.Tags LIKE '%<r>%'
answer: The total score is 25. This sums the scores of questions tagged 'r' that link to the question "A Probability distribution value exceeding 1 is OK?". A question that links twice would be counted twice; I did not check for that.

sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS player_count
FROM (
  SELECT pa.player_api_id, pa.volleys,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pa.player_api_id ORDER BY pa.date DESC, pa.id DESC) AS rn
  FROM Player_Attributes pa
) latest
JOIN Player p ON p.player_api_id = latest.player_api_id
WHERE latest.rn = 1 AND p.height > 180 AND latest.volleys > 70
answer: 416 players are over 180 cm and have a volleys score above 70 on their latest rating record. I used the record with the latest date for each player, and the highest id when several share that date. "Over 180" and "above 70" are strict, so exactly 180 cm or exactly 70 volleys does not count. A null volleys value on the latest record does not count either. The Player and Player Attributes terms are still draft (uncertified).

sql: SELECT s.name, s.releaseDate FROM sets s WHERE s.type=(SELECT type FROM sets WHERE name='From the Vault: Lore') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode=s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(t.translation)<>'') ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.name
answer: Three sets of type from_the_vault (the same type as "From the Vault: Lore") have no foreign-language name: From the Vault: Dragons (2008-08-29), From the Vault: Transform (2017-11-24) and Commander Collection: Green (2020-12-04). "From the Vault: Lore" itself has translations, so it is excluded. I read "never received a name" as having no non-null, non-empty translation in set_translations, which covers sets with no rows and sets whose rows are all null. The Card Set and Set Translation terms the query relies on are still draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.SEX='F' THEN p.ID END) AS F, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.SEX='M' THEN p.ID END) AS M FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE l.Date>='1994-01-01' AND l.Date<='1994-12-31' AND l.GOT<60
answer: F: 80, M: 16. I read "normal GOT" as GOT < 60 (the normal range in the docs). A patient counts once if any 1994 test had a normal GOT. Patients with no recorded sex are not counted.

sql: SELECT SUM(i.amount) AS total_dues FROM income i WHERE i.source = 'Dues' AND i.link_to_member IN (SELECT a.link_to_member FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.event_name = 'Football game')
answer: Members who attended the Football game paid $1,100 in membership dues in total. I counted a member if they attended either of the two events named 'Football game', and counted each member once so their dues aren't doubled. Dues are the income rows with source = 'Dues'. The Event and Income terms in the ontology are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Patient WHERE LOWER(Diagnosis) LIKE '%psoriatic arthritis%'
answer: 2 patients. I used the Patient table's Diagnosis column and matched 'psoriatic arthritis' without regard to case, because the data spells it two ways ('Psoriatic Arthritis' and 'Psoriatic arthritis'), one patient each. I applied no time or follow-up filter.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT d.forename||' '||d.surname AS n, r.name AS rn, r.year AS ry, q.q3 AS t FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId WHERE d.nationality='British' AND CAST(substr(d.dob,1,4) AS INTEGER)>1980 AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3<>'' AND q.q3 LIKE '_:__.___') SELECT n AS driver_full_name, rn AS race_name, ry AS race_year, t AS q3_time FROM c WHERE t=(SELECT MIN(t) FROM c)
answer: Lewis Hamilton set the fastest Q3 time among British drivers born after 1980: 1:04.424 at the 2017 Austrian Grand Prix. There is no tie, so the query returns one row. I read "British" as nationality = 'British' and "born after 1980" as a birth year above 1980. "Fastest" is the lowest Q3 time. The Driver, Race and Qualifying Result terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select count(*) from Patient p where exists(select 1 from Examination e where e.ID=p.ID) and not exists(select 1 from Examination e where e.ID=p.ID and e.Thrombosis<>0) and exists(select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and l.SM in ('negative','0')) and exists(select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and l."U-PRO" in ('30','100','300','>=300','>=1000','+1(30)','+2(100)'));
answer: 2 patients. Assumptions: "no thrombosis" means the patient has at least one examination and none of them has Thrombosis other than 0. Significant proteinuria means a U-PRO value of 30, 100, 300, >=300, >=1000, +1(30) or +2(100). Values of 0-4, '-', 'TR', '-15' and '%%' were treated as not significant.

sql: select frameVersion, count(*) from cards where artist='John Avon' and cardKingdomFoilId is not null and cardKingdomId is not null and frameVersion glob '[0-9]*' group by frameVersion having frameVersion=(select max(frameVersion) from cards where artist='John Avon' and cardKingdomFoilId is not null and cardKingdomId is not null and frameVersion glob '[0-9]*')
answer: 가장 최근 프레임 연도는 2015이고, 해당 카드는 100장입니다. 'powerful foil'은 문서 설명(cardKingdomFoilId가 cardKingdomId와 함께 있으면 매우 강력함)에 따라 두 ID가 모두 있는 카드로 해석했습니다. 'future'라는 프레임 버전이 1장 있지만 연도가 아니므로 제외했습니다. 포함하면 결과는 future 1장입니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE ','||REPLACE(keywords,', ',',')||',' LIKE '%,Flying,%' AND ','||REPLACE(keywords,', ',',')||',' LIKE '%,Cycling,%'
answer: 32 cards (printings) have both Flying and Cycling in their keywords. Each printing counts as its own card, so this is a row count rather than a count of distinct names. I matched Flying and Cycling as whole items in the comma-separated keywords column. Variants such as Landcycling or Swampcycling do not count. The Card Term the query relies on is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: select count(*) from cards where duelDeck='b' and hasFoil=0 and power glob '[0-9]*' and CAST(power AS INTEGER)<3
answer: 213 cards in duel deck B have hasFoil=0 and a numeric power below 3 (power 0: 13, 1: 74, 2: 126). Cards with no power (non-creatures) and variable power '*' are excluded, since they have no numeric power below 3.

sql: select d.nationality from qualifying q join drivers d on d.driverId=q.driverId where q.raceId=(select raceId from races where year=2017 and name='Italian Grand Prix') and q.q3=(select min(q3) from qualifying where raceId=(select raceId from races where year=2017 and name='Italian Grand Prix') and coalesce(q3,'')<>'')
answer: British. The driver with the fastest Q3 time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix (raceId 981) is British, and no other driver shares that time. The q3 times are text in m:ss.mmm format, so the lowest string is also the fastest time. I left out NULL and empty q3 values.

sql: select p.Admission, count(*) as patients, round(avg(cast((strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',p.Birthday)) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09')<strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)) as int)),1) as avg_age from Patient p where p.Admission in ('+','-') and p.Birthday is not null and p.ID in (select ID from Laboratory where RBC<3.5) group by p.Admission
answer: 입원(+) 환자는 41명이고 평균 만 나이는 70.3세, 외래(-) 환자는 29명이고 평균 만 나이는 73.6세입니다. 기준일은 2026-10-09입니다. RBC가 3.5 미만인 검사 결과가 한 번이라도 있는 환자를 한 명으로 계산했습니다. Admission 값이 정확히 '+' 또는 '-'인 환자만 포함했습니다. '+(' 같은 변형 값과 빈 값은 제외했습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cards.name) AS card_count FROM cards INNER JOIN legalities ON cards.uuid = legalities.uuid WHERE cards.manaCost = '{0}' AND legalities.format = 'commander' AND legalities.status = 'Legal'
answer: 43 different cards have a printed mana cost of {0} and are legal in Commander. I counted distinct card names, since the cards table has one row per printing. I required manaCost to equal '{0}' exactly and the Commander legality status to be 'Legal', so banned and restricted cards are excluded. The Card and Card Legality ontology terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select d.forename||' '||d.surname as full_name from lapTimes l join drivers d using(driverId) group by d.driverId order by min(l.milliseconds), d.driverId limit 20
answer: 각 드라이버의 최단 랩(lapTimes.milliseconds 최솟값) 기준으로 중복 없이 20명을 뽑았습니다. 1위는 Lewis Hamilton, 이어서 Daniel Ricciardo, Kimi Räikkönen, Sebastian Vettel, Valtteri Bottas 순이며 20위는 Pascal Wehrlein입니다. 한 드라이버가 여러 번 등장하지 않도록 드라이버별 최단 기록으로 해석했습니다.

sql: select round((max(milliseconds)-min(milliseconds))*100.0/max(milliseconds),2) from results r join races ra using(raceId) where ra.year=1988 and ra.name like '%Australian%' and milliseconds is not null
answer: 1.16%. I took the winner's time (1:53:14.676) and the time of the last finisher who completed all 82 laps and has a recorded time (4th place, 1:54:34.764). Later finishers were laps down or had no time.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(ha.attribute_value), 1) AS avg_intelligence
FROM superhero AS s
INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id
INNER JOIN attribute AS a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id AND a.attribute_name = 'Intelligence'
WHERE ha.attribute_value IS NOT NULL
  AND s.id IN (
    SELECT hp.hero_id FROM hero_power AS hp
    INNER JOIN superpower AS sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id
    WHERE sp.power_name IN ('Super Speed', 'Death Touch'))
answer: The average intelligence score of heroes with Super Speed or Death Touch is 85.9. Each hero is counted once, even if they have both powers, and heroes with no intelligence score are excluded. The result relies on draft (uncertified) Terms.

sql: select p.Admission, count(distinct p.ID) as patients from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where cast(l.RNP as real)>16 and l.RNP glob '[0-9]*' and p.Admission in ('+','-') group by p.Admission
answer: 7 patients were admitted ('+') and 4 were followed at the outpatient clinic ('-'). I counted a patient if any lab reading had a numeric RNP above 16; in this data those readings are 64 and 256. I counted each patient once. The RNP values 'negative' and '0' were not counted, and neither was 16. I left out 3 patients whose Admission is '+(' and those with a blank Admission, because the question names only '+' and '-'.

sql:
WITH r AS (
  SELECT p.ID, CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) AS lvl
  FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID
  WHERE p."First Date" >= '1991-01-01' AND p."First Date" < '1992-01-01'
    AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND l.RNP <> 'negative'
), m AS (SELECT ID, MAX(lvl) AS lvl FROM r GROUP BY ID)
SELECT ID, lvl AS RNP FROM m WHERE lvl = (SELECT MAX(lvl) FROM m) ORDER BY ID
answer: Three patients tie at the highest anti-RNP level (256) among those whose first hospital visit (Patient."First Date") was in 1991: IDs 912147, 4632548 and 4649885. Choices made: patients with no First Date are excluded. RNP is stored as text, so I compared it as a number, and I treated "negative" as no measurable level. Where a patient has several measurements, I used their highest. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are draft, not certified.

sql: select round(100.0*count(distinct case when r.statusId=1 or s.status like '+%' then r.driverId end)/count(distinct r.driverId),2) as pct_classified from results r join races ra using(raceId) join status s using(statusId) where ra.year=1957 and ra.name='British Grand Prix' and r.statusId not in (81,97)
answer: 52.63%. 10 of the 19 drivers in the 1957 British Grand Prix were classified finishers. I counted a driver as classified if their status was 'Finished' or a lapped finish ('+N Laps'). The race has 22 result rows but only 19 distinct drivers because of shared drives, so I counted drivers, not rows. A driver counts as classified if any of their rows is a classified finish. Counting rows instead would give 10 of 22, or 45.45%.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.atom_id2) FROM connected c JOIN atom a1 ON c.atom_id = a1.atom_id WHERE a1.element = 'cl'
answer: 271 atoms are bonded to chlorine ('cl') across all molecules. This counts distinct atoms that have a bond to a chlorine atom, using the `connected` table (every bond appears in both directions) with chlorine as the first atom. The `Atom` ontology term used is still a draft.

sql: SELECT id FROM cards WHERE borderColor='borderless' AND (cardKingdomId IS NULL OR cardKingdomFoilId IS NULL)
answer: I read "lacks a regular-version listing or a foil-version listing" as: the printing has a borderless border and either cardKingdomId (regular) or cardKingdomFoilId (foil) is NULL. The query ran without errors. I only viewed the first 5 rows (23004, 25350, 25355, 25357, 25359) and did not count the full result. It relies on the Card term, which is still a draft and not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(e."aCL IgM"),2) AS avg_acl_igm FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=e.ID WHERE ','||replace(replace(p.Diagnosis,' ',''),char(29),',')||',' LIKE '%,SJS,%' AND e."aCL IgM" > 0
answer: 평균 anti-cardiolipin IgM 농도는 2.89입니다. Patient.Diagnosis 항목 중 정확히 'SJS'인 환자만 포함했고(다른 진단과 함께 적힌 경우도 포함, 'SJS susp'는 제외), 값이 0인 검사는 평균에서 뺐습니다. 날짜 제한은 두지 않았습니다.

sql:
SELECT e.event_name
FROM event e
LEFT JOIN (SELECT link_to_event, SUM(amount) AS b FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event) bt ON bt.link_to_event = e.event_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.link_to_event, SUM(x.cost) AS s, COUNT(x.expense_id) AS n FROM budget b JOIN expense x ON x.link_to_budget = b.budget_id GROUP BY b.link_to_event) et ON et.link_to_event = e.event_id
WHERE e.status = 'Closed' AND COALESCE(et.s,0) <= COALESCE(bt.b,0)
ORDER BY COALESCE(et.n,0) DESC, e.event_id ASC
LIMIT 1
answer: October Speaker. Readings I chose: "purchases" means expense records, and "total spending" is the sum of expense costs against the sum of budget amounts. Both are totalled per event. Events with no budget lines or no expenses count as 0 and stay in. Ties go to the alphabetically first event_id. The Event, Budget and Expense terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS hydrogen_bond_count FROM connected c JOIN atom a1 ON a1.atom_id=c.atom_id JOIN atom a2 ON a2.atom_id=c.atom_id2 WHERE a1.molecule_id=(SELECT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element='y') AND (a1.element='h' OR a2.element='h')
answer: 2 bonds in the yttrium-containing molecule have a hydrogen atom at one end. I counted distinct bonds, since `connected` stores each bond in both directions. I read "hydrogen bonding pattern" as bonds involving hydrogen, not intermolecular hydrogen bonds. The result relies on the draft `Atom` Term.

sql:
SELECT r.year, ROUND(AVG(s.milliseconds)/1000.0, 2) AS mean_winner_seconds
FROM results s JOIN races r ON r.raceId = s.raceId
WHERE s.positionOrder = 1 AND s.milliseconds IS NOT NULL AND r.year < 1975
GROUP BY r.year ORDER BY r.year
answer:
The query returns 25 rows, one for each year from 1950 to 1974. The mean winner time falls from 9712.60 s in 1950 to 6047.11 s in 1974, with a peak of 11323.32 s in 1957.

I took the winner to be the result row with positionOrder = 1. I counted only races where that row has a recorded time in milliseconds, and I divided by 1000 to get seconds. The mean is taken per year over those races. ROUND on the exact mean gives two decimals, and SQLite rounds halves away from zero. The Race and Race Result terms I used are still draft in the ontology.

sql: select b.bond_id, b.molecule_id from bond b join molecule m on m.molecule_id=b.molecule_id where m.label='+' and exists(select 1 from atom a where a.molecule_id=b.molecule_id and not exists(select 1 from atom o where o.element=a.element and o.molecule_id<>a.molecule_id));
answer: 112개 결합이 해당합니다. 발암성('+') 분자 중 다른 어떤 분자에도 없는 원소를 가진 분자(TR238, TR430 등)에 속한 모든 결합입니다. 해석: 그런 원소를 가진 분자의 모든 결합을 반환했고, 그 원소가 들어 있는 결합만 고르지는 않았습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM frpm f JOIN schools s USING(CDSCode) WHERE s.County='Los Angeles' AND s.Charter=0 AND f."Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)" < 0.0018
answer: 1 non-charter Los Angeles County school has a K-12 free-meal percentage below 0.18%. The percent column is a 0-1 fraction, so 0.18% is 0.0018. Reading the threshold as a raw value of 0.18 (18%) would give 201 instead.

For all three card types (classic, gold and junior), the smallest home district is Jesenik, with 42,821 inhabitants. No ties turned up. I read "home district" as the district of the client who holds the card. A card is linked to its holder through the disp table, which covers both owners and disponents. The inhabitants column (A4) is stored as text, so I cast it to integer before taking the minimum.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(s.NumTstTakr,0)),2) AS avg_sat_test_takers FROM schools sc LEFT JOIN satscores s ON s.cds = sc.CDSCode AND s.rtype='S' WHERE sc.County='Los Angeles' AND sc.OpenDate >= '2007-01-01' AND sc.OpenDate < '2008-01-01' AND sc.DOC IN ('00','52','54','56') AND sc.CDSCode NOT LIKE '%0000000'
answer: 14.57 average SAT test takers per school. Reading used: school-level records only (district-level records excluded); run by a school district means DOC 00 (county office of education), 52 (elementary), 54 (unified) or 56 (high school district); opened from 2007-01-01 through 2007-12-31; schools with no SAT record count as 0. The School and SAT Score Record Terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
WITH rare AS (SELECT element FROM atom GROUP BY element HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id)=1)
SELECT a.molecule_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS bond_count
FROM atom a
JOIN rare r ON r.element=a.element
JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id=a.molecule_id AND m.label='+'
JOIN connected c ON c.atom_id=a.atom_id
GROUP BY a.molecule_id ORDER BY a.molecule_id
answer: Two carcinogenic molecules qualify: TR430 (6 bonds) and TR499 (1 bond). I treated an element as rare if its atoms appear in exactly one molecule, carcinogenic or not. The bond count is the number of distinct bonds that touch at least one atom of the rare element in that molecule, so a bond between two atoms of that element counts once. The Atom and Molecule terms the query relies on are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT Id FROM users WHERE DisplayName='Michael' AND Age IS NOT NULL ORDER BY Age ASC, Id ASC LIMIT 1
answer: 27969. I read "youngest" as the lowest Age value, and I excluded accounts with no Age recorded. That value is null for 79% of users. The youngest Michael is 17. The next youngest are 28 and 29, so there is no tie.

sql: SELECT s.name, s.releaseDate FROM sets s WHERE s.type = (SELECT type FROM sets WHERE name='From the Vault: Lore') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode=s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(t.translation)<>'') ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.name
answer: Three sets share the type of "From the Vault: Lore" (from_the_vault) and have no non-null foreign-language name: From the Vault: Dragons (2008-08-29), From the Vault: Transform (2017-11-24), Commander Collection: Green (2020-12-04). "Never received a name" was read as no non-empty translation row in set_translations, which includes sets with no rows at all. Card Set and Set Translation Terms are still draft.

sql: select count(*) from superhero s left join race r on r.id=s.race_id where s.publisher_id=(select publisher_id from superhero where superhero_name='A-Bomb') and (r.id is null or r.race='-');
answer: 171 characters. A-Bomb's publisher is Marvel Comics. I counted "no race listed" as either a missing race_id (1 character) or the placeholder race '-' (170 characters).

sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.alignment='Good' THEN s.id END) / COUNT(DISTINCT s.id), 2) AS pct
FROM superhero s
JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id = a.id
JOIN hero_power hp ON hp.hero_id = s.id
WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics'
answer: 64.97 (Marvel Comics 히어로 중 슈퍼파워가 한 건 이상 기록된 히어로를 기준으로, 선(Good) 비율입니다.)

sql: select round(100.0*sum(SEX='F')/count(*),1) as female_pct from Patient p where SEX in ('F','M') and cast(substr(Birthday,1,4) as int) between 1936 and 1956 and not exists (select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and l.CPK>=250)
answer: 85.3% of the group are women (353 women out of 414 men and women). I used birth years 1936 to 1956 inclusive, and counted a patient as exceeding the range only if some CPK result was 250 or higher. Patients with no CPK results stay in the group. Patients with a blank sex value are left out of the denominator.

sql:
SELECT s.School AS school_name, s.Phone AS phone, s.Website AS website, t.AvgScrRead AS avg_sat_reading, t.AvgScrMath AS avg_sat_math, t.AvgScrWrite AS avg_sat_writing, s.Charter AS is_charter, f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enrollment_k12_2014_15, ROUND(f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)" * 100, 2) AS frpm_percent, m.max_math AS highest_avg_sat_math, m.max_math - t.AvgScrMath AS points_below_highest
FROM schools s
LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode
LEFT JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode
CROSS JOIN (SELECT MAX(t2.AvgScrMath) AS max_math FROM satscores t2 JOIN schools s2 ON s2.CDSCode = t2.cds WHERE s2.StatusType = 'Active' AND t2.rtype = 'S' AND t2.NumTstTakr >= 10) m
WHERE s.CDSCode = '07618040113118'
answer: Dougherty Valley High, phone (925) 479-6400, website www.srvusd.net. Average SAT scores: reading 604, math 651, writing 613. Not a charter school. 2014-15 K-12 enrollment is 2,645, and 5.90% of students are eligible for free or reduced price meals. The highest average SAT math among active schools with at least 10 test takers is 699, so this school is 48 points below it. Assumptions: the stored CDS code has a leading zero ('07618040113118'); the meal percentage is the FRPM share (free and reduced-price together) times 100; the highest score uses school-level SAT rows only (not district rows). The ontology Terms used are draft, not certified.

sql: with c as (select f.language, count(distinct f.uuid) n from foreign_data f where f.flavorText is not null and f.flavorText<>'' and f.language in (select language from set_translations) group by f.language) select language, n from c where n=(select min(n) from c) order by language
answer: Korean has the fewest, with 6,782 printings whose flavor text was translated into Korean. Languages were limited to those in set_translations (10 languages). A printing is a distinct card uuid in foreign_data with a non-empty flavorText in that language. Empty-string flavor texts are excluded, which is why this is lower than Korean's 9,692 raw rows. No other language ties.

sql:
WITH t AS (SELECT team_api_id id FROM Team WHERE team_long_name='KSV Cercle Brugge'),
lm AS (SELECT MAX(m.date) d FROM Match m, t WHERE m.season='2012/2013' AND t.id IN (m.home_team_api_id,m.away_team_api_id))
SELECT ta.buildUpPlaySpeedClass FROM Team_Attributes ta, t, lm
WHERE ta.team_api_id=t.id AND ta.date<=lm.d ORDER BY ta.date DESC LIMIT 1;
answer: Fast. The snapshot in effect was dated 2012-02-22. The next snapshot, from 2013-09-20, came after the season's last match.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(u.UpVotes),2) AS avg_upvotes, ROUND(AVG(u.Age),2) AS avg_age FROM users u WHERE u.Id IN (SELECT OwnerUserId FROM posts WHERE CreaionDate >= '2012-01-01' AND CreaionDate < '2013-01-01' AND OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY OwnerUserId HAVING COUNT(*) > 10)
answer: 2012년에 게시글을 10개 넘게 작성한 사용자의 평균 추천 투표 수(UpVotes)는 505.63, 평균 나이는 36.14입니다. 질문과 답변을 모두 게시글로 셌고, 게시글 생성일은 `posts.CreaionDate`(원래 오타인 컬럼명)로 2012년 범위를 걸렀습니다. 나이가 비어 있는 사용자는 평균에서 제외됩니다. 쿼리에 쓴 Post, User 항목은 아직 draft 상태입니다.

sql: select round(100.0*count(distinct case when a.defensive_work_rate='high' then p.player_api_id end)/count(distinct p.player_api_id),2) as pct_high from Player p join Player_Attributes a on a.player_api_id=p.player_api_id where p.birthday>='1991' and a.defensive_work_rate in ('high','medium','low');
answer: 17.41. I counted only players born in 1991 or later with at least one valid rating (high, medium or low). Other values in the column, such as numbers and typos, were treated as no rating. A player counts as high if any of their records is high.

sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN substr(e.event_date,1,4)='2019' THEN b.spent ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN substr(e.event_date,1,4)='2020' THEN b.spent ELSE 0 END) AS difference FROM budget b INNER JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
answer: Total spent on events in 2019 minus the total in 2020 is 2086.05 dollars. I read "spent on events" as budget.spent summed per event and grouped by the year of the event date, because the expense table only has 2019 dates. The Budget and Event Terms the query relies on are drafts, not certified.

sql:
select round(avg(p.height),2) as avg_height_cm from Player p join (
 select player_api_id, defensive_work_rate d, row_number() over (partition by player_api_id order by date desc, id desc) rn
 from Player_Attributes where defensive_work_rate in ('low','medium','high')) a
 on a.player_api_id=p.player_api_id and a.rn=1
where a.d='medium' and p.birthday>='1990-01-01' and p.birthday<'1996-01-01';
answer: 평균 키는 180.85cm입니다. 각 선수의 가장 최근 기록 중 등급이 있는 것(low, medium, high)을 기준으로 삼았습니다. 이 등급이 medium이고 1990년 1월 1일부터 1995년 12월 31일 사이에 태어난 선수만 계산했습니다. 데이터에 섞여 있는 '0', '1', 'o', 'ormal' 같은 값과 빈 값은 등급으로 보지 않고 건너뛰었습니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(s.NumTstTakr,0)),2) FROM schools c LEFT JOIN satscores s ON s.cds=c.CDSCode WHERE c.CharterNum='0756' AND c.MailCity='San Diego'
answer: The average is 41.33 SAT test takers per school. It covers 6 schools. I read "charter number 756" as the stored value '0756', because CharterNum is zero-padded text. I counted all statuses and treated a missing SAT record as 0.

sql: select d.forename, d.surname from results r join drivers d using(driverId) where d.dob between '1980-01-01' and '1990-12-31' and r.fastestLapSpeed is not null group by d.driverId order by max(cast(r.fastestLapSpeed as real)) desc, d.dob asc, d.surname asc limit 3
answer: Fernando Alonso (253.874 km/h), Antônio Pizzonia (253.566), Jenson Button (252.262). I read "born between 1980 and 1990" as dob from 1980-01-01 to 1990-12-31, and I used each driver's highest fastestLapSpeed in results, cast from text to a number.

sql: select t.team_long_name from Team_Attributes a join Team t on t.team_api_id=a.team_api_id where substr(a.date,1,4)='2012' and a.buildUpPlayPassing > (select avg(buildUpPlayPassing) from Team_Attributes where substr(date,1,4)='2012');
answer: The query returns 129 rows, one for each 2012 attribute record with buildUpPlayPassing above the 2012 average of about 49.33. I read "average" as the average across 2012 records, not across all years. I did not de-duplicate team names, because each team has at most one record per year.

sql: select element, count(distinct case when atom_id in (select atom_id from connected union select atom_id2 from connected) then atom_id end) as bonded_atoms from atom where molecule_id='TR397' group by element order by element
answer: TR397 안에서 결합에 참여하는 원자 수는 c 34, h 24, n 6, na 0, o 16, s 4개입니다. 질문이 "분자에 있는 각 원소"를 묻고 있어 na(원자 4개, 결합 없음)도 0으로 포함했습니다. 결합 참여 여부는 connected 테이블의 atom_id와 atom_id2 양쪽을 모두 확인해 판단했습니다.

sql:
WITH e AS (SELECT DISTINCT link_to_event AS id FROM budget WHERE category = 'Advertisement' AND link_to_event IS NOT NULL)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(c), 2) AS avg_attendance FROM (SELECT id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event = e.id) AS c FROM e)
answer: 12.53 members per event on average. I counted every event with an 'Advertisement' budget line (15 events, no date filter). Events with no attendance records count as 0 attendees. If you only counted the 7 events that have attendance records, the average would be 26.86.

sql:
WITH t AS (
 SELECT DISTINCT c.type AS card_type, d.A2 AS district, CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) AS inh, d.district_id
 FROM card c JOIN disp p ON p.disp_id=c.disp_id JOIN client cl ON cl.client_id=p.client_id JOIN district d ON d.district_id=cl.district_id)
SELECT card_type, district, inh AS inhabitants FROM t t1
WHERE inh=(SELECT MIN(inh) FROM t t2 WHERE t2.card_type=t1.card_type)
ORDER BY card_type, district;
answer: For all three card types (classic, gold, junior), the smallest home district among card-holding clients is Jesenik, with 42,821 inhabitants. There were no ties. I read "clients holding that type" as clients linked through disp to a card of that type, and "home district" as the client's own district. Inhabitants come from district.A4, which is stored as text, so I cast it to integer.

sql: SELECT code, releaseDate FROM sets s WHERE releaseDate BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.language = 'Spanish' AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND t.translation <> '')
answer: The query returns 34 rows, which is every set released in 2020, each with its set code and release date. None of the 2020 sets has a Spanish name. I counted a set as having no Spanish name if it has no 'Spanish' row in set_translations, or if that row's translation is NULL or empty. The data has 24 Spanish rows with a NULL translation, so the NULL case matters. I took "calendar year 2020" as release dates from 2020-01-01 through 2020-12-31.

sql:
SELECT CAST(ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg)) AS INTEGER) AS avg_weight_kg
FROM superhero s
JOIN hero_attribute h ON h.hero_id = s.id AND h.attribute_id = 2
WHERE h.attribute_value = (SELECT h2.attribute_value FROM hero_attribute h2 JOIN superhero s2 ON s2.id = h2.hero_id WHERE s2.superhero_name = 'Hulk' AND h2.attribute_id = 2)
  AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: 2106589 kg. Hulk's Strength is 100, and 47 heroes with that score have a recorded weight. I treated weight_kg of 0 or NULL as unknown, since the docs say both mean missing, and left those heroes out. The average is very large because Godzilla is listed at 90,000,000 kg, and I kept him in because you asked for every hero.

sql: SELECT s.type, COUNT(CASE WHEN t.setCode IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) AS translated_set_count, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.setCode IS NOT NULL THEN s.totalSetSize END), 0) AS total_cards FROM sets s LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT setCode FROM set_translations WHERE translation IS NOT NULL AND translation <> '') t ON t.setCode = s.code GROUP BY s.type ORDER BY s.type;
answer: The query returns all 19 set types in alphabetical order. For each type it gives the number of sets that have at least one non-empty translation in set_translations, and the sum of those sets' totalSetSize. I read "total number of cards" as the sets table's totalSetSize, not a count of rows in cards. Examples: expansion has 61 sets and 14,023 cards, core has 13 sets and 4,584 cards, and funny, promo and token have 0 and 0.

sql: WITH s AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT e.expense_description) AS kinds, SUM(e.cost) AS total FROM expense e JOIN member m ON m.member_id = e.link_to_member WHERE e.expense_date >= '2019-10-01' AND e.expense_date < '2019-12-01' GROUP BY m.member_id) SELECT full_name, kinds, total FROM s WHERE kinds = (SELECT MAX(kinds) FROM s)
answer: Two members tie with 5 kinds of items each in Oct–Nov 2019: Sacha Harrison ($407.90) and Phillip Cullen ($464.99). Assumptions: "kinds of items" = distinct expense_description values; the period is 2019-10-01 to 2019-11-30; unapproved expenses are included. The Expense and Member terms are still draft (uncertified).

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.Admission = '-' AND l.RNP IN ('0', 'negative')
answer: 41 patients. Reading used: outpatient-only means Admission = '-'. A normal RNP result means RNP is '0' or 'negative', with at least one such test per patient. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still draft (uncertified).

sql: WITH m AS (SELECT substr(Date,1,4) y, Date, SUM(Consumption) t FROM yearmonth WHERE substr(Date,1,4) IN ('2012','2013') GROUP BY Date) SELECT CAST(ROUND((SELECT MAX(t) FROM m WHERE y='2013') - (SELECT MAX(t) FROM m WHERE y='2012')) AS INTEGER) AS difference
answer: The 2013 peak month's total consumption was 338,745,665 units higher than the 2012 peak month's. Total consumption is the sum of Consumption over all customers per month. Data covers 201112 to 201311, so 2013 is January to November only. The Monthly Customer Consumption Term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.text) FROM rulings r JOIN cards c ON c.uuid = r.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Mishra''s Factory' AND r.date = (SELECT MAX(r2.date) FROM rulings r2 JOIN cards c2 ON c2.uuid = r2.uuid WHERE c2.name = 'Mishra''s Factory')
answer: 2. On the latest ruling date for Mishra's Factory (2016-06-08), there were 2 distinct rulings. The table stores each ruling once per printing, so that date has 46 rows (2 rulings × 23 printings), and I counted distinct ruling texts. If you want raw rows instead, the count is 46.

sql: select round(avg(coalesce(s.NumTstTakr,0)),2) from schools c left join satscores s on s.cds=c.CDSCode where c.County='Los Angeles' and c.OpenDate>='2007-01-01' and c.OpenDate<'2008-01-01' and c.DOC in ('00','52','54','56')
answer: 14.57 SAT test takers per school on average. This covers 47 Los Angeles County schools that opened in 2007. I counted a school as district-run if its District Ownership Code is county office of education, elementary, unified or high school district. That excluded one State Board of Education school. Schools with no SAT record count as 0.

sql: select s.School,s.District,s.County,t.AvgScrWrite from satscores t join schools s on s.CDSCode=t.cds where t.rtype='S' and s.StatusType='Closed' and t.AvgScrWrite is not null and t.AvgScrWrite=(select max(t2.AvgScrWrite) from satscores t2 join schools s2 on s2.CDSCode=t2.cds where t2.rtype='S' and s2.StatusType='Closed' and t2.AvgScrWrite<(select max(t3.AvgScrWrite) from satscores t3 join schools s3 on s3.CDSCode=t3.cds where t3.rtype='S' and s3.StatusType='Closed'))
answer: FAME Public Charter (district: Alameda County Office of Education, county: Alameda) had the second-highest average SAT writing score among closed schools, at 505. The highest is 579, at Northcoast Preparatory and Performing Arts Academy. I used only school-level rows (rtype='S'), because the satscores table also has district-level rows. Those would otherwise add a spurious 515 entry for a closed district record with no school name. District and county come from the schools table. No other school shares the 505 score.

sql:
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN m.label='+' THEN 1 WHEN m.label='-' THEN -1 ELSE 0 END) FILTER (WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bond b WHERE b.molecule_id=m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type<>'-')) AS all_single_diff,
SUM(CASE WHEN m.label='+' THEN 1 WHEN m.label='-' THEN -1 ELSE 0 END) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bond b WHERE b.molecule_id=m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type<>'-')) AS other_diff
FROM molecule m
answer: Molecules with only single bonds: carcinogenic minus non-carcinogenic = 9. All other molecules: -48. A molecule counts as all-single if it has no bond whose type is not '-'. Every molecule has at least one bond, so none is counted by default. The Molecule and Bond terms are still draft, not certified.

sql: select sum(c.colour='No Colour')-sum(c.colour='Blue') from superhero s join colour c on c.id=s.eye_colour_id where s.weight_kg is null or s.weight_kg=0
answer: 122. I treated weight as unrecorded when weight_kg is NULL or 0, because the docs say both mean the weight is missing. I used eye colour names from the colour table.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg),2) AS avg_weight_kg
FROM hero_attribute ha
JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id=a.id
JOIN superhero s ON ha.hero_id=s.id
WHERE a.attribute_name='Intelligence'
AND s.weight_kg IS NOT NULL AND s.weight_kg>0
AND ha.attribute_value = (SELECT ha2.attribute_value FROM hero_attribute ha2 JOIN attribute a2 ON ha2.attribute_id=a2.id JOIN superhero s2 ON ha2.hero_id=s2.id WHERE a2.attribute_name='Intelligence' AND s2.superhero_name='Abomination')
answer: The average weight is 103.6 kg. The cohort is every hero whose Intelligence score equals Abomination's, with Abomination included. Heroes with a missing weight (NULL or 0) are left out. The Terms used (Attribute, Hero Attribute Score, Superhero) are draft, not certified.

sql: select max(cast(frameVersion as int))-min(cast(frameVersion as int)) as years from cards where name='Tarmogoyf' and frameVersion glob '[0-9]*'
answer: 12년입니다. Tarmogoyf 인쇄본의 프레임 스타일은 2003, 2015, future 세 가지입니다. 'future'는 연도가 아니라서 제외했고, 2015 − 2003 = 12로 계산했습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT s.code) FROM sets s JOIN set_translations t ON t.setCode = s.code WHERE s.block = 'Ice Age' AND t.language = 'Italian' AND t.translation IS NOT NULL
answer: 1. Only Coldsnap (CSP, 'Ondata Glaciale') has an Italian translation. The Ice Age set (ICE) has an Italian row, but its translation value is empty (NULL), so I did not count it. If you count any Italian row, the answer would be 2.

sql: SELECT CASE MIN(CASE substr(GSserved,1,instr(GSserved,'-')-1) WHEN 'K' THEN 0 ELSE CAST(substr(GSserved,1,instr(GSserved,'-')-1) AS INTEGER) END) WHEN 0 THEN 'K' ELSE MIN(CASE substr(GSserved,1,instr(GSserved,'-')-1) WHEN 'K' THEN 0 ELSE CAST(substr(GSserved,1,instr(GSserved,'-')-1) AS INTEGER) END) END AS lowest_grade FROM schools WHERE NCESDist='0632640' AND GSserved LIKE '%-%'
answer: K (kindergarten). I used GSserved (grade span served, the lowest grade with enrolled students) rather than GSoffered, where one school lists P (preschool). All statuses are included, and Active-only gives the same result. One school has a null grade span and was ignored. The School term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: select (select avg(a.ball_control) from Player_Attributes a join Player p using(player_api_id) where p.player_name='Abdou Diallo') - (select avg(a.ball_control) from Player_Attributes a join Player p using(player_api_id) where p.player_name='Aaron Appindangoye') as diff
answer: 0.8 (Abdou Diallo's mean ball_control is 49.4 over 10 records. Aaron Appindangoye's is 48.6 over 5 records.) I averaged every Player_Attributes row for each player. The query returns 0.799999999999997, which is floating-point noise around 0.8.

sql: select d.department, coalesce(sum(i.amount),0) as total_dues from (select distinct department from major where college=(select college from major where department like '%Electrical and Computer%')) d left join major m on m.department=d.department left join member b on b.link_to_major=m.major_id and exists(select 1 from attendance a where a.link_to_member=b.member_id) left join income i on i.link_to_member=b.member_id and i.source='Dues' group by d.department;
answer: College of Engineering has four departments. Dues received (in dollars) from members who attended at least one event: Biological Engineering 0, Civil and Environmental Engineering 200, Electrical and Computer Engineering 50, Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering 0. Assumptions: "dues" means income rows with source 'Dues'. "Took part in events" means the member has at least one attendance record. Each dues payment is counted once, however many events the member attended.

sql: with l as (select *, row_number() over (partition by player_api_id order by date desc, id desc) rn from Player_Attributes) select round(100.0*sum(attacking_work_rate='low')/count(*),1) as pct from l where rn=1 and preferred_foot='left' and attacking_work_rate in ('low','medium','high');
answer: 3.9% of left-footed players have a low attacking work rate in their most recent record. The base is 2,426 players whose latest record has a valid rating (high, medium or low). Records with NULL, empty or garbage values such as 'None', 'le', 'norm', 'stoc' and 'y' were treated as having no rating and excluded.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(SEX='F')/COUNT(*),2) FROM Patient WHERE 2026-CAST(strftime('%Y',Birthday) AS INT)>55 AND ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE PT>=14);
answer: 72.73% (8 of 11 patients). Assumptions: abnormal PT means PT >= 14, since the docs give normal as PT < 14. Age on 2026-10-09 is 2026 minus birth year, which is the wiki's age convention, and it must be over 55. The denominator includes one patient with an empty SEX value, counted as not female.

sql:
WITH a AS (SELECT code FROM sets WHERE code IN (SELECT setCode FROM cards WHERE name='Abyssal Horror') ORDER BY releaseDate ASC, code ASC LIMIT 1),
b AS (SELECT code FROM sets WHERE releaseDate IS NOT NULL ORDER BY releaseDate DESC, code ASC LIMIT 1),
t AS (SELECT code FROM a UNION SELECT code FROM b)
SELECT s.name, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN c.manaCost IS NOT NULL AND c.manaCost<>'' AND c.convertedManaCost<=3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS pct
FROM t JOIN sets s ON s.code=t.code JOIN cards c ON c.setCode=s.code GROUP BY s.code ORDER BY s.releaseDate;
answer: Urza's Saga (the earliest set containing Abyssal Horror): 58.15%. Time Spiral Remastered (the most recently released set): 80.00%. Reading used: the denominator is all cards in the set, and a card counts as having a mana cost only if its manaCost is non-empty. Rows are ordered by release date.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(a.alignment='Neutral')/count(*),2) as neutral_pct, sum(a.alignment='Neutral' and p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics') as neutral_marvel from superhero s left join alignment a on a.id=s.alignment_id left join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id;
answer: Neutral superheroes are 3.73% of all 750 superheroes, and 10 of them were published by Marvel Comics. I counted every row in superhero as the denominator, including heroes with no alignment or an 'N/A' alignment.

sql: select round(avg(u.Reputation)) from posts p join users u on u.Id=p.OwnerUserId where p.Tags like '%<r>%' and p.Score<20;
answer: 499. This is the average reputation of the owners of posts tagged exactly `<r>` with a score below 20. The query matches 7,000 posts. I averaged per post, so a user who owns several of them counts once for each. Averaging over distinct users would give a different number.

sql: SELECT e.event_name, e.event_date, (SELECT SUM(b.amount) FROM budget b WHERE b.link_to_event = e.event_id) AS total_budget, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event = e.event_id) AS attendee_count FROM event e ORDER BY e.event_name ASC, e.event_date ASC;
answer: The query returns all 42 events with name, date, total budget (sum of budget.amount across categories) and distinct attendee count, sorted by name and then date. I used subqueries so the budget and attendance counts don't multiply each other. Events with no budget rows show a NULL budget (21 of the 42 events), and events with no attendance rows show 0 attendees. I kept those events because the question asks for every event.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID WHERE l.TG >= 200 AND p.Birthday IS NOT NULL AND CAST(strftime('%Y','2026-10-09') AS INT) - CAST(strftime('%Y',p.Birthday) AS INT) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09') < strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)) > 50
answer: 106 distinct patients had at least one triglyceride (Laboratory.TG) result of 200 or more and were older than 50 (full years of age) on 2026-10-09.

sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN d.forename='Peter' THEN d.driverId END) AS peter_winners,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN d.forename='John' THEN d.driverId END) AS john_winners
FROM results r JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=r.driverId
WHERE r.positionOrder=1 AND d.forename IN ('Peter','John')
answer: Peter: 3 distinct race-winning drivers; John: 2. The counts are not equal. I counted a win as a result row with positionOrder = 1, matched forenames exactly, and counted each driver once however many races they won. The Driver and Race Result terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID WHERE p.SEX='F' AND l.WBC>3.5 AND l.WBC<9.0 AND (l.FG<=150 OR l.FG>=450) AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>15
answer: 1 female patient. Normal WBC = 3.5 < WBC < 9.0. Abnormal fibrinogen = FG <= 150 or >= 450 (outside 150 < N < 450). RNP is text and was cast to a number, keeping values above 15. A patient counts if any lab date meets all three conditions, and each patient is counted once.

sql: SELECT s.School, s.Street FROM frpm f JOIN schools s ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode WHERE s.School IS NOT NULL AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > 30 AND f."High Grade" IN ('K','1','2','3','4','5','6','7','8')
answer:
The query returns each school's name and street address. It returns more than 100 rows, and the run showed only the first 100 (truncated), so I haven't counted the full list. The SQL above returns all of them.

Choices I made:
- A school counts if K-12 enrollment minus ages 5-17 enrollment is greater than 30.
- The highest grade is the `High Grade` column in `frpm`. It is text, so I matched it to 'K' and '1' through '8'.
- No rows with a highest grade of 'P' (preschool) met the enrollment condition, so that choice doesn't change the result.
- "Named school" means `schools.School` is not null. This drops district-office rows.
- `frpm` and `schools` join one-to-one on `CDSCode`, so each school appears once.
- The FRPM and School terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.
- `frpm` is the 2014-2015 academic year.

sql: SELECT code, releaseDate FROM sets WHERE releaseDate BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31' AND code NOT IN (SELECT setCode FROM set_translations WHERE language = 'Spanish' AND translation IS NOT NULL AND translation <> '')
answer: 34개 세트가 해당합니다. 쿼리는 2020년에 출시된 세트 중 스페인어 이름이 없는 세트의 코드와 출시일을 반환합니다. 'Spanish' 번역 행이 없는 세트는 31개입니다. 번역 행은 있지만 translation이 비어 있는 세트가 3개 더 있어, 이 경우도 스페인어 이름이 없는 것으로 보고 포함했습니다. 빈 값을 제외하고 번역 행이 없는 세트만 원하면 31개입니다.

sql:
SELECT s.School AS name, s.Phone AS phone, s.Website AS website,
 t.AvgScrRead AS avg_read, t.AvgScrMath AS avg_math, t.AvgScrWrite AS avg_write,
 s.Charter AS is_charter,
 f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enrollment_k12,
 ROUND(f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)"*100,2) AS frpm_pct,
 (SELECT MAX(t2.AvgScrMath) FROM satscores t2 JOIN schools s2 ON s2.CDSCode=t2.cds
   WHERE s2.StatusType='Active' AND t2.NumTstTakr>=10 AND t2.rtype='S') AS max_math,
 (SELECT MAX(t2.AvgScrMath) FROM satscores t2 JOIN schools s2 ON s2.CDSCode=t2.cds
   WHERE s2.StatusType='Active' AND t2.NumTstTakr>=10 AND t2.rtype='S') - t.AvgScrMath AS gap
FROM schools s LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds=s.CDSCode
LEFT JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode AND f."Academic Year"='2014-2015'
WHERE s.CDSCode='07618040113118';
answer:
Dougherty Valley High, phone (925) 479-6400, website www.srvusd.net. Average SAT scores are 604 reading, 651 math and 613 writing. It is not a charter school (0). K-12 enrollment for 2014-2015 is 2,645, and 5.90% of students are eligible for free or reduced price meals. The highest average SAT math score among active schools with at least 10 test takers is 699, so this school's math score is 48 points below it.

Assumptions:
- The CDS code is stored with a leading zero (07618040113118), so I matched that form.
- "Free or reduced price meals" is the FRPM percentage, the stored fraction times 100.
- The comparison set is school-level SAT rows (rtype='S'), which excludes district rows.

sql:
SELECT p.player_name, COUNT(DISTINCT m.id) AS matches_played
FROM Player p
LEFT JOIN "Match" m ON m.season='2015/2016' AND p.player_api_id IN (m.home_player_1,m.home_player_2,m.home_player_3,m.home_player_4,m.home_player_5,m.home_player_6,m.home_player_7,m.home_player_8,m.home_player_9,m.home_player_10,m.home_player_11,m.away_player_1,m.away_player_2,m.away_player_3,m.away_player_4,m.away_player_5,m.away_player_6,m.away_player_7,m.away_player_8,m.away_player_9,m.away_player_10,m.away_player_11)
WHERE p.player_name LIKE 'Aaron%' AND p.birthday >= '1991-01-01'
GROUP BY p.player_api_id, p.player_name
ORDER BY p.player_name
answer: 6 players match (born 1991 or later, name starts with 'Aaron'). 2015/2016 starting-line-up matches: Aaron Appindangoye 0, Aaron Doran 0, Aaron Kuhl 5, Aaron Lennox 1, Aaron Splaine 1, Aaron Taylor-Sinclair 0. Choices I made: "born after 1990" means birthday on or after 1991-01-01. I counted a match once if the player is in any of the 22 home or away starting slots. I kept players with 0 matches, since the question says "every player". Drop them by switching to an inner join if only players with playing time are wanted. The Match and Player terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT l.ID, l.RNP, l.CPK, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY l.ID ORDER BY l.Date DESC) rn FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE p.SEX='F' AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL) WHERE rn=1 AND RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(RNP AS REAL)>64 AND CPK<250
answer: 2. Two female patients had a latest anti-RNP result above 64 with CPK below 250 on that same laboratory record. "Most recent" means the latest record with a non-null RNP. RNP is stored as text, so only numeric values were compared; "negative" and null were excluded. A record with null CPK is not counted. The Laboratory Test and Patient terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select round(sum(e.cost)*1.0/count(distinct b.link_to_event),2) from expense e join member m on m.member_id=e.link_to_member join budget b on b.budget_id=e.link_to_budget where m.first_name='Elijah' and m.last_name='Allen' and substr(e.expense_date,6,2) in ('09','10');
answer: 98.77. Elijah Allen's expenses dated in September or October total 592.62 across 8 expenses tied to 6 distinct events, so the mean per event is 592.62 / 6 = 98.77. I read "mean total expense per event" as total cost divided by the number of distinct events, with expenses linked to events through their budgets.

sql: select sum(SEX='M')*1.0/sum(SEX='F') as male_to_female_ratio from (select distinct p.ID, p.SEX from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where (p.SEX='M' and l.UA>8.0) or (p.SEX='F' and l.UA>6.5));
answer: 남성 대 여성 비율은 0.22입니다(남성 11명, 여성 50명). 상한은 문서 기준으로 남성 8.0, 여성 6.5를 적용했고, 초과(>)한 검사 결과가 한 번이라도 있는 환자를 한 명으로 계산했습니다. 비율은 남성 수를 여성 수로 나눈 값입니다.

sql: SELECT t.AvgScrMath, t.NumTstTakr FROM schools s JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE s.CDSCode = '01611190130609' AND s.FundingType = 'Directly funded'
answer: The school is directly funded, and its average SAT math score is 593. 20 students took the SAT. The database stores the CDS code with a leading zero (01611190130609), so I matched on that 14-digit form.

sql: SELECT l.ID, l.Date, l.DNA FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE p.SEX='F' AND p.Admission LIKE '+%' AND l.DNA GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(l.DNA AS REAL)=(SELECT MAX(CAST(l2.DNA AS REAL)) FROM Laboratory l2 JOIN Patient p2 ON p2.ID=l2.ID WHERE p2.SEX='F' AND p2.Admission LIKE '+%' AND l2.DNA GLOB '[0-9]*') ORDER BY l.ID
answer:
Patient 2933261, lab date 1988-04-25, anti-DNA level 185. It is the only record at the maximum.

Choices I made:
- "Anti-DNA level" is the `DNA` column. It is stored as text, so I compared the values numerically and ignored non-numeric entries such as "-" and "+".
- "Admitted as inpatient" is `Admission` starting with '+'. That includes 3 patients recorded as "+(".
- I did not use the `DNA-II` column.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(e.d) - julianday(p."First Date"))) AS avg_delay_days
FROM "Patient" p
JOIN (SELECT ID, MIN("Examination Date") AS d FROM "Examination" GROUP BY ID) e ON e.ID = p.ID
WHERE p."Admission" LIKE '+%' AND p."First Date" IS NOT NULL AND e.d IS NOT NULL
answer: The average delay is 1616 days. Admitted means the Admission value starts with '+' (this covers both '+' and '+('). First visit is Patient."First Date" and first examination is each patient's earliest Examination Date. Patients missing either date are excluded. The Patient and Special Examination terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
WITH t AS (
 SELECT c.Segment s, c.CustomerID id, SUM(y.Consumption) tot
 FROM customers c JOIN yearmonth y ON y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID
 WHERE c.Currency='CZK' AND y.Date LIKE '2013%' AND c.Segment IN ('SME','LAM','KAM')
 GROUP BY c.Segment, c.CustomerID),
m AS (SELECT s, tot, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s ORDER BY tot, id) rn FROM t),
p AS (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN s='SME' THEN tot END) sme, MAX(CASE WHEN s='LAM' THEN tot END) lam, MAX(CASE WHEN s='KAM' THEN tot END) kam FROM m WHERE rn=1)
SELECT ROUND(sme-lam,2) AS sme_minus_lam, ROUND(lam-kam,2) AS lam_minus_kam, ROUND(kam-sme,2) AS kam_minus_sme FROM p;
answer: SME − LAM = -14009.34, LAM − KAM = 6046.62, KAM − SME = 7962.72. I only counted CZK customers who have at least one 2013 row in yearmonth, so customers with no 2013 consumption records are not candidates for lowest. I summed Consumption over months starting with '2013'.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT y.CustomerID FROM yearmonth y JOIN customers c USING(CustomerID) WHERE c.Segment='KAM' AND c.Currency='CZK' AND y.Date LIKE '2013%' GROUP BY y.CustomerID HAVING SUM(y.Consumption)>1000000);
answer: 335 KAM-segment customers paying in CZK had total 2013 fuel consumption above 1,000,000. I summed each customer's monthly Consumption from the yearmonth table for months 201301 to 201311, then kept customers whose sum was over 1,000,000. The data has no December 2013 month, so the totals cover 11 months of the year.

sql: select round(avg(m),1) from (select name, max(convertedManaCost) m from cards c where types like '%Creature%' and edhrecRank between 1 and 1000 and exists(select 1 from legalities l where l.uuid=c.uuid and l.status='Banned') group by name)
answer: 평균 마나 값은 3.4입니다. EDHRec 1~1000위 안에 있고 하나 이상의 포맷에서 'Banned' 상태인 크리처 카드는 이름 기준으로 7장입니다. 여러 세트에 인쇄된 카드는 이름별로 한 번만 계산했고, 같은 이름의 인쇄본은 순위와 마나 값이 모두 같았습니다. 크리처는 types에 'Creature'가 들어간 카드로 보았습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT u.Id) FROM users u JOIN badges b ON b.UserId = u.Id WHERE b.Name = 'Yearling' AND b.Date < '2014-01-01' AND u.Location LIKE '%India%' AND u.Location NOT LIKE '%Indiana%'
answer: 6 users located in India earned a Yearling badge before 1 January 2014. I counted distinct users (8 badge awards in total). I treated a location as India if it contains "India" in any case, and I excluded Indiana and Indianapolis. I used badge Date < '2014-01-01'.

sql:
SELECT g.gender AS gender, COUNT(x.id) AS hero_count
FROM gender g
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT s.id, s.gender_id FROM superhero s
  JOIN colour c ON s.hair_colour_id = c.id
  WHERE c.colour = 'Blue'
    AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id) >= 10
) x ON x.gender_id = g.id
WHERE g.gender IN ('Male','Female')
GROUP BY g.gender
ORDER BY g.gender DESC
answer: Male: 3, Female: 0. Blue hair means hair colour exactly 'Blue' (mixed colours like 'Blue/White' excluded). Power count is the number of hero_power rows per hero, with 10 or more qualifying. 'N/A' gender is excluded. A LEFT JOIN from gender makes Female show as 0 instead of being missing. The Colour, Gender and Superhero Terms used are draft, not certified.

sql:
SELECT s.School, s.DOCType
FROM frpm f JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode
WHERE s."FundingType" = 'Locally funded'
  AND (f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)") >
      (SELECT AVG(f2."Enrollment (K-12)" - f2."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)")
       FROM frpm f2 JOIN schools s2 ON s2.CDSCode = f2.CDSCode
       WHERE s2."FundingType" = 'Locally funded')
answer: 57개 학교가 해당합니다. 지방 재정(Locally funded)은 schools.FundingType 기준으로 판단했고, 평균도 같은 조건의 학교만으로 계산했습니다. 각 학교의 차이는 frpm의 K-12 등록 인원에서 5-17세 등록 인원을 뺀 값이며, 이 값이 평균보다 큰 학교를 골랐습니다. 출력은 디렉터리 학교명(schools.School)과 DOC 유형(schools.DOCType) 두 열입니다. 쿼리가 쓴 두 용어(Free or Reduced Price Meal Record, School)는 아직 초안 상태이고 인증되지 않았습니다.

sql: select artist, count(distinct name) c from cards where ','||types||',' like '%,Creature,%' and artist is not null group by artist having c=(select max(c) from (select count(distinct name) c from cards where ','||types||',' like '%,Creature,%' and artist is not null group by artist))
answer: Kev Walker has illustrated the most different creature cards, 275, with no tie. I counted a card as a creature if `types` includes Creature, which also covers Artifact Creature. "Different" means distinct card names, so reprints are counted once.

sql: select f.`Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)`, f.`District Code` from schools s join frpm f using(CDSCode) where s.AdmFName1='Alusine' or s.AdmFName2='Alusine' or s.AdmFName3='Alusine'
answer: Percent Eligible Free (K-12) is about 0.7015 (70.15%) and the district code is 64857. I checked all three administrator first-name columns. Only one school matches, with Alusine in the first slot.

sql: select d.forename, d.surname, strftime('%H:%M:%f', r2.date||' '||r2.time, '+'||(r.milliseconds/1000.0)||' seconds') as finish_time, d.url from results r join drivers d using(driverId) join races r2 using(raceId) where r2.year=2017 and r2.name='Azerbaijan Grand Prix' and r.positionOrder=1
answer: Daniel Ricciardo won the 2017 Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Finish time: 15:03:55.573. URL: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Ricciardo. I computed the finish time as the race start in the database (races.time, 13:00:00, which the docs describe as the local time at the location) plus the winner's race duration (2:03:55.573). This assumes the stored start time is local. Real-world Baku local start was 17:00, so if the database value is actually UTC, add 4 hours to get the true local time.

sql:
with recursive ev as (select distinct link_to_event e from budget where amount-spent<0),
d as (select x.expense_description s from expense x join budget b on b.budget_id=x.link_to_budget where b.link_to_event in (select e from ev)),
sp(item, rest) as (select '', s||',' from d union all select trim(substr(rest,1,instr(rest,',')-1)), substr(rest,instr(rest,',')+1) from sp where rest<>'')
select count(distinct lower(item)) as kinds from sp where item<>''
answer: 7. The club bought 7 different kinds of things for over-budget events: water, cookies, chips, pizza, posters, parking and travel mug. An event counts as over budget if any of its budget lines has budgeted amount minus spent below zero, which covers 5 events. I counted every purchase linked to any budget line of those events, split the descriptions on commas, and ignored case when comparing items. I used all records with no date filter. The Budget and Expense terms in the ontology are still drafts.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN uuid IN (SELECT uuid FROM foreign_data WHERE language='Chinese Simplified') THEN uuid END) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards), 2) AS pct FROM cards
answer: 35.38% of card printings (rows in cards, identified by uuid) have a Simplified Chinese translation in foreign_data (language = 'Chinese Simplified'). The denominator is all rows in cards. The Card and Card Foreign Data terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select count(distinct m.major_id) from member b join major m on b.link_to_major=m.major_id where m.department='Political Science Department'
answer: Club members from the Political Science Department represent 2 different majors. I counted distinct majors among members whose major belongs to that department. Majors with no members are not counted.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM cards c JOIN sets s ON s.code=c.setCode WHERE s.name='Dark Ascension' AND (','||REPLACE(c.keywords,', ',',')||',') LIKE '%,Flash,%' AND c.convertedManaCost=(SELECT MAX(c2.convertedManaCost) FROM cards c2 JOIN sets s2 ON s2.code=c2.setCode WHERE s2.name='Dark Ascension' AND (','||REPLACE(c2.keywords,', ',',')||',') LIKE '%,Flash,%') ORDER BY c.name
answer: Three Dark Ascension cards with the Flash keyword tie for the highest converted mana cost: Briarpack Alpha, Hollowhenge Spirit and Nephalia Seakite. I didn't print the cost itself, so I haven't stated the value. I matched Flash as a whole item in the comma-separated keywords list. A plain substring match also picks up Flashback cards such as Increasing Ambition, so I excluded those. Each name is listed once, even if the set has more than one printing. The Card and Card Set terms I used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.Tags LIKE '%<r>%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct FROM posts p JOIN users u ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id WHERE u.DisplayName = 'Community'
answer: 0.00%. Community (user Id -1) owns 211 posts. All 211 are answers, and answers have no Tags value, so none carry the `<r>` tag. I read "authored by Community" as posts whose owner has DisplayName 'Community'. I read "uses the R tag" as `posts.Tags` containing `<r>`. The Post and User terms used are still draft in the ontology.

sql:
with o as (select UserId, min(Date) d from badges where Name='Organizer' group by UserId)
select count(*) from o join users u on u.Id=o.UserId where u.Location like '%Germany%' and (select count(*) from badges b where b.UserId=o.UserId and b.Date<o.d)>=5
answer: 11 users. I read "had already earned 5 badges" as at least 5. I used each user's earliest Organizer badge date and counted only badges dated strictly before it, which excludes the Organizer badge itself and any badge earned at the same moment. I treated a user as based in Germany if their Location contains "Germany", and the check I ran found no non-German matches such as Germantown.

sql:
SELECT s.type,
 SUM(EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode=s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND t.translation<>'')) AS sets_with_translated_name,
 COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode=s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND t.translation<>'') THEN s.totalSetSize END),0) AS total_cards
FROM sets s
GROUP BY s.type
ORDER BY s.type
answer: The query returns all 22 set types in alphabetical order. Each row gives the number of sets with at least one non-empty row in set_translations and the sum of totalSetSize for those sets. Two readings were my choice. "Total number of cards" is totalSetSize from the sets table, not a count of rows in cards. "Officially translated name" means a non-empty translation row. Types with no translated sets show 0 and 0: funny, masterpiece, memorabilia, promo, spellbook, starter, token, treasure_chest and vanguard. The largest type is expansion, with 61 sets and 14,023 cards.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(case when Score>50 then 1 else 0 end)/count(*),2) as percentage from posts where OwnerUserId=(select Id from users order by Reputation desc limit 1);
answer: 0.66% of the top-reputation user's 1,204 posts have a score above 50. I took "posts by the user" to mean posts whose OwnerUserId is that user, and I used the single user with the highest Reputation.

sql:
WITH t AS (
 SELECT code FROM sets WHERE code IN (SELECT setCode FROM cards WHERE name='Abyssal Horror') ORDER BY releaseDate, code LIMIT 1
), l AS (
 SELECT code FROM sets ORDER BY releaseDate DESC, code LIMIT 1
)
SELECT s.name AS set_name,
 ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN c.manaCost IS NOT NULL AND c.manaCost<>'' AND c.convertedManaCost<=3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS pct
FROM sets s JOIN cards c ON c.setCode=s.code
WHERE s.code IN (SELECT code FROM t UNION SELECT code FROM l)
GROUP BY s.code, s.name ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.code
answer: Urza's Saga (where Abyssal Horror was first printed): 58.15%. Time Spiral Remastered (most recently released set): 80.00%. Percentages use all card printings in the set as the denominator. A card counts as having a mana cost only if manaCost is non-NULL and non-empty, and convertedManaCost <= 3. Tie-breaks follow the question (release date, then set code). The Card and Card Set terms are still draft (not certified).

sql: select d.forename||' '||d.surname as driver, p.duration as pit_stop_time, r.name as race_name, c.name as circuit_name, c.location as circuit_location from pitStops p join races r on r.raceId=p.raceId join drivers d on d.driverId=p.driverId join circuits c on c.circuitId=r.circuitId where r.date between '2016-09-01' and '2016-09-30' and p.milliseconds=(select min(p2.milliseconds) from pitStops p2 join races r2 on r2.raceId=p2.raceId where r2.date between '2016-09-01' and '2016-09-30');
answer: 2016년 9월 최速 피트스톱은 23.633초이고, 두 명이 같은 기록입니다. 둘 다 이탈리아 그랑프리(Autodromo Nazionale di Monza, 위치 Monza)에서 나왔습니다. 해당 드라이버는 Lewis Hamilton과 Daniel Ricciardo입니다. 'September 2016'은 레이스 날짜가 2016-09-01부터 2016-09-30 사이인 경우로 보았고, 기록 비교는 밀리초 값으로 했습니다.

sql: select Age from users where Location in ('York','York, England','York, United Kingdom','York, UK') and Reputation=(select max(Reputation) from users where Location in ('York','York, England','York, United Kingdom','York, UK'))
answer: The age is 24. The top user in York is Id 24789 (reputation 106, location "York, United Kingdom"), and no one else ties. I counted a location as York if it was exactly "York", "York, England", "York, United Kingdom" or "York, UK". I left out North Yorkshire, Yorkshire, York, PA and New York.

sql:
WITH b AS (
SELECT c.client_id, c.gender, c.birth_date, cd.type AS card_type,
 CAST(strftime('%Y',cd.issued) AS INT) - CAST(strftime('%Y',c.birth_date) AS INT) AS age_at_issue,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id = d.account_id) AS loan_count,
