 (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(l.amount),0) FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id = d.account_id) AS total_borrowed,
 di.A2 AS district_name, di.A11 AS district_avg_salary
FROM card cd
JOIN disp d ON cd.disp_id = d.disp_id
JOIN client c ON d.client_id = c.client_id
JOIN district di ON c.district_id = di.district_id
WHERE cd.issued >= '1994-01-01' AND cd.issued < '1995-01-01')
SELECT client_id, gender, birth_date, card_type, age_at_issue, loan_count, total_borrowed,
 CASE WHEN loan_count>0 AND age_at_issue<30 THEN 'Young borrower'
      WHEN loan_count>0 THEN 'Mature borrower' ELSE 'Non-borrower' END AS borrower_classification,
 district_name, district_avg_salary,
 RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY gender ORDER BY age_at_issue DESC) AS age_rank_within_gender
FROM b ORDER BY client_id
answer:
The query returns one row per client issued a card in 1994, ordered by client id, with the 11 requested columns. I ran it and checked only the first 5 rows, not the full result or the row count. The terms it relies on (Client, Credit Card, Disposition, District, Loan) are draft, not certified.

Choices where the question was ambiguous:
- District: the client's own district (client.district_id), not the account's district.
- Loans: counted on the account of the card's disposition, owner or disponent. Total borrowed is 0 when there are no loans.
- Age rank: within gender among the 1994 card holders only, oldest as rank 1, using RANK() so ties share a rank and the next is skipped. To make the youngest rank 1, change DESC to ASC.
- Age at issue: card issue year minus birth year, as specified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers c WHERE c.Currency='EUR' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM yearmonth y WHERE y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID AND y.Date LIKE '2012%' AND y.Consumption>0) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM yearmonth y WHERE y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID AND y.Date LIKE '2013%' AND y.Consumption>0)
answer: 1516 customers who pay in EUR had consumption in 2012 and also in 2013. I read "had gas consumption" as at least one month in the year with Consumption > 0. If any monthly record counts, including zero or negative values, the count is 1517. The `yearmonth` table only holds total monthly consumption, so I treated that as gas consumption. The Customer and Monthly Customer Consumption terms are draft (not certified).

sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name='Yearly Kickoff' THEN b.amount END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name='October Meeting' THEN b.amount END) AS ratio FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event=e.event_id WHERE b.category='Advertisement' AND e.event_name IN ('Yearly Kickoff','October Meeting')
answer: The ratio is about 2.727 (150 / 55). The Yearly Kickoff Advertisement budget is $150 and the October Meeting's is $55. I read "ratio" as Yearly Kickoff divided by October Meeting. The Budget and Event terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
WITH s AS (SELECT player_api_id, overall_rating, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC) rn FROM Player_Attributes WHERE date<='2010-12-31'),
top AS (SELECT player_api_id FROM s WHERE rn=1 AND overall_rating>80),
pm AS (SELECT player_api_id, COUNT(*) n FROM (
 SELECT home_player_1 player_api_id FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_2 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_3 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_4 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_5 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_6 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_7 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_8 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_9 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_10 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_11 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011'
 UNION ALL SELECT away_player_1 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_2 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_3 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_4 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_5 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_6 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_7 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_8 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_9 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_10 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_11 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011') WHERE player_api_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY player_api_id)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(pm.n),2) AS avg_matches FROM top JOIN pm USING(player_api_id);
answer: 24.91 matches on average. Choices I made: (1) A player's rating as of 31 Dec 2010 is their latest Player_Attributes snapshot dated on or before 2010-12-31, and it must be strictly above 80. This gives 235 players. (2) A match played means the player is in one of the 22 starting-lineup slots of a 2010/2011 match, because only starters are recorded. (3) Only the 212 shortlisted players with at least one recorded start in that season are averaged. The other 23 have no lineup records that season, which could mean they didn't play or that their league has no lineup data, so I left them out. If you count them as 0 matches, the average is 22.47 instead.

sql: select count(distinct q.driverId) from qualifying q join races r using(raceId) where r.year=1995 and q.q1 glob '*:*.*' and cast(substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1) as int)*60000+cast(substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,':')+1,2) as int)*1000+cast(substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,'.')+1) as int) > 120000
answer: 10 drivers set a Q1 time strictly over 2:00.000 in 1995. I converted the m:ss.mmm text to milliseconds and counted distinct drivers. One of the 10 (driver 87) has an odd value of 16:42.640, which is literally over two minutes, so I counted it. Without it the count would be 9.

sql: select round((select max(t) from (select sum(Consumption) t from yearmonth where Date like '2013%' group by Date)) - (select max(t) from (select sum(Consumption) t from yearmonth where Date like '2012%' group by Date))) as diff
answer: The 2013 peak month's total consumption is 338,745,665 units higher than the 2012 peak month's. I summed Consumption across all customers for each month and took the highest month in each year. Negative rows are included. yearmonth has no rows for Oct–Dec 2012, so the 2012 peak comes from only Jan–Sep 2012 (Dec 2011 is excluded). That gap could make the difference look larger than it really is.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(ha.attribute_value), 1) AS avg_intelligence
FROM hero_attribute ha
INNER JOIN attribute a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id
WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Intelligence'
  AND ha.attribute_value IS NOT NULL
  AND ha.hero_id IN (
    SELECT hp.hero_id FROM hero_power hp
    INNER JOIN superpower sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id
    WHERE sp.power_name IN ('Super Speed', 'Death Touch'))
answer: The average intelligence score of heroes with Super Speed or Death Touch is 85.9. I matched the exact power names 'Super Speed' and 'Death Touch' and left out 'Speed Force'. A hero with both powers is counted once, and only heroes with a non-null Intelligence score are averaged. The Superpower, Hero Attribute Score and Attribute terms are still drafts in the ontology, not certified.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.bond_id FROM connected c JOIN atom a1 ON c.atom_id=a1.atom_id JOIN atom a2 ON c.atom_id2=a2.atom_id WHERE a1.element='p' AND a2.element='n' ORDER BY c.bond_id
answer: Six bonds connect a phosphorus atom and a nitrogen atom: TR032_2_3, TR032_3_5, TR058_1_3, TR058_1_4, TR058_1_5 and TR298_1_5. I read the question as bonds linking one phosphorus (p) atom and one nitrogen (n) atom, and returned only the bond IDs. Each bond is stored in both directions in the connected table, so putting phosphorus on the first atom and nitrogen on the second returns each bond once. The query relies on the Atom term, which is still a draft and not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND l.WBC > 3.5 AND l.WBC < 9.0 AND l.FG IS NOT NULL AND (l.FG <= 150 OR l.FG >= 450) AND l.RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 15
answer: 1 female patient meets all three conditions on the same laboratory record. I used the normal ranges from docs/Laboratory.csv: WBC between 3.5 and 9.0 (exclusive), abnormal fibrinogen as FG outside 150 to 450 (the only recorded FG value is 27), and RNP as a numeric value above 15 (text values such as 'negative' are excluded). The query checks all laboratory dates. It relies on draft (uncertified) ontology Terms.

sql: SELECT p.Id, u.DisplayName FROM posts p LEFT JOIN users u ON u.Id = p.OwnerUserId WHERE p.CreaionDate >= '2010-01-01' AND p.CreaionDate < '2011-01-01' ORDER BY p.FavoriteCount DESC LIMIT 1
answer: Post 1595, owned by Fabian Fagerholm, is the 2010 post with the most favorites. I took "owner's display name" from users.DisplayName, joined through posts.OwnerUserId, because posts.OwnerDisplayName is null for about 93% of rows. The creation date column is spelled `CreaionDate` in the schema. I did not check for ties on the favorite count, and the Post and User terms the query relies on are still drafts.

sql: select round(100.0*count(distinct case when a.defensive_work_rate='high' then p.player_api_id end)/count(distinct p.player_api_id),2) as pct_high from Player p join Player_Attributes a on a.player_api_id=p.player_api_id where p.birthday>='1991' and a.defensive_work_rate in ('low','medium','high')
answer: 17.41. Assumptions: only 'low', 'medium' and 'high' count as a defensive work rating, and the other junk values are excluded. The base is players born in 1991 or later with at least one valid rating. A player counts as high if any of their rows says 'high'.

sql: select sum(Score) from posts where Tags like '%<r>%' and Id in (select l.PostId from postLinks l join posts t on t.Id=l.RelatedPostId where t.Title='A Probability distribution value exceeding 1 is OK?')
answer: The total score is 22. I took "link to" to mean postLinks rows where the target (RelatedPostId) is that question, with any link type. I counted each linking question once, because some pairs have both a type 1 and a type 3 link. I matched the exact tag `<r>`.

sql:
WITH t AS (SELECT c.Currency, y.CustomerID, SUM(y.Consumption) s FROM yearmonth y JOIN customers c ON c.CustomerID=y.CustomerID WHERE y.Date LIKE '2012%' AND c.Currency IN ('CZK','EUR') GROUP BY c.Currency, y.CustomerID)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN Currency='CZK' THEN s END) - AVG(CASE WHEN Currency='EUR' THEN s END)) AS diff FROM t
answer: 14308. The CZK average minus the EUR average of 2012 consumption is 14,308, rounded to the nearest whole unit. I took each customer's total consumption over 2012 (customers with at least one 2012 monthly record) and averaged those totals within each currency. Amounts are in each customer's own currency with no CZK-to-EUR conversion. The query relies on draft (uncertified) Terms: Customer and Monthly Customer Consumption.

sql:
WITH r AS (SELECT uuid, COUNT(*) n FROM rulings GROUP BY uuid)
SELECT f.name AS japanese_name, c.type AS card_type, COALESCE(SUM(r.n),0) AS total_rulings
FROM cards c
JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid = c.uuid AND f.language = 'Japanese'
LEFT JOIN r ON r.uuid = c.uuid
WHERE c.watermark = 'boros'
GROUP BY f.name, c.type
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 96장이 나왔습니다. 열은 일본어 카드명, 영어 카드 타입(cards.type), 룰링 총수 순이고, 룰링이 없는 카드는 0으로 표시됩니다.

적용한 해석은 세 가지입니다.
- 대상은 watermark가 'boros'이고 foreign_data에 Japanese 언어 행이 있는 인쇄본입니다.
- 일본어 이름과 영어 type이 모두 같은 인쇄본은 한 장으로 묶고, 둘 중 하나라도 다르면 따로 나열합니다. 예를 들어 '反応 // 反正'은 Instant와 Sorcery로 두 줄입니다.
- 룰링 수는 rulings를 uuid별로 먼저 세고 묶은 그룹에서 합산해, 조인 중복으로 부풀지 않게 했습니다. 합산 범위는 boros 워터마크가 있고 일본어판이 있는 인쇄본이며, 같은 이름과 type이지만 워터마크가 없는 인쇄본의 룰링은 포함하지 않았습니다.

사용한 Card, Card Foreign Data 용어는 아직 draft(미인증) 상태입니다. 온톨로지 설명에는 watermark가 '100% null'로 적혀 있었지만, 실제로는 boros가 166행 있었습니다.

sql: select p.Birthday from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where p.ID in (select ID from Laboratory where RNP glob '[0-9]*' and CAST(RNP as real)>=16) group by p.ID having max(l.GPT)<60 order by max(l.GPT) desc, p.ID limit 3
answer: Birthdays: 1958-10-23, 1969-11-30, 1962-01-18. I read "liver enzymes stayed in the normal range" as every recorded GPT for the patient being below 60, so patients with any GPT of 60 or more are excluded. Patients with an RNP result of 16 or higher are those with a numeric RNP value >= 16 (the 'negative' text and blanks are ignored). Ranking uses each patient's highest GPT (57, 56, 41), with ties broken by the smaller ID. If you instead meant only that some GPT values were normal, the top three would be different patients: 1949-05-11, 1958-10-23 and 1963-12-13.

sql: select round(avg(c),2) from (select r.raceId, (select count(*) from pitStops p where p.raceId=r.raceId) c from races r where r.year=2017 and r.name not in (select name from races where year=2000))
answer: The average is 39.71 pit stops per race, over 7 races. I read "not hosted in 2000" as a 2017 race whose Grand Prix name has no 2000 race with the same name. A race's pit stops are the rows for it in pitStops. I counted every qualifying 2017 race, including any with no pit stop rows.

sql: select count(distinct c.name) from cards c join legalities l on l.uuid=c.uuid where l.format='brawl' and l.status='Legal' and c.isPromo=1 and c.types like '%Creature%' and c.supertypes like '%Legendary%'
answer: 98 distinct legendary creature cards that are Brawl-legal and have a promotional printing (isPromo=1). I assumed a Brawl commander must be a legendary creature, and I counted distinct card names.

sql: select distinct name from cards where setCode='DKA' and ','||replace(keywords,', ',',')||',' like '%,Flash,%' and convertedManaCost=(select max(convertedManaCost) from cards where setCode='DKA' and ','||replace(keywords,', ',',')||',' like '%,Flash,%') order by name;
answer: Three Dark Ascension (set code DKA) cards with the Flash keyword tie at the highest converted mana cost of 4: Briarpack Alpha, Hollowhenge Spirit and Nephalia Seakite. I matched "Flash" as a whole keyword, so cards that only have Flashback are excluded. Flashback cards cost up to 5, so a plain substring match would have returned the wrong cards. I left out the Dark Ascension Promos set (PDKA).

sql: select count(distinct case when t.k_symbol='SIPO' then t.trans_id end) as household_payments, count(distinct case when trim(t.k_symbol)<>'' and t.k_symbol<>'SIPO' then t.trans_id end) as other_purpose_payments from trans t where t.amount>4000 and t.account_id in (select d.account_id from disp d join client c on c.client_id=d.client_id where c.gender='M' and substr(c.birth_date,1,4) in ('1974','1975','1976'))
answer: Household payments: 1556. Other-purpose payments: 337. I read 'household payment' as trans.k_symbol = 'SIPO'. Other-purpose means any other non-blank k_symbol. NULL and single-space k_symbol (no purpose recorded) are in neither count. Each transaction is counted once, even if its account has more than one qualifying male client. Payments are rows in trans, not rows in order.

sql: SELECT SUM(SEX='F') - SUM(SEX='M') FROM Patient p WHERE Diagnosis='RA' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.UN<30)
answer: 23. 해석: 진단명이 정확히 'RA'인 환자 중, 요소질소(UN) 정상 기준(30 미만)인 검사 기록이 한 번이라도 있는 환자를 한 명씩 셌습니다. 여성 30명, 남성 7명이라 차이는 23입니다. 'RA susp'나 'SJS, RA' 같은 복합 진단은 제외했습니다.

sql: SELECT SUM(SEX='M') AS male, SUM(SEX='F') AS female FROM Patient WHERE ID NOT IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE GPT >= 60)
answer:
178 male and 956 female patients have never had an ALT (GPT) result above the normal range. Patients with no lab results are included.

Choices I made:
- The docs give the normal range for GPT as N < 60, so I counted any result of 60 or higher as abnormal. 19 results equal exactly 60, so the cutoff matters. Using > 60 instead would change the counts.
- 13 patients have a blank sex value. They are excluded because you asked for exactly male and female.

sql: select round(100.0*count(distinct case when s.alignment_id=1 then s.id end)/count(distinct s.id),2) from superhero s join hero_power hp on hp.hero_id=s.id where s.publisher_id=13
answer: 64.39. I counted each Marvel Comics hero once, and only those with at least one row in hero_power. The percentage is the share of those heroes whose alignment is 'Good'.

sql: select avg(weight_kg) from superhero where weight_kg>0 and race_id in (select race_id from superhero where race_id is not null group by race_id having sum(gender_id=2)=0)
answer: 평균 체중은 약 156,709.09 kg입니다. 이 값은 이상치(Godzilla 90,000,000 kg, King Kong 9,000,000 kg)에 크게 영향을 받았습니다. 계산에서는 다음과 같이 해석했습니다. 데이터 문서에 따라 weight_kg가 NULL 또는 0이면 체중 미기록으로 보고 제외했습니다. 영웅이 한 명이라도 여성(gender_id=2)인 종족은 제외했습니다. race_id가 없는 영웅은 어느 종족에도 속하지 않는 것으로 보고 뺐습니다.

sql: with r as (select e.event_name n, sum(b.spent)*1.0/sum(b.amount) x from event e join budget b on b.link_to_event=e.event_id where e.status='Closed' group by e.event_id) select n as event_name from r where x=(select max(x) from r)
answer: Three closed events tie at a spent-to-budget ratio of 1.01: Officers meeting - November, Officers meeting - September and Officers meeting - October. I read "closed" as event.status = 'Closed' (budget.event_status agrees on every row). Spending is budget.spent, which matches the sum of expense costs, and each event's ratio is its total spent divided by its total budget amount.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT replace(text, char(10), ' / ') AS text FROM cards WHERE name = 'Benalish Knight' AND text IS NOT NULL
answer: Benalish Knight's rules text is: "Flash (You may cast this spell any time you could cast an instant.) / First strike (This creature deals combat damage before creatures without first strike.)". I used the `text` column and replaced the line break between the two abilities with " / " so the result fits on one line. The `originalText` column holds older printings' wording, which I did not use.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(Consumption), 2) FROM yearmonth WHERE CustomerID = 15621 AND Date LIKE '2013%' AND Consumption > 0
answer: 6.02. I used the yearmonth table's monthly Consumption for customer 15621 in 2013, and counted only months with Consumption above 0. Those are 201306 (3.5), 201307 (12.91) and 201310 (1.65). Months recorded as 0.0 (201304, 201305, 201309) were treated as months with no fuel purchase and left out.

sql: SELECT c.colors, COUNT(DISTINCT l.format) AS legal_formats FROM cards c JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid=c.uuid WHERE c.id BETWEEN 1 AND 20 AND l.status='Legal' GROUP BY c.colors
answer: White cards (colors = 'W') are legal in 14 formats and black cards (colors = 'B') in 10 formats, among cards with ID 1 to 20. I read 'card color' as the MTG color in the `colors` column, not the border color, because every card in that range has a black border. Within the range, 16 cards are white and 4 are black. A format counts once per color if at least one card of that color has status 'Legal' in it. The `Card` and `Card Legality` terms are still draft (not certified).

sql:
WITH a AS (SELECT atom_id, element FROM atom WHERE molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM molecule WHERE label='+')),
tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM a),
b AS (SELECT element, COUNT(*) c FROM a WHERE atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id FROM connected UNION SELECT atom_id2 FROM connected) GROUP BY element)
SELECT element, ROUND(100.0*(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM a a2 WHERE a2.element=b.element)/(SELECT n FROM tot),2) AS pct
FROM b WHERE c=(SELECT MAX(c) FROM b);
answer: 수소(h)가 가장 많습니다. '+' 분자의 전체 원자 중 42.5%입니다. 결합에 참여하는 원자는 connected 테이블의 atom_id나 atom_id2에 나오는 원자로 보았고, 비율의 분모는 '+' 분자의 모든 원자입니다. 공동 1위는 없습니다.

sql: select s.name, s.keyruneCode, count(distinct t.language) as language_count from sets s left join set_translations t on t.setCode=s.code and t.translation is not null and t.translation<>'' where s.releaseDate>='2020-01-01' and s.releaseDate<'2021-01-01' group by s.id order by s.releaseDate
answer:
The query returns 34 sets released in 2020. Only 3 of them have any translated name, and each of those has 1 language: Theros Beyond Death (THB), Ikoria: Lair of Behemoths (IKO) and Core Set 2021 (M21). The other 31 sets show 0.

Choices I made:
- A language counts only if the translation is non-null and non-empty. The table has 231 null translations, which I excluded.
- I counted distinct languages per set.
- Sets with no translation rows are kept in the result with a count of 0 (left join).
- Sets are ordered by release date.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(t),2) AS mean_total_expense_per_event FROM (SELECT SUM(e.cost) AS t FROM expense e JOIN member m ON e.link_to_member=m.member_id JOIN budget b ON e.link_to_budget=b.budget_id WHERE m.first_name='Elijah' AND m.last_name='Allen' AND substr(e.expense_date,6,2) IN ('09','10') GROUP BY b.link_to_event)
answer: 98.77. I summed Elijah Allen's expense costs per event (event reached via the expense's budget), counting only expenses dated in month 09 or 10 of any year, then averaged those per-event totals. I did not filter on the approved flag. The Expense, Member and Budget terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select case p.Admission when '+' then 'admitted to the hospital' else 'followed at the outpatient clinic' end as patient_group, count(*) as normal_ldh_measurements from Laboratory l join Patient p on p.ID=l.ID where l.LDH<500 and p.Admission in ('+','-') group by p.Admission order by p.Admission='+' desc
answer: Normal LDH measurements (LDH < 500, the normal range given in the docs and wiki), counted across all lab records: admitted to the hospital 4881, followed at the outpatient clinic 4991. Records with a NULL LDH are not counted. Patients whose Admission value is blank are left out because the question names only '+' and '-'.

sql: SELECT MIN(CAST(strftime('%Y', L.Date) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', P.Birthday) AS INTEGER)) AS youngest_age FROM Laboratory L JOIN Patient P ON P.ID = L.ID WHERE L.RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(L.RNP AS REAL) >= 64;
answer: 18. I read RNP as a text column and kept only numeric values of at least 64 (64 and 256), skipping 'negative' and smaller values. Age is the test year minus the birth year.

sql: select p.ID, p.SEX, cast((strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',p.Birthday)) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09')<strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)) as int) as age from Patient p where p.ID in (select ID from Laboratory where GLU>=180 and "T-CHO"<250) order by p.ID
answer: 13명이 조건에 맞습니다. 한 검사 기록에서 GLU >= 180과 T-CHO < 250을 동시에 만족하는 환자를 골랐습니다. 나이는 2026-10-09 기준 만 나이이며, 생일이 아직 지나지 않았으면 1을 뺐습니다. 앞쪽 결과는 57266(M, 103), 2371753(F, 93), 3354706(F, 89)입니다.

sql: select s.NCESSchool from frpm f join schools s on s.CDSCode=f.CDSCode where f.CDSCode in ('01751010130583','01612910137588','01611760134270') and f.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`=(select max(`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`) from frpm where CDSCode in ('01751010130583','01612910137588','01611760134270'))
answer: NCES school ID 09282. That school (CDS 01751010130583) has the highest ages 5-17 enrollment of the three, at 2,550. The other two have 2,511 and 2,216, so there is no tie. The database stores CDS codes as 14-digit text with a leading zero, so I matched on that form.

sql: select s.superhero_name, p.publisher_name from superhero s left join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id where s.eye_colour_id=s.hair_colour_id and s.hair_colour_id=s.skin_colour_id and s.eye_colour_id<>1
answer: 4 heroes have the same known eye, hair and skin colour: Beast (Marvel Comics), Beast Boy (DC Comics), Hulk (Marvel Comics) and Purple Man (Marvel Comics). I read "known" as excluding colour id 1, 'No Colour'. Another 155 heroes match only because all three colours are 'No Colour'. The publisher is a left join, so a hero without a publisher would still be listed with a null name.

sql: SELECT Id, DisplayName, Views, Reputation FROM users WHERE (Location LIKE '%California%' AND Location NOT LIKE '%South Africa%' OR Location LIKE '%, CA' OR Location LIKE '% CA' OR Location LIKE '%, CA,%') AND Views = (SELECT MAX(Views) FROM users WHERE (Location LIKE '%California%' AND Location NOT LIKE '%South Africa%' OR Location LIKE '%, CA' OR Location LIKE '% CA' OR Location LIKE '%, CA,%'))
answer: The California-based user with the most profile views is Zach (user id 2817), with 1,244 views and a reputation of 9,604. No other California user ties with him. I counted a user as California-based if their location contains "California" (except "California, South Africa") or ends in ", CA" or " CA", or has ", CA," in the middle. Every user with 1,244 or more views was checked, and none of the others gives a California location. The `User` term used is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: select count(*) from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) where d.code is null and d.forename in (select forename from drivers group by forename having count(*)>1) and q.q1 like '%:%' and cast(substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1) as int)*60+cast(substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,':')+1) as real) > 120
answer: 23 Q1 times were slower than 2:00. Readings I chose: "no code" means drivers.code IS NULL. "Shares a first name" means the forename appears on at least one other driver row, counting all drivers including those with a code. "Slower than two minutes" means strictly more than 120 seconds. Empty or NULL q1 values are skipped.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT u.DisplayName) FROM users u JOIN badges b ON b.UserId = u.Id WHERE b.Name = 'Supporter' AND u.Age BETWEEN 19 AND 65
answer: 2940 distinct display names among users aged 19–65 (inclusive) who obtained the Supporter badge, all time. Display names are counted once each, even if shared by several users or if a user earned the badge more than once. The Badge and User terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select round(cast(count(hp.power_id) as real)/count(distinct s.id),2) from superhero s join race r on r.id=s.race_id join gender g on g.id=s.gender_id left join hero_power hp on hp.hero_id=s.id where r.race='God / Eternal' and g.gender='Male'
answer: 16.18. I read "God / Eternal" as the race value 'God / Eternal'. There are 17 male heroes with that race, and I counted all of them, including 3 who have no recorded superpowers. If you count only heroes who have at least one power (14 heroes), the average is 19.64.

sql: select 100.0*sum(strftime('%Y',Date)='2010')/count(*) - 100.0*sum(strftime('%Y',Date)='2011')/count(*) as diff_pct_points from badges where Name='Student'
answer: 2010 share minus 2011 share is about -9.54 percentage points. I read "share" as each year's portion of all Student badges across every year (2010 to 2014). 2010 has 542 badges and 2011 has 1,959.

sql: SELECT CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER) AS frame_year, COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS card_count FROM cards WHERE leadershipSkills LIKE '%''commander'': True%' AND cardKingdomId IS NOT NULL AND cardKingdomFoilId IS NOT NULL AND frameVersion GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER)) FROM cards WHERE leadershipSkills LIKE '%''commander'': True%' AND cardKingdomId IS NOT NULL AND cardKingdomFoilId IS NOT NULL AND frameVersion GLOB '[0-9]*')
answer:
The latest frame year is 2015, and 558 cards in the group have it. I ran the query and it returned the single row (2015, 558).

How I read the question:
- **Commander-leadable:** `leadershipSkills` contains `'commander': True`.
- **Both printings listed:** the card row has both `cardKingdomId` (non-foil) and `cardKingdomFoilId` (foil) filled in.
- **Frame year:** `frameVersion` holds 1993, 1997, 2003, 2015 or 'future'. I left out 'future' because it isn't a calendar year.
- **Card count:** distinct card names, because the table has one row per printing. Counting printings instead would give 820.

The `Card` term this relies on is still a draft in the ontology.

sql:
WITH j AS (SELECT l."T-CHO" AS tcho, p."Admission" AS adm, p."ID" AS id FROM "Laboratory" l JOIN "Patient" p ON p."ID"=l."ID" WHERE p."Admission" IN ('+','-') AND l."T-CHO" IS NOT NULL)
SELECT DISTINCT tcho AS "T-CHO", adm AS "Admission", id AS "ID" FROM j WHERE tcho=(SELECT MAX(tcho) FROM j j2 WHERE j2.adm=j.adm) ORDER BY CASE adm WHEN '+' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, id
answer: Admitted ('+'): highest T-CHO is 568, patient ID 1185720. Outpatient ('-'): highest T-CHO is 443, patient ID 3380563. Neither group had a tie. I took the maximum over all Laboratory rows with a T-CHO value, and I excluded the blank and '+(' Admission values because they fit neither group. The Laboratory Test and Patient terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT s.AvgScrMath, s.NumTstTakr FROM satscores AS s INNER JOIN schools AS sc ON s.cds = sc.CDSCode WHERE sc.CDSCode = '01611190130609' AND sc.FundingType = 'Directly funded'
answer: The school is directly funded. Its average SAT math score is 593 and 20 students took the SAT. The CDS code you gave has 13 digits, but it is stored as the 14-digit text '01611190130609', so I added the leading zero. The query returns no rows if the school is not directly funded. The Terms used (SAT Score Record, School) are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
WITH sc AS (SELECT * FROM schools WHERE County IN ('Amador','Madera') AND School IS NOT NULL),
nm AS (SELECT CDSCode, AdmFName1 n FROM sc UNION SELECT CDSCode, AdmFName2 FROM sc UNION SELECT CDSCode, AdmFName3 FROM sc),
top AS (SELECT n FROM nm WHERE n IS NOT NULL GROUP BY n ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, n LIMIT 2),
d AS (SELECT CDSCode, District FROM schools WHERE County IN ('Amador','Madera') AND School IS NULL AND DOC IN ('00','52','54','56'))
SELECT d.District, top.n AS FirstName,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM nm JOIN sc ON sc.CDSCode=nm.CDSCode WHERE substr(sc.CDSCode,1,7)=substr(d.CDSCode,1,7) AND nm.n=top.n) AS SchoolCount
FROM d CROSS JOIN top ORDER BY d.District, top.n;
answer:
The top two first names are Stacy (8 schools) and Avetik (4 schools). Avetik, Gary and Kuljeet are tied at 4 schools, and Avetik comes first alphabetically. The query returns 48 rows: 24 public school districts (unified, elementary, high school districts and county offices of education) times 2 names. Stacy's 8 schools are all in Yosemite Unified. Avetik's 4 are all in Madera County Office of Education. Every other row is 0.

How I read the question:
- A "school" is a row with a non-null School value, in any status (open, closed or merged). The district's own record is not counted.
- A school counts once per name, even if the name appears in more than one of its three administrator slots.
- A school belongs to a district when the first 7 digits of their CDS codes match.
- A district is a record with no School value and a DOC code of 00, 52, 54 or 56.

sql: select a.frequency, o.k_symbol from account a join "order" o on o.account_id = a.account_id where a.account_id = 3 and o.amount = 3539
answer: Account 3 receives statements monthly (POPLATEK MESICNE). Its scheduled payment (standing order) of 3,539 has payment-purpose code k_symbol = POJISTNE (insurance payment).

sql: SELECT s.AdmFName1, s.AdmLName1 FROM satscores t JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = t.cds WHERE t.rtype = 'S' AND substr(s.CDSCode,1,2) = '16' ORDER BY t.NumGE1500 DESC, s.CDSCode ASC LIMIT 1
answer:
Rodney Brumit (school CDS 16639821635606, 37 students scoring 1500 or higher).

CDS code 1611430131177 is not in the `schools` table, so I couldn't look up its county. I used its first two digits, 16, which is the Kings County code. All 16-prefixed schools in the data are listed as Kings. If that code belongs to a different county, the answer would change.

I used only school-level SAT rows (`rtype = 'S'`) to exclude district roll-ups. I took the administrator from the first administrator fields (`AdmFName1`, `AdmLName1`).

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.driverId) FROM results r JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId = r.raceId JOIN status s ON s.statusId = r.statusId WHERE ra.year = 1962 AND ra.name = 'British Grand Prix' AND s.status = 'Withdrew'
answer: 5 drivers withdrew from the 1962 British Grand Prix. I read "withdrew" as results rows with status 'Withdrew' (statusId 54). I did not count other retirements such as engine, brakes or battery failures. The five rows were for five distinct drivers.

sql: select s.School, s.County, s.District, s.City, f.`Enrollment (K-12)`, f.`FRPM Count (K-12)`, f.`Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)`, t.NumTstTakr, t.AvgScrRead, t.AvgScrMath, t.AvgScrWrite, t.NumGE1500 from schools s left join frpm f on f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode left join satscores t on t.cds=s.CDSCode where s.CDSCode='01612590137943'
answer:
해당 학교는 Oakland Unified 교육구 소속의 Skyline High(Alameda 카운티, Oakland 시)입니다. K-12 재학생은 1845명입니다. 무상 또는 할인 급식 대상(FRPM) K-12 학생은 1438명이고, 비율은 표에 저장된 값 그대로 0.77940379403794(약 77.9%)입니다. SAT는 응시자 179명, 평균 읽기 447점, 수학 446점, 쓰기 447점이며, 총점 1500점 이상은 49명입니다.

sql: with t as (select e.type, count(distinct a.link_to_member) n from event e join attendance a on a.link_to_event=e.event_id where e.event_date>='2019-09-01' and e.event_date<'2020-06-01' group by e.type) select type, n as members from t where n=(select max(n) from t)
answer: Meeting and Registration tie, with 30 members each. I counted distinct members per event type, so someone who went to several events of one type counts once. All events in the data fall between 2019-09-01 and 2020-05-05, so the date filter excludes nothing.

sql:
SELECT c.Currency, COUNT(*) AS customer_count
FROM (SELECT CustomerID FROM yearmonth
      WHERE Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201311' AND Consumption > 0
      GROUP BY CustomerID
      HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT Date) = 11) y
JOIN customers c USING (CustomerID)
GROUP BY c.Currency
answer: CZK: 61 customers, EUR: 4 customers. I read "bought fuel in a month" as a yearmonth row with Consumption > 0, and counted customers who have such a row in all 11 months from 201301 to 201311. If rows with zero or negative consumption counted as purchases, CZK would be 62 and EUR would stay at 4.

18.67. Landon Donovan's overall rating on 12 July 2013 was 18.67% higher than the average across all players. sql: SELECT p.player_name FROM Player p JOIN Player_Attributes a ON a.player_api_id=p.player_api_id WHERE p.height=(SELECT MAX(height) FROM Player) OR p.height=(SELECT MIN(height) FROM Player) GROUP BY p.player_api_id ORDER BY AVG(a.finishing) DESC LIMIT 1
answer: Juan Quero. He is the shortest player (157 cm) and averages 60.9 finishing over 10 assessments. The tallest, Kristof van Hout (208 cm), averages 15.5 over 14. I read "tallest and shortest" as the single player with the maximum height and the single player with the minimum height.

sql: select d.forename||' '||d.surname as driver, r.name as race, r.year, q.q3 from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) join races r using(raceId) where d.nationality='British' and cast(substr(d.dob,1,4) as int)>1980 and q.q3 is not null and q.q3<>'' and q.q3 = (select min(q3) from qualifying q2 join drivers d2 using(driverId) where d2.nationality='British' and cast(substr(d2.dob,1,4) as int)>1980 and q2.q3<>'')
answer: Lewis Hamilton, Austrian Grand Prix, 2017, Q3 time 1:04.424. Reading used: nationality = 'British', birth year later than 1980. The fastest time is the lowest Q3 value. Q3 times are text in M:SS.mmm format, and the query compares them as text. Rows with an empty Q3 were excluded. Only one result had this time, so there is no tie.

sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, p.Birthday FROM Patient p WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE LDH >= 500) AND p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE "U-PRO" IN ('100','300','>=300','>=1000','+2(100)')) ORDER BY p.ID
answer:
18명이 조건에 맞습니다(ID 912147부터 5441886까지, 여성 16명, 남성 2명: 3182521, 5181621). 쿼리는 ID, SEX, Birthday를 환자당 한 행씩 ID 순으로 반환합니다.

해석: U-PRO는 텍스트 컬럼이라 mg/dL 100 이상으로 볼 값만 골랐습니다. 포함한 값은 '100', '300', '>=300', '>=1000', '+2(100)'입니다. 단계 등급으로 보이는 '1', '2', '3', '4'는 mg/dL 값이 아니라고 보고 제외했습니다. '+1(30)', '30', 'TR', '-', '0'도 제외했습니다. 이 등급 값을 포함하면 결과가 달라질 수 있습니다. LDH는 500 이상(500 포함)이며, 두 조건은 서로 다른 검사일에서 충족해도 됩니다.

sql: SELECT d.code FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(q.q3)<>'' ORDER BY d.code
answer: 10 drivers set a Q3 time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix: BOT, HAM, MAS, OCO, RAI, RIC, STR, VAN, VER, VET. A driver counts if their q3 value is neither null nor empty. The Driver, Qualifying Result and Race terms the query relies on are still drafts in the ontology.

sql:

WHERE e.s=m.lo AND l.s=m.hi;
answer: 가장 이른 시작은 fuji(04:30:00), 가장 늦은 시작은 americas(20:00:00)이고, 두 시각의 차이는 55,800초입니다. 동률인 서킷은 없어 각각 한 곳씩 나왔습니다. races.time이 비어 있는(NULL) 722개 레이스는 시작 시각을 알 수 없어 제외했고, 시각이 있는 레이스는 모든 시즌에서 비교했습니다.

sql: select g as lowest_grade from (select substr(GSoffered,1,instr(GSoffered,'-')-1) g from schools where NCESDist='0632640' and GSoffered like '%-%') order by case g when 'P' then -2 when 'K' then 0 else cast(g as int) end limit 1
answer: The lowest grade is 'P' (preschool). One school in district 0632640 offers P-6. The other schools start at K (K-2, K-6, K-8) or at a higher grade. I read the first part of the GSoffered span as the grade where a school starts. I ranked the grades as P < K < 1 and up, because GSoffered is free text and can't be compared numerically. If you only want K-12 grades, the answer is 'K'.

sql: SELECT s.NCESSchool FROM frpm f JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode WHERE f.CDSCode IN ('01751010130583','01612910137588','01611760134270') AND f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" = (SELECT MAX("Enrollment (Ages 5-17)") FROM frpm WHERE CDSCode IN ('01751010130583','01612910137588','01611760134270'))
answer: NCES school ID 09282 is the school with the highest enrollment of students aged 5-17 among the three. There is no tie. I padded the CDS codes to 14 digits with a leading zero and used frpm."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" (2014-2015). The terms used are drafts and not yet certified.

sql:

sql: with c as (select college, count(distinct major_id) n from major where major_id in (select link_to_major from member) group by college) select college, n from c where n=(select max(n) from c) order by college
answer: Two colleges tie for the most majors on the roster, with 6 each: College of Agriculture and Applied Sciences, and College of Humanities and Social Sciences. I counted distinct majors held by any member, whatever their position. One member has no major recorded (Randy Woodard), so they are left out of the count.

sql:
WITH s AS (SELECT * FROM schools WHERE County IN ('Amador','Madera')),
adm AS (SELECT CDSCode, AdmFName1 AS fn FROM s UNION SELECT CDSCode, AdmFName2 FROM s UNION SELECT CDSCode, AdmFName3 FROM s),
top2 AS (SELECT fn FROM adm WHERE fn IS NOT NULL GROUP BY fn ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT CDSCode) DESC, fn ASC LIMIT 2),
d AS (SELECT DISTINCT County, District FROM s WHERE DOCType IN ('Unified School District','Elementary School District','High School District','County Office of Education (COE)'))
SELECT d.District AS district_name, t.fn AS first_name,
 (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.CDSCode) FROM s JOIN adm a ON a.CDSCode=s.CDSCode WHERE s.County=d.County AND s.District=d.District AND a.fn=t.fn) AS num_schools
FROM d CROSS JOIN top2 t ORDER BY d.District, t.fn
answer: The top two first names are Stacy and Avetik. The query returns 50 rows (25 public districts x 2 names). Yosemite Unified has 8 schools run by a Stacy, and Madera County Office of Education has 4 run by an Avetik. Every other district has 0 for both names. Assumptions: every row in `schools` for the two counties counts as a school regardless of status (including closed schools and district-office rows). Administrators 1 to 3 all count, each school once per name. The `School` Term is draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superhero WHERE publisher_id = (SELECT publisher_id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = 'A-Bomb') AND (race_id IS NULL OR race_id = 1)

sql: SELECT SEX, COUNT(*) FROM Patient p WHERE SEX IN ('F','M') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID = p.ID) GROUP BY SEX

sql: select round(avg(s.weight_kg),2) from superhero s join gender g on g.id=s.gender_id join alignment a on a.id=s.alignment_id where g.gender='Female' and a.alignment='Good' and s.weight_kg>0
answer: The average weight of good-aligned female superheroes is 70.76 kg. I counted weight as unknown when weight_kg is NULL or 0, because the wiki and data use 0 as a missing-value marker, so those rows are excluded.

sql: select c.name, c.location, c.country, r.year, p.milliseconds as pit_stop_milliseconds from pitStops p join races r on r.raceId=p.raceId join circuits c on c.circuitId=r.circuitId where p.milliseconds=(select max(milliseconds) from pitStops)
answer: The longest single pit stop was at Autódromo José Carlos Pace in São Paulo, Brazil, in the 2016 season. It lasted 2,011,266 ms (about 33 min 31.266 s, as shown in the duration text). No other stop ties with it, so the query returns one row. I measured length by the integer `milliseconds` column. The data only covers 2011–2017, so "all seasons" means those years. The 2016 Brazilian race was long delayed by rain, so this stop is probably a red-flag wait in the pit lane. That is my inference and I did not check it.

sql:
SELECT e.type AS event_type,
 (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) FROM attendance a JOIN event e2 ON a.link_to_event = e2.event_id WHERE e2.type = e.type AND e2.event_date >= '2019-01-01' AND e2.event_date < '2020-01-01') AS members_attended,
 (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(b.amount),0) FROM budget b JOIN event e3 ON b.link_to_event = e3.event_id WHERE e3.type = e.type AND e3.event_date >= '2019-01-01' AND e3.event_date < '2020-01-01') AS total_budgeted

GROUP BY e.type
ORDER BY e.type
answer: The query returns 8 event types for 2019, in alphabetical order. Each row shows distinct members attended and total budgeted dollars (planned `budget.amount`, not spent): Budget 5 / $0; Community Service 13 / $0; Election 0 / $0; Game 24 / $0; Guest Speaker 29 / $785; Meeting 30 / $1175; Registration 30 / $300; Social 24 / $0. I read 2019 as the calendar year (2019-01-01 up to but not including 2020-01-01) and counted each member once per type. Types with no budget lines or no attendance show 0. The Event and Budget terms in the ontology are drafts, not certified.

sql:

sql: SELECT l.ID, l.Date, l.DNA FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND p.Admission = '+' AND CAST(l.DNA AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(l2.DNA AS REAL)) FROM Laboratory l2 JOIN Patient p2 ON p2.ID = l2.ID WHERE p2.SEX = 'F' AND p2.Admission = '+') ORDER BY l.ID;
answer: Patient 2933261, lab test date 1988-04-25, anti-DNA level 185. Only one record has the highest level, so there are no ties. I took "admitted as inpatients" to mean Patient.Admission = '+'. Three patients have the malformed Admission value '+(', and I left them out. sql: SELECT s.full_name FROM hero_attribute ha JOIN superhero s ON ha.hero_id=s.id JOIN attribute a ON ha.attribute_id=a.id WHERE a.attribute_name='Strength' AND ha.attribute_value=(SELECT MAX(ha2.attribute_value) FROM hero_attribute ha2 JOIN attribute a2 ON ha2.attribute_id=a2.id WHERE a2.attribute_name='Strength') AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name<>'-'
answer: The query returned 35 known full names of heroes tied for the highest Strength value, including Abraxas, Thanos, Doomsday, Thor Odinson, Kal-El and Robert Bruce Banner. I treated "known" as excluding NULL or '-' full names, so tied heroes with no known full name are left out. The Terms behind the query (Attribute, Hero Attribute Score, Superhero) are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT d.number, d.surname FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3<>'' AND (CAST(substr(q.q3,1,instr(q.q3,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60 + CAST(substr(q.q3,instr(q.q3,':')+1) AS REAL)) < 98.0
answer: Seven drivers were under 1:38.000 in Q3 at the 2017 Italian GP: 44 Hamilton, 33 Verstappen, 3 Ricciardo, 18 Stroll, 31 Ocon, 77 Bottas, 7 Räikkönen. I used drivers.number as the permanent career number (not qualifying.number, the weekend entry number). Q3 text times were converted to seconds and compared strictly under 98.0. The Driver, Qualifying Result and Race terms are still drafts.

sql: select 100.0*(sum(case when substr(l.date,1,4)='1997' then amount end)-sum(case when substr(l.date,1,4)='1996' then amount end))/sum(case when substr(l.date,1,4)='1996' then amount end) as growth_pct from loan l join disp d on d.account_id=l.account_id and d.type='OWNER' join client c on c.client_id=d.client_id and c.gender='M' where substr(l.date,1,4) in ('1996','1997')

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(Reputation),2) AS avg_reputation FROM users WHERE (Location='India' OR Location LIKE '%, India') AND Id IN (SELECT OwnerUserId FROM posts WHERE CreaionDate >= '2010-01-01' AND CreaionDate < '2011-01-01')

I averaged over distinct users who created at least one post (of any type) in 2010, so each user counts once. The posts date column is spelled CreaionDate in the schema. The Post and User terms used are still draft, not certified.

sql: select round(avg(A11),2) from district where district_id in (select district_id from client where gender='F' and birth_date<'1950-01-01')
answer: 9031.68. I used district.A11 as the average salary. I averaged once per distinct district where at least one female client born before 1950-01-01 lives. If you weight each district by its number of such clients, the figure is 9518.51.

sql: select round(sum(coalesce(f."FRPM Count (Ages 5-17)",0))*1.0/count(*),2) from schools s left join frpm f on f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode and f."Academic Year"='2014-2015' where s.SOC='11'
answer: 5.42. Reading chosen: "Youth Authority school" means SOC code 11 (Youth Authority Facilities, 43 schools in any status), not just the 6 with EdOpsCode YTH. The measure is FRPM Count (Ages 5-17) for 2014-2015. Schools with no frpm row count as 0.

sql: select c.Text, coalesce(u.DisplayName,c.UserDisplayName) as DisplayName from comments c join posts p on p.Id=c.PostId left join users u on u.Id=c.UserId where p.Title='Analysing wind data with R' order by c.CreationDate desc, c.Id desc limit 10
answer: The query returns the 10 newest comments on 'Analysing wind data with R', newest first, with each comment's text and its author's display name. Display name comes from users via UserId, falling back to comments.UserDisplayName. All 10 rows had a matching user. Ties on CreationDate are broken by higher comment Id first. The newest comment is by eliavs (2011-02-14 08:50:44).

sql:
WITH x AS (
SELECT m.season, v.p FROM "Match" m JOIN League l ON l.id=m.league_id
JOIN (SELECT id, home_player_1 p FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_2 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_3 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_4 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_5 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_6 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_7 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_8 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_9 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_10 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_11 FROM "Match"
UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_1 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_2 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_3 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_4 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_5 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_6 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_7 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_8 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_9 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_10 FROM "Match" UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_11 FROM "Match") v ON v.id=m.id
WHERE l.name='Italy Serie A' AND m.season IN ('2008/2009','2015/2016') AND v.p IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY m.season, v.p)
SELECT x.season, COUNT(*) AS player_count, ROUND(AVG(p.height),2) AS avg_height_cm FROM x JOIN Player p ON p.player_api_id=x.p GROUP BY x.season ORDER BY x.season
answer:
Serie A 2008/2009: 472 players, average height 181.79 cm. Serie A 2015/2016: 508 players, average height 182.14 cm. I ran the query with one unused extra CTE, which I removed from the final SQL. The final text itself was not re-run.

Reading I chose: a player counts if they appear in any of the 22 lineup slots (home_player_1..11 and away_player_1..11) of a Serie A match in that season. Each player is counted once per season, so a player who appeared in both seasons shows up in both rows. Height is `Player.height`, which holds centimeters, and each player is weighted equally. The Player, Match and League Terms are still in draft status, not certified.

sql: SELECT "Diagnosis" FROM "Patient" WHERE "First Date" BETWEEN '1998-02-15' AND '1998-02-28' AND "Admission"='+' ORDER BY "Birthday" ASC, "ID" ASC LIMIT 1
answer: BEHCET. Assumptions: "first seen" = First Date; inpatient = Admission '+' (the '+(' variant is excluded); oldest = earliest Birthday, ties go to the smaller ID. The Patient term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: select f.`Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)`, f.`District Code` from frpm f join schools s using(CDSCode) where s.AdmFName1='Alusine' or s.AdmFName2='Alusine' or s.AdmFName3='Alusine'
answer: Alusine Conteh administers Buena Vista Elementary (Palmdale). Its Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12) is 0.7015 (about 70.2%), and its district code is 64857. I matched the first name in any of the three administrator columns, and only this one school matched.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.height_cm > 0 THEN s.height_cm END), 2) AS avg_height_cm, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END), 2) AS avg_weight_kg
FROM superhero s
JOIN colour c ON s.skin_colour_id = c.id
JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id = a.id
WHERE c.colour = 'Green' AND a.alignment = 'Bad'
answer: 녹색 피부의 악당은 평균 키가 194.2cm, 평균 몸무게가 161.75kg입니다. 악당은 정렬 값이 'Bad'인 캐릭터, 녹색 피부는 피부색이 'Green'인 캐릭터로 보았고, 키와 몸무게가 NULL이거나 0이면 기록이 없는 것으로 보고 해당 평균에서만 제외했습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "Laboratory" l WHERE l."Date" = (SELECT MIN("Date") FROM "Laboratory" WHERE ID = l.ID) AND l."GOT" < 60 AND CAST(l."RNP" AS REAL) > 10
answer: 6명입니다. 환자별로 검사일(Date)이 가장 이른 기록을 첫 검사로 보고, 그 기록의 GOT가 60 미만이고 RNP가 10 초과인 환자를 셌습니다. RNP는 텍스트 컬럼이라 숫자로 변환해 비교했고, 'negative'는 0으로 변환되어 제외됩니다. 첫 기록의 GOT나 RNP가 비어 있으면 조건을 만족하지 않는 것으로 처리했습니다. 쿼리가 쓴 'Laboratory Test' 용어는 아직 인증되지 않은 초안 상태입니다.

sql: with c as (select sum(p.publisher_name='DC Comics') dc, sum(p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics') m from superhero s join publisher p on s.publisher_id=p.id) select case when dc=m then 'Tie' when dc>m then 'DC Comics' else 'Marvel Comics' end as publisher, abs(dc-m) as difference from c
answer: Marvel Comics has more superheroes: 387 against 224 for DC Comics, a difference of 163. The query returns the publisher name (or 'Tie') and the difference. I counted rows in `superhero` joined to `publisher` by publisher_id.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.ID FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p."Admission" = '-' AND l.CPK < 250 AND l.RNP <> 'negative' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 4 ORDER BY p.ID
answer: 7 patient ids: 2320830, 3175008, 4018722, 4398703, 4915498, 5122312, 5400270. Reading used: outpatient = Admission '-'; CPK < 250; RNP (text) cast to a number and > 4, with 'negative' excluded. A patient counts if a single lab result meets both the CPK and RNP conditions; ids are distinct. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT s.School, s.County, s.District, s.City, f.`Enrollment (K-12)`, f.`FRPM Count (K-12)`, f.`Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)`, t.NumTstTakr, t.AvgScrRead, t.AvgScrMath, t.AvgScrWrite, t.NumGE1500 FROM schools s LEFT JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds=s.CDSCode WHERE s.CDSCode='01612590137943'
answer:
The school is Skyline High in Oakland Unified district, Oakland, Alameda County. K-12 enrollment is 1845. 1438 students are eligible for free or reduced price meals, which is 0.77940379403794 as stored (a fraction, about 77.9%). SAT: 179 test takers, average reading 447, math 446, writing 447, and 49 test takers with a total score of at least 1500.

Assumptions: The CDS code is stored with a leading zero (01612590137943), so the query uses that form. I read "free or reduced price meals" as the FRPM count and percent columns, not the free-meal-only columns.

sql: select round(100.0*count(f.uuid)/count(*),2) as percentage from cards c left join (select distinct uuid from foreign_data where language='French') f on f.uuid=c.uuid where c.power is null or c.power like '%*%'
answer: 47.95% of the 31,078 matching printings have a French translation. I counted a printing as matching if its power is NULL or contains '*' (a variable value such as '*' or '*²'). Values like '∞', '?' and '-1' are not counted as variable. A French translation means a `foreign_data` row with language 'French'.

sql:
WITH t AS (
 SELECT d.surname, r.name AS race,
  CAST(substr(q.q2,1,instr(q.q2,':')-1) AS INT)*60000 + CAST(substr(q.q2,instr(q.q2,':')+1,2) AS INT)*1000 + CAST(substr(q.q2,-3) AS INT) AS ms
 FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId
 WHERE r.year=2017 AND q.q2 LIKE '_:__.___')
SELECT surname, race FROM t WHERE ms=(SELECT MIN(ms) FROM t)
answer: The quickest 2017 Q2 time was set by Bottas at the Austrian Grand Prix. There is no tie. I converted the m:ss.mmm text times to milliseconds to compare them, and I skipped NULL and empty Q2 values.

sql:
WITH s AS (
 SELECT code FROM (
  SELECT s.code FROM sets s WHERE s.code IN (SELECT setCode FROM cards WHERE name='Abyssal Horror') ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.code LIMIT 1)
 UNION ALL
 SELECT code FROM (SELECT code FROM sets ORDER BY releaseDate DESC, code LIMIT 1)
)
SELECT st.name AS set_name,
 ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN c.manaCost IS NOT NULL AND c.manaCost<>'' AND c.convertedManaCost<=3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS pct
FROM s JOIN sets st ON st.code=s.code JOIN cards c ON c.setCode=st.code
GROUP BY st.code, st.name
answer: Time Spiral Remastered: 80.00%. Urza's Saga: 58.15%. The query returns them in that order, which is not chronological. Readings I chose: the denominator is all cards in the set, and a card counts only if manaCost is non-null and non-empty and convertedManaCost <= 3. I used cards.convertedManaCost as the mana value. The Card and Card Set terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
WITH s AS (SELECT cds, AvgScrRead+AvgScrMath+AvgScrWrite AS sat FROM satscores WHERE rtype='S' AND AvgScrRead IS NOT NULL AND AvgScrMath IS NOT NULL AND AvgScrWrite IS NOT NULL)
SELECT sc.FundingType, COUNT(*) AS charter_schools, SUM(f."Enrollment (K-12)") AS total_enrollment_k12, ROUND(AVG(f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)")*100,2) AS avg_pct_frpm, ROUND(AVG(s.sat),2) AS avg_sat_total
FROM schools sc JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode=sc.CDSCode LEFT JOIN s ON s.cds=sc.CDSCode
WHERE sc.Charter=1 AND sc.StatusType='Active' AND sc.FundingType IN ('Directly funded','Locally funded')
GROUP BY sc.FundingType
answer:
Directly funded: 779 active charters, 372,954 K-12 students, 63.88% average FRPM eligibility, average SAT 1350.84. Locally funded: 319 active charters, 150,022 students, 44.84%, SAT 1480.15.

Choices I made: charters are schools.Charter=1 with StatusType='Active'. The one 'Not in CS funding model' school is excluded. Enrollment and meal data come from frpm (2014-15), joined on CDSCode, so active charters with no frpm row are not counted. Meal eligibility is the simple average of each school's FRPM fraction, times 100. SAT is the simple average of each school's reading+math+writing averages, over schools with all three scores. It is not weighted by test takers.

sql: SELECT L.name FROM Match M JOIN League L ON L.id = M.league_id WHERE M.season = '2009/2010' GROUP BY L.id, L.name HAVING AVG(M.home_team_goal) > AVG(M.away_team_goal)
answer: 11개 리그가 해당합니다. 2009/2010 시즌에 홈팀 평균 득점이 원정팀보다 높은 리그는 Belgium Jupiler League, England Premier League, France Ligue 1, Germany 1. Bundesliga, Italy Serie A, Netherlands Eredivisie, Poland Ekstraklasa, Portugal Liga ZON Sagres, Scotland Premier League, Spain LIGA BBVA, Switzerland Super League입니다. 리그별로 경기당 홈팀 평균 득점과 원정팀 평균 득점을 비교했습니다. 사용한 Match, League Term은 아직 인증되지 않은 draft 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT p.Birthday FROM Patient p JOIN (SELECT ID, MAX(GPT) g FROM Laboratory WHERE GPT < 60 GROUP BY ID) m ON m.ID=p.ID WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(RNP AS REAL) >= 16) ORDER BY m.g DESC, p.ID ASC LIMIT 3
answer: The three patients' Birthdays, in rank order, are 1949-05-11, 1958-10-23 and 1963-12-13. Anti-RNP is stored as text, so I counted a patient if any test had a numeric RNP value of 16 or higher; 'negative' and null don't count. Each patient's value is their highest GPT among tests with GPT below 60. Ties go to the smaller patient ID. The query uses the draft Terms Laboratory Test and Patient.

sql: select round(avg(case when height_cm>0 then height_cm end),1) as avg_height_cm, round(avg(case when weight_kg>0 then weight_kg end),1) as avg_weight_kg from superhero s join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id where p.publisher_name='George Lucas'
answer: George Lucas's heroes (the publisher 'George Lucas') average 187.2 cm tall and 83.0 kg. I treated height or weight values of 0 or NULL as unknown, as the docs describe, and left them out of the matching average.

sql: select count(distinct artist) from cards where borderColor='black' and availability like '%arena%' and availability not like '%mtgo%' and power glob '[0-9]*' and power not like '%*%' and cast(power as integer)>=5
answer: 56 artists. I counted cards whose power is a plain number of 5 or more. That leaves out '*' and '1+*', which vary, and no '∞' values showed up among Arena cards. I counted every printing in the table, and artists with no name recorded are not counted.

sql: SELECT d.nationality FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE q.raceId=(SELECT raceId FROM races WHERE year=1995 AND name='Japanese Grand Prix') AND q.q1=(SELECT MAX(q1) FROM qualifying WHERE raceId=(SELECT raceId FROM races WHERE year=1995 AND name='Japanese Grand Prix') AND q1<>'')
answer: Belgian. The slowest Q1 time at the 1995 Japanese GP was 1:48.289, with no tie. I compared the time strings directly, since all the values are in m:ss.mmm format. I did not rerun the final query itself, only the ordering query it is based on.

sql: with l as (select player_api_id, max(date) d from Player_Attributes group by 1), r as (select a.player_api_id, max(a.id) id from Player_Attributes a join l on l.player_api_id=a.player_api_id and l.d=a.date group by 1) select round(avg(p.height),2) from Player p join r on r.player_api_id=p.player_api_id join Player_Attributes a on a.id=r.id where a.defensive_work_rate in ('low','high')
answer: 평균 키는 180.95cm입니다. 선수별로 date가 가장 최근인 평가 기록(같은 날짜면 id가 큰 쪽)을 현재 등급으로 보았습니다. 'medium이 아닌' 등급은 유효한 값인 low와 high로 한정했고, '_0', 'o', 숫자 같은 오염된 값과 NULL은 제외했습니다. 오염된 값까지 포함하면 결과가 달라질 수 있는데, 이 경우는 계산하지 않았습니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 2) FROM superhero s JOIN gender g ON g.id = s.gender_id WHERE g.gender = 'Female' AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: 78.51 kg. I counted weight_kg of 0 or NULL as unknown, as docs/superhero.csv says. That leaves 144 Female heroes. If you left the zeros in, the average would be 60.78.

sql: select d.driverRef, d.nationality, d.dob, q.q1 from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) join races r using(raceId) where r.name='Japanese Grand Prix' and r.year=1995 and q.q1<>'' and q.q1=(select max(q2.q1) from qualifying q2 where q2.raceId=r.raceId and q2.q1<>'')
answer: 1995 일본 그랑프리 Q1에서 가장 느린 기록을 낸 드라이버는 gachot(벨기에, 생일 1962-12-23)이고, 기록은 1:48.289입니다. 동률은 없습니다. 이 시기(1994~2002년)에는 q1 열에 예선 단일 기록이 들어 있어 그 값을 Q1 시간으로 봤습니다. 기록은 모두 m:ss.mmm 형식이라 문자열 최댓값이 가장 느린 시간입니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND l.PT < 14 AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) >= 16
answer: 3명입니다. PT와 RNP는 같은 검사 기록(Laboratory의 같은 행)에서 읽었고, 조건은 성별 'F', PT 14 미만, RNP 16 이상입니다. RNP 열이 텍스트라 숫자로 변환해 비교했으며 'negative'는 0으로 처리됩니다. 같은 환자의 기록이 여러 건이어도 한 명으로 세려고 환자 ID 중복을 제거했습니다. 사용한 용어(Patient, Laboratory Test)는 아직 인증되지 않은 draft 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superhero s WHERE s.publisher_id = (SELECT publisher_id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name='Blackwulf') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM superhero o WHERE o.eye_colour_id = s.eye_colour_id AND o.publisher_id IS NOT NULL AND o.publisher_id <> s.publisher_id)
answer: 382. Blackwulf's publisher is Marvel Comics (publisher_id 13). The count is of Marvel heroes whose eye colour (matched on eye_colour_id) is also held by at least one hero from another publisher. Heroes with no publisher were not treated as another publisher. The query used the draft, uncertified Superhero term.

sql: SELECT COUNT(l.ID) AS total_lab_tests, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN l.ID IS NULL THEN p.ID END) AS patients_without_labs FROM Patient p LEFT JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE LOWER(p.Diagnosis) = 'psoriatic arthritis'
answer: Two patients have the diagnosis (spelled "Psoriatic Arthritis" and "Psoriatic arthritis"), so I matched it case-insensitively. Together they have 56 laboratory tests across all dates. One of them has no laboratory record.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid=c.uuid WHERE c.artist='Erica Yang' AND l.format='pauper' AND l.status='Legal' AND ','||c.availability||',' LIKE '%,paper,%'
answer: 23 printings. I counted each row in `cards` as one printing. A card counts if its artist is 'Erica Yang', its pauper legality status is 'Legal' (banned cards are excluded), and its availability list includes 'paper'.

sql: SELECT p.Id, u.DisplayName FROM posts p LEFT JOIN users u ON u.Id = p.OwnerUserId WHERE p.CreaionDate >= '2010-01-01' AND p.CreaionDate < '2011-01-01' ORDER BY p.FavoriteCount DESC LIMIT 1
answer: Post 1595 (233 favorites, no tie) was the most favorited post created in 2010. Its owner is Fabian Fagerholm. I took the owner's display name from users.DisplayName through OwnerUserId, because posts.OwnerDisplayName is empty for about 93% of posts. The Post and User terms in the ontology are still drafts and not certified.

sql: SELECT d.driverRef FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND (q.q2 IS NULL OR q.q2='') ORDER BY q.q1 DESC, q.driverId ASC
answer: Five drivers were eliminated in Q1 at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, listed slowest Q1 time first: grosjean (1:43.355), wehrlein (1:41.875), ericsson (1:41.732), jolyon_palmer (1:40.646), kevin_magnussen (1:40.489). I treated "eliminated after the first session" as having no Q2 time. The data stores that as NULL for grosjean and as an empty string for the other four, so the query checks for both. The Q1 times are text in m:ss.mmm format, so sorting them as text gives the right time order. The ties rule (lower driverId first) is in the ORDER BY, though no two Q1 times matched here. The Driver, Qualifying Result and Race terms the query relies on are still draft, not certified.

sql:
SELECT s.name, s.keyruneCode, COUNT(DISTINCT t.language) AS language_count
FROM sets s
LEFT JOIN set_translations t ON t.setCode = s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND t.translation <> ''
WHERE s.releaseDate BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31'
GROUP BY s.code, s.name, s.keyruneCode
ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.name
answer: The query returns 34 sets released in 2020. Most have 0 translated names. Only Theros Beyond Death, Ikoria: Lair of Behemoths and Core Set 2021 have 1 each. I counted distinct languages that have a non-empty translation, and I kept sets with no translations in the result with a count of 0 (LEFT JOIN). Each set code is its own row, so promos and variants appear separately. Several sets share a keyrune code (for example PMEI and JMP), and that is how the data stores it.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(UpVotes),2) AS avg_upvotes, ROUND(AVG(Age),2) AS avg_age FROM users WHERE Id IN (SELECT OwnerUserId FROM posts WHERE CreaionDate LIKE '2012%' GROUP BY OwnerUserId HAVING COUNT(*)>10)
answer: Among the 268 users who created more than ten posts in 2012, the average number of up-votes is 505.63 and the average age is 36.14. I read "posts created in 2012" as the posts table's creation date column (spelled `CreaionDate` in the schema) starting with 2012. Users with no recorded age are skipped in the age average, because AVG ignores NULLs.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN a.alignment = 'Neutral' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS neutral_percentage,
       SUM(CASE WHEN a.alignment = 'Neutral' AND p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS neutral_marvel_count
FROM superhero AS s
LEFT JOIN alignment AS a ON s.alignment_id = a.id
LEFT JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
answer: 3.73% of all superheroes have Neutral alignment, and 10 of those Neutral superheroes were published by Marvel Comics. The denominator is all superhero rows, with LEFT JOINs so heroes missing an alignment or publisher are still counted. The Alignment and Publisher terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) AS patient_count FROM Laboratory WHERE SSA IS NOT NULL AND SSA NOT IN ('negative','0') AND ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE "U-PRO" IS NOT NULL AND "U-PRO" NOT IN ('-','0'))
answer: 15 patients. Anti-SSA counts as abnormal if it is non-NULL and not 'negative' or '0'. In the data this means 1, 4, 16, 64 or 256. Proteinuria counts as positive if U-PRO is non-NULL and not '-' or '0', so 'TR' (trace) counts as positive. The two findings are matched per patient across all of that patient's Laboratory rows, not per visit. The odd value '-15' is ambiguous. Treating it as negative or as positive gives the same count of 15.

sql: select count(distinct c.name) from cards c join legalities l on l.uuid=c.uuid where c.manaCost='{0}' and l.format='commander' and l.status='Legal'
answer: 43 different cards have a printed mana cost of exactly {0} and a Legal Commander entry. I counted distinct card names, because the 176 printings in the database include reprints of the same card. If you wanted printings instead of cards, the count would be 176.

sql:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT s.CDSCode, s.School, s.County, s.City, s.MailStreet, s.MailCity, s.MailState, s.MailZip, s.Website,
         f.`Enrollment (K-12)` AS enr, f.`FRPM Count (K-12)` AS frpm,
         f.`FRPM Count (K-12)` * 1.0 / f.`Enrollment (K-12)` AS share,
         t.AvgScrRead + t.AvgScrMath + t.AvgScrWrite AS avg_sat,
         t.NumGE1500 * 100.0 / t.NumTstTakr AS pct1500,
         s.OpenDate, CASE WHEN s.ClosedDate IS NOT NULL AND s.ClosedDate <> '' THEN 'closed' ELSE 'open' END AS status
  FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode
  LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode AND t.rtype = 'S' AND t.NumTstTakr > 0
  WHERE s.Charter = 0 AND f.`Charter School (Y/N)` = 0 AND s.EdOpsCode = 'TRAD'
    AND f.`Enrollment (K-12)` > 100 AND f.`FRPM Count (K-12)` IS NOT NULL
), parts AS (
  SELECT 1 AS p, 'largest FRPM-eligible count' AS label, * FROM c WHERE frpm = (SELECT MAX(frpm) FROM c)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 2, 'smallest FRPM share', * FROM c WHERE share = (SELECT MIN(share) FROM c)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 3, 'the CDS code from my notes', * FROM c WHERE CDSCode = '04615150435602'
)
SELECT label, School AS school_name, County, City, MailStreet AS mailing_street, MailCity AS mailing_city,
       MailState AS mailing_state, MailZip AS mailing_zip, Website, enr AS enrollment_k12, frpm AS frpm_count,
       share AS frpm_share, avg_sat AS avg_total_sat, pct1500 AS pct_sat_takers_1500_plus, OpenDate AS opening_date, status
FROM parts ORDER BY p, School;
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 확인했고, 세 부분이 각각 한 학교로 나와 총 3행입니다.

- 가장 많은 FRPM 대상 학생 수: Paramount High (Los Angeles 카운티, Paramount). 재학생 4,814명 중 4,419명(91.8%)이 대상입니다. SAT 평균 총점은 1272, 1500점 이상 응시자는 14.8%입니다. 개교일 1953-07-01, 상태 open. 웹사이트는 데이터에 없습니다.
- 가장 낮은 FRPM 비율: Orinda Intermediate (Contra Costa 카운티, Orinda). 재학생 907명 중 2명(0.22%)이 대상입니다. SAT 기록이 없어 SAT 두 항목은 빈 값입니다. 개교일 1980-07-01, 상태 open. 웹사이트는 데이터에 없습니다.
- 메모의 CDS 코드: Oroville High (Butte 카운티, Oroville). 재학생 982명 중 692명(70.5%)이 대상입니다. SAT 평균 총점은 1395, 1500점 이상 응시자는 32.7%입니다. 개교일 1980-07-01, 상태 open. 웹사이트는 http://ohs.ouhsd.org 입니다.

판단한 내용은 다음과 같습니다.
- 메모의 코드 4615150435602는 14자리 CDS 코드의 앞자리 0이 빠진 형태로 보고 04615150435602로 조회했습니다.
- '일반 학교'는 EdOpsCode가 TRAD(전통 학교)인 학교로 해석했습니다. 대안학교, 연속학교, 특수학교 등은 제외했습니다.
- 비차터 조건은 schools와 frpm 양쪽에서 모두 0인 학교로 했고, K-12 재학생 100명 초과 조건을 적용했습니다.
- FRPM 비율은 FRPM 대상 학생 수를 K-12 재학생 수로 나눈 값입니다.
- SAT 점수는 학교 단위 기록(rtype 'S')만 사용했습니다. 평균 총점은 읽기, 수학, 쓰기 평균을 더한 값이고, 1500점 이상 비율은 1500점 이상 인원을 응시자 수로 나눈 백분율입니다.
- SAT 기록이 없는 학교도 제외하지 않았습니다.
- 동점은 모두 포함하도록 작성했는데, 실제 결과에는 동점이 없었습니다.
- 폐교일이 기록되어 있으면 closed, 없으면 open으로 표시했습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE SEX='F' AND Admission='+' AND "First Date" >= '1998-01-01' AND "First Date" <= '1998-12-31'
answer: 13 female patients were admitted and had a first hospital visit in 1998. I used "First Date" as the first visit date and counted only Admission = '+' as admitted. The '+(' value was not counted. I counted only SEX = 'F' and left out blank sex entries. The Patient Term is still draft (not certified).

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM member m WHERE m.link_to_major = major.major_id) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_majors_without_members FROM major
answer: 76.99% of the 113 majors have no club member. I counted members of every position, including 'Inactive'. The one member with no major doesn't affect the result. The Major term is still draft (not certified).

sql: select 100.0*sum(strftime('%Y',Date)='2010')/count(*) - 100.0*sum(strftime('%Y',Date)='2011')/count(*) as diff_pp from badges where Name='Student'
answer: 2010년 점유율에서 2011년 점유율을 뺀 값은 약 -9.54%p입니다. 기준은 전체 Student 배지 14,847건이며, 연도는 배지 수여일(Date)로 구분했습니다. 2011년 비중이 2010년보다 큽니다.

sql: SELECT SUM(convertedManaCost) FROM cards WHERE artist = 'Rob Alexander' AND originalReleaseDate LIKE '2013/%'
answer: The total is 4.0. Only one Rob Alexander printing has an original release date in 2013 (2013/1/11, converted mana cost 4). I matched the year on the date text, which is stored as YYYY/M/D. Cards with no original release date are excluded.

sql: select case when sum(GSserved like 'K%')>0 then 'K' else min(substr(GSserved,1,instr(GSserved,'-')-1)) end as lowest_grade from schools where NCESDist='0632640' and School is not null and GSserved is not null
answer: The lowest grade is K (kindergarten). I read "serving students" as the grade span actually enrolled (GSserved), which covers K-12 only. Under that reading the lowest start grade is K, shared by several schools, and 1 at Rincon Valley Charter is higher. If you used the grade span offered (GSoffered), Redwood Consortium for Student Services lists P (preschool), so the answer would be P. I counted all schools in the district, including closed ones, and left out the district record, which has no grade data.

sql: select name, n from (select c.name name, count(distinct r.date||r.text) n from cards c join rulings r on r.uuid=c.uuid where c.originalType='Creature - Elf' group by c.name) where n=(select max(n) from (select count(distinct r.date||r.text) n from cards c join rulings r on r.uuid=c.uuid where c.originalType='Creature - Elf' group by c.name))
answer: Gempalm Strider, with 4 rulings. I grouped printings by card name and counted distinct rulings (date plus text), because the same ruling is stored once per printing. Counting raw rows would give 8 for this card. It is the only card at the top, so there is no tie.

sql: select distinct name from cards where setCode='DKA' and ','||replace(keywords,', ',',')||',' like '%,Flash,%' and convertedManaCost=(select max(convertedManaCost) from cards where setCode='DKA' and ','||replace(keywords,', ',',')||',' like '%,Flash,%') order by name;
answer: Three Dark Ascension cards have Flash and tie at the highest converted mana cost of 4: Briarpack Alpha, Hollowhenge Spirit and Nephalia Seakite. I matched Flash as a whole keyword, because a plain text match would also catch Flashback. That would wrongly add Increasing Devotion and Increasing Ambition (cost 5), which have Flashback but not Flash. I used only the main Dark Ascension set (code DKA) and left out the promo set.

sql: select round(avg(coalesce(t.NumTstTakr,0)),2) from schools s left join satscores t on t.cds=s.CDSCode where s.CharterNum='0756' and s.MailCity='San Diego'
answer: 평균 SAT 응시자 수는 학교당 41.33명입니다. charter number 756은 CharterNum 값 '0756'(정확히 일치)으로 보았고, '1756'은 다른 번호라 제외했습니다. 우편 주소 도시가 San Diego인 학교 6곳을 운영 상태와 관계없이 모두 포함했으며, SAT 기록이 없는 학교는 응시자 0명으로 계산했습니다.

sql: SELECT SUM(u.Reputation) AS total_reputation FROM users u WHERE u.Id IN (SELECT p.OwnerUserId FROM posts p WHERE p.Tags LIKE '%<r>%' AND p.LasActivityDate >= '2014-08-27 00:00:00' AND p.LasActivityDate < '2014-08-28 00:00:00')
answer: 3773. 2014-08-27에 마지막으로 활동한 글 중 '<r>' 태그가 달린 글의 소유자들의 평판 합계입니다. 한 사용자가 여러 글을 갖고 있어도 한 번만 더했고, 날짜는 하루 전체(00:00:00 이상, 다음 날 00:00:00 미만)를 포함했습니다.

sql:
SELECT p.ID, CAST((strftime('%Y','2026-10-09') - strftime('%Y',p.Birthday)) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09') < strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)) AS INTEGER) AS age
FROM Patient p
WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE LDH > 600 AND LDH < 800 AND "U-PRO" IN ('300','>=300','>=1000'))
ORDER BY p.ID
answer: 3 patients qualify: 3182521 (age 73), 4425292 (age 71), 4632548 (age 99), as of 2026-10-09. A patient qualifies if one lab visit (one Laboratory row) has LDH strictly between 600 and 800 and U-PRO of '300', '>=300' or '>=1000'. Bare '3'/'4' were read as mg/dL numbers (below 300), grade-style entries like '+2(100)' as 100, and '%%'/'-15' were excluded. Age is completed years (birthday adjustment applied). The Laboratory Test and Patient terms are still draft.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT f.language) FROM foreign_data f JOIN cards c ON c.uuid = f.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Swamp'
answer: Swamp has been printed in 11 foreign languages: German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Chinese Simplified, Chinese Traditional and Phyrexian. I counted distinct `language` values in `foreign_data` for every card named exactly 'Swamp', across all sets. I counted Phyrexian as a language because the data lists it as one. Without it the count is 10.

sql: select a.account_id, a.frequency from account a join district d on d.district_id=a.district_id where d.A3='east Bohemia' and a.date>='1995-01-01' and a.date<'2001-01-01'
answer: 364개 계정이 조회됩니다. 'East Bohemia'는 district.A3 = 'east Bohemia'로, 개설 기간은 1995-01-01부터 2000-12-31까지(2000년 포함)로 해석했습니다. 명세서 발급 주기는 account.frequency 값 그대로(POPLATEK MESICNE, POPLATEK TYDNE, POPLATEK PO OBRATU) 반환합니다.

sql: SELECT e.location, COUNT(DISTINCT x.expense_description) FROM event e JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event=e.event_id JOIN expense x ON x.link_to_budget=b.budget_id WHERE e.event_id IN (SELECT link_to_event FROM budget WHERE amount>40) GROUP BY e.location;
answer: Campus Common: 1, MU 215: 10. I took "events with a budget line over $40" to mean events with at least one budget line whose amount is above 40. For those events I counted the distinct expense descriptions across all of their budget lines, grouped by event location. I read "different things bought" as distinct expense descriptions.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_api_id) FROM Player_Attributes WHERE jumping >= 80 AND date >= '2007-02-22' AND date < '2007-08-31'
answer: 654 players. I counted distinct players (player_api_id), because the same player can have several assessments in the period. Counting assessment rows instead would give 1049. Dates are stored as timestamps, so I used date < '2007-08-31' to include all of 30 August.

sql:
WITH q AS (SELECT DISTINCT ds.raceId FROM driverStandings ds JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=ds.driverId WHERE d.nationality='Australian' AND ds.position<20)
SELECT r.year, COUNT(p.raceId) AS total_pit_stops FROM races r JOIN q ON q.raceId=r.raceId LEFT JOIN pitStops p ON p.raceId=r.raceId WHERE r.year BETWEEN 2002 AND 2013 GROUP BY r.year ORDER BY r.year
answer: 2002-2010: 0 each (the database has no pit stop data before 2011); 2011: 1069; 2012: 905; 2013: 898. Assumptions: "better than 20th" means standing position < 20; Australian drivers are identified by nationality 'Australian'; seasons without pit stop data are kept with a count of 0. The pit stop count includes all drivers at the qualifying races.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN pa.defensive_work_rate = 'high' THEN p.player_api_id END) / COUNT(DISTINCT p.player_api_id), 2) AS high_share_pct
FROM Player p
JOIN Player_Attributes pa ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
WHERE p.birthday >= '1991-01-01' AND pa.defensive_work_rate IN ('high','medium','low')
answer: 17.41% (실행 결과). 가정: 방어 작업률이 있는 선수는 기록값이 high, medium, low 중 하나인 선수로 봤습니다. 숫자나 깨진 값은 제외했습니다. 기준 선수는 1991년 1월 1일 이후 출생자 중 유효한 기록이 한 번이라도 있는 선수입니다. 경력 중 한 번이라도 high였던 선수를 high로 계산했습니다. 사용한 Player와 Player Attributes 용어는 아직 인증되지 않은 초안입니다.

sql: select round(avg(weight_kg)) from superhero where publisher_id=4 and weight_kg>0 and eye_colour_id in (select eye_colour_id from superhero where publisher_id=13 and eye_colour_id is not null)
answer: 102 kg. 문서에 weight_kg가 NULL 또는 0이면 '알 수 없음'이라고 되어 있어서 두 경우를 모두 제외했습니다. 눈 색 'No Colour'(id 1)도 다른 색과 똑같이 비교했습니다.

sql: select count(distinct p.id) from superhero s join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id where s.height_cm>200 and p.publisher_name<>''
answer: 7 publishers have at least one hero taller than 200 cm: Dark Horse Comics, DC Comics, George Lucas, Image Comics, J. R. R. Tolkien, Marvel Comics and Microsoft. Publisher id 1 is a blank placeholder name, not a real company, so I excluded it. Two tall heroes are filed under that blank publisher. Counting it would give 8. Heroes with no publisher at all (NULL) drop out of the join.

sql: select count(distinct player_api_id) from Player_Attributes where jumping>=80 and date>='2007-02-22' and date<'2007-08-31'
answer: 654 distinct players had a jumping score of 80 or higher in assessments dated 22 Feb 2007 to 30 Aug 2007 (inclusive). I counted distinct players, not assessment rows. There are 1,049 matching rows. The dates carry a time of 00:00:00, so I used date < '2007-08-31' to include all of 30 Aug.

sql: select count(distinct p.ID) from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where p.SEX='F' and l.WBC>3.5 and l.WBC<9.0 and (l.FG<=150 or l.FG>=450) and l.RNP glob '[0-9]*' and CAST(l.RNP as real)>15
answer: 1 female patient. Readings I chose: normal WBC is 3.5 < WBC < 9.0; abnormal fibrinogen is FG ≤ 150 or ≥ 450, since the docs give 150 < N < 450 as normal. RNP is stored as text, so I counted only numeric values above 15 and excluded 'negative'. I counted distinct patients across all laboratory dates.

sql: SELECT ROUND(1.0 * (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId WHERE q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(q.q3) <> '' AND d.dob BETWEEN '1981-01-01' AND '1991-12-31') / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM drivers WHERE dob BETWEEN '1981-01-01' AND '1991-12-31'), 2) AS avg_q3_laps_per_driver;
answer: A driver born between 1981 and 1991 set 29.18 Q3 lap times on average. I counted every qualifying row with a non-empty q3 for those drivers (both NULL and empty-string q3 values mean no Q3 time) and divided by all drivers born 1981-01-01 to 1991-12-31, including those with no Q3 times. I read "between 1981 and 1991" as inclusive of both years.
