sql: SELECT e.event_name, e.event_date, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(b.amount) FROM budget b WHERE b.link_to_event = e.event_id), 0) AS total_budgeted, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event = e.event_id) AS members_attended FROM event e ORDER BY e.event_name ASC, e.event_date ASC;
answer: The query returns all 42 events with name, date, total budgeted amount and number of distinct attending members, sorted by name and then date. The budget total and the attendee count are computed in separate subqueries so the two don't multiply each other. Events with no budget rows show 0 (a judgment call; they could also be shown as NULL). Events with no attendance records show 0 attendees. I ran an earlier draft of the query that returned NULL instead of 0 for events with no budget, and it returned 42 rows. I did not re-run the final version.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT f.language) FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Swamp'
answer: Swamp has been printed in 11 foreign languages: German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Chinese Simplified, Chinese Traditional and Phyrexian. I counted each language in `foreign_data` once, across all Swamp printings, and I counted Phyrexian as a language because the data lists it as one. Removing it would give 10.

The top three Italian constructors by career points are Ferrari (6991.5 points, http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari), Benetton (861.5, http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_Formula) and Toro Rosso (381.0, http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Toro_Rosso). There are no ties in the top three.

I read "points the constructor finished each season with" as the cumulative constructorStandings points at the constructor's last race of each year, summed over all years. I took "Italian" from constructors.nationality, and "introduction website" as constructors.url. Italian constructors with no standings rows count as 0 and are still ranked, using RANK() so ties share a rank and the next rank is skipped.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(weight_kg), 2) FROM superhero WHERE id <> 1 AND weight_kg > 0 AND id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id IN (SELECT power_id FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id = 1))
answer: 282411.79 kg. I treated a weight of 0 as missing, along with NULL. docs/superhero.csv says both mean the weight is missing. Counting 0 as a real weight would give 224776.73. The figure is large because six heroes have recorded weights above 1,000 kg (the largest is 90,000,000 kg), and I kept them in.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superhero s JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id=a.id WHERE a.alignment='Neutral' AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(s.full_name)<>'' AND TRIM(s.full_name)<>'-'
answer: 16 neutral-alignment heroes have a known full name. I treated NULL, empty and the placeholder '-' as unknown. The Alignment and Superhero Terms in the ontology are still drafts.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN height_cm > 0 THEN height_cm END), 2) AS avg_height_cm,
       ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN weight_kg > 0 THEN weight_kg END), 2) AS avg_weight_kg
FROM superhero
WHERE skin_colour_id = (SELECT id FROM colour WHERE colour = 'Green')
  AND alignment_id = (SELECT id FROM alignment WHERE alignment = 'Bad');
answer: 초록색 피부의 악당(alignment 'Bad')은 6명입니다. 평균 키는 194.2cm, 평균 몸무게는 161.75kg입니다. 이 데이터에서는 기록이 없는 키와 몸무게가 NULL이 아니라 0으로 들어 있어서, 0은 미기록으로 보고 평균에서 뺐습니다. 키는 1명, 몸무게는 2명이 제외되었습니다. 악당은 alignment가 'Bad'인 경우로 해석했습니다.

sql: SELECT type, COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM cards c WHERE watermark='azorius' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM foreign_data f WHERE f.uuid=c.uuid) GROUP BY type ORDER BY card_count DESC, type ASC
answer: 26개 카드 유형이 해당합니다. Instant가 29장으로 가장 많고, Creature — Human Knight, Enchantment, Sorcery가 각 8장으로 뒤를 잇습니다. 아조리우스 워터마크가 있고 cards 테이블의 uuid가 foreign_data에 하나 이상 있는 카드를 외국어 인쇄본이 있는 카드로 보았습니다. 카드 한 장은 cards 테이블의 행 하나로 계산했고, 유형은 type 열의 값을 그대로 썼습니다.

sql:
SELECT p.ID, CAST((strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',p.Birthday)) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09') < strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)) AS INTEGER) AS age
FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID
WHERE l.HCT >= 52
GROUP BY p.ID, p.Birthday
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
answer: 3 patients: ID 2307640 (age 73), 3182521 (age 73), 4007151 (age 58). I read "at least two laboratory results" as at least two Laboratory rows with HCT >= 52 for the same patient. Age is completed years on 2026-10-09 (subtract one if the birthday hasn't passed yet). The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are draft, not certified.

sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.driverId) AS drivers_outqualified
FROM qualifying d
JOIN races r ON r.raceId = d.raceId
JOIN qualifying o ON o.raceId = d.raceId AND o.driverId <> d.driverId AND o.position > d.position
WHERE d.driverId = 810 AND r.year = 2010;
answer: 9 distinct drivers. I read the question as the number of different drivers he beat in qualifying in at least one 2010 race, comparing the position column within the same race. Counting every race-by-race head-to-head win instead would give 34.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(s.status='Finished' or s.status like '+% Lap%')/count(*),2) as finisher_percentage from results r join races ra using(raceId) join status s using(statusId) where ra.year=1957 and ra.name like '%British%'
answer: 45.45% (10 of 22 drivers). I counted a driver as a classified finisher if their status was "Finished" or "+N Laps". Retirements such as accident, engine or gearbox were not counted.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL THEN 'u'||p.OwnerUserId ELSE 'n'||p.OwnerDisplayName END) AS n FROM votes v JOIN posts p ON p.Id=v.PostId WHERE v.BountyAmount>=30 AND v.CreationDate>='2010-01-01' AND v.CreationDate<'2011-01-01' AND (p.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL OR p.OwnerDisplayName IS NOT NULL)
answer: 32 users offered a bounty of 30 or more between 2010-01-01 and 2011-01-01. I counted the post owner as the offering user: OwnerUserId where recorded, otherwise OwnerDisplayName. The bounty date is votes.CreationDate. Posts with neither owner field are excluded. The Post and Vote terms are still draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.height_cm > 0 THEN s.height_cm END),1) AS avg_height_cm, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END),1) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'George Lucas'
answer: George Lucas's heroes average 187.2 cm in height and 83.0 kg in weight. I read "created by George Lucas" as heroes whose publisher is 'George Lucas', the only link to him in the data. Heights and weights of NULL or 0 are treated as unknown and excluded from the matching average. The Superhero and Publisher Terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
WITH b AS (SELECT link_to_event e, SUM(spent) s, SUM(amount) a FROM budget GROUP BY 1),
c AS (SELECT bu.link_to_event e, COUNT(*) n FROM expense x JOIN budget bu ON x.link_to_budget=bu.budget_id GROUP BY 1)
SELECT ev.event_name FROM event ev LEFT JOIN b ON b.e=ev.event_id LEFT JOIN c ON c.e=ev.event_id
WHERE ev.status='Closed' AND COALESCE(b.s,0)<=COALESCE(b.a,0)
ORDER BY COALESCE(c.n,0) DESC, ev.event_id LIMIT 1
answer: October Speaker. It has 5 purchases, the same as November Speaker, and its event ID (recEVTik3MlqbvLFi) sorts first. I counted purchases as expense rows linked to the event through its budget lines. I compared the event's total spent with its total budgeted amount from the budget table. Closed events with no budget rows were treated as 0 against 0, so they stay in the comparison.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / 12 AS avg_schools_opened_per_month FROM schools WHERE County='San Diego' AND DOC IN ('52','54','56') AND OpenDate>='1980-01-01' AND OpenDate<'1981-01-01'
answer:
47.666666666666664 schools per month. That is 572 schools opened in 1980 in San Diego County, divided by 12 months.

Reading chosen: "under a school district's jurisdiction" means a District Ownership Code (DOC) of 52 (Elementary School District), 54 (Unified School District) or 56 (High School District). I left out county office of education (00), state, ROC/P and other codes. Counting only unified districts would give 318/12 instead.

Note: the School Term this relies on is still a draft in the ontology, not certified.

sql: SELECT ID, Date, RNP FROM Laboratory WHERE GOT >= 60 AND CAST(RNP AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(RNP AS REAL)) FROM Laboratory WHERE GOT >= 60 AND RNP IS NOT NULL)
answer: Patient ID 1650222, tested on 1989-07-18, with an anti-RNP reading of 256. Only one test has this value, so there is no tie. RNP is stored as text, so I cast it to a number to compare. 'negative' counts as 0. I read "60 or higher" as GOT >= 60.

sql: select e.event_name, e.event_date, coalesce(b.t,0) as total_budgeted, coalesce(a.n,0) as attendees from event e left join (select link_to_event k, sum(amount) t from budget group by 1) b on b.k=e.event_id left join (select link_to_event k, count(distinct link_to_member) n from attendance group by 1) a on a.k=e.event_id order by e.event_name, e.event_date
answer: The query returns all 42 events, sorted by name and then date. I aggregated budget and attendance separately before joining, so one doesn't multiply the other. Events with no budget lines show a budget of 0, and events with no attendance rows show 0 attendees. I read "total amount budgeted" as the sum of budget.amount per event. Event names repeat (for example, two "Community Theater" events), so each event is counted by event_id, not by name. Only 9 events have both budget and attendance rows, so many rows show a 0 in one of the two columns.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(SEX='F')/count(*),1) as female_pct from Patient p where Birthday between '1936-01-01' and '1956-12-31' and SEX in ('F','M') and not exists (select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and l.CPK>=250)
answer: 여성 비율은 85.3%입니다. 1936~1956년생 중 CPK가 250 이상인 기록이 없는 환자 414명(여성 353명, 남성 61명) 기준입니다. CPK 검사 기록이 없는 환자도 포함했고, 성별이 F 또는 M이 아닌 환자는 없었습니다. 출생일은 1956-12-31까지를 포함했습니다.

sql: select d.forename||' '||d.surname as full_name from lapTimes l join drivers d using(driverId) group by d.driverId order by min(l.milliseconds), d.driverId limit 20
answer: I read the question as the 20 distinct drivers ranked by each driver's own fastest lap, with the shortest first. The query gives each driver once rather than listing the 20 fastest laps, which could repeat a driver. The list starts with Lewis Hamilton, Daniel Ricciardo, Kimi Räikkönen, Sebastian Vettel and Valtteri Bottas. It ends with Carlos Sainz and Pascal Wehrlein. Ties on lap time are broken by driverId.

sql:
WITH v AS (SELECT CDSCode, County, School FROM schools WHERE Virtual='F'),
c AS (SELECT County, COUNT(*) n FROM v GROUP BY County),
top AS (SELECT County, n FROM c WHERE n >= (SELECT n FROM c ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 4)),
s AS (SELECT v.County, v.School, t.AvgScrRead r FROM v JOIN satscores t ON t.cds=v.CDSCode WHERE t.AvgScrRead IS NOT NULL),
m AS (SELECT County, MAX(r) mr FROM s GROUP BY County)
SELECT top.County, top.n AS virtual_school_count, COALESCE(s.School,'None') AS school_name
FROM top LEFT JOIN m ON m.County=top.County LEFT JOIN s ON s.County=m.County AND s.r=m.mr
ORDER BY top.n DESC, top.County, school_name;
answer:
I read "exclusively virtual" as schools.Virtual = 'F'. The top five counties, with Sacramento and San Bernardino tied at 5 for fifth place, are:
- Los Angeles, 12 schools. Highest average SAT reading: California Virtual Academy @ Los Angeles.
- San Joaquin, 10 schools. Highest average SAT reading: California Connections Academy @ Ripon.
- San Diego, 8 schools. None of them has a reported reading average, so the name is 'None'.
- Sacramento, 5 schools. 'None'.
- San Bernardino, 5 schools. 'None'.
No county had a tie for the top reading average. Reading averages come from satscores, and schools without a non-null AvgScrRead are ignored.

sql:
SELECT d.A2 AS district, l.amount, l.date AS approval_date,
 (SELECT t.balance FROM trans t WHERE t.account_id=l.account_id AND t.date<=l.date ORDER BY t.date DESC, t.trans_id DESC LIMIT 1) AS balance
FROM loan l JOIN account a ON a.account_id=l.account_id
JOIN district d ON d.district_id=a.district_id
WHERE l.duration=24 AND a.frequency='POPLATEK TYDNE'
ORDER BY l.amount DESC, l.date ASC LIMIT 10;
answer:
I ran the query and it returns ten rows. The largest is Strakonice at 192,552, approved 1994-11-12, with an end-of-day balance of 14,203. The next is Prachatice at 189,696, approved 1996-01-01, with a balance of 88,662. The other eight follow in descending amount.

Readings I chose:
- "Weekly statement issuance" means `account.frequency = 'POPLATEK TYDNE'`.
- "District of the branch" is `district.A2` (the district name), reached through `account.district_id`.
- "Balance at the end of the day the loan was approved" is the `balance` of the account's last transaction on or before the loan date. The last one is the latest date, then the highest `trans_id`. I used "on or before" because some accounts have no transaction on the loan date itself. A check across all 24-month loans on weekly accounts found 11 such loans. I did not check whether any of them are in the top ten, so some balances shown may come from an earlier day.
- Ties on amount are broken by the earlier approval date. Two Tachov loans share the date 1995-12-12 but have different amounts, so that tie rule did not come into play there.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT power_id) AS power_count FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id = (SELECT id FROM superpower WHERE power_name = 'Super Strength'))
answer: 154. I read "held only by heroes who have Super Strength" as the powers held by at least one Super Strength hero, as the question defines it. That count includes Super Strength itself.

sql:
WITH r AS (SELECT DISTINCT t.team_api_id, t.team_short_name sn FROM Team t JOIN Team_Attributes a USING(team_api_id) WHERE a.chanceCreationPassingClass='Risky'),
c AS (SELECT sn, COUNT(*) n FROM r GROUP BY sn HAVING COUNT(*)>1),
f AS (SELECT r.sn, a.chanceCreationPassing v FROM r JOIN Team_Attributes a ON a.team_api_id=r.team_api_id WHERE a.date=(SELECT MAX(date) FROM Team_Attributes b WHERE b.team_api_id=r.team_api_id AND date<='2014-09-19 23:59:59'))
SELECT c.sn AS team_short_name, c.n AS club_count, ROUND(AVG(f.v),1) AS avg_risk FROM c LEFT JOIN f ON f.sn=c.sn GROUP BY c.sn ORDER BY avg_risk DESC, c.sn;
answer: 6개 약칭이 조건에 맞습니다. REA 69.5, GEN 66.5, WOL 61.5, MAR 58.0, HAM 56.0, LEV 53.5이고, 각 약칭을 쓰는 구단은 모두 2곳입니다. 해석은 세 가지로 잡았습니다. (1) 'Risky'였던 적이 있는 팀만 먼저 추린 뒤, 그 팀들 안에서 약칭을 공유하는 구단 수를 셌습니다. (2) 2014-09-19에 유효한 값은 그 날짜 이전(당일 포함)의 가장 최근 Team_Attributes 기록으로 봤습니다. (3) 평균은 chanceCreationPassing 숫자 값으로 계산했습니다.

sql:
SELECT s.FundingType AS funding_type, COUNT(*) AS charter_schools, SUM(f."Enrollment (K-12)") AS total_enrollment_k12, ROUND(AVG(f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)")*100,2) AS avg_frpm_pct, ROUND(AVG(t.AvgScrRead+t.AvgScrMath+t.AvgScrWrite),2) AS avg_sat_total
FROM schools s LEFT JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds=s.CDSCode AND t.rtype='S'
WHERE s.Charter=1 AND s.StatusType='Active' AND s.FundingType IN ('Directly funded','Locally funded')
GROUP BY s.FundingType
answer:
Directly funded: 902 active charters, 372,954 enrolled (K-12, 2014-15), average FRPM eligibility 63.88%, average SAT 1350.84. Locally funded: 340 active charters, 150,022 enrolled, 44.84%, 1480.15.

Readings I chose: charters are schools.Charter=1 with StatusType='Active', grouped by schools.FundingType. I left out the 'Not in CS funding model' category and charters with no funding type. The school count comes from the directory, so it includes 123 directly funded and 21 locally funded charters with no frpm row. Those schools add nothing to enrollment or the meal average. Meal eligibility is the frpm FRPM percentage (free or reduced-price), converted from a 0-1 fraction to 0-100. The SAT average is taken over school-level rows with non-null reading, math and writing averages: 302 directly funded and 104 locally funded schools. It is a plain average across schools, not weighted by test takers.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments c JOIN posts p ON p.Id=c.PostId WHERE c.Score=0 AND c.PostId IN (SELECT PostId FROM comments GROUP BY PostId HAVING COUNT(*)=1)
answer: 10,999개입니다. 댓글이 정확히 1개 달린 게시글(`posts`에 실제 존재하는 글)의 댓글 가운데 점수가 0인 것의 수입니다. 'comment record가 정확히 1개'는 `comments` 테이블에서 같은 `PostId`를 가진 행이 1개라는 뜻으로 해석했습니다. 쿼리에 쓴 `Comment`와 `Post` 용어는 draft 상태이며 인증되지 않았습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_api_id) FROM Player_Attributes WHERE jumping >= 80 AND date >= '2007-02-22' AND date < '2007-08-31'
answer: 654 players. I counted distinct players with a Player_Attributes snapshot dated 2007-02-22 to 2007-08-30 inclusive and jumping >= 80. Player_Attributes.date is the assessment date, since no Term covers assessment date. The Player Attributes Term is still a draft.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.name) FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid=c.uuid WHERE c.colors='B' AND c.types LIKE '%Artifact%' AND f.flavorText IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(f.flavorText)<>'';
answer: 11. I counted distinct card names whose colors are exactly 'B', whose types include Artifact (so Artifact Creature counts), and that have at least one foreign_data row with non-empty flavor text. Counting by scryfallOracleId also gives 11.

sql: SELECT SUM(c.n) AS accounts_opened, COUNT(*) AS districts, ROUND(AVG(c.sal),2) AS avg_salary FROM (SELECT d.district_id, d.A11 AS sal, COUNT(*) AS n FROM account a JOIN district d ON a.district_id=d.district_id WHERE a.frequency='POPLATEK MESICNE' AND a.date>='1997-01-01' AND a.date<'1998-01-01' AND CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER)>=100000 GROUP BY d.district_id, d.A11) c
answer: 569 monthly-statement accounts were opened in 1997 across 46 districts with at least 100,000 inhabitants. The average salary across those 46 districts is 9189.52. I counted each district once in the average, not weighted by accounts. Monthly statements are frequency 'POPLATEK MESICNE'. The population column is stored as text, so I cast it to integer. The Account and District terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT s.MailStreet, s.School FROM satscores t JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = t.cds WHERE t.rtype = 'S' AND t.AvgScrMath IS NOT NULL ORDER BY t.AvgScrMath DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 6
answer: 5172 Orange Avenue, Oxford Academy (average SAT math score 669, seventh-highest among school-level records; no ties at that rank). I read "average mathematics score" as satscores.AvgScrMath and excluded district rows.

sql: SELECT s.MailStreet, s.School FROM satscores t JOIN schools s ON t.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE t.rtype = 'S' AND t.AvgScrMath IS NOT NULL ORDER BY t.AvgScrMath DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 6
answer: Oxford Academy, mailing street address 5172 Orange Avenue (average SAT math score 669). I counted school-level rows only (rtype='S') with a non-null AvgScrMath. If district rows were included, the seventh row would be a district record at 25 Churchill Avenue with no school name.

sql: select 100.0*sum(r.laps>50)/count(*) as percentage from results r join races ra on ra.raceId=r.raceId join drivers d on d.driverId=r.driverId where ra.year between 2000 and 2005 and d.dob<'1985-01-01'
answer: About 64.88%. I read the question as: among 2000–2005 race results by drivers born before 1985-01-01, the share with more than 50 laps. The result was the same when I used all 2000–2005 results as the denominator, because every driver in those years was born before 1985.

sql: select distinct s.name, s.releaseDate from cards c join sets s on s.code=c.setCode where c.name='Tarmogoyf' and c.isReprint=1 and c.frameVersion glob '[0-9]*' and cast(substr(s.releaseDate,1,4) as int)-cast(c.frameVersion as int)>=10
answer: Only one set qualifies: Modern Masters, released 2013-06-07. Its Tarmogoyf uses the 2003 frame, so the gap is exactly 10 years (inclusive). The other reprints (Modern Masters 2015, Modern Masters 2017, Ultimate Box Topper, Ultimate Masters) use the 2015 frame, which is too recent. The original Future Sight printing (2007) has frameVersion 'future' and is not a reprint, so it is excluded. I read "reprint" as isReprint=1 and used the frameVersion column, not frameEffects.

sql: select name, releaseDate from sets s where type=(select type from sets where name='From the Vault: Lore') and not exists(select 1 from set_translations t where t.setCode=s.code and t.translation is not null and t.translation<>'') order by releaseDate
answer:
Three sets share the type 'from_the_vault' with "From the Vault: Lore" and have no foreign-language name:
- From the Vault: Dragons, 2008-08-29
- From the Vault: Transform, 2017-11-24
- Commander Collection: Green, 2020-12-04

Reading chosen: "same expansion type" means the same `sets.type` value. "Never received a name" means no `set_translations` row with a non-empty translation. 231 of the 1,210 translation rows have a NULL translation, so I treated those as having no name. "From the Vault: Lore" itself has translations, so it is not in the list.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT d.nationality FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId WHERE q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM qualifying WHERE q3 <> '')
answer: Finnish. The fastest Q3 time is 1:04.251, and only one driver set it. I ignored NULL and empty Q3 values. All Q3 times use the same m:ss.mmm format, so they sort correctly as text.

sql:
SELECT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS driver_full_name, p.duration AS pit_stop_time, r.name AS race_name, c.name AS circuit_name, c.location AS circuit_location
FROM pitStops p JOIN races r ON r.raceId=p.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId=r.circuitId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=p.driverId
WHERE r.date >= '2016-09-01' AND r.date < '2016-10-01'
AND p.milliseconds = (SELECT MIN(p2.milliseconds) FROM pitStops p2 JOIN races r2 ON r2.raceId=p2.raceId WHERE r2.date >= '2016-09-01' AND r2.date < '2016-10-01')
answer: The fastest pit stop in a September 2016 race was 23.633 seconds, and two drivers tied for it. Both stops were in the Italian Grand Prix at Autodromo Nazionale di Monza (location: Monza). The drivers are Lewis Hamilton and Daniel Ricciardo. I read "September 2016" as race dates from 2016-09-01 up to, but not including, 2016-10-01. I took "fastest" to mean the lowest `milliseconds` value in `pitStops`. The Terms the query relies on (Circuit, Driver, Pit Stop, Race) are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers c WHERE c.Currency='EUR' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM yearmonth y WHERE y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID AND y.Date LIKE '2012%' AND y.Consumption>0) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM yearmonth y WHERE y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID AND y.Date LIKE '2013%' AND y.Consumption>0)
answer: 1516 EUR customers had gas consumption in both 2012 and 2013. I counted a year only if some month in it had Consumption > 0, because the table has 180 rows with zero, negative or null consumption.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) FROM cards c JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.borderColor = 'white' AND l.status = 'Banned';
answer: 89 white-bordered printings (distinct card uuids) are banned in at least one format. I counted each printing separately, since legalities are stored per printing uuid, and did not collapse printings by card name.

sql:
with g as (select Id,Reputation from users where Location like '%Germany%' or Location like '%Deutschland%')
select coalesce(sum(case when p.LastEditorUserId in (select Id from g) then p.Score end),0) as german_editor_score,
coalesce(sum(case when p.LastEditorUserId is null or p.LastEditorUserId not in (select Id from g) then p.Score end),0) as other_score,
(select count(distinct p2.LastEditorUserId) from posts p2 join g on g.Id=p2.LastEditorUserId where strftime('%Y',p2.CreaionDate)='2012') as german_editors,
(select sum(Reputation) from g where Id in (select LastEditorUserId from posts where strftime('%Y',CreaionDate)='2012')) as german_editors_reputation
from posts p where strftime('%Y',p.CreaionDate)='2012'
answer:
2012년에 작성된 게시물 중 마지막 수정자가 독일 사용자인 게시물의 점수 합계는 349입니다. 그 밖의 2012년 게시물은 63,191입니다. 2012년 게시물을 마지막으로 수정한 독일 사용자는 32명이고, 이들의 프로필 평판 합계는 26,816입니다.

- 작성 연도는 posts 테이블의 CreaionDate 컬럼(철자가 이렇게 되어 있음)으로 판단했습니다.
- 마지막 수정자가 없거나 독일 사용자가 아닌 2012년 게시물은 모두 '그 밖의 게시물'로 계산했습니다.

sql: select count(distinct text) from rulings where uuid in (select uuid from cards where name='Mishra''s Factory') and date=(select max(date) from rulings where uuid in (select uuid from cards where name='Mishra''s Factory'))
answer: 2. The latest ruling date for Mishra's Factory is 2016-06-08. The table stores each ruling once per printing: 23 printings, 46 rows on that date. Those rows hold only 2 distinct ruling texts, so I counted distinct texts. Counting raw rows would give 46.

sql:
WITH d AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y', a.date) AS yr, a.district_id, COUNT(*) AS n, COALESCE(SUM(l.amount),0) AS lent
  FROM account a
  JOIN district di ON di.district_id = a.district_id
  LEFT JOIN loan l ON l.account_id = a.account_id
  WHERE di.A3 = 'central Bohemia' AND a.date >= '1996-01-01'
  GROUP BY 1, 2)
SELECT yr AS year, SUM(n) AS accounts_opened, SUM(lent) AS total_lent, ROUND(AVG(1.0*lent/n),2) AS avg_lent_per_account_across_districts
FROM d GROUP BY yr ORDER BY yr
answer: 1996: 191 accounts opened, 4,887,024 lent, 23,639.03 average across districts of lent per account. 1997: 114 accounts, 1,971,468 lent, 19,809.53. Readings chosen: loans are attributed to the account's opening year, and accounts with no loan count as 0 lent. The average is the unweighted mean over districts that had accounts opened that year, of each district's lent total divided by its accounts. Region is district.A3 = 'central Bohemia'. The Account, Loan and District terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(l.ALB), 4) AS avg_alb FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND instr(',' || replace(p.Diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',', ',SLE,') > 0 AND l.PLT > 400
answer: The average ALB is 4.0000 (the query returns 4). I treated SLE as one item in the comma-separated Diagnosis list, so 'SLE, SJS' counts and 'SLE susp' does not. If only Diagnosis = 'SLE' exactly is counted, the average is 3.9123. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still draft.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.bond_id FROM connected c JOIN atom a ON a.atom_id=c.atom_id JOIN atom b ON b.atom_id=c.atom_id2 WHERE a.element='p' AND b.element='n'
answer: I read the question as asking for bond IDs where one end of the bond is phosphorus ('p') and the other is nitrogen ('n'). The `connected` table stores each bond in both directions, so I filter one direction (p to n) and use DISTINCT. I ran a version that checked both directions and got six bonds: TR032_2_3, TR032_3_5, TR058_1_3, TR058_1_4, TR058_1_5 and TR298_1_5. I did not run the one-direction query returned here. It should give the same six, since both directions are stored.

sql:
WITH a AS (SELECT s.code,s.name FROM sets s WHERE s.code IN (SELECT setCode FROM cards WHERE name='Abyssal Horror') ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.code LIMIT 1),
b AS (SELECT code,name FROM sets ORDER BY releaseDate DESC, code LIMIT 1),
t AS (SELECT * FROM a UNION SELECT * FROM b)
SELECT t.name, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN c.manaCost IS NOT NULL AND c.manaCost<>'' AND c.convertedManaCost<=3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS pct
FROM t JOIN cards c ON c.setCode=t.code GROUP BY t.code,t.name;
answer: Urza's Saga (earliest printing of Abyssal Horror): 58.15%. Time Spiral Remastered (latest release, 2021-03-19): 80.0%. I used all cards in each set as the denominator, and counted a card only if its manaCost is non-empty and its convertedManaCost is 3 or less. The query returns the rows in set-code order (TSR before USG), not in the order the question lists the sets.

sql: select m.first_name, m.last_name from member m join attendance a on a.link_to_member=m.member_id group by m.member_id having count(distinct a.link_to_event)>7
answer: 29명의 학생이 7개를 넘는 행사(8개 이상)에 참석했습니다. 이름은 first_name, last_name 두 열로 냈습니다(예: Grant Gilmour, Luisa Guidi, Connor Hilton). 동명이인이 합쳐지지 않도록 member_id 기준으로 묶었습니다.

sql: select c.colour from superhero s join race r on r.id=s.race_id join colour c on c.id=s.hair_colour_id where r.race='Human' and s.height_cm>0 and s.height_cm=(select min(s2.height_cm) from superhero s2 join race r2 on r2.id=s2.race_id where r2.race='Human' and s2.height_cm>0)
answer: Brown. Of the heroes whose race is exactly 'Human', the shortest is 71 cm, and that hero has brown hair. I treated height 0 or missing as unmeasured and excluded it. I excluded variants such as 'Human / Altered' and kept only the plain 'Human' race. Shorter heroes in the data (for example 61 cm and 64 cm) belong to other races.

sql: SELECT s.type, COUNT(DISTINCT t.setCode) AS japanese_name_set_count FROM sets s LEFT JOIN set_translations t ON t.setCode = s.code AND t.language = 'Japanese' AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND t.translation <> '' GROUP BY s.type ORDER BY s.type
answer:
The query lists all 20 set types alphabetically, with the number of sets that have a Japanese translation row with a non-null, non-empty name. Types with none show 0. I read "carries a Japanese name entry" as requiring an actual name, so rows with a null translation don't count. The Card Set and Set Translation Terms it uses are drafts, not certified.

Counts: archenemy 1, box 3, commander 7, core 7, draft_innovation 2, duel_deck 16, expansion 41, from_the_vault 8, funny 0, masterpiece 0, masters 5, memorabilia 0, planechase 2, premium_deck 1, promo 0, spellbook 0, starter 0, token 0, treasure_chest 0, vanguard 0.

sql:
WITH v AS (SELECT s.CDSCode, s.County, s.School, t.AvgScrRead FROM schools s LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE s.Virtual = 'F'),
c AS (SELECT County, COUNT(*) n, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) r FROM v GROUP BY County),
m AS (SELECT County, MAX(AvgScrRead) mx FROM v GROUP BY County)
SELECT c.County, c.n, COALESCE(v.School, 'None') AS School
FROM c JOIN m ON m.County = c.County
LEFT JOIN v ON v.County = c.County AND m.mx IS NOT NULL AND v.AvgScrRead = m.mx
WHERE c.r <= 5
ORDER BY c.n DESC, c.County, School
answer: Top counties by exclusively virtual schools (Virtual='F'): Los Angeles 12 (California Virtual Academy @ Los Angeles), San Joaquin 10 (California Connections Academy @ Ripon), San Diego 8 (None), Sacramento 5 (None), San Bernardino 5 (None). Sacramento and San Bernardino tie for fifth, so both are included. 'None' means no school in that county has a reported SAT reading average. The School and SAT Score Record terms are still draft.

sql: with t as (select d.driverRef r,d.nationality n,d.dob b,q.q1 t, cast(substr(q1,1,instr(q1,':')-1) as int)*60000+cast(substr(q1,instr(q1,':')+1,2) as int)*1000+cast(substr(q1,-3) as int) ms from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) join races ra using(raceId) where ra.year=1995 and ra.name='Japanese Grand Prix' and coalesce(q1,'')<>'') select r,n,b,t from t where ms=(select max(ms) from t)
answer: blundell, British, born 1966-04-08, Q1 time 16:42.640. Caution: that time is far outside the normal range and looks like a data entry error. The next slowest is Gachot at 1:48.289 (Belgian, 1962-12-23). I chose the literal reading: I compared times numerically (minutes, seconds, milliseconds), skipped NULL or empty Q1 values, and took the maximum. Only one driver has that time.

sql: select a.buildUpPlayDribblingClass from Team t join Team_Attributes a on a.team_api_id=t.team_api_id where t.team_short_name='POR' and date(a.date)='2015-09-10' and t.team_api_id in (select m.home_team_api_id from Match m join League l on l.id=m.league_id join Country c on c.id=l.country_id where c.name='England')
answer: Little. Two teams use the short name POR: FC Porto (Portugal) and Portsmouth. I chose the English one, Portsmouth, because it appears as a home team in England Premier League matches. Its build-up play dribbling class on 2015-09-10 is 'Little' (the dribbling value is 32).

sql: SELECT SEX, COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE SEX IN ('F','M') AND ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory) GROUP BY SEX ORDER BY SEX
answer: 검사 기록이 있는 환자는 여성(F) 252명, 남성(M) 47명입니다. 검사 기록이 있는 환자 중 성별이 빈 값('')인 3명은 여성도 남성도 아니라서 제외했습니다.

sql:
WITH mp AS (
SELECT country_id, home_player_1 p FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_2 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_3 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_4 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_5 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_6 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_7 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_8 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_9 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_10 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_11 FROM "Match"
UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_1 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_2 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_3 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_4 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_5 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_6 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_7 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_8 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_9 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_10 FROM "Match" UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_11 FROM "Match"
), c AS (
SELECT co.name AS name, COUNT(DISTINCT mp.p) AS n
FROM mp JOIN Player pl ON pl.player_api_id = mp.p JOIN Country co ON co.id = mp.country_id
WHERE pl.weight >= 210 GROUP BY co.id, co.name)
SELECT name, n FROM c WHERE n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM c) ORDER BY name
answer: England had the most players weighing 210 pounds or more, with 12 distinct players, and no other country tied it. Each player is counted once per country, even if they appeared in many matches there. A player counts if they are listed in any of the 22 home or away lineup slots of a match in that country. Weight is read as pounds from Player.weight. The Country and Player terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.

sql: WITH r AS (SELECT e.event_name, SUM(b.spent)*1.0/SUM(b.amount) AS ratio FROM event e JOIN budget b ON e.event_id=b.link_to_event WHERE e.status='Closed' GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name) SELECT event_name FROM r WHERE ratio=(SELECT MAX(ratio) FROM r)
answer: Three closed events tie for the highest ratio of total spending to total budget: "Officers meeting - November", "Officers meeting - September" and "Officers meeting - October". The ratio is SUM(budget.spent) / SUM(budget.amount) per event, a ratio of totals. Spending comes from the budget table's already summarized `spent` column. The Event and Budget terms used are still draft (not certified).

sql:
WITH RECURSIVE s(id, tok, rest) AS (
  SELECT ID, '', REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(Diagnosis, char(11), ','), char(29), ','), '  ', ',') || ',' FROM Patient WHERE Diagnosis IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT id, TRIM(SUBSTR(rest, 1, INSTR(rest, ',') - 1)), SUBSTR(rest, INSTR(rest, ',') + 1) FROM s WHERE rest <> ''
),
t AS (SELECT id, tok FROM s WHERE tok <> '' AND tok NOT LIKE '%susp%'),
p AS (
  SELECT id FROM t GROUP BY id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT tok) = 2 AND SUM(tok = 'RA') >= 1 AND SUM(tok = 'SJS') >= 1
)
SELECT
  COUNT(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.id AND l.PLT > 100 AND l.PLT < 400) THEN 1 END) AS with_normal_plt,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.id AND l.PLT > 100 AND l.PLT < 400) THEN 1 END) AS never_normal_plt
FROM p;
answer:
Of 38 patients whose own diagnosis is exactly RA and SJS, 5 have had at least one normal platelet result and 33 never have (this includes patients with no lab rows).

Readings I chose:
- Diagnosis: I split the Patient.Diagnosis text into diseases and dropped any marked "susp". A patient qualifies if the remaining diagnoses are exactly RA and SJS, in either order. That includes 'RA, SJS', 'RA,SJS', 'SJS, RA', 'SJS  RA', 'RA, SJS, SLE susp' (the SLE is only suspected), and 'RA, SJS susp^K^]SJS', where SJS also appears once without "susp". Cases like 'RA, SJS susp' are excluded because SJS is only suspected there, leaving RA alone.
- Normal platelets: the docs give 100 < PLT < 400, and I applied it strictly. The check uses every Laboratory row for the patient, with no date filter. A NULL PLT is not normal.

sql:

Sacha Harrison has 12 expense rows. I counted each row as one purchase and grouped them by exact description text. The result:
- Alumni Glass: 1
- Bakery - Donuts, muffins: 1
- Pizza: 1

sql: SELECT (SELECT bond_type FROM bond WHERE molecule_id='TR010' GROUP BY bond_type ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1) AS bond_type, (SELECT CASE WHEN label='+' THEN 'YES' ELSE 'NO' END FROM molecule WHERE molecule_id='TR010') AS carcinogenic
answer: TR010 에서 가장 흔한 결합 유형은 단일 결합('-')이고, 이 분자는 발암성이 아닙니다(NO). 발암성은 molecule.label 이 '+'이면 YES, '-'이면 NO로 읽었습니다. Bond, Molecule 용어는 아직 draft(미인증) 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN Currency='EUR' THEN q END),2) AS eur_avg, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN Currency='CZK' THEN q END),2) AS czk_avg FROM (SELECT c.CustomerID, c.Currency, SUM(y.Consumption) AS q FROM yearmonth y JOIN customers c ON y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID WHERE y.Date IN ('201304','201305','201306') GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.Currency)
answer: 2013년 2분기(4~6월)에 소비 기록이 있는 고객 기준으로, 고객별 분기 소비량 합계의 평균은 EUR 고객 3627.03, CZK 고객 44462.45입니다. 금액은 각 고객의 통화 기준이며 환산하지 않았습니다. 고객별로 세 달 소비량을 먼저 합산한 뒤 통화별로 평균을 냈고, 통화는 customers.Currency로 구분했습니다. 사용한 용어(Customer, Monthly Customer Consumption)는 아직 인증되지 않은 초안입니다.

sql: select count(distinct p.ID) from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where p.Description is null and (l.CRP in ('+','2+','3+') or l.CRP like '>%' or (l.CRP glob '[0-9]*' and cast(l.CRP as real)>=1.0))
answer: 42명입니다. CRP 양성은 '+', '2+', '3+', '>6'처럼 '>'로 시작하는 값, 그리고 기준치(1.0 미만이 정상) 이상인 숫자 값으로 보았습니다. 환자 설명 없음은 Patient.Description이 NULL인 경우입니다(빈 문자열은 없음). 기준을 1.0 초과로 바꿔도 결과는 같습니다.

sql: select f.`School Type`, s.School, s.Latitude from schools s left join frpm f on f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode where s.Latitude is not null and (f.`School Type` in ('Intermediate/Middle Schools (Public)','Junior High Schools (Public)') or s.School like '%Middle%') and s.Latitude = (select max(s2.Latitude) from schools s2 left join frpm f2 on f2.CDSCode=s2.CDSCode where s2.Latitude is not null and (f2.`School Type` in ('Intermediate/Middle Schools (Public)','Junior High Schools (Public)') or s2.School like '%Middle%'))
answer: Butte Valley Elementary, School Type "Junior High Schools (Public)", latitude 41.964204, is the northernmost middle school, with no ties. I counted a school as a middle school if its School Type (from frpm) is "Intermediate/Middle Schools (Public)" or "Junior High Schools (Public)", or if its name contains "Middle". Open and closed schools are both included. The runner-up is Crescent Elk Middle at 41.756.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.height_cm),1) AS avg_height_cm FROM superhero s WHERE s.superhero_name <> '3-D Man' AND s.height_cm IS NOT NULL AND s.height_cm > 0 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp JOIN hero_power hp3 ON hp3.power_id = hp.power_id JOIN superhero d ON d.id = hp3.hero_id WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id AND d.superhero_name = '3-D Man')
answer: 3-D Man과 초능력을 하나 이상 공유하는 영웅(3-D Man 제외, 키가 NULL이거나 0인 영웅 제외)의 평균 키는 339.5cm입니다. 영웅은 한 명으로만 세어 중복을 막았습니다. 키가 30480cm인 극단값을 걸러내지 않아 평균이 크게 나왔습니다. 사용한 Superhero Term은 draft(인증 전)입니다.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(r.positionOrder<>1)/count(*),2) as non_win_percentage from results r join drivers d using(driverId) join races ra using(raceId) where d.forename='Lewis' and d.surname='Hamilton' and ra.year>=2010;
answer: 66.2% of Lewis Hamilton's race entries from 2010 onward were not wins. That is 94 of 142 entries, with 48 wins. I counted every row in `results` for those years as an entry, and a win as a finishing order (`positionOrder`) of 1.

sql: select round(avg(t),2) from (select p.player_api_id, coalesce(sum(m.home_team_goal),0) t from Player p left join Match m on m.home_player_3=p.player_api_id group by p.player_api_id)
answer: 3.46. I read "whole player population" as all 11,060 rows in Player. Players who were never the home team's third listed player count as 0 goals. Each player's total is the sum of home_team_goal over matches where Match.home_player_3 equals their player_api_id. If you averaged only players who appeared in that slot, the result would be higher.

sql:
WITH a AS (SELECT account_id, date FROM account WHERE district_id=(SELECT district_id FROM district WHERE A2='Tabor') AND date<='1996-12-31'),
t AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) n, SUM(CASE WHEN type='PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) mi,
 SUM(CASE WHEN type IN ('VYDAJ','VYBER') THEN amount ELSE 0 END) mo, MAX(balance) pk
 FROM trans WHERE date>='1997-01-01' AND date<='1997-12-31' GROUP BY account_id),
c AS (SELECT d.account_id, COUNT(*) n FROM card c JOIN disp d USING(disp_id) WHERE c.issued<='1996-12-31' GROUP BY d.account_id),
l AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) n, MAX(status='B') b, MAX(status IN ('C','D')) r FROM loan WHERE date<='1996-12-31' GROUP BY account_id),
p AS (SELECT a.account_id, a.date opened, cl.gender,
 CAST(strftime('%Y','1996-12-31')-strftime('%Y',cl.birth_date) - (strftime('%m-%d',cl.birth_date)>'12-31') AS INT) age,
 COALESCE(c.n,0) cards, COALESCE(l.n,0) loans,
 CASE WHEN l.n IS NULL THEN 'no loan' WHEN l.b=1 THEN 'defaulted' WHEN l.r=1 THEN 'repaying' ELSE 'paid off' END standing,
 COALESCE(t.n,0) txns, COALESCE(t.mi,0) money_in, COALESCE(t.mo,0) money_out, COALESCE(t.pk,0) peak
 FROM a LEFT JOIN disp d ON d.account_id=a.account_id AND d.type='OWNER' LEFT JOIN client cl ON cl.client_id=d.client_id
 LEFT JOIN t ON t.account_id=a.account_id LEFT JOIN c ON c.account_id=a.account_id LEFT JOIN l ON l.account_id=a.account_id)
SELECT account_id, opened, gender, age, cards, loans, standing, txns, money_in, money_out, peak,
 RANK() OVER (ORDER BY peak DESC) peak_rank FROM p ORDER BY peak_rank, account_id;
answer:
The query returns 36 rows, one per Tabor account (district 21) opened on or before 1996-12-31. I ran it and the top row is account 7606, with a 1997 peak balance of 132,635 and rank 1.

Readings I chose:
- **Branch:** the account's district is Tabor.
- **Age:** whole years completed at 1996-12-31. Since that date is the last day of the year, this is the year difference.
- **Cards:** counted across all dispdispositions on the account, if issued on or before 1996-12-31.
- **Money out:** transactions of type VYDAJ or VYBER. VYBER is a cash withdrawal, and it appears as a type value in some rows.
- **Peak balance:** the highest `balance` value among 1997 transactions. It is 0 if the account had none, and the rank is computed on that value.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p WHERE p.Admission = '-' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND (l.HCT <= 29 OR l.HCT >= 52)) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 16)
answer: 2 patients. I read "followed at the outpatient clinic" as Patient.Admission = '-'. I read "non-normal hematocrit" as HCT <= 29 or >= 52, because the docs give the normal range as 29 < HCT < 52. I read "RNP above 16" as the numeric value of Laboratory.RNP being greater than 16. That column is text with values like 'negative', 0, 4, 16, 64 and 256, and 'negative' casts to 0. Each condition is checked across all of a patient's lab dates.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.atom_id2) FROM connected c JOIN atom a ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id WHERE a.element = 'cl'
answer: 271 distinct atoms are bonded to a chlorine ('cl') atom. I counted each neighbouring atom once. Counting bonds instead of atoms gives 314, because some atoms bond to more than one chlorine.

sql:
SELECT d.A2 AS branch_name, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count
FROM trans t
JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id
WHERE d.A3 = 'north Moravia'
  AND t.date <= '1998-10-14'
  AND (t.k_symbol IS NULL OR TRIM(t.k_symbol) = '')
GROUP BY d.district_id, d.A2
ORDER BY transaction_count DESC, branch_name ASC
LIMIT 3;
answer: 1. Karvina: 16,820. 2. Ostrava - mesto: 16,748. 3. Olomouc: 9,928. A branch is the district of the account (region 'north Moravia'). "No characterization" means `k_symbol` is NULL or blank (a single space), since the data uses both for missing values. If only NULL counted, the top three names and order stay the same, with counts of 15,224, 14,826 and 9,164.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(s.NumTstTakr,0)),2) AS avg_sat_test_takers FROM schools sc LEFT JOIN satscores s ON s.cds=sc.CDSCode AND s.rtype='S' WHERE sc.County='Los Angeles' AND sc.OpenDate>='2007-01-01' AND sc.OpenDate<'2008-01-01' AND sc.DOC IN ('00','52','54','56')
answer: 14.57 average SAT test takers per school. This covers the 47 Los Angeles County schools opened in 2007 and run by a school district (DOC 52, 54, 56, or 00 for a county office of education). One State Board of Education school is excluded. Schools with no SAT record count as 0. The Terms used (School, SAT Score Record) are drafts, not certified.

sql: select coalesce(sum(m.major_id is not null),0) as in_college, coalesce(sum(m.major_id is null),0) as not_in_college from member b left join major m on m.major_id=b.link_to_major and m.college='College of Humanities and Social Sciences'
answer: Of 33 members, 7 major in a department of the College of Humanities and Social Sciences and 26 do not. One member has no major recorded, so I counted them in the "not" group to make the two counts add up to the full roster.

sql: select frameVersion, round(100.0*count(*)/(select count(*) from cards where name='Tarmogoyf'),2) from cards where name='Tarmogoyf' and frameVersion glob '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]' group by 1 order by 1 desc limit 1

sql: select L.`T-BIL`, L.Date, L.ID, P.SEX, P.Birthday from Laboratory L join Patient P on P.ID=L.ID where CAST(L.RNP AS REAL)=(select max(CAST(RNP AS REAL)) from Laboratory) and L.`T-BIL`=(select max(L2.`T-BIL`) from Laboratory L2 where CAST(L2.RNP AS REAL)=(select max(CAST(RNP AS REAL)) from Laboratory))

sql: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE isPromo = 1 AND layout IN ('split','transform','modal_dfc','adventure','aftermath','flip','meld') AND originalReleaseDate LIKE '2019/%'
answer: 31 cards match. I read "promotional" as isPromo = 1 and "multiple faces" as a layout of split, transform, modal_dfc, adventure, aftermath, flip or meld. sql: select p.SEX, count(distinct p.ID) as patient_count from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where l.ALB<3.5 and p.SEX in ('F','M') group by p.SEX;

sql:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT player_api_id, defensive_work_rate,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) rn
  FROM Player_Attributes

SELECT ROUND(AVG(p.height), 2) AS avg_height_cm

Players born 1990-01-01 through 1995-12-31 whose latest graded value is 'medium' are averaged. The Player and Player Attributes Terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM superhero s JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id=a.id LEFT JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id=p.id WHERE a.alignment='Good' AND (p.publisher_name IS NULL OR p.publisher_name <> 'DC Comics')

358 superheroes have alignment Good and are not published by DC Comics.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(cnt), 2) AS avg_attendees FROM (SELECT e.event_id, COUNT(a.link_to_member) AS cnt FROM event e LEFT JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.event_id IN (SELECT link_to_event FROM budget WHERE category = 'Advertisement') GROUP BY e.event_id)

sql: select (max(strftime('%s',Date||' '||Time))-min(strftime('%s',Date||' '||Time)))/60 as minutes_elapsed from transactions_1k t join gasstations g using(GasStationID) where g.Country='CZE' and t.Price>1000;

sql: SELECT AVG(HCT) AS avg_hematocrit FROM Laboratory WHERE Date >= '1991-01-01' AND Date < '1992-01-01' AND "U-PRO" IN ('300','>=300','>=1000') AND HCT IS NOT NULL
answer: The average hematocrit for 1991 lab tests with proteinuria of at least 300 mg/dL is 41.6. It is based on 5 tests, all of which had a hematocrit value. sql: SELECT a.account_id, a.frequency FROM account a JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id WHERE d.A3 = 'east Bohemia' AND a.date >= '1995-01-01' AND a.date < '2001-01-01' ORDER BY a.account_id

sql:

FROM satscores s JOIN schools sc ON s.cds = sc.CDSCode
WHERE s.rtype='S' AND sc.StatusType='Closed' AND s.AvgScrWrite IS NOT NULL
AND s.AvgScrWrite = (SELECT MAX(s2.AvgScrWrite) FROM satscores s2 JOIN schools c2 ON s2.cds=c2.CDSCode WHERE s2.rtype='S' AND c2.StatusType='Closed' AND s2.AvgScrWrite IS NOT NULL AND s2.AvgScrWrite < (SELECT MAX(s3.AvgScrWrite) FROM satscores s3 JOIN schools c3 ON s3.cds=c3.CDSCode WHERE s3.rtype='S' AND c3.StatusType='Closed' AND s3.AvgScrWrite IS NOT NULL))
answer: The second-highest average SAT writing score among Closed schools is 505, and only one school has it: FAME Public Charter, district Alameda County Office of Education, county Alameda. I used school-level SAT rows only (rtype='S'), StatusType='Closed', and took district and county from the schools table. The ontology terms used (SAT Score Record, School) are drafts, not certified.

sql:
WITH cty AS (SELECT County FROM schools WHERE CDSCode='01612590125716'),
f AS (
 SELECT fr.*, 
  (SELECT s.AvgScrRead+s.AvgScrMath+s.AvgScrWrite FROM satscores s WHERE s.cds=fr.CDSCode AND s.rtype='S') AS sat
 FROM frpm fr
 WHERE fr.`County Name`=(SELECT County FROM cty)
  AND fr.`Free Meal Count (K-12)`>500 AND fr.`FRPM Count (K-12)`<700)
SELECT (SELECT County FROM cty) AS county_name,
 COUNT(*) AS school_count,
 ROUND(AVG(ROUND(`Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)`*100,2)),2) AS avg_free_pct,
 ROUND(AVG(ROUND(`Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)`*100,2)),2) AS avg_frpm_pct,
 SUM(`Charter School (Y/N)`=1) AS charter_schools,
 SUM(`Charter School (Y/N)`=0) AS non_charter_schools,
 ROUND(AVG(sat),2) AS avg_sat
FROM f;
answer:
Fremont High (CDS 01612590125716, stored with a leading zero) is in Alameda County. Of the K-12 schools there with more than 500 free meals and fewer than 700 FRPM meals, the result is: 13 schools, average free-meal percentage 73.53, average FRPM percentage 80.65, 0 charter schools, 13 non-charter schools, average SAT 1189.00.

Choices I made: percentages are the stored K-12 fractions times 100, rounded to 2 decimals per school before averaging. SAT uses school-level records only (rtype='S'), summing the reading, math and writing averages. Schools without an SAT record are left out of the SAT average only, not out of the other columns.

sql: select 100.0*sum(strftime('%Y',Date)='2010')/count(*) - 100.0*sum(strftime('%Y',Date)='2011')/count(*) as diff from badges where Name='Student';

sql: select s.id,s.name,(select count(distinct t.language) from set_translations t where t.setCode=s.code) as languages from sets s where s.type='commander' and s.releaseDate between '2020-01-01' and '2020-12-31' and s.totalSetSize=(select max(totalSetSize) from sets where type='commander' and releaseDate between '2020-01-01' and '2020-12-31') order by s.id
answer: Commander 2020 (set id 44) has the largest total card count among 2020 commander-type sets: 322 cards, ahead of Zendikar Rising Commander at 142. There is no tie. The database has no rows in set_translations for this set, so its language count comes out as 0. That means no translation data is recorded, not that the set had no languages. I counted languages as distinct set_translations.language values for the set code. I used totalSetSize for the card count, since it covers promotional and supplemental products and excludes Alchemy modifications.

sql:

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Examination e ON e.ID=p.ID WHERE p.SEX='F' AND p.Admission='+' AND e."ANA Pattern"='P' AND strftime('%Y',p.Birthday) BETWEEN '1945' AND '1989'

sql: select p.Title, count(*) as related_count from posts p join postLinks l on l.PostId=p.Id where p.Title like '%principal component scores%' group by p.Id having count(*)=(select max(c) from (select count(*) c from posts p2 join postLinks l2 on l2.PostId=p2.Id where p2.Title like '%principal component scores%' group by p2.Id))
answer: "How do I analyse principal component scores?" has the most related posts, with 3. There is no tie: the only other matching post, "What are principal component scores?", has 2. sql:
WITH d AS (SELECT district_id, A2 name, A3 region, CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) pop, A11 sal FROM district),
rk AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY pop DESC) rnk,
  FIRST_VALUE(name) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY pop DESC, district_id) topname,
  FIRST_VALUE(pop) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY pop DESC, district_id) toppop FROM d),
t AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) n,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type='PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) inc,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type IN ('VYDAJ','VYBER') THEN amount ELSE 0 END) exp
  FROM trans GROUP BY account_id)
SELECT a.account_id, a.date AS account_open_date, a.frequency, rk.name AS district_name, rk.region,
  CASE WHEN rk.district_id = c.district_id THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS is_home_district,
  rk.sal AS average_salary, COALESCE(l.status,'none') AS loan_status, COALESCE(l.amount,0) AS loan_amount,
  COALESCE(t.n,0) AS transaction_count, COALESCE(t.inc,0) AS total_income, COALESCE(t.exp,0) AS total_expense,
  COALESCE(t.inc,0)-COALESCE(t.exp,0) AS net_balance,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM client cl JOIN district dd ON dd.district_id=cl.district_id WHERE dd.A3=rk.region) AS clients_in_region,
  rk.topname AS top_district_name, rk.toppop AS top_district_population, rk.rnk AS population_rank
FROM client c JOIN disp ON disp.client_id=c.client_id JOIN account a ON a.account_id=disp.account_id
JOIN rk ON rk.district_id=a.district_id LEFT JOIN loan l ON l.account_id=a.account_id LEFT JOIN t ON t.account_id=a.account_id
WHERE c.client_id=3541
ORDER BY transaction_count DESC, a.account_id;
answer:
Client 3541 can access one account, 2932, through a DISPONENT disposition. I counted any disposition type as access.

The account was opened 1993-05-04 and has monthly frequency (POPLATEK MESICNE). It is held in Olomouc, in north Moravia, which is not the client's home district. Average salary there is 8994. The account has no loan, so status is 'none' and amount is 0.

It has 655 transactions, with income of 2,821,377 and expenses of 2,787,425, so net balance is 33,952. Expenses include both VYDAJ and VYBER (cash withdrawal) transactions. Net balance is income minus expenses.

920 clients have a home district in north Moravia. The most populous district there is Ostrava - mesto, with 323,870 inhabitants. Olomouc ranks 4th by population in its region.

Population comes from district column A4, which is stored as text, so I cast it to an integer. Ranks use RANK, so ties share a rank and the next rank is skipped.

sql: select frameVersion, round(100.0*count(*)/(select count(*) from cards where name='Tarmogoyf'),2) as pct from cards where name='Tarmogoyf' and frameVersion=(select max(frameVersion) from cards where name='Tarmogoyf' and frameVersion glob '[0-9]*')
answer: The newest frame version is 2015, used by 66.67% of Tarmogoyf's printings (4 of 6). The other printings are one 2003 and one 'future'. I treated 'future' as a style label, not a year, so I ignored it when picking the newest year.

sql: with c as (select sp.power_name, count(distinct h.id) n from superhero h join publisher p on p.id=h.publisher_id join hero_power hp on hp.hero_id=h.id join superpower sp on sp.id=hp.power_id where p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics' and h.full_name is not null and trim(h.full_name) not in ('','-') group by sp.id) select power_name, n from c where n=(select max(n) from c)
