sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c JOIN sets s ON s.code = c.setCode WHERE c.originalReleaseDate LIKE '2014%' AND s.mtgoCode IS NOT NULL AND s.mtgoCode <> ''
answer: 293 card printings. I counted rows in `cards` (one row per printing, no DISTINCT on name) whose `originalReleaseDate` falls in 2014 and whose set has a non-null, non-empty `mtgoCode`. Dates in that column are stored as 'YYYY/M/D', so I matched on the '2014' prefix. Only 2,065 of 56,822 printings have an `originalReleaseDate`, and I used it as the question asks instead of falling back to the set's release date. Without the MTGO condition the 2014 count is 302. The `Card` and `Card Set` Terms I relied on are still draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT s.School, s.MailStreet FROM schools s JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE s.DOCType = 'State Board of Education' AND t.rtype = 'S' AND t.AvgScrRead = (SELECT MAX(t2.AvgScrRead) FROM schools s2 JOIN satscores t2 ON t2.cds = s2.CDSCode WHERE s2.DOCType = 'State Board of Education' AND t2.rtype = 'S')
answer: San Francisco Flex Academy, 1350 7th Avenue. It is the only school with the highest average SAT reading score among schools run by the State Board of Education, so there is no tie. I identified State Board schools by DOCType = 'State Board of Education'. I used school-level SAT rows only (rtype = 'S'), not district rows. For the address I returned the unabbreviated MailStreet, which has the street line only, not city or zip. The ontology terms I used (School, SAT Score Record) are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
WITH c AS (SELECT j.major_name, COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) n FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON e.event_id=a.link_to_event JOIN member m ON m.member_id=a.link_to_member JOIN major j ON j.major_id=m.link_to_major WHERE e.event_name='Football game' GROUP BY j.major_name)
SELECT major_name, n FROM c WHERE n=(SELECT MAX(n) FROM c) ORDER BY major_name;
answer:
Three majors tie at 2 attendees each: Elementary Education, Environmental Engineering, and Human Development and Family Studies.

Assumptions: the database has two 'Football game' events (2019-09-12 and 2019-10-10), so I combined them. I counted each member once, even if they went to both games. If you count attendances instead, Elementary Education leads with 3, because one of its members went to both games.

sql: with t as (select d.forename,d.surname,q.q1, substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1)*60+substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,':')+1) s from qualifying q join races r using(raceId) join drivers d using(driverId) where r.year=1995 and r.name='Japanese Grand Prix' and q.q1 like '%:%') select forename,surname,q1 from t where s=(select min(s) from t where s>=30)
answer: Michael Schumacher, 1:38.023. Mark Blundell's Q1 is recorded as 16:42.640, which can't be a real lap time. It would sort first as text, so I treated it as bad data and left it out. Without it, Schumacher is fastest with no tie.

sql: select p.SEX, count(distinct case when l.CRE>=1.5 then p.ID end) as abnormal_patients, count(distinct p.ID) as total_patients, round(100.0*count(distinct case when l.CRE>=1.5 then p.ID end)/count(distinct p.ID),1) as pct from Patient p left join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where p.SEX in ('M','F') group by p.SEX order by p.SEX desc
answer: M: 7 of 202 patients (3.5%) had at least one creatinine result of 1.5 or higher. F: 7 of 1023 patients (0.7%). Patients are counted once each, and the totals include patients with no lab results. I excluded 13 patients with blank sex, since you asked only for M and F.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT s.name, s.releaseDate FROM cards c JOIN sets s ON s.code = c.setCode WHERE c.name = 'Tarmogoyf' AND c.isReprint = 1 AND c.frameVersion GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(strftime('%Y', s.releaseDate) AS INTEGER) - CAST(c.frameVersion AS INTEGER) >= 10 ORDER BY s.releaseDate
answer: Only one set qualifies: Modern Masters (released 2013-06-07). Assumptions: a printing counts as a reprint when isReprint=1; frameVersion (the frame style's year) is compared with the set's release year, ignoring frameEffects; the non-numeric version 'future' is excluded; the 10-year gap is inclusive (>=10). The Card and Card Set ontology terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT bank, account, COUNT(*) AS payment_count, SUM(amount) AS total_paid FROM trans WHERE account_id = (SELECT account_id FROM loan WHERE amount = 98832 AND date = '1996-01-03') AND type = 'VYDAJ' AND date < '1996-01-03' AND bank IS NOT NULL AND bank <> '' AND account IS NOT NULL GROUP BY bank, account ORDER BY total_paid DESC
answer: The loan (loan_id 5999) belongs to account 4907. Before 1996-01-03 it paid three counterparties, largest total first: bank YZ, account 25638538, 18 payments, 70,884 total; bank AB, account 5604631, 18 payments, 22,554; bank QR, account 82890259, 19 payments, 6,175. I left out 18 cash withdrawals (VYBER, 37,400 total). They have no bank and a placeholder account of 0, so they have no counterparty. Another 54 debits with no bank or account are excluded for the same reason.

sql: select count(distinct case when d.forename='Peter' then d.driverId end) as peter, count(distinct case when d.forename='John' then d.driverId end) as john from results r join drivers d using(driverId) where r.position=1;
answer: Peter: 3, John: 2. I counted distinct drivers whose forename is exactly 'Peter' or 'John' and who have at least one result with finishing position 1 in the results table. The counts are not equal.

sql: select count(*) from cards where borderColor='black' and availability like '%mtgo%' and cast(power as integer)>=10
answer: 83. I counted cards whose availability includes 'mtgo' (this also covers mtgo,paper and arena,mtgo), with a black border and numeric power of 10 or more. Power is stored as text, so I cast it to an integer. Non-numeric values such as '∞', '*' and '?' are excluded.

sql:
SELECT
  SUM(CASE WHEN s=1 AND label='+' THEN 1 WHEN s=1 AND label='-' THEN -1 ELSE 0 END) AS single_only_diff,
  SUM(CASE WHEN s=0 AND label='+' THEN 1 WHEN s=0 AND label='-' THEN -1 ELSE 0 END) AS other_diff
FROM (
  SELECT m.label,
    NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bond b WHERE b.molecule_id=m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type<>'-') AS s
  FROM molecule m
);
answer: Molecules with only single bonds: 9 (carcinogenic minus non-carcinogenic). All other molecules: -48. The query returns one row with these two columns, in that order. I checked each number with a grouped version of the query. All 343 molecules have at least one bond, so none falls into the single-bond group by default. Molecules with only single bonds have slightly more carcinogenic than non-carcinogenic cases. Among molecules with any double or triple bond, non-carcinogenic ones outnumber carcinogenic ones by 48. This only compares counts. It does not compare rates, because the two groups differ in size.

sql: select d.code, q.q3 from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) join races r using(raceId) where r.year=2017 and r.name='Italian Grand Prix' and coalesce(q.q3,'')<>'' and q.q3=(select min(q3) from qualifying q2 join races r2 using(raceId) where r2.year=2017 and r2.name='Italian Grand Prix' and coalesce(q3,'')<>'')
answer: HAM (Lewis Hamilton) set the fastest Q3 time, 1:35.554. No other driver tied. I compared the m:ss.mmm text times directly, which sorts correctly because every Q3 time has the same format. I ignored NULL and empty Q3 values.

sql: SELECT SUM(convertedManaCost) FROM cards WHERE artist = 'Rob Alexander' AND originalReleaseDate LIKE '2013/%'
answer: 4. Only one Rob Alexander printing has an original release date in 2013 (2013/1/11), and its converted mana cost is 4. Dates are stored as 'YYYY/M/D' text, so I filtered on the '2013/' prefix. Cards with no original release date are excluded. The Card term is still a draft.

sql: SELECT SUM(Reputation) AS total_reputation FROM users WHERE Id IN (SELECT OwnerUserId FROM posts WHERE Score = 10 AND Tags LIKE '%<r>%')
answer: 50,863. This is the combined reputation of distinct users who own at least one post with Score = 10 tagged exactly <r>. I counted each user once. If you count a user once per post instead, the total is 75,563.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.date || '|' || r.text) AS ruling_count FROM rulings r JOIN cards c ON r.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Fireball'
answer:
Fireball has 4 distinct official rulings across all time, with no date filter. I did not run this exact final query. It uses the same join and distinct expression as my check query, which returned 4.

Fireball has 36 printings, and the rulings table stores each ruling once per printing. Of those printings, 34 have rulings, which gives 136 rows for 4 distinct rulings. I counted distinct date and text pairs so the same ruling isn't counted once per printing. If you want the raw row count, it is 136, but that counts the same four rulings repeatedly. The Card and Card Ruling terms I relied on are still drafts and not certified.

sql: SELECT 1.0*(SELECT b.amount FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event=e.event_id WHERE e.event_name='Yearly Kickoff' AND b.category='Advertisement')/(SELECT b.amount FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event=e.event_id WHERE e.event_name='October Meeting' AND b.category='Advertisement') AS ratio
answer: Yearly Kickoff의 Advertisement 예산은 150, October Meeting은 55이므로 비율은 약 2.727(150/55)입니다. 각 행사에 Advertisement 예산이 한 건씩만 있어 그대로 나눴습니다.

Three artists tie with 2 cards each: Chase Stone, Jonathan Kuo and Zoltan Boros. I counted each row in the cards table (each printing) as a card, and kept black-bordered rows whose availability includes "arena" and whose numeric power is 10 or higher. If you count unique card names instead, Zoltan Boros leads with 1 and several artists have 1 each, so the tie would be much larger.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM superhero s JOIN alignment a ON a.id = s.alignment_id WHERE a.alignment = 'Neutral'
answer: 28 superheroes have the 'Neutral' alignment. I read "neither good nor bad" as the alignment value 'Neutral'. The 6 heroes with no alignment recorded (NULL) are not counted, because their alignment is unknown. The 'N/A' alignment exists in the lookup table but no hero uses it.

sql: SELECT d.driverRef FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3<>'' AND q.q3=(SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying q2 WHERE q2.raceId=r.raceId AND q2.q3<>'')
answer: hamilton. He set the fastest Q3 time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, and the query returned a single row, so there was no tie. I took "fastest" as the lowest q3 text value, which compares correctly because all times use the same M:SS.mmm format. Rows with no Q3 time are excluded. The Driver, Qualifying Result and Race terms it relies on are still drafts and not certified.

sql:
WITH top AS (SELECT * FROM Laboratory WHERE CAST(RNP AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(RNP AS REAL)) FROM Laboratory WHERE RNP IS NOT NULL))
SELECT t."T-BIL", t."Date", p.ID, p.SEX, p.Birthday FROM top t JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = t.ID WHERE t."T-BIL" = (SELECT MAX("T-BIL") FROM top)
answer: One test matches: total bilirubin 0.4, lab date 1989-07-18, patient ID 1650222, sex F, birthday 1947-03-17. I read the highest anti-RNP result as the highest numeric value (256), since RNP is stored as text. Among those tests I took the highest T-BIL, and ties would each get their own row. The Laboratory Test and Patient Terms are still in draft status.

sql: select frameVersion, count(*) from cards where artist='John Avon' and cardKingdomFoilId is not null and cardKingdomId is not null and frameVersion glob '[0-9]*' group by frameVersion having frameVersion=(select max(frameVersion) from cards where artist='John Avon' and cardKingdomFoilId is not null and cardKingdomId is not null and frameVersion glob '[0-9]*')
answer: The most recent frame year is 2015, and 100 of John Avon's cards carry it. I read "powerful foils" as the docs describe it: cards with both a cardKingdomFoilId and a cardKingdomId. I matched the artist exactly on 'John Avon'. A looser match on the name returned no extra artists. One of his qualifying cards has frameVersion 'future', which isn't a year, so I left it out. If you count it as the most recent, the result would be 'future' with 1 card.

sql:
WITH risky AS (SELECT DISTINCT team_api_id FROM Team_Attributes WHERE chanceCreationPassingClass='Risky'),
rt AS (SELECT t.team_api_id, t.team_short_name FROM Team t JOIN risky r USING(team_api_id)),
inforce AS (SELECT a.team_api_id, a.chanceCreationPassing v FROM Team_Attributes a WHERE a.date=(SELECT MAX(date) FROM Team_Attributes b WHERE b.team_api_id=a.team_api_id AND date<='2014-09-19 23:59:59'))
SELECT rt.team_short_name, COUNT(DISTINCT rt.team_api_id) AS club_count, ROUND(AVG(i.v),1) AS avg_risk
FROM rt LEFT JOIN inforce i USING(team_api_id)
GROUP BY rt.team_short_name HAVING club_count>1 ORDER BY avg_risk DESC, rt.team_short_name;
answer: 6 short names are shared by more than one Risky club: REA (2 clubs, avg 69.5), GEN (2, 66.5), WOL (2, 61.5), MAR (2, 58.0), HAM (2, 56.0), LEV (2, 53.5). Readings I chose: (1) "Risky at any point" means a club has at least one attribute record with class Risky, and only those clubs are counted per short name. (2) The record "in force on 19 Sep 2014" is each club's latest record dated on or before that day. Clubs with no such record are still counted but left out of the average.

sql: SELECT a.account_id, a.frequency FROM account a JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id WHERE d.A3 = 'east Bohemia' AND a.date >= '1995-01-01' AND a.date < '2001-01-01' ORDER BY a.account_id
answer: The query returns account_id and frequency for accounts in east Bohemia (district.A3 = 'east Bohemia') whose creation date falls in 1995-01-01 through 2000-12-31. I read "East Bohemia districts" as the region value 'east Bohemia'. Frequency is the raw code: 'POPLATEK MESICNE' is monthly, 'POPLATEK TYDNE' is weekly, 'POPLATEK PO OBRATU' is after transaction. The data only holds accounts created up to 1997-12-28, so in practice the result covers 1995 to 1997. The run_sql output was capped at 100 rows (truncated), so I can't give the full count. Terms Account and District are still draft, not certified.

sql: select round(avg(weight_kg),2) from superhero where superhero_name<>'3-D Man' and weight_kg>0 and id in (select hero_id from hero_power where power_id in (select power_id from hero_power where hero_id=(select id from superhero where superhero_name='3-D Man')));
answer: 282411.79 kg. I treated weight_kg of 0 or NULL as unrecorded, as the docs say, and excluded both. I kept extreme recorded weights such as Godzilla at 90,000,000 kg, which pull the average up a lot.

sql: SELECT AVG(weight_kg) FROM superhero WHERE weight_kg > 0 AND race_id > 1 AND race_id NOT IN (SELECT race_id FROM superhero WHERE gender_id = 2 AND race_id IS NOT NULL)
answer: The average weight is about 156,709.09 kg. I made three choices. Weight 0 or NULL counts as not recorded, per the wiki's data-quirks page. Race id 1 ('-') and NULL race are not real races, so those heroes are left out. A race qualifies only if none of its heroes has gender 'Female'. The average is dominated by an extreme outlier (Godzilla at 90,000,000 kg).

sql: select round(100.0*sum(s.Virtual in ('F','V','C','P'))/count(*),1) as pct from satscores t join schools s on s.CDSCode=t.cds where t.AvgScrMath>400
answer: 22.3% of the 1,537 schools with an average SAT Math score above 400 offer virtual instruction. I counted any school coded F, V, C or P as offering it, and schools coded N or with no Virtual value as not offering it. They stay in the denominator.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.ID, CAST((strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',p.Birthday)) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09')<strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)) AS INTEGER) AS age FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE l.LDH>600 AND l.LDH<800 AND l."U-PRO" IN ('300','>=300','>=1000') ORDER BY p.ID
answer: 3 patients qualify (ID, completed age on 2026-10-09): 3182521 (73), 4425292 (71), 4632548 (99). Reading used: both findings on the same Laboratory row (same date); U-PRO counted as ≥300 mg/dL when '300', '>=300' or '>=1000'; other plain numbers (e.g. '3','4') are treated as mg/dL and excluded, as are '+2(100)'-style values. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still draft (uncertified).

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM member m WHERE m.link_to_major = major.major_id) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_majors_without_members FROM major
answer: 76.99% of the 113 majors have no club member. I counted every row in the member table as a club member, including those marked "Inactive". The `Major` term used is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT SUM(Reputation) FROM users WHERE Id IN (SELECT OwnerUserId FROM posts WHERE Tags LIKE '%<r>%' AND LasActivityDate >= '2014-08-27' AND LasActivityDate < '2014-08-28')
answer: The combined reputation is 3773. I read "users who own the posts" as each distinct owner counted once. The 27 matching posts have 22 distinct owners. If an owner were counted once per post, the total would be 3999. "Tagged R" means the exact tag <r>, so tags like <r-squared> don't match. The whole of 2014-08-27 is covered by checking LasActivityDate (the column name is spelled that way in the posts table) from 2014-08-27 up to but not including 2014-08-28.

sql:
SELECT CASE p.Admission WHEN '+' THEN 'admitted to the hospital' ELSE 'followed at the outpatient clinic' END AS patient_group, COUNT(*) AS normal_ldh_measurements
FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID
WHERE p.Admission IN ('+','-') AND l.LDH < 500
GROUP BY p.Admission ORDER BY p.Admission = '+' DESC
answer:
The admitted group has 4,881 LDH measurements in the normal range. The outpatient group has 4,991.

I took "normal range" from docs/Laboratory.csv, which defines it as LDH < 500. NULL LDH values are not counted. Every Laboratory row for each patient counts, with no date filter. Patients whose Admission is blank (34) or '+(' (3) are left out, because the question names only '+' and '-'. The Terms Laboratory Test and Patient are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select count(*) from Patient p where p.Admission='-' and exists(select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and (l.HCT<=29 or l.HCT>=52)) and exists(select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and l.RNP glob '[0-9]*' and cast(l.RNP as real)>16)
answer: 2 patients. Assumptions: outpatient means Admission = '-'. Normal hematocrit is 29 < HCT < 52 per the docs, so non-normal means HCT <= 29 or >= 52. RNP is stored as text, so I compared numeric values only (above 16, i.e. 64 and 256). Non-numeric values such as '-', '+-' and 'negative' were excluded. Each condition is checked across all of a patient's lab dates.

sql: select count(distinct coalesce('u'||p.OwnerUserId,'n'||p.OwnerDisplayName)) as user_count from votes v join posts p on p.Id=v.PostId where v.VoteTypeId=8 and v.BountyAmount>=30 and v.CreationDate>='2010-01-01' and v.CreationDate<'2011-01-01'
answer: 22 distinct users. I counted bounty-start votes (VoteTypeId 8) with BountyAmount >= 30 and a CreationDate in 2010. I took the bounty offerer to be the post's owner: OwnerUserId where recorded, otherwise OwnerDisplayName. Those votes cover 32 bounties. One of them has no OwnerUserId and falls back to the display name.

sql: select round(avg(height_cm),1) from superhero where id!=1 and height_cm>0 and id in (select hero_id from hero_power where power_id in (select power_id from hero_power where hero_id=1))
answer: 3-D Man와 초능력을 하나 이상 공유하는 다른 히어로들의 평균 키는 339.5cm입니다. 키가 NULL이거나 0인 히어로는 문서에서 키 미상으로 정의하므로 제외했고, 3-D Man(id 1)도 뺐습니다. 평균이 높게 나온 것은 Surtur나 Ymir처럼 키가 304.8m로 기록된 극단값이 포함되었기 때문일 수 있습니다.

sql:
SELECT p.SEX AS sex,
 COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN l.CRE >= 1.5 THEN p.ID END) AS abnormal_patients,
 COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS total_patients,
 ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN l.CRE >= 1.5 THEN p.ID END) / COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID), 1) AS pct
FROM Patient p LEFT JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID
WHERE p.SEX IN ('M','F')
GROUP BY p.SEX
ORDER BY p.SEX DESC
answer: M: 7 of 202 patients (3.5%) have at least one creatinine result of 1.5 or higher. F: 7 of 1023 patients (0.7%). Assumptions: out of range means CRE >= 1.5 in any Laboratory row. Totals include patients with no lab rows (LEFT JOIN). Patients with a blank SEX value are excluded. The query also returns a leading sex label column so the rows are identifiable. The Patient and Laboratory Test Terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT f.language) FROM foreign_data f JOIN cards c ON c.uuid = f.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Swamp'
answer: Swamp has been printed in 11 foreign languages: German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Chinese Simplified, Chinese Traditional and Phyrexian. I matched the exact card name 'Swamp', which leaves out Snow-Covered Swamp. I counted each language once across all sets and years, and counted Phyrexian because the data lists it as a language. Without it the count is 10.

sql: select round(100.0*count(distinct case when a.defensive_work_rate='high' then p.player_api_id end)/count(distinct p.player_api_id),2) from Player p join Player_Attributes a on a.player_api_id=p.player_api_id where p.birthday>='1991' and a.defensive_work_rate in ('high','medium','low')
answer: 17.41. I counted a player as having a rating only if some record says high, medium or low. The column also holds junk values such as numbers, 'o', 'ean' and 'es', and I excluded those. A player counts as high if any record says high.

sql:
WITH t AS (
 SELECT code FROM sets WHERE code=(SELECT s.code FROM sets s WHERE s.code IN (SELECT setCode FROM cards WHERE name='Abyssal Horror') ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.code LIMIT 1)
 UNION
 SELECT code FROM sets WHERE code=(SELECT code FROM sets ORDER BY releaseDate DESC, code LIMIT 1)
)
SELECT s.name, ROUND(100.0*SUM(c.manaCost IS NOT NULL AND c.convertedManaCost<=3)/COUNT(*),2) AS pct
FROM t JOIN sets s ON s.code=t.code JOIN cards c ON c.setCode=s.code
GROUP BY s.code, s.name ORDER BY s.releaseDate;
answer: Urza's Saga: 58.15%. Time Spiral Remastered: 80.00%. Urza's Saga is the earliest-released set containing Abyssal Horror. Time Spiral Remastered (2021-03-19) is the latest-released set. I took the percentage over all card rows (printings) in each set. A card counts toward the numerator only if its manaCost is not NULL and convertedManaCost is 3 or less. Cards without a printed mana cost, such as lands, stay in the denominator.

sql: select u.DisplayName from posts p join users u on u.Id=p.LastEditorUserId where p.Title='Examples for teaching: Correlation does not mean causation'
answer: Abhilash. I matched the post by its exact title and joined LastEditorUserId (43889) to users to get the display name.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "Patient" p WHERE p."Admission"='-' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "Laboratory" l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND (l.HCT<=29 OR l.HCT>=52)) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "Laboratory" l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>16)
answer:
2 outpatient patients have both a non-normal hematocrit and an anti-RNP value above 16.

Readings I chose where the question was ambiguous:
- Outpatient means Patient.Admission = '-'.
- The documented normal hematocrit range is 29 < HCT < 52, so non-normal means HCT <= 29 or HCT >= 52.
- RNP is stored as text. I cast it to a number and kept values above 16, so 'negative' is excluded and 16 itself is not above 16.
- Each condition is checked separately, so the two readings can come from different test dates.

The Patient and Laboratory Test terms I relied on are still draft, not certified.

sql: select c.Street, c.City, c.Zip, c.State from satscores s join schools c on c.CDSCode=s.cds where s.rtype='S' and s.NumTstTakr>=700 order by s.NumGE1500*1.0/s.NumTstTakr, s.cds limit 1
answer: Granada Hills Charter High: 10535 Zelzah Avenue, Granada Hills, 91344-5902, CA. I read "schools" as school-level rows (rtype 'S'), which excludes district rows. Excellence rate is NumGE1500 divided by NumTstTakr. Only this school had at least 700 test takers (748), with a rate of 67.5%. That rate is high, not low, so it isn't one of the "worst" schools. The lowest rates under the 700 cutoff belong to districts, which I excluded.

sql: SELECT e.expense_description, COUNT(*) AS times_bought FROM expense e JOIN member m ON e.link_to_member = m.member_id WHERE m.first_name='Sacha' AND m.last_name='Harrison' GROUP BY e.expense_description
answer: Sacha Harrison's expenses, grouped by description, give 7 items: Alumni Glass 1, Bakery - Donuts, muffins 1, Pizza 1, Post Cards, Posters 1, Posters 3, Travel Mug 2, Water, chips, cookies 3. I used the expense description as the item name and counted every expense under her name, approved or not. Only one expense in the table is unapproved, and I didn't check whether it is hers. Descriptions are counted as written, so similar ones such as "Posters" and "Post Cards, Posters" stay separate. The Expense and Member terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: with c as (select uuid,count(*) n from rulings group by uuid) select distinct cards.name,cards.artist,cards.isPromo from c join cards using(uuid) where n=(select max(n) from c);
answer: I read "printing" as one card row (one uuid) and counted rulings per uuid. The printings tied for the most rulings give two combinations: Teferi's Protection / Chase Stone / isPromo=0, and Teferi's Protection / Chase Stone / isPromo=1.

sql:
SELECT c.colour AS eye_colour, COUNT(*) AS hero_count, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rank
FROM superhero s
INNER JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
INNER JOIN colour c ON s.eye_colour_id = c.id
WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND c.colour <> 'No Colour'
GROUP BY c.colour
ORDER BY hero_count DESC, eye_colour ASC
answer: Blue is the most common eye colour among Marvel Comics heroes (126), then Brown (89), Green (40), Red (31), Yellow (13), White (12), Black (11), Grey (4), Hazel (3), Gold and Purple (2 each, rank 10), and seven colours with 1 hero each (rank 12). The query returns 18 colours. I treated the colour 'No Colour' as unknown and excluded it, because the docs don't define "unknown". Tied colours share a rank (RANK()) and are ordered alphabetically within a tie. The Colour and Publisher terms used are still drafts.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics') / COUNT(*), 2) AS percentage FROM superhero s LEFT JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE s.height_cm BETWEEN 150 AND 180;
answer: 60.87% (140 of 230 heroes with height 150–180 cm are published by Marvel Comics). Heroes with no publisher stay in the denominator; those with no recorded height are excluded.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) FROM cards c WHERE hasContentWarning = 1 AND ','||availability||',' LIKE '%,paper,%' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cards d WHERE d.name = c.name AND ','||d.availability||',' LIKE '%,mtgo,%')
answer: 5 different cards. I counted a card once by name, and only if no printing of it has ever been on MTGO. That is the stricter reading of "never been available". If you only exclude printings that are on MTGO themselves, the count is 7. Two cards have a content-warning paper printing that is not on MTGO, but another printing of the same name is.

sql: select count(*) from cards where duelDeck='b' and hasFoil=0 and power glob '[0-9]*' and cast(power as real)<3
answer: 213 cards in duel deck B are not available in foil and have power below 3. That is 13 with power 0, 74 with power 1 and 126 with power 2. I counted only cards with a numeric power. Cards with null power (non-creatures) and cards with '*' power are excluded, because their power is unknown rather than below 3.

sql: select p.ID, cast((strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',Birthday)) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09')<strftime('%m-%d',Birthday)) as int) as age from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where l.HCT>=52 group by p.ID having count(*)>=2
answer: 3 patients have at least two lab results with HCT >= 52. They are 2307640 (age 73), 3182521 (age 73) and 4007151 (age 58). Age is completed years on 2026-10-09, computed from Birthday. I counted each lab row (ID, Date) as one result.

sql:
SELECT d.department, COALESCE(SUM(i.amount),0) AS total_dues
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT department FROM major WHERE college = (SELECT college FROM major WHERE department='Electrical and Computer Engineering Department' LIMIT 1)) d
LEFT JOIN major mj ON mj.department = d.department
LEFT JOIN member m ON m.link_to_major = mj.major_id AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_member = m.member_id)
LEFT JOIN income i ON i.link_to_member = m.member_id AND i.source = 'Dues'
GROUP BY d.department ORDER BY d.department
answer: The Electrical and Computer Engineering Department is in the College of Engineering, which has four departments. Dues received from members who attended at least one event: Biological Engineering $0, Civil and Environmental Engineering $200, Electrical and Computer Engineering $50, Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering $0. I read "enrolled members" as members linked to a major in that department, and "took part in events" as having at least one attendance record. "Dues" means income rows with source 'Dues', linked to the member. Each attending member is counted once, so multiple attendances do not inflate the totals. The Income, Major and Member terms in the ontology are still draft (not certified).

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE setCode IN (SELECT s.code FROM sets s WHERE s.code IN (SELECT setCode FROM cards WHERE name='Ancestor''s Chosen') AND s.releaseDate=(SELECT MAX(s2.releaseDate) FROM sets s2 WHERE s2.code IN (SELECT setCode FROM cards WHERE name='Ancestor''s Chosen'))) AND types LIKE '%Creature%' AND power GLOB '[0-9]*' AND toughness GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(power AS INTEGER)>CAST(toughness AS INTEGER)
answer: 25. 'Ancestor's Chosen' 카드가 들어 있는 세트 중 가장 최근에 출시된 세트는 UMA(Ultimate Masters) 하나였습니다. 이 세트에서 Creature 타입이면서 power가 toughness보다 큰 카드는 25장입니다. power나 toughness가 '*'처럼 숫자가 아닌 카드는 비교할 수 없어서 제외했습니다. 이 세트에서는 카드 수(25장)와 서로 다른 이름의 수(25개)가 같아서 어느 쪽으로 세어도 결과가 같습니다. 쿼리에 쓴 Card, Card Set 용어는 아직 인증되지 않은 초안(draft) 상태입니다.

sql: select count(*) from superhero a where a.publisher_id=(select publisher_id from superhero where superhero_name='Blackwulf') and a.eye_colour_id is not null and exists(select 1 from superhero b where b.eye_colour_id=a.eye_colour_id and b.publisher_id is not null and b.publisher_id<>a.publisher_id)
answer: 382 heroes. Blackwulf's publisher (id 13) has many heroes. I counted each hero of that publisher once (not each distinct eye colour) when another hero with a non-null, different publisher shares their eye colour. Heroes with no eye colour were excluded.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(mv),1) AS average_mana_value FROM (SELECT name, MAX(convertedManaCost) mv FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND edhrecRank BETWEEN 1 AND 1000 AND name IN (SELECT c2.name FROM cards c2 JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid=c2.uuid WHERE l.status='Banned') GROUP BY name)
answer: 3.4 — the average mana value of 7 distinct creature cards (exact 3.43) that are banned in at least one format and have EDHRec rank 1–1000. Cards are deduplicated by name (mana value and rank were identical across printings). "Banned in any format" was interpreted as any format, not just Commander. Ontology terms used are still draft.

sql: SELECT p.ViewCount, u.DisplayName FROM posts p LEFT JOIN users u ON u.Id = p.LastEditorUserId WHERE p.Title = 'Computer game datasets'
answer: The post 'Computer game datasets' has 1708 views, and its last editor's display name is 'mbq'. I found the editor by joining posts.LastEditorUserId to users.Id. The query returned one row. It relies on draft (not yet certified) Terms Post and User.

sql: SELECT l.ID, l.Date, l.DNA FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND p.Admission = '+' AND l.DNA IS NOT NULL AND CAST(l.DNA AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(l2.DNA AS REAL)) FROM Laboratory l2 JOIN Patient p2 ON p2.ID = l2.ID WHERE p2.SEX = 'F' AND p2.Admission = '+' AND l2.DNA IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY l.ID
answer: Patient 2933261, lab date 1988-04-25, anti-DNA level 185. This is the only record at the maximum. I read "admitted as inpatients" as Patient.Admission = '+' and "female" as SEX = 'F'. DNA is stored as text, so I cast it to a number before comparing. All non-null values were numeric.

sql: select d.department, coalesce(sum(i.amount),0) as total_dues from (select distinct department from major where college=(select college from major where department='Electrical and Computer Engineering Department')) d left join major m on m.department=d.department left join member b on b.link_to_major=m.major_id and exists(select 1 from attendance a where a.link_to_member=b.member_id) left join income i on i.link_to_member=b.member_id and i.source='Dues' group by d.department;
answer: College of Engineering has 4 departments. Total dues ($) from members who attended at least one event: Biological Engineering 0; Civil and Environmental Engineering 200; Electrical and Computer Engineering 50; Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering 0. Assumptions: only income with source 'Dues' counts. A member counts once if they attended any event. Every dues payment row is summed, so the 2 members with two dues rows count twice.

sql: SELECT notes FROM income WHERE date_received = '2019-09-14' AND source = 'Fundraising'
answer: The note is "Secured donations to help pay for speaker gifts." I read "fundraising proceeds" as income rows with source = 'Fundraising'. Only one row matched that source on 2019-09-14 (200 dollars).

sql: SELECT p.ID, l.Date, l.DNA FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND p.Admission = '+' AND l.DNA IS NOT NULL AND CAST(l.DNA AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(l2.DNA AS REAL)) FROM Laboratory l2 JOIN Patient p2 ON p2.ID = l2.ID WHERE p2.SEX = 'F' AND p2.Admission = '+' AND l2.DNA IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY p.ID
answer:
The highest anti-DNA level among female inpatients is 185, from patient 2933261 on the 1988-04-25 lab test. Only one record has that level, so there are no ties. The Laboratory and Patient Terms it relies on are still draft, not certified.

I read "admitted as inpatients" as Patient.Admission = '+', and "female" as SEX = 'F'. The anti-DNA value is stored as text in Laboratory.DNA, so the query casts it to a number before taking the maximum. Comparing it as text would wrongly rank '95.5' above '185'.

sql: SELECT s.id, s.name, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t.language) FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode=s.code) AS languages FROM sets s WHERE s.type='commander' AND s.releaseDate BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31' AND s.totalSetSize=(SELECT MAX(totalSetSize) FROM sets WHERE type='commander' AND releaseDate BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31') ORDER BY s.id
answer: Commander 2020 (set id 44) has the highest total card count among Commander-type sets released in 2020. The data shows 0 languages for it, because set_translations has no rows for this set's code. I used sets.totalSetSize as the total card count, which includes promotional and supplemental cards. I did not check the docs for how it treats Alchemy modifications. Languages are counted as distinct set_translations.language values. Only one set came back, so there was no tie. The Card Set and Set Translation terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT h.UserId FROM postHistory h JOIN posts p ON p.Id = h.PostId WHERE p.ViewCount >= 1000 AND h.UserId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY h.UserId, h.PostId HAVING COUNT(*) = 1
answer: 270명입니다. 조회수가 1,000 이상인 게시글 중 한 곳 이상에서 해당 사용자의 수정 이력(postHistory)이 정확히 1건인 사용자를 찾았습니다. 사용자와 게시글을 짝지어 이력 수를 센 해석을 택했고, UserId가 비어 있는 행은 제외했습니다.

sql:
SELECT season, COUNT(DISTINCT pid) AS player_count FROM (
SELECT season, away_player_1 pid FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal-away_team_goal>=5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_2 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal-away_team_goal>=5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_3 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal-away_team_goal>=5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_4 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal-away_team_goal>=5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_5 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal-away_team_goal>=5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_6 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal-away_team_goal>=5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_7 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal-away_team_goal>=5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_8 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal-away_team_goal>=5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_9 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal-away_team_goal>=5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_10 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal-away_team_goal>=5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_11 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal-away_team_goal>=5
) WHERE pid IS NOT NULL GROUP BY season ORDER BY season;
answer: 시즌별로 원정팀이 5골 차 이상 패한 경기(home_team_goal - away_team_goal >= 5)의 원정 선발 명단(away_player_1~11, 선수 id)에서 서로 다른 선수 수를 셌습니다. 한 시즌 안에서 같은 선수가 여러 경기에 나와도 1명으로 계산했고, 명단이 비어 있는 칸(NULL)은 제외했습니다. 결과는 2008/2009 242명, 2009/2010 320명, 2010/2011 465명, 2011/2012 525명, 2012/2013 420명, 2013/2014 354명, 2014/2015 525명, 2015/2016 462명으로 8개 시즌입니다.

sql:
WITH t AS (SELECT DISTINCT c.circuitRef, r.time FROM races r JOIN circuits c USING(circuitId) WHERE r.time IS NOT NULL AND r.time<>''),
e AS (SELECT circuitRef, time FROM t WHERE time=(SELECT MIN(time) FROM t)),
l AS (SELECT circuitRef, time FROM t WHERE time=(SELECT MAX(time) FROM t))
SELECT e.circuitRef AS earliest_circuitRef, l.circuitRef AS latest_circuitRef,
 (strftime('%s','2000-01-01 '||l.time)-strftime('%s','2000-01-01 '||e.time)) AS gap_seconds FROM e, l;
answer: The earliest start is at fuji (04:30:00) and the latest is at americas (20:00:00), a gap of 55,800 seconds. The tie rule is built into the query, but each extreme belongs to a single circuit. I used all seasons and left out the 722 races with no recorded start time. Start times are compared as time of day only, ignoring the date.

sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(COUNT(t.id) AS REAL)/COUNT(DISTINCT s.code),2) AS avg_languages FROM sets s LEFT JOIN set_translations t ON t.setCode=s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND t.translation<>'' WHERE s.releaseDate>='2016-01-01' AND s.releaseDate<'2017-01-01'
answer: 4.74. 2016년 출시 세트 전체를 분모로 계산했고, 번역이 없는 세트는 0개 언어로 넣었습니다. translation이 null이거나 빈 값인 행은 번역된 언어로 세지 않았습니다.

sql: select g.gender, count(x.id) as hero_count from gender g left join (select s.id,s.gender_id from superhero s join colour c on c.id=s.hair_colour_id where c.colour='Blue' and (select count(distinct power_id) from hero_power h where h.hero_id=s.id)>=10) x on x.gender_id=g.id where g.gender in ('Male','Female') group by g.gender order by g.gender desc
answer: Male: 3, Female: 0. I read "blue-haired" as hair colour exactly 'Blue'. One more male hero has 'Black/Blue' hair and 23 powers, and I left him out; including him would make the male count 4. Only 4 heroes have any blue in their hair colour, and none of them is female, so the female count is 0. The query still returns a Female row with 0.

sql:
WITH c AS (SELECT d.forename||' '||d.surname AS full_name, r.name AS race_name, r.year AS race_year, q.q3 AS q3_time FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId WHERE d.nationality='British' AND CAST(substr(d.dob,1,4) AS INTEGER)>1980 AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3<>'')
SELECT full_name, race_name, race_year, q3_time FROM c WHERE (CAST(substr(q3_time,1,instr(q3_time,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60+CAST(substr(q3_time,instr(q3_time,':')+1) AS REAL)) = (SELECT MIN(CAST(substr(q3_time,1,instr(q3_time,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60+CAST(substr(q3_time,instr(q3_time,':')+1) AS REAL)) FROM c)
answer: Lewis Hamilton set the fastest Q3 time among British drivers born after 1980: 1:04.424 at the 2017 Austrian Grand Prix. Only one qualifying result has that time, so there is no tie. I read "British" as nationality = 'British' and "born after 1980" as birth year > 1980. I compared Q3 times numerically in seconds and skipped blank Q3 values. The Driver, Qualifying Result and Race terms used are still drafts in the ontology.

sql: with c as (select r.race, count(*) n from superhero s join race r on r.id=s.race_id where s.publisher_id=(select publisher_id from superhero where full_name='Charles Chandler') and r.race<>'-' group by r.race) select race, n from c where n=(select max(n) from c)
answer: Human, 84 superheroes. Charles Chandler (3-D Man) is published by publisher 13. The race table stores 'no race' as the placeholder '-' (id 1), so I excluded it. It was the largest group at 170 heroes. No other race ties with Human.

sql:
with w as (
select t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name, t.team_short_name, count(*) n
from Match m join Team t on t.team_api_id=m.home_team_api_id
where m.home_team_goal-m.away_team_goal>=3
and (select a.buildUpPlaySpeedClass from Team_Attributes a where a.team_api_id=m.home_team_api_id and a.date<=m.date order by a.date desc, a.id desc limit 1)='Fast'
group by t.team_api_id)
select team_long_name, team_short_name, n from w where n=(select max(n) from w) order by 1;
answer:
Borussia Dortmund (DOR) has the most such home wins, with 29 wins by 3+ goals while its latest rating dated on or before the match was 'Fast'. No other club ties with it.

I read the question as asking for the top club or clubs by count, because of the tie clause. If you wanted every club with at least one such win, drop the final `where n = max` filter. Clubs are grouped by team_api_id, so two clubs that share a short name stay separate. Matches where the club had no rating on or before the match date don't count.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 2) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero s JOIN gender g ON s.gender_id = g.id WHERE g.gender = 'Female' AND s.weight_kg IS NOT NULL AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: The average weight of Female heroes is 78.51 kg. I treated a weight of 0 as unknown, the same as NULL, following the ontology's "Weight Known" filter, so those rows are excluded. The Superhero and Gender terms are still draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT id FROM cards WHERE borderColor = 'borderless' AND (cardKingdomId IS NULL OR cardKingdomFoilId IS NULL)
answer: 72개의 카드 id를 반환합니다. 'Card Kingdom에 일반판 또는 foil판 등록이 없다'는 조건은 borderColor가 'borderless'이면서 cardKingdomId 또는 cardKingdomFoilId가 NULL인 경우로 해석했습니다. 빈 문자열 값은 없었습니다.

sql: SELECT p.SEX, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS patient_count FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.Date BETWEEN '1994-01-01' AND '1994-12-31' AND l.GOT < 60 AND p.SEX IN ('F','M') GROUP BY p.SEX ORDER BY p.SEX
answer: F: 80 patients, M: 16 patients. I read "normal GOT" as GOT < 60, the normal range in docs/Laboratory.csv. A patient counts once if at least one 1994 test had a normal value. Patients with several 1994 tests are not counted twice.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p."SEX"='F' THEN p."ID" END) AS F, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p."SEX"='M' THEN p."ID" END) AS M FROM "Laboratory" l INNER JOIN "Patient" p ON p."ID"=l."ID" WHERE l."Date" >= '1994-01-01' AND l."Date" <= '1994-12-31' AND l."GOT" < 60
answer: F = 80, M = 16. 정상 GOT는 문서 기준 N < 60으로 봤고, 1994년에 정상 GOT 검사가 한 번이라도 있는 환자를 1명으로 셌습니다(같은 해 비정상 결과가 있어도 포함). GOT가 비어 있는 검사는 제외했습니다. Patient, Laboratory Test 용어는 인증 전 초안입니다.

sql: select s.name, s.releaseDate from sets s where s.code in (select setCode from cards where name='Aven Mindcensor' and frameVersion='2015') and s.releaseDate=(select max(s2.releaseDate) from sets s2 where s2.code in (select setCode from cards where name='Aven Mindcensor' and frameVersion='2015'))
answer: Amonkhet Remastered, released 2020-08-13. Aven Mindcensor has printings with frame versions '2015' (Amonkhet, Amonkhet Remastered, Amonkhet Invocations, Amonkhet Promos) and 'future' (Future Sight). I treated the 2015 frame as the newest, because the 'future' frame is the 2007 Future Sight style and is older. Among the 2015 printings, Amonkhet Remastered has the latest release date.

sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(b.spent) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM event), 2) AS avg_spent_per_event FROM budget b;
answer: $49.67 per event. I summed budget.spent across all budget categories (2,086.05 in total) and divided by all 42 recorded events, with no date filter. 19 of those events have no budget line, so they count as $0 spent. If you only count the 23 events that have a budget line, the average is $90.70.

sql: select round(avg(A11),2) from district where district_id in (select district_id from client where gender='F' and birth_date<'1950-01-01')
answer: 9031.68. Reading chosen: each district counts once, even if several qualifying clients live there (female, born before 1950-01-01, A11 = average salary). If every client were weighted instead, the figure would be 9518.51.

sql: select a.buildUpPlayDribblingClass from Team t join Team_Attributes a on a.team_api_id=t.team_api_id where t.team_short_name='POR' and date(a.date)='2015-09-10' and t.team_api_id in (select m.home_team_api_id from Match m join League l on l.id=m.league_id join Country c on c.id=l.country_id where c.name='England')
answer: Little. Two teams share the short name POR: FC Porto (Portugal) and Portsmouth. I picked the English one by checking which team played home matches in an English league. Portsmouth's 2015-09-10 record has buildUpPlayDribblingClass = 'Little'.

sql: select count(*) from superhero a where publisher_id=(select publisher_id from superhero where superhero_name='Blackwulf') and eye_colour_id is not null and exists(select 1 from superhero b where b.publisher_id is not null and b.publisher_id<>a.publisher_id and b.eye_colour_id=a.eye_colour_id)
answer: 382. Blackwulf is published by Marvel Comics. I counted every Marvel hero (not just Blackwulf) whose eye colour is shared by at least one hero from another publisher. Heroes with no publisher were not treated as another publisher. Marvel heroes with no eye colour recorded were excluded.

sql: select l.ID, l.Date, l.DNA from Laboratory l join Patient p on p.ID=l.ID where p.SEX='F' and p.Admission like '+%' and l.DNA!='' and cast(l.DNA as real)=(select max(cast(l2.DNA as real)) from Laboratory l2 join Patient p2 on p2.ID=l2.ID where p2.SEX='F' and p2.Admission like '+%' and l2.DNA!='') order by l.ID
answer: Patient 2933261, lab test date 1988-04-25, anti-DNA level 185. This is the only record with the highest level. Assumptions: the anti-DNA value is the Laboratory.DNA column (stored as text, so I compared it as a number; DNA-II is empty). Inpatients are those with Admission starting with '+', which includes 3 patients recorded as '+('. Excluding those 3 gives the same result.

sql: SELECT s.School, s.MailStreet FROM satscores t JOIN schools s ON t.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE s.DOCType = 'State Board of Education' AND t.rtype = 'S' AND t.AvgScrRead = (SELECT MAX(t2.AvgScrRead) FROM satscores t2 JOIN schools s2 ON t2.cds = s2.CDSCode WHERE s2.DOCType = 'State Board of Education' AND t2.rtype = 'S')
answer: San Francisco Flex Academy, 1350 7th Avenue (the only school with the top average SAT reading score among State Board of Education schools). Assumptions: State Board schools are those with DOCType 'State Board of Education' (DOC 02); only school-level SAT rows (rtype 'S') are used, so no district figures; the full address comes from MailStreet, not the abbreviated MailStrAbr. The School and SAT Score Record terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select count(*) from Player_Attributes p join (select player_api_id pid, max(date) md from Player_Attributes where date<'2015-01-02' group by player_api_id) m on p.player_api_id=m.pid and p.date=m.md where p.preferred_foot='left' and p.attacking_work_rate in ('low','medium')
answer: 1,795 players. I used each player's latest Player_Attributes record dated on or before 1 January 2015, and counted those with preferred_foot = 'left' and attacking_work_rate of 'low' or 'medium'. Records with a blank, NULL or malformed work rate (for example 'None', 'le', 'norm') are not counted. The first, slower version of the query was stopped by the time limit and was not used. The query shown ran in about 0.2 seconds.

sql:
SELECT p.player_name, COUNT(DISTINCT m.id) AS matches_played
FROM Player p
LEFT JOIN Match m ON m.season='2015/2016' AND p.player_api_id IN (
 m.home_player_1,m.home_player_2,m.home_player_3,m.home_player_4,m.home_player_5,m.home_player_6,m.home_player_7,m.home_player_8,m.home_player_9,m.home_player_10,m.home_player_11,
 m.away_player_1,m.away_player_2,m.away_player_3,m.away_player_4,m.away_player_5,m.away_player_6,m.away_player_7,m.away_player_8,m.away_player_9,m.away_player_10,m.away_player_11)
WHERE p.player_name LIKE 'Aaron%' AND p.birthday >= '1991-01-01'
GROUP BY p.player_api_id, p.player_name
ORDER BY p.player_name;
answer: Six players named Aaron were born after 1990 (birthday from 1991-01-01 on). Their 2015/2016 starting line-up appearances: Aaron Appindangoye 0, Aaron Doran 0, Aaron Kuhl 5, Aaron Lennox 1, Aaron Splaine 1, Aaron Taylor-Sinclair 0. I read "for every player" as including players with 0 starts, so they are listed with 0. Drop them by using an inner join if you only want players who played. A match counts once per player if he appears in any of the 22 starting slots (home or away).

sql: SELECT DISTINCT m.first_name, m.last_name, m.phone FROM member m JOIN expense e ON e.link_to_member = m.member_id WHERE e.cost > (SELECT AVG(cost) FROM expense)
answer: Three members had at least one expense above the overall average cost (average taken over all 32 expense rows, approved or not): Sacha Harrison (840-555-4781), Phillip Cullen (905-555-5035) and Elijah Allen (724-555-5721). DISTINCT lists each member once. The Expense and Member Terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select count(distinct u.Id) from users u join badges b on b.UserId=u.Id where b.Name='Yearling' and b.Date<'2014-01-01' and u.Location like '%India%' and u.Location not like '%Indiana%' and u.Location not like '%Indianapolis%';
answer: 6 users located in India earned a Yearling badge before 1 January 2014. I counted each user once, even if they had several Yearling badges. I matched any location containing 'India' and excluded 'Indiana' and 'Indianapolis' (US places). A narrower match on locations ending in 'India' gives the same 6.

sql: select (select avg(ball_control) from Player_Attributes a join Player p using(player_api_id) where p.player_name='Abdou Diallo') - (select avg(ball_control) from Player_Attributes a join Player p using(player_api_id) where p.player_name='Aaron Appindangoye') as diff
answer: Abdou Diallo's mean ball control is 49.4 (10 records) and Aaron Appindangoye's is 48.6 (5 records). The difference is about 0.8. I averaged all attribute records per player, ignoring NULL values.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(case when r.positionOrder<>1 then 1 else 0 end)/count(*),2) as pct_not_wins from results r join drivers d using(driverId) join races ra using(raceId) where d.forename='Lewis' and d.surname='Hamilton' and ra.year>=2010;
answer: 66.2% (94 of 142 race entries from 2010 onward were not wins). I counted each row in `results` as one entry and a win as `positionOrder = 1`. Using `position = 1` gives the same result.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(c.uuid in (select uuid from foreign_data where language='French'))/count(*),2) from cards c where power is null or power='*'
answer: 47.96%. 'No recorded power' means power IS NULL (30,624 cards), and 'variable power' means power = '*' (429 cards). I left out values like '*²' and '1+*', which are variable only in part. A printing counts as having a French translation if foreign_data has a row with language 'French' for its uuid.

sql: SELECT t.team_long_name FROM Match m JOIN Team t ON t.team_api_id=m.away_team_api_id WHERE m.league_id=19694 AND m.season='2009/2010' AND m.away_team_goal>m.home_team_goal GROUP BY t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name HAVING COUNT(*)=(SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM Match WHERE league_id=19694 AND season='2009/2010' AND away_team_goal>home_team_goal GROUP BY away_team_api_id))
answer: Rangers and Celtic are tied with 11 away wins each in the Scotland Premier League 2009/2010. I counted an away win as a match where away_team_goal is greater than home_team_goal.

sql:
with g as (select Id,Reputation from users where lower(Location) like '%germany%'),
p as (select Score, LastEditorUserId from posts where CreaionDate>='2012-01-01' and CreaionDate<'2013-01-01')
select (select sum(Score) from p where LastEditorUserId in (select Id from g)) as germany_editor_score,
(select sum(Score) from p where LastEditorUserId is null or LastEditorUserId not in (select Id from g)) as other_score,
(select count(*) from g where Id in (select LastEditorUserId from p)) as german_editor_count,
(select sum(Reputation) from g where Id in (select LastEditorUserId from p)) as german_editor_reputation
answer: 2012 posts whose last editor is Germany-based have a total score of 349. All other 2012 posts have a total score of 63,191. 32 Germany-based users were last editor of at least one 2012 post, with a combined profile reputation of 26,816. Assumptions: a user is Germany-based if the profile Location contains "Germany" (case-insensitive), which also catches variants like "Aachen Germany" and "Germany - Frankfurt" but not "Germantown, MD". "Other" posts include 2012 posts with no last editor (NULL). The year comes from posts.CreaionDate, the misspelled column name in this database.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT m.major_name) FROM major m WHERE m.college = (SELECT mj.college FROM member b JOIN major mj ON mj.major_id=b.link_to_major WHERE b.first_name='Tyler' AND b.last_name='Hewitt') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM member b WHERE b.link_to_major=m.major_id)
answer: 2 majors. Tyler Hewitt's major belongs to a college, and 2 of the majors that college offers have no club members. I counted distinct major names. I read "enrolled" as any member row linked to the major. Excluding members whose position is 'Inactive' also gives 2. The Major and Member Terms are still draft (not certified).

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS patients_with_lab, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN l."T-BIL" >= 2.0 THEN p.ID END) AS patients_with_elevated_tbil FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NULL OR TRIM(p.SEX) = ''
answer: Of the 13 patients with no sex recorded (empty value in SEX; none are NULL), 3 have at least one laboratory result, and 0 of them have an elevated total bilirubin. I read "elevated" as T-BIL of 2.0 or higher, because the docs give the normal range as N < 2.0. All dates are included.

sql: select s.School, s.Street from frpm f join schools s using(CDSCode) where f.`Low Grade` in ('9','10','11','12') and f.`Enrollment (K-12)` - f.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)` > 30 order by s.CDSCode
answer: 쿼리를 실행해 결과를 확인했습니다. 결과 행은 많고(출력이 약 36KB), 첫 행은 Alameda High(2201 Encinal Avenue)입니다. frpm 테이블의 같은 레코드에서 Low Grade가 9, 10, 11, 12 중 하나이고 Enrollment (K-12)에서 Enrollment (Ages 5-17)를 뺀 값이 30보다 큰 학교를 골랐습니다. 학교명(School)과 도로명 주소(Street)를 CDS 코드 오름차순으로 정렬했습니다. 'K', 'P', 'Adult' 같은 숫자가 아닌 하한 학년은 9학년 이상이 아닌 것으로 보고 제외했습니다.

sql: SELECT s.School, s.Street FROM frpm f JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode=f.CDSCode WHERE s.School IS NOT NULL AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > 30 AND f."High Grade" IN ('K','1','2','3','4','5','6','7','8')
answer:
The query returns school name and street address for each named school with K-12 enrollment more than 30 above ages 5-17 enrollment and a highest grade of K or 1-8. The run was cut off at 100 rows, so I don't have the full row count. It returns one row per school, because frpm and schools join one-to-one on CDSCode.

Readings I chose:
- "Highest grade" is frpm."High Grade", with K and 1 through 8 counted as grade 8 or below. Preschool ('P'), Adult, 9 and above, and Post Secondary are excluded.
- "Named school" means schools.School is not null, which also drops the district-office rows.
- Enrollment is from the 2014-2015 FRPM table.
- The address is schools.Street, the physical street address.
- I did not filter on StatusType, so closed or merged schools are included if they have FRPM rows.
- The Terms the query relies on (School, Free or Reduced Price Meal Record) are still draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT m.first_name, m.last_name FROM member m JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_event) > 7
answer: 29명이 7개를 넘는 행사에 참석했습니다. 이름은 first_name, last_name 두 열로 냈고, 행사 수는 attendance 행 수로 셌습니다. attendance의 기본키가 (행사, 회원) 쌍이라 행 수와 고유 행사 수는 같습니다. 가장 많이 참석한 사람은 16회인 Phillip Cullen과 Elijah Allen입니다.

sql: select m.molecule_id from molecule m where m.label='-' and exists(select 1 from atom a where a.molecule_id=m.molecule_id and a.element in ('na','sn','pb','ca','zn','k','cu','y')) and exists(select 1 from bond b where b.molecule_id=m.molecule_id and b.bond_type='-') order by m.molecule_id limit 3
answer: TR011, TR101, TR139. I read "metal" as any atom whose element is na, sn, pb, ca, zn, k, cu or y. I excluded te (tellurium), which counts as a metalloid and doesn't appear in the data anyway. "Single bonds" means the molecule has at least one bond of type '-'. "Non-carcinogenic" means label '-'. "First three" means the first three molecule_ids in ascending text order.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN currency='EUR' THEN total END),2) AS eur_avg, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN currency='CZK' THEN total END),2) AS czk_avg FROM (SELECT c.CustomerID, c.Currency AS currency, SUM(y.Consumption) AS total FROM yearmonth y JOIN customers c ON y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID WHERE y.Date IN ('201304','201305','201306') AND y.Consumption IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.Currency)
answer: 2013년 2분기 평균 소비량은 EUR 고객 3,627.03, CZK 고객 44,462.45입니다. 고객별로 4~6월 소비량을 먼저 합산한 뒤 통화별로 평균했습니다. 두 값은 각 통화 그대로의 금액이며 환산하지 않았습니다. 사용한 용어 'Customer'와 'Monthly Customer Consumption'은 아직 인증되지 않은 초안 상태입니다.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(case when t.k_symbol='SIPO' then t.amount end)/sum(t.amount),2) as sipo_pct from trans t join account a on a.account_id=t.account_id where a.district_id=18 and t.type in ('VYDAJ','VYBER') and trim(coalesce(t.k_symbol,''))<>''
answer: 93.31% of the amount of outgoing payments with a stated purpose went to SIPO household bill payments. I counted accounts held in the Pisek district (district_id 18), all dates, and outgoing transactions with type VYDAJ or VYBER. "States a purpose" means k_symbol is neither NULL nor blank. The result is the same at 93.31% if only VYDAJ is counted.

sql: SELECT m.first_name, m.last_name FROM member m INNER JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.first_name, m.last_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_event) > 7
answer: 29 members attended more than 7 events (counted as distinct events per member). All club members are treated as students. Name is returned as first_name and last_name columns. Examples: Grant Gilmour, Luisa Guidi, Connor Hilton, Sacha Harrison, Carlo Jacobs, and 24 others. The Member term is still a draft (not certified).

sql: SELECT Age FROM users WHERE Location IN ('York, United Kingdom','York') AND Reputation = (SELECT MAX(Reputation) FROM users WHERE Location IN ('York, United Kingdom','York'))
answer: The highest-reputation user in York, England is 24 years old. Only one user has the top reputation, so there is no tie. I counted locations "York, United Kingdom" and "York" and excluded North Yorkshire, Yorkshire, York, PA and the New York variants. The `User` term the query relies on is still a draft.

sql: select count(*) from Patient p where Diagnosis='MCTD' and exists(select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and PLT>100 and PLT<400) and exists(select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and RNP glob '[0-9]*' and CAST(RNP as REAL)>5)
answer: 1명입니다. 기준은 세 가지로 잡았습니다. MCTD 단독 진단은 Patient.Diagnosis가 정확히 'MCTD'인 경우로 봤습니다. 혈소판 정상 범위는 문서에 적힌 100 < PLT < 400(경계값 제외)을 적용했습니다. RNP는 텍스트 컬럼이라 숫자로 된 값만 골라 5보다 큰지 비교했고, 'negative'와 빈 값은 제외했습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.account_id) FROM account a JOIN loan l ON l.account_id = a.account_id WHERE a.district_id = 1 AND a.date <= '1995-12-31' AND l.status IN ('C','D')

select count(distinct artist) from cards where borderColor='black' and ','||availability||',' like '%,arena,%' and ','||availability||',' not like '%,mtgo,%' and power glob '[0-9]*' and power not glob '*[^0-9]*' and cast(power as integer)>=5 and artist is not null
answer: 56 artists. I counted each printing (card row) on its own, and only rows whose power is purely digits (so `*`, `∞` and `?` are excluded). Rows with no artist were left out.

sql: select distinct t.team_long_name from Team_Attributes a join Team t on t.team_api_id=a.team_api_id where a.date like '2012%' and a.buildUpPlayPassing > (select avg(buildUpPlayPassing) from Team_Attributes where date like '2012%')
answer: 128개 팀이 해당합니다. 기준은 2012년에 기록된 팀 속성 행의 buildUpPlayPassing 평균(약 49.33)이고, 이보다 높은 값이 있는 팀을 중복 없이 뽑았습니다. 전체 기간 평균이 아니라 2012년 평균을 기준으로 읽었습니다.

sql: select avg(HCT) from Laboratory where Date like '1991%' and "U-PRO" in ('300','>=300','>=1000') and HCT is not null
answer: 평균 헤마토크릿은 41.6입니다. 1991년 검사 중 U-PRO가 '300', '>=300', '>=1000'이고 HCT 값이 있는 5건의 평균입니다. '>=' 표기는 하한값이라 기준을 충족하는 것으로 계산했습니다. U-PRO의 '1'~'4'는 mg/dL 값인지 등급 코드인지 알 수 없어 제외했습니다. '+2(100)'처럼 100 mg/dL 수준인 값과 '%%' 같은 이상값도 제외했습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid=c.uuid WHERE c.artist='Erica Yang' AND l.format='pauper' AND l.status='Legal' AND (','||c.availability||',') LIKE '%,paper,%'
answer: 23 printings. I counted each row in cards (one row per printing) with artist 'Erica Yang', a legalities status of 'Legal' in pauper, and 'paper' in availability. Banned cards are excluded, and I treated 'legal' as status = 'Legal' only.

sql: select round((select max(t) from (select sum(Consumption) t from yearmonth where Date like '2013%' group by Date)) - (select max(t) from (select sum(Consumption) t from yearmonth where Date like '2012%' group by Date)))
answer: The 2013 peak is 390,532,826.93 (October 2013) and the 2012 peak is 51,787,161.74 (March 2012). The difference is 338,745,665 consumption units. I summed Consumption over all customers per month and took each year's highest month. Note that the data has no Oct–Dec 2012 months, and 2012 has only partial data (September 2012 and earlier), so the 2012 peak may understate a full year.

sql: WITH m AS (SELECT '2010-'||printf('%02d',value) AS ym FROM generate_series(1,12)), c AS (SELECT substr(l.CreationDate,1,7) ym, COUNT(DISTINCT l.RelatedPostId) n FROM postLinks l JOIN posts p ON p.Id=l.RelatedPostId WHERE p.AnswerCount<=2 AND l.CreationDate LIKE '2010-%' GROUP BY 1) SELECT ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(c.n,0)),2) FROM m LEFT JOIN c USING(ym);
answer: The average is 5.33 posts per month in 2010. I read "received a link" as the post being the link target (postLinks.RelatedPostId). Each post counts once per month, and posts with AnswerCount <= 2 qualify. Months with no such posts count as 0, and the average is taken over all 12 months.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE isPromo = 1 AND side IS NOT NULL AND originalReleaseDate LIKE '2019/%'
answer:
The query returns 31 distinct card names. All of them are adventure cards, such as "Decorated Knight // Present Arms".

I read the conditions as follows:
- **Promotional:** `isPromo = 1`.
- **Multiple faces:** `side IS NOT NULL`. Among the 2019 promos, only adventure cards have a side value. No split or transform cards turned up with a 2019 date.
- **Originally released in 2019:** the card's own `originalReleaseDate`, not the set's date. That column is stored as text like '2019/12/1' without zero-padding, so I matched it with `LIKE '2019/%'`.

`DISTINCT` lists a card once even if it has several promo printings.

sql: SELECT p.player_name FROM Player p WHERE p.height IN ((SELECT MAX(height) FROM Player),(SELECT MIN(height) FROM Player)) ORDER BY (SELECT AVG(a.finishing) FROM Player_Attributes a WHERE a.player_api_id=p.player_api_id) DESC LIMIT 1
answer: Juan Quero (shortest, 157 cm) has the higher average finishing, 60.9, against 15.5 for Kristof van Hout (tallest, 208 cm). Both extremes were unique players, so no tie-breaking was needed.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) FROM cards WHERE ','||promoTypes||',' LIKE '%,release,%'
answer: 54 different cards (by distinct name) have a release promotion printing. I matched 'release' as a whole entry in the comma-separated promoTypes list, so 'prerelease' is excluded. There are 58 release-promo printings in total, and some cards were printed more than once. If you meant individual printings, the number is 58.

sql: select count(distinct p.ID) from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where l.Date between '1981-01-01' and '1986-12-31' and l.PLT between 100 and 400 and p.Birthday is not null and (cast(strftime('%Y',l.Date) as int)-cast(strftime('%Y',p.Birthday) as int)-(strftime('%m-%d',l.Date)<strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)))<50 and l."U-PRO" in ('1','2','3','4','30','100','300','+1(30)','+2(100)','>=300','>=1000');
answer: 45 patients. Proteinuria reading: the U-PRO column's normal range is 0<N<30, so I counted 1, 2, 3 and 4 as positive. In the 1981–1986 data these are the grades for 30, 100, 300 and 1000 mg/dl, and I also included the higher text codes (+1(30), >=300 and similar). I excluded 0, '-', 'TR' (trace), '%%' and blank. The first query used only 30/100/300-style codes and returned 0, because the 1981–1986 data uses the 1–4 grades. Age is completed years on the test date, computed from Birthday. A patient counts once if any one test meets all the conditions.

sql:
SELECT p.player_api_id
FROM Player p JOIN Player_Attributes a ON a.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
WHERE p.height > 180 AND a.heading_accuracy IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY p.player_api_id
ORDER BY AVG(a.heading_accuracy) DESC, p.player_api_id ASC
LIMIT 10
answer:
The ten players taller than 180 cm with the highest mean heading accuracy, highest first, are these player API IDs: 30699 (mean 91.80), 33030 (91.52), 30627 (91.33), 28480 (90.39), 30709 (90.26), 35606 (90.26), 30822 (90.24), 30638 (90.18), 33085 (90.18) and 34231 (89.80).

I read "mean recorded heading accuracy" as the average of `heading_accuracy` over all of a player's rating snapshots in `Player_Attributes`, ignoring nulls. "Taller than 180 cm" is `Player.height > 180`. Ties are broken by lower `player_api_id`, which settles 30709 before 35606 and 30638 before 33085. The query returns only `player_api_id`, because the question asks for players and not for the means. I ran the version that also returns the mean to check the ordering. The `Player` and `Player Attributes` ontology terms are still draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments c JOIN posts p ON p.Id=c.PostId WHERE c.Score=0 AND c.PostId IN (SELECT PostId FROM comments GROUP BY PostId HAVING COUNT(*)=1)
answer: 10,999개입니다. `posts`에 존재하는 게시글 중 댓글 기록이 정확히 1건인 게시글에 달린 댓글을 대상으로, `Score`가 0인 댓글을 셌습니다.

sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, c.name FROM qualifying q JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId JOIN constructors c ON c.constructorId=q.constructorId LEFT JOIN results r ON r.raceId=q.raceId AND r.driverId=q.driverId WHERE ra.year=2017 AND ra.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2<>'' ORDER BY q.q2, CASE WHEN r.grid=0 THEN 99 ELSE r.grid END LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1
answer: Valtteri Bottas, driving for Mercedes. His Q2 time was 1:35.396, behind Lewis Hamilton's 1:34.660. I counted only drivers who have a Q2 time, since drivers eliminated in Q1 have none. Ties would be broken by starting grid position from the race results (grid 0, a pit-lane start, ranked last). No tie came up here. Q2 times are text in m:ss.mmm format, so they sort correctly as strings. The ontology Terms used are all still drafts, not certified.

sql:
SELECT d.A2 AS branch_name, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count
FROM "trans" t
JOIN "account" a ON t.account_id = a.account_id
JOIN "district" d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
WHERE d.A3 = 'north Moravia'
  AND t.date <= '1998-10-14'
  AND (t.k_symbol IS NULL OR TRIM(t.k_symbol) = '')
GROUP BY d.district_id, d.A2
ORDER BY transaction_count DESC, d.A2 ASC
LIMIT 3
answer:
north Moravia에서 14 October 1998 이전(해당 날짜 포함)에 거래 특성(k_symbol)이 기록되지 않은 거래가 가장 많은 지점은 다음 세 곳입니다.
1. Karvina: 16,820건
2. Ostrava - mesto: 16,748건
3. Olomouc: 9,928건

적용한 해석은 세 가지입니다. 첫째, 지점은 계좌가 속한 district(A2)이고, 지역은 district.A3 = 'north Moravia'로 골랐습니다. 둘째, '특성 없음'은 k_symbol이 NULL이거나 공백(' ')인 경우로 보았습니다. 문서에 공백도 해당 없음으로 적혀 있습니다. 셋째, 해당 지점 계좌의 모든 거래를 셌습니다. 동률은 지점명 알파벳순으로 정렬하도록 했지만, 실제 결과에는 동률이 없었습니다. 쿼리에 쓴 Transaction, Account, District Term은 아직 draft 상태(인증 전)입니다.

sql:
WITH ab AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.ID FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE p.Admission='-' AND l.SSA IS NOT NULL AND l.SSA NOT IN ('0','negative','-','+-')),
r AS (SELECT l.ID, l.RNP, CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) v FROM Laboratory l JOIN ab ON ab.ID=l.ID WHERE l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND l.RNP NOT IN ('negative','-','+-'))
SELECT DISTINCT ID, RNP FROM r WHERE v=(SELECT MAX(v) FROM r)
answer: Patient 4915498 has the highest anti-RNP titer, 256, and no other patient ties. Readings I chose: outpatient means Admission = '-'. Abnormal anti-SSA means any value other than '0', 'negative', '-' or '+-' (the docs list '-' and '+-' as normal), in any lab row across all years. The highest titer was compared numerically across all of the patient's lab rows. The Patient and Laboratory Terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select round(avg(s.weight_kg),1) as avg_weight_kg, count(*) as hero_count from superhero s join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id where p.publisher_name='DC Comics' and s.weight_kg>0
answer: DC Comics superheroes average 101.9 kg, based on 156 heroes. I treated weight_kg of 0 as unknown, as well as NULL, since 172 heroes in the table have a weight of 0. Including those zeros would lower the average.

sql:
WITH pm AS (
SELECT country_id, home_player_1 p FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_2 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_3 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_4 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_5 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_6 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_7 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_8 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_9 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_10 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_11 FROM Match
UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_1 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_2 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_3 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_4 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_5 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_6 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_7 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_8 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_9 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_10 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_11 FROM Match),
c AS (SELECT co.name, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN pl.weight<=160 THEN pl.player_api_id END) n
FROM Country co LEFT JOIN pm ON pm.country_id=co.id LEFT JOIN Player pl ON pl.player_api_id=pm.p GROUP BY co.id)
SELECT name FROM c WHERE n=(SELECT MIN(n) FROM c);
answer: Poland. I counted distinct players per country, across all seasons, who appeared in the starting lineup (home or away slots 1–11) of that country's matches and weigh 160 lb or less. I included countries with zero such players. Poland had the fewest, and no other country tied with it.

sql: SELECT s.AvgScrMath, s.NumTstTakr FROM satscores AS s INNER JOIN schools AS c ON s.cds = c.CDSCode WHERE c.CDSCode = '01611190130609' AND c.FundingType = 'Directly funded'
answer: The school (CDS 01611190130609, stored with a leading zero) is directly funded. Its average SAT math score is 593 and 20 students took the SAT. If the school were not directly funded, the query would return no row. Both ontology terms used (SAT Score Record, School) are draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg),1) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero s INNER JOIN colour c ON s.skin_colour_id = c.id WHERE c.colour = 'Green' AND s.weight_kg IS NOT NULL AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer:
The average weight of green-skinned heroes is 1354.6 kg. It covers 15 heroes with a known weight, out of 21 with green skin.

Choices I made:
- **Green skin:** I matched skin colour exactly to 'Green'. 'Green/Blue' is a separate colour and is excluded.
- **Known weight:** I treated a weight of 0 as missing, as the column description says, along with NULL. That excludes 6 heroes, including the Ninja Turtles and Swamp Thing.

Fin Fang Foom weighs 18,000 kg and pulls the average far above a typical weight. Without him the average of the other 14 is about 135 kg (my own calculation, not a query result). If you want a typical value for the class, consider using the median or leaving him out.

The Colour and Superhero terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: with t as (select c.Currency cur, y.CustomerID, sum(y.Consumption) s from yearmonth y join customers c using(CustomerID) where y.Date like '2012%' group by 1,2) select round(avg(case when cur='CZK' then s end) - avg(case when cur='EUR' then s end)) as diff from t;
answer: 14308. I summed each customer's monthly consumption over 2012 (dates starting '2012'), averaged those yearly totals per currency, and subtracted the EUR average from the CZK average. Only customers with 2012 consumption records are included. I chose per-customer yearly totals rather than the average of individual monthly rows.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(c.gender='M')/count(*),2) from client c where c.district_id=(select district_id from district where A3='south Bohemia' order by cast(A4 as integer) desc limit 1)
answer: 40.00% of clients are male in Ceske Budejovice, the most populous south Bohemia district. I read "resident clients" as clients whose client.district_id is that district, and I cast the text column A4 to an integer to find the largest population.

sql:

 FROM Player_Attributes WHERE date <= '2010-12-31 23:59:59'),
sl AS (SELECT player_api_id FROM latest WHERE rn=1 AND overall_rating>80),
ap AS (
 SELECT p, COUNT(*) c FROM (
 SELECT home_player_1 p FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_2 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_3 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_4 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_5 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_6 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_7 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_8 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_9 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_10 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT home_player_11 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011'
 UNION ALL SELECT away_player_1 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_2 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_3 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_4 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_5 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_6 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_7 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_8 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_9 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_10 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT away_player_11 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011') GROUP BY p)

answer: 22.47 matches on average. (3) Shortlisted players with no starts that season count as 0 in the average.

sql:

2012년에 작성된 게시물 중 마지막 수정자가 독일 사용자인 게시물의 점수 합계는 349입니다. 그 밖의 2012년 게시물은 63,191입니다. 독일 사용자 32명이 2012년 게시물 하나 이상을 마지막으로 수정했고, 이들의 프로필 평판 합계는 26,816입니다.
