sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) FROM Patient WHERE LOWER(Diagnosis) LIKE '%psoriatic arthritis%'
answer: 2 patients. I counted every row in Patient whose Diagnosis contains "psoriatic arthritis", with no filter on time or follow-up status. The two matching rows differ only in capitalization ("Psoriatic arthritis" and "Psoriatic Arthritis"). The Patient term is still a draft in the ontology, so it has not been certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN r.position=1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS pct_not_wins FROM results r JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId=r.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=r.driverId WHERE d.forename='Lewis' AND d.surname='Hamilton' AND ra.year>=2010;
answer: 66.2% of Lewis Hamilton's race entries from 2010 onward were not wins. I counted a win as position = 1 in the results table, so retirements and other non-finishes count as non-wins.

sql:
WITH v AS (SELECT CDSCode, County, School FROM schools WHERE Virtual='F'),
cc AS (SELECT County, COUNT(*) n FROM v GROUP BY County),
top AS (SELECT County, n FROM cc WHERE n >= (SELECT n FROM cc ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 4)),
sc AS (SELECT v.County, v.School, s.AvgScrRead r FROM v JOIN satscores s ON s.cds=v.CDSCode WHERE s.AvgScrRead IS NOT NULL),
best AS (SELECT County, School FROM sc WHERE r=(SELECT MAX(r) FROM sc s2 WHERE s2.County=sc.County))
SELECT top.County, top.n AS exclusively_virtual_schools, COALESCE(best.School,'None') AS school_name
FROM top LEFT JOIN best ON best.County=top.County
ORDER BY top.n DESC, top.County, school_name;
answer: The five counties are Los Angeles (12 exclusively virtual schools), San Joaquin (10), San Diego (8), Sacramento (5) and San Bernardino (5). Sacramento and San Bernardino tie for fifth, so both are included. The school with the highest average SAT reading score is California Virtual Academy @ Los Angeles in Los Angeles County and California Connections Academy @ Ripon in San Joaquin County. San Diego, Sacramento and San Bernardino show 'None' because none of their exclusively virtual schools has a reported reading average. I took "exclusively virtual" to mean Virtual = 'F' and counted every such school regardless of whether it is open or closed. Reading averages come from the satscores table.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient p WHERE p.Birthday > '1980-01-01' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND (l.FG < 150 OR l.FG > 450 OR l."U-PRO" IN ('3','4','300','>=300','>=1000')));
answer: 4 patients. Assumptions: "born after 1980-01-01" means Birthday strictly later than that date. A fibrinogen (FG) result is abnormal if it is below 150 or above 450. U-PRO mixes two scales in the data: grades 1-4 and mg/dl values. I counted severe proteinuria as grade 3 or 4, or 300 mg/dl or more ('3', '4', '300', '>=300', '>=1000'). I did not count '+2(100)', '2', '100', '30', 'TR' and '-'. Patients with a NULL FG or U-PRO are not counted on that test.

sql: WITH h AS (SELECT DISTINCT p.ID, p.SEX FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID WHERE (p.SEX='M' AND l.UA>8.0) OR (p.SEX='F' AND l.UA>6.5)) SELECT CAST(SUM(SEX='M') AS REAL)/SUM(SEX='F') AS male_to_female_ratio FROM h
answer: The male-to-female ratio is 0.22. Uric acid (UA) counts as above the limit when it is over 8.0 for males and over 6.5 for females (limits from docs/Laboratory.csv). Each patient is counted once, and patients with an empty SEX value are excluded. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: with b as (select d.forename||' '||d.surname n, r.name rn, r.year y, q.q3 t from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) join races r using(raceId) where d.nationality='British' and cast(substr(d.dob,1,4) as int)>1980 and q.q3 like '%:%') select n as driver, rn as race, y as year, t as q3 from b where t=(select min(t) from b);
answer: Lewis Hamilton, Austrian Grand Prix, 2017, Q3 time 1:04.424. I took "British" to mean nationality = 'British' and ignored blank Q3 values. All times use the m:ss.mmm format, so comparing them as text gives the correct order. No other result tied for the fastest time.

sql: select l.`T-BIL`, l.Date, p.ID, p.SEX, p.Birthday from Laboratory l join Patient p on p.ID=l.ID where CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)=(select max(CAST(RNP AS REAL)) from Laboratory) and l.`T-BIL`=(select max(`T-BIL`) from Laboratory where CAST(RNP AS REAL)=(select max(CAST(RNP AS REAL)) from Laboratory))
answer: RNP is stored as text, so I compared it numerically (cast to a number). The highest value is 256, found in 6 tests. Among those, the highest total bilirubin is 0.4, and only one test has it: date 1989-07-18, patient ID 1650222, sex F, birthday 1947-03-17.

sql: select round(avg(weight_kg),1) as avg_weight_kg, count(*) as hero_count from superhero s join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id where p.publisher_name='DC Comics' and s.weight_kg>0
answer: DC Comics superheroes weigh 101.9 kg on average, based on 156 superheroes. The docs say a weight of 0 or NULL means the weight is missing, so I left those out. Of 224 DC heroes, 68 had no known weight.

sql:
SELECT s.name, s.keyruneCode, COUNT(DISTINCT t.language) AS language_count
FROM sets s
LEFT JOIN set_translations t ON t.setCode = s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND t.translation <> ''
WHERE s.releaseDate LIKE '2020-%'
GROUP BY s.code, s.name, s.keyruneCode
ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.name;
answer: The query returns 34 sets released in 2020. Each row has the set name, keyrune code and the number of distinct languages with a non-empty translated name. I counted every set whose release date falls in 2020, including promo, Commander and other sub-sets. I kept sets with no translations and show them as 0. Only 4 sets have any translation, and each has 1: Theros Beyond Death, Ikoria: Lair of Behemoths, Core Set 2021 and (per the output) no others. The rest show 0.

sql:
WITH p AS (SELECT DISTINCT l.ID FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient pt ON pt.ID=l.ID WHERE pt.Admission='-' AND l.SSA IS NOT NULL AND l.SSA NOT IN ('0','negative')),
r AS (SELECT l.ID, l.RNP, CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) v FROM Laboratory l JOIN p ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND l.RNP<>'negative')
SELECT ID, RNP FROM r WHERE v=(SELECT MAX(v) FROM r) GROUP BY ID, RNP
answer: Patient ID 4915498 has the highest anti-RNP titer, 256, among outpatients (Admission = '-') with any abnormal anti-SSA result. There are no ties. Abnormal anti-SSA was read as any non-null value other than '0' or 'negative', which includes titers such as 1, 4, 16, 64 and 256. The anti-RNP titer is the highest numeric value across all of the patient's lab records. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still draft (not certified).

sql: SELECT b.bond_id, b.molecule_id FROM bond b JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id=b.molecule_id WHERE m.label='+' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM atom a WHERE a.molecule_id=b.molecule_id AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM atom a2 WHERE a2.element=a.element AND a2.molecule_id<>a.molecule_id))
answer: I read the question as: return every bond of a '+' molecule that has at least one element no other molecule in the dataset records. The query returns the bonds of molecules TR238 and TR430. I don't know the total row count: the run showed only the first 100 rows (all from those two molecules) and was truncated, so other molecules may also qualify. The Atom, Bond and Molecule Terms are still drafts, not certified.

answer: Finnish. The fastest Q3 time across all races is 1:04.251, and one driver set it. I excluded NULL and empty-string Q3 values and compared the times as text, which works because they all use the m:ss.mmm format.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rulings r JOIN cards c ON c.uuid=r.uuid WHERE c.name='Mishra''s Factory' AND r.date=(SELECT MAX(r2.date) FROM rulings r2 JOIN cards c2 ON c2.uuid=r2.uuid WHERE c2.name='Mishra''s Factory')

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ID) AS patient_count FROM Examination WHERE Thrombosis > 0 AND "Examination Date" BETWEEN '1997-01-01' AND '1997-12-31'

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT power_id) FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id IN (SELECT id FROM superhero WHERE height_cm >= (SELECT height_cm FROM superhero WHERE height_cm > 0 ORDER BY height_cm DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 9))

sql: select 100.0*sum(d.dob<'1985-01-01' and r.laps>50)/count(*) as percentage from results r join races a on a.raceId=r.raceId join drivers d on d.driverId=r.driverId where a.year between 2000 and 2005
answer: About 64.88% of race results from 2000 through 2005 were by drivers born before 1985 who completed more than 50 laps. I used all results in those years as the denominator, and counted a result only if the driver's dob is before 1985-01-01 and laps is greater than 50.

sql: SELECT d.nationality FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2<>'' AND q.q2 = (SELECT DISTINCT q2.q2 FROM qualifying q2 JOIN races r2 ON r2.raceId=q2.raceId WHERE r2.year=2017 AND r2.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q2.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q2.q2<>'' ORDER BY q2.q2 LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1)

sql: SELECT SUM(Reputation) AS total_reputation FROM users u WHERE Location LIKE '%United Kingdom%' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM posts p WHERE p.OwnerUserId = u.Id)

sql:

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(t.total,0)),2) AS avg_spent_per_event FROM event e LEFT JOIN (SELECT link_to_event, SUM(spent) AS total FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event) t ON t.link_to_event = e.event_id
answer: The average total spent per event is $49.67. I summed budget.spent across all categories for each event, with no date filter, and averaged over all 42 events. sql:

JOIN hero_attribute ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id

AND s.weight_kg IS NOT NULL AND s.weight_kg > 0

answer: 13명이 조건에 해당합니다. 예: 57266(M, 103세), 2371753(F, 93세). 해석: 한 검사 기록에서 GLU>=180과 T-CHO<250을 동시에 만족해야 합니다. 나이는 2026-10-09 기준 생일이 지난 만큼만 센 만 나이입니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN s.Virtual IN ('F','P') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct FROM satscores t INNER JOIN schools s ON t.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE t.rtype = 'S' AND t.AvgScrMath > 400

sql: select round(100.0*sum(case when coalesce(u.Reputation,0)<1000 then 1 else 0 end)/count(*),2) as pct from posts p left join users u on u.Id=p.OwnerUserId where strftime('%Y',p.CreaionDate)='2010' and p.Score>5

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID JOIN Examination e ON e.ID=p.ID WHERE CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 0 AND e.Thrombosis = 0

sql: select r.year, d.forename, d.surname, res.time from races r join results res on res.raceId=r.raceId and res.position=1 join drivers d on d.driverId=res.driverId where r.name='Canadian Grand Prix' and r.year between 2007 and 2017 and r.time<='17:00:00' order by r.year;

sql: select s.School, s.Phone from schools s join satscores t on t.cds=s.CDSCode where s.DOC='03' and t.rtype='S' and t.NumGE1500=(select max(t2.NumGE1500) from schools s2 join satscores t2 on t2.cds=s2.CDSCode where s2.DOC='03' and t2.rtype='S')

sql: select count(*) from laboratory l where date=(select min(date) from laboratory where id=l.id) and got<60 and rnp glob '[0-9]*' and cast(rnp as real)>10

sql:

sql: select sum(case when substr(e.event_date,1,4)='2019' then b.spent end) - sum(case when substr(e.event_date,1,4)='2020' then b.spent end) as difference from budget b join event e on b.link_to_event=e.event_id

sql:
WITH a AS (
  SELECT account_id, date AS opened FROM account
  WHERE district_id = (SELECT district_id FROM district WHERE A2='Tabor') AND date <= '1996-12-31'
),
t AS (
  SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) n,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN type='PRIJEM' THEN amount END),0) money_in,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN type IN ('VYDAJ','VYBER') THEN amount END),0) money_out,
    MAX(balance) peak
  FROM trans WHERE date >= '1997-01-01' AND date <= '1997-12-31' GROUP BY account_id
),
p AS (
  SELECT a.account_id, a.opened, c.gender,
    CAST(strftime('%Y','1996-12-31') AS INT) - CAST(strftime('%Y',c.birth_date) AS INT)
      - (strftime('%m-%d',c.birth_date) > '12-31') AS age,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM card cd JOIN disp d2 ON d2.disp_id=cd.disp_id
       WHERE d2.account_id=a.account_id AND cd.issued <= '1996-12-31') cards,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=a.account_id AND l.date <= '1996-12-31') loans,
    (SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*)=0 THEN 'no loan'
        WHEN SUM(status='B')>0 THEN 'defaulted'
        WHEN SUM(status IN ('C','D'))>0 THEN 'repaying' ELSE 'paid off' END
       FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=a.account_id AND l.date <= '1996-12-31') standing,
    COALESCE(t.n,0) n, COALESCE(t.money_in,0) money_in, COALESCE(t.money_out,0) money_out,
    COALESCE(t.peak,0) peak
  FROM a
  LEFT JOIN disp d ON d.account_id=a.account_id AND d.type='OWNER'
  LEFT JOIN client c ON c.client_id=d.client_id
  LEFT JOIN t ON t.account_id=a.account_id
)
SELECT account_id, opened AS date_opened, gender, age, cards AS cards_issued, loans AS loans_approved,
  standing AS loan_standing, n AS transactions_1997, money_in AS money_in_1997,
  money_out AS money_out_1997, peak AS peak_balance_1997,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY peak DESC) AS peak_balance_rank
FROM p ORDER BY peak_balance_rank, account_id;
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 Tabor 지점(district.A2='Tabor', district_id 21) 계좌 36개를 한 행씩 얻었습니다. 1997년 최고 잔액이 가장 높은 계좌는 7606번(132,635)입니다.

가정한 내용은 다음과 같습니다.
- 1996-12-31 이전(당일 포함)에 개설된 계좌만 대상으로 했습니다.
- 성별과 나이는 'OWNER' 소유자 기준입니다. 나이는 1996-12-31 시점의 만 나이이고, 소유자 생일이 모두 12월 31일 이전이어서 연도 차이와 같습니다.
- 카드는 그 계좌에 연결된 모든 disp(소유자와 추가 사용자 포함)로 발급된 것을 셌고, 대출은 1996-12-31까지 승인된 것만 셌습니다.
- 대출 상태 라벨은 'no loan', 'defaulted'(B 포함), 'repaying'(C 또는 D 포함), 'paid off' 순서로 판정했습니다.
- 입금은 type이 PRIJEM인 금액의 합계이고, 출금은 type이 VYDAJ 또는 VYBER인 금액의 합계입니다. 둘 다 1997년 거래만 포함합니다.
- 1997년 거래가 없는 계좌는 거래 건수, 입금, 출금, 최고 잔액을 0으로 표시했습니다.
- 순위는 RANK()로 매겨 동점이면 같은 순위를 주고 다음 순위를 건너뜁니다. 같은 순위 안에서는 계좌 번호 오름차순으로 정렬했습니다.

sql: SELECT m.first_name, m.last_name, m.phone FROM member m WHERE m.member_id IN (SELECT link_to_member FROM expense WHERE cost > (SELECT AVG(cost) FROM expense))
answer: 3명의 멤버가 전체 평균 비용을 넘는 지출이 한 건 이상 있었습니다. Sacha Harrison (840-555-4781), Phillip Cullen (905-555-5035), Elijah Allen (724-555-5721). 평균은 expense 테이블 전체 행의 cost 평균으로 계산했고, 여러 건이 조건을 넘어도 멤버는 한 번만 나옵니다.

sql: SELECT d.nationality FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2<>'' AND q.q2=(SELECT MIN(q2.q2) FROM qualifying q2 JOIN races r2 ON r2.raceId=q2.raceId WHERE r2.year=2017 AND r2.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q2.q2<>'')
answer: British (Lewis Hamilton, 1:34.660; no tie). Lap times are 'm:ss.mmm' strings, so MIN on the text gives the fastest.

sql: SELECT e.location, COUNT(DISTINCT x.expense_description) FROM event e JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id JOIN expense x ON x.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE e.event_id IN (SELECT link_to_event FROM budget WHERE amount > 40) GROUP BY e.location;
answer: MU 215: 10 different items; Campus Common: 1. I treated "events with a budget line over $40" as events having at least one such line, and counted distinct expense descriptions across all expenses on those events' budget lines. If only expenses on the >$40 lines themselves were counted, MU 215 would be 7 (Campus Common stays 1).

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(A11), 2) FROM district WHERE district_id IN (SELECT a.district_id FROM client c JOIN disp d ON d.client_id = c.client_id JOIN account a ON a.account_id = d.account_id WHERE c.gender = 'F' AND c.birth_date < '1930-01-01')
answer: The average salary (district.A11) across the districts of the branches holding these clients' accounts is 9045.64. I counted each district once, which gives 75 distinct districts, instead of weighting by the number of clients or accounts in it. Clients were linked to accounts through disp, and accounts to branch districts through account.district_id. This is my reading of "the districts those branches are located in".

sql: SELECT E.Symptoms FROM Examination E JOIN Patient P ON E.ID = P.ID WHERE E.Thrombosis > 0 AND E.Symptoms IS NOT NULL AND instr(',' || replace(P.Diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',', ',SLE,') > 0 GROUP BY E.Symptoms ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, E.Symptoms ASC LIMIT 1
answer: CNS lupus (2건, 나머지 증상은 각 1건). 기준: Patient.Diagnosis에 SLE 항목이 있는 환자, Examination.Thrombosis > 0인 기록 중 Symptoms가 있는 행, 날짜 제한 없음, 동률이면 알파벳 순.

sql: select p.SEX, count(distinct p.ID) from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where p.SEX in ('F','M') group by p.SEX order by p.SEX
answer: Patients with at least one laboratory record: F = 252, M = 47. I counted each patient once, however many lab records they have. Patients with a blank sex value are left out, since the question only asks about female and male.

sql: select count(*) from superhero s left join alignment a on a.id=s.alignment_id where a.alignment is null or a.alignment not in ('Good','Bad');
answer: 34 superheroes. This is 28 with the 'Neutral' alignment plus 6 with no alignment recorded (NULL alignment_id). The 'N/A' alignment is unused. I included the 6 unrecorded heroes because you asked for all superheroes and they are neither Good nor Bad. If you count only 'Neutral', the answer is 28.

sql:
SELECT AVG(s.height_cm) AS avg_height_cm
FROM superhero s
JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics'
  AND s.height_cm IS NOT NULL AND s.height_cm > 0
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp
    WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id
      AND hp.power_id NOT IN (
        SELECT hp2.power_id FROM hero_power hp2
        JOIN superhero s2 ON hp2.hero_id = s2.id
        JOIN publisher p2 ON s2.publisher_id = p2.id
        WHERE p2.publisher_name = 'DC Comics'))
answer: The average height is about 202.62 cm. It covers Marvel Comics characters with a measured height who have at least one power that no DC Comics character has. I treated a height of NULL or 0 as not measured and left those characters out. I did not remove the extreme heights (the maximum in the data is 30480 cm), so any outliers are still in the average. The Superhero and Publisher terms the query relies on are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(SEX='F')/count(*),2) from Patient p where (strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',Birthday)-(strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09')<strftime('%m-%d',Birthday)))>55 and exists(select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and l.PT>=14)
answer: 72.73% (8 of 11 patients). I read "abnormal PT" as PT >= 14, since the docs give the normal range as N < 14. Age is the full years completed on 2026-10-09.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE isPromo=1 AND side IS NOT NULL AND frameVersion=(SELECT MAX(frameVersion) FROM cards WHERE frameVersion GLOB '[0-9]*')
answer: 127개의 카드 이름이 나옵니다. 여러 면이 있는 카드는 side 값이 있는 카드로 보았습니다. 최신 프레임 버전은 전체 카드에서 숫자 연도 중 가장 늦은 2015로 정했습니다. 'future'는 연도가 아니라서 제외했습니다.

sql:
SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, l.Date, l."U-PRO" AS proteinuria
FROM Patient p
JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID
WHERE l."U-PRO" IS NOT NULL
  AND l.Date = (SELECT MAX(x.Date) FROM Laboratory x WHERE x.ID = p.ID AND x."U-PRO" IS NOT NULL)
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 보니 295명이 나왔고, 이는 U-PRO 값이 있는 검사를 받은 환자 수(295명)와 같습니다. 열은 환자 ID, 성별, 가장 최근 단백뇨 검사일, 그 검사의 단백뇨 수치(U-PRO) 순서입니다.

해석 기준은 두 가지입니다. 첫째, 'U-PRO가 비어 있지 않은 검사'를 단백뇨 검사로 보았습니다. 최근 검사일도 이런 검사 중에서 골랐으므로, 단백뇨 값이 비어 있는 더 늦은 검사는 무시합니다. 둘째, U-PRO는 원본이 텍스트라서 '-', 'TR', '30', '>=300', '+1(30)' 같은 값이 섞여 있습니다. 변환하지 않고 원본 그대로 보여 줍니다. (ID, Date)가 기본키이므로 같은 날짜가 겹쳐 한 환자가 두 줄로 나오는 경우는 없습니다.

sql: with c as (select s.School, s.District, s.County, t.AvgScrWrite w from satscores t join schools s on s.CDSCode=t.cds where s.StatusType='Closed' and t.rtype='S' and t.AvgScrWrite is not null) select School, District, County, w as AvgScrWrite from c where w=(select max(w) from c where w<(select max(w) from c))
answer: FAME Public Charter (district: Alameda County Office of Education, county: Alameda) has the second-highest average SAT writing score among closed schools, 505. The highest is Northcoast Preparatory and Performing Arts Academy at 579. I counted only school-level rows (rtype 'S') in satscores, because the district-level rows ('D') would otherwise appear as nameless entries. District and county come from the schools table. No other closed school has a score of 505.

sql: select buildUpPlaySpeedClass from Team_Attributes where team_api_id=9984 and date<=(select max(date) from Match where season='2012/2013' and 9984 in (home_team_api_id,away_team_api_id)) order by date desc limit 1;
answer: Fast. Cercle Brugge's last 2012/2013 match was on 2013-03-16. The snapshot in effect then is the one dated 2012-02-22, and its build-up-play speed class is Fast. The next snapshot is dated 2013-09-20, which is after that match.

sql: with w as (select away_team_api_id id, count(*) c from Match where league_id=19694 and season='2009/2010' and away_team_goal>home_team_goal group by 1) select t.team_long_name from w join Team t on t.team_api_id=w.id where c=(select max(c) from w)
answer: Rangers and Celtic are tied with 11 away wins each in the 2009/2010 Scotland Premier League. I counted a win as a match where away goals exceeded home goals, and I returned the teams' long names.

sql: SELECT CAST((strftime('%s',MAX(t.Date||' '||t.Time)) - strftime('%s',MIN(t.Date||' '||t.Time)))/60 AS INTEGER) AS minutes_elapsed FROM transactions_1k t JOIN gasstations g ON g.GasStationID=t.GasStationID WHERE g.Country='CZE' AND t.Price>1000
answer: 3670분이 지났습니다. 체코(Country='CZE') 주유소에서 Price가 1000을 넘는 거래 중 첫 거래와 마지막 거래 사이의 간격을 분 단위로 내림한 값입니다. 해석은 세 가지로 잡았습니다. 첫째, transactions_1k의 모든 거래를 주유소 거래로 보았고 연료 상품만 따로 걸러내지 않았습니다. 둘째, 'price over 1000'은 Price 컬럼(단가) 기준으로 적용했고 Amount×Price 합계는 쓰지 않았습니다. 셋째, 시각은 Date와 Time을 합쳐서 계산했습니다. 사용한 Term인 Transaction과 Gas Station은 아직 draft 상태(인증 전)입니다.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT text FROM cards WHERE name = 'Benalish Knight'
answer:
I read "rules text" as the `text` column, not `originalText`. Every printing of Benalish Knight has the same `text`, so the query returns one distinct value: "Flash (You may cast this spell any time you could cast an instant.)
First strike (This creature deals combat damage before creatures without first strike.)". The `
` marks a line break in the stored text. I did not run this exact final query; I ran a version that also selected `originalText`. The `Card` term it relies on is still a draft in the ontology. `originalText` differs on two printings: one says "play" instead of "cast", and another uses the older wording "First strike
You may play Benalish Knight whenever you could play an instant."

sql:
SELECT MIN(CAST(strftime('%Y', l.Date) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', p.Birthday) AS INTEGER)) AS youngest_age
FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID
WHERE l.RNP GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) >= 64
answer: 18. RNP is stored as text (values 0, 1, 4, 15, 16, 64, 256, "negative"), so I cast numeric values to compare against 64 and ignored "negative". Age = test year minus birth year. The Terms used are still draft (not certified).

sql:
SELECT t.team_long_name, t.team_short_name, COUNT(*) AS home_wins
FROM "Match" m
JOIN "Team" t ON t.team_api_id = m.home_team_api_id
JOIN "Team_Attributes" ta ON ta.team_api_id = m.home_team_api_id
 AND ta.date = (SELECT MAX(ta2.date) FROM "Team_Attributes" ta2 WHERE ta2.team_api_id = m.home_team_api_id AND ta2.date <= m.date)
WHERE m.home_team_goal - m.away_team_goal >= 3 AND ta.buildUpPlaySpeedClass = 'Fast'
GROUP BY t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name, t.team_short_name
ORDER BY home_wins DESC, t.team_long_name
answer: 65 clubs have at least one home win by 3 or more goals while their latest build-up speed rating on or before the match date was 'Fast'. The top clubs are Borussia Dortmund (DOR, 29), Celtic (CEL, 26) and SL Benfica (BEN, 17). Clubs are grouped by team_api_id, so the two 'HAM' clubs (Hamburger SV and Hamilton Academical FC, 2 wins each) stay separate. I listed every club rather than only the top one, since the question doesn't ask for a maximum, and tied clubs all appear. Dortmund would be the only club if you meant just the highest count. The Match, Team and Team Attributes terms are drafts, and the Match to Team_Attributes join on team_api_id isn't a modeled relationship.

sql: select s.block, count(distinct case when exists(select 1 from set_translations t where t.setCode=s.code and t.translation is not null and t.translation<>'') then s.code end) as translated_sets, sum(s.baseSetSize) as total_base from sets s where s.block in ('Masques','Mirage') group by s.block
answer:
Masques: 2 sets have a translated name, 640 base-set cards in total. Mirage: 1 set has a translated name, 684 base-set cards in total.

Reading I chose: a set counts as translated if it has at least one non-null, non-empty row in set_translations. Many translation rows have a null translation, so they don't count. Base-set cards are summed over all sets in the block, including the promo sets, and every set is counted whether or not it has a translation.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.nationality, CAST(substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60 + CAST(substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,':')+1) AS REAL) AS s FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=1995 AND r.name='Japanese Grand Prix' AND q.q1 IS NOT NULL) SELECT nationality FROM t WHERE s=(SELECT MAX(s) FROM t)
answer: British. The slowest Q1 time is 16:42.640, compared numerically (not as text), and no other driver tied. That value looks like a data error, but I counted it as recorded. If it is excluded, the slowest is 1:48.289 and the nationality would be Belgian.

sql: SELECT t.team_long_name FROM "Match" m JOIN "League" l ON m.league_id=l.id JOIN "Team" t ON m.away_team_api_id=t.team_api_id WHERE l.name='Scotland Premier League' AND m.season='2009/2010' AND m.home_team_goal<m.away_team_goal GROUP BY t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name HAVING COUNT(*)=(SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM "Match" m2 JOIN "League" l2 ON m2.league_id=l2.id WHERE l2.name='Scotland Premier League' AND m2.season='2009/2010' AND m2.home_team_goal<m2.away_team_goal GROUP BY m2.away_team_api_id))
answer: Rangers and Celtic are tied for the most away wins in the Scottish Premier League 2009/2010 season. An away win means the away team scored more goals than the home team. The query uses the league named 'Scotland Premier League', and the Match, Team and League Terms it relies on are still drafts.

sql: SELECT SOCType AS "School Type", School, Latitude FROM schools WHERE (SOC IN ('62','64') OR School LIKE '%Middle%') AND Latitude = (SELECT MAX(Latitude) FROM schools WHERE (SOC IN ('62','64') OR School LIKE '%Middle%'))
answer: Crescent Elk Middle (School Type: Intermediate/Middle Schools (Public)) is the northernmost middle school, at latitude 41.756316. No other school ties. I counted a school as a middle school if its type is Intermediate/Middle or Junior High, or its name contains 'Middle', and I included both open and closed schools. The next one south is Scott Valley Junior High at 41.609.

sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(1.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender='Male' THEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id=s.id) END) / SUM(g.gender='Male'), 2) AS male_avg_powers,
  ROUND(1.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender='Female' THEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id=s.id) END) / SUM(g.gender='Female'), 2) AS female_avg_powers
FROM superhero s JOIN gender g ON g.id=s.gender_id
WHERE s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name <> '-';
answer: Male 8.49, Female 6.83. I counted heroes with a real full_name as those where full_name is neither NULL nor '-'. Heroes with no power records count as 0 powers. The final single-row query is a rewrite of a grouped version I ran and checked (Male 8.49, Female 6.83), and I didn't run the rewrite itself.

sql: SELECT e.expense_description, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM expense e JOIN budget b ON b.budget_id = e.link_to_budget WHERE b.category = 'Food' GROUP BY e.expense_description ORDER BY record_count DESC, e.expense_description ASC LIMIT 1
answer: Pizza, with 7 purchase records. I took "purchases" to mean expense records, "food budget" to mean budget category 'Food', and "item" to mean the expense description text as written. Combined descriptions such as "Water, chips, cookies" count as their own items, and the next highest has 5 records.

sql: select d.type, count(distinct d.account_id) from disp d join account a on a.account_id=d.account_id join district s on s.district_id=a.district_id where s.A11>8000 and s.A11<=9000 and d.type<>'OWNER' group by d.type
answer: DISPONENT is the only non-OWNER type in those districts, with 461 distinct accounts. I read "district" as the account's district (account.district_id) and "average salary" as district.A11.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverId) AS driver_count FROM results r JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = r.driverId WHERE r.rank = 2 AND d.dob >= '1976-01-01';
answer: 25 drivers born on or after 1 January 1976 have set the second-fastest lap of a race. I read "second-fastest lap of a race" as results.rank = 2, which is the driver's rank by fastest lap in that race, and counted each driver once.

sql: select round(count(distinct l.PostId||'-'||strftime('%m',l.CreationDate))/12.0,2) as avg_posts_per_month from postLinks l join posts p on p.Id=l.PostId where p.AnswerCount<=2 and l.CreationDate>='2010-01-01' and l.CreationDate<'2011-01-01'
answer: 평균은 월 7.25건입니다. 2010년 각 월에 postLinks의 PostId로 링크가 생긴 글 중 AnswerCount가 2 이하인 글을 월별로 세어(한 글이 같은 달에 링크를 여러 개 받아도 1건) 12로 나눴습니다. 링크가 없는 달은 0으로 계산됩니다. 링크 건수 기준으로 세면 8.67입니다.

sql: select coalesce(sum(has_normal),0) as with_normal_platelet, coalesce(sum(1-has_normal),0) as never_normal_platelet from (select p.ID, exists(select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and l.PLT>100 and l.PLT<400) as has_normal from Patient p where p.Diagnosis in ('RA, SJS','SJS, RA','RA,SJS','SJS  RA'))
answer: 36 patients have exactly RA and SJS. 5 have at least one normal platelet result, and 31 have never had one (this includes patients with no lab results). I read the diagnosis field as exactly RA and SJS in either order, so it matches 'RA, SJS', 'SJS, RA', 'RA,SJS' and 'SJS  RA'. The last two are spacing variants of the same pair. I excluded any record with another disease or with 'susp' (suspected). Normal platelet count is PLT > 100 and < 400, per docs/Laboratory.csv, across all dates. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(case when u.Reputation>=1000 then 0 else 1 end)/count(*),2) from posts p left join users u on u.Id=p.OwnerUserId where p.CreaionDate>='2010-01-01' and p.CreaionDate<'2011-01-01' and p.Score>5
answer: 33.44. Of 2,171 posts created in 2010 with Score > 5, 33.44% were not made by a user with reputation of at least 1000. Assumption: 85 posts with no owner (null OwnerUserId) count as "not high-reputation". The posts date column is spelled `CreaionDate` in this database.

sql:
SELECT s.School AS name, s.Phone AS phone, s.Website AS website,
 t.AvgScrRead AS avg_read, t.AvgScrMath AS avg_math, t.AvgScrWrite AS avg_write,
 s.Charter AS is_charter, f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enrollment_k12_2014_15,
 ROUND(f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)"*100,2) AS frpm_pct,
 (SELECT MAX(t2.AvgScrMath) FROM satscores t2 JOIN schools s2 ON s2.CDSCode=t2.cds WHERE s2.StatusType='Active' AND t2.NumTstTakr>=10) AS max_math,
 (SELECT MAX(t2.AvgScrMath) FROM satscores t2 JOIN schools s2 ON s2.CDSCode=t2.cds WHERE s2.StatusType='Active' AND t2.NumTstTakr>=10) - t.AvgScrMath AS gap
FROM schools s LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds=s.CDSCode
LEFT JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode AND f."Academic Year"='2014-2015'
WHERE s.CDSCode='07618040113118';
answer:
The school is Dougherty Valley High (San Ramon, Contra Costa). Phone is (925) 479-6400 and website is www.srvusd.net. Average SAT scores are 604 reading, 651 math and 613 writing. It is not a charter school (0). K-12 enrollment for 2014-2015 is 2,645, and 5.9% of students are eligible for free or reduced price meals. The highest average SAT math score among active schools with at least 10 test takers is 699, so this school's math score is 48 points below it.

Assumptions:
- The CDS code in the question has 13 digits. The database stores it with a leading zero (07618040113118), so I matched on that.
- "Eligible for free or reduced price meals" is the K-12 FRPM percentage (stored as a fraction), multiplied by 100 and rounded to two decimals. It is not the free-meal-only percentage.
- For the highest math score I counted every active row in satscores, which includes district-level rows. Restricted to school rows only, the maximum is also 699 (the highest district row is 671), so the result is the same either way.

sql: with b as (select u.Id,u.DisplayName,count(*) n from users u join badges g on g.UserId=u.Id where u.Location like '%Germany%' group by u.Id) select DisplayName,n as badge_total from b where n=(select max(n) from b where n<(select max(n) from b)) order by DisplayName
answer: Bernd Weiss, with 49 badges. I counted a user as located in Germany if their Location contains "Germany" (case-insensitive), which also catches entries like "Berlin, Germany" and "Germany - Frankfurt". Locations written only as "Deutschland" would be missed, but I found none. Users with no badges are not counted.

sql: select count(distinct p.ID) from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where l.TG>=200 and p.Birthday<='1975-10-09'
answer: 106 distinct patients. I read "older than 50" as having turned 51 or more by 2026-10-09, meaning a birthday on or before 1975-10-09. Using a strict "before" cutoff gives the same count.

sql: select count(distinct p.ID) from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where p.Admission='-' and l.RNP in ('-','negative','0')
answer: 41 patients. I read "never admitted" as Patient.Admission = '-' (outpatient). I counted a normal RNP as '-', 'negative' or '0' in Laboratory.RNP, and counted each patient once.

sql:
SELECT r.date, d.forename, d.surname, res.fastestLapTime
FROM races r
LEFT JOIN results res ON res.raceId=r.raceId AND res.fastestLapTime IS NOT NULL
  AND (CAST(substr(res.fastestLapTime,1,instr(res.fastestLapTime,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60000
   + CAST(substr(res.fastestLapTime,instr(res.fastestLapTime,':')+1,2) AS INTEGER)*1000
   + CAST(substr(res.fastestLapTime,instr(res.fastestLapTime,'.')+1) AS INTEGER)) > 90000
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=res.driverId
WHERE r.name='French Grand Prix' AND r.year>=1990
ORDER BY r.date, d.surname, res.fastestLapTime, d.forename;
answer: The query returns 19 rows, one for each French Grand Prix from 1990 to 2008 (2008 is the latest in the database). In every row the driver and lap time are empty. No driver has a fastest lap slower than 90 seconds. I read "slower than 90 seconds" as longer than 1:30.000, using `results.fastestLapTime`. That column is only filled in for 2004–2008, and the slowest value in those years is 1:21.663. The 1990–2003 editions have no fastest-lap data in `results`. I did not check `lapTimes` for those years, but a 90-second lap there would not change the result for 2004–2008. Dates run from 1990-07-08 to 2008-06-22.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT y.CustomerID FROM yearmonth y JOIN customers c ON c.CustomerID = y.CustomerID WHERE c.Segment = 'KAM' AND c.Currency = 'CZK' AND y.Date LIKE '2013%' GROUP BY y.CustomerID HAVING SUM(y.Consumption) > 1000000)
answer: 335 KAM-segment customers paying in CZK had total 2013 fuel consumption above 1,000,000. I summed each customer's monthly Consumption over 2013 and kept totals strictly above 1,000,000. The data ends at 201311, so "2013" covers January to November only. Negative monthly values are included in the sums as stored.

sql:
WITH j AS (SELECT l."T-CHO" AS tcho, p."Admission" AS adm, p."ID" AS pid FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p."ID"=l."ID" WHERE p."Admission" IN ('+','-') AND l."T-CHO" IS NOT NULL)
SELECT DISTINCT tcho AS "T-CHO", adm AS "Admission", pid AS "ID" FROM j WHERE tcho=(SELECT MAX(tcho) FROM j j2 WHERE j2.adm=j.adm) ORDER BY CASE adm WHEN '+' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, pid
answer: 입원 환자(+) 그룹의 최고 T-CHO는 568이며 환자 ID는 1185720입니다. 외래 환자(-) 그룹의 최고 T-CHO는 443이며 환자 ID는 3380563입니다. 두 그룹 모두 동점 환자는 없었습니다. Admission이 '+'와 '-'인 환자만 비교했고(빈 값과 '+('는 제외), 환자별 모든 검사 일자 중 가장 높은 T-CHO 값을 기준으로 했습니다. Laboratory Test와 Patient 용어는 아직 draft 상태(인증 전)입니다.

sql: select count(distinct p.ID) from Patient p join Examination e on e.ID=p.ID where p.SEX='F' and p.Admission='+' and cast(strftime('%Y',p.Birthday) as int) between 1945 and 1989 and e.`ANA Pattern`='P'

sql: select round(avg(A11),2) from district where district_id in (select c.district_id from client c join disp d on d.client_id=c.client_id and d.type='OWNER' join district k on k.district_id=c.district_id where k.A3='central Bohemia' and not exists (select 1 from disp d2 join card cd on cd.disp_id=d2.disp_id where d2.account_id=d.account_id))

sql: select count(distinct hp.power_id) from hero_power hp join superhero s on s.id=hp.hero_id join gender g on g.id=s.gender_id where g.gender='Male' and s.weight_kg>0 and s.weight_kg<70
answer: 102 different superpowers. The docs say a weight_kg of NULL or 0 means the weight is missing, so I excluded both and counted only weights from 1 to 69 kg. 172 heroes have weight 0 in the data. "Male" comes from the gender table.

sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, c.name FROM qualifying q JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId JOIN constructors c ON c.constructorId=q.constructorId LEFT JOIN results r ON r.raceId=q.raceId AND r.driverId=q.driverId WHERE ra.year=2017 AND ra.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2<>'' ORDER BY q.q2, CASE WHEN r.grid=0 THEN 99 ELSE r.grid END LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1
answer: Valtteri Bottas, driving for Mercedes. His Q2 time was 1:34.660 for Hamilton (fastest) and 1:35.396 for Bottas, so there was no tie to break. I took the Q2 times as text, which sorts correctly because they all use the m:ss.mmm format. Drivers with no Q2 time were excluded. The tie-break uses the starting grid from the results table, with pit-lane starts (grid 0) ranked last. The ontology terms involved are still drafts, and the join to results is not a declared relationship.

sql:
WITH last AS (
  SELECT l.ID, l.IGG FROM Laboratory l
  WHERE l.IGG IS NOT NULL
    AND l.Date = (SELECT MAX(l2.Date) FROM Laboratory l2 WHERE l2.ID = l.ID AND l2.IGG IS NOT NULL)
)
SELECT CASE p.Admission WHEN '+' THEN 'admitted to the hospital' ELSE 'followed at the outpatient clinic' END AS care_setting,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN last.IGG > 900 AND last.IGG < 2000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_normal_igg
FROM Patient p LEFT JOIN last ON last.ID = p.ID
WHERE p.Admission IN ('+','-')
GROUP BY p.Admission
ORDER BY p.Admission ASC
answer:
15.8% of admitted patients ('admitted to the hospital') and 13.6% of outpatient-followed patients ('followed at the outpatient clinic') had a normal IgG at their most recent IgG measurement.

Choices I made where the question was open:
- **Most recent measurement:** the latest Laboratory.Date on which IGG is not null for that patient.
- **Normal range:** 900 < IGG < 2000, with both limits exclusive, taken from the Laboratory column documentation.
- **Denominator:** every Patient with Admission '+' or '-'. Patients with no IgG result stay in the denominator and add nothing to the numerator. Patients whose Admission is '' or '+(' (unclear status) are left out.
- **Ontology status:** the Patient and Laboratory Test Terms are still draft, not certified.
- **Check run:** the figures come from the run with the sort direction reversed (outpatient row first). I then changed the order to ASC (admitted first) and did not re-run it.

Averaging over clients instead of distinct districts would give a different number.

sql: select frameVersion, round(100.0*count(*)/(select count(*) from cards where name='Tarmogoyf'),2) as pct from cards where name='Tarmogoyf' and frameVersion glob '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]' group by frameVersion order by frameVersion desc limit 1
answer: The newest year-based frame version is 2015. It covers 4 of Tarmogoyf's 6 printings, which is 66.67%. One printing has frameVersion 'future', and I left it out when picking the newest because it isn't a year. It still counts in the 6-printing denominator.

sql: select b.bond_type, count(*) as cnt from bond b join molecule m on m.molecule_id=b.molecule_id join connected c on c.bond_id=b.bond_id and c.atom_id<c.atom_id2 join atom a1 on a1.atom_id=c.atom_id join atom a2 on a2.atom_id=c.atom_id2 where m.label='+' and a1.element='c' and a2.element='c' group by b.bond_type
answer: 탄소-탄소 결합 수(발암성 분자, label '+'): 단일결합('-') 843개, 이중결합('=') 478개입니다. 삼중결합('#')은 0개라 결과에 나오지 않습니다. 발암성 분자의 삼중결합 3개는 모두 탄소-탄소 결합이 아니었습니다. 발암성은 molecule.label='+'로 해석했고, connected 테이블에 결합이 양방향으로 두 번 저장되어 있어 atom_id<atom_id2 조건으로 한 번만 계산했습니다.

sql: SELECT c.Segment, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT CustomerID, SUM(Consumption) AS s FROM yearmonth WHERE Date BETWEEN '201201' AND '201212' GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING SUM(Consumption) < 30000) y JOIN customers c USING(CustomerID) GROUP BY c.Segment
answer: 2012년 총 소비가 30,000 미만(30,000 이하 제외)인 고객 수는 세그먼트별로 KAM 1,123명, LAM 2,031명, SME 21,869명입니다. 2012년에 yearmonth 기록이 있는 고객만 센 값입니다. yearmonth에 201210~201212 데이터가 없어서 2012년 합계는 1~9월 기준입니다. 음수 소비도 그대로 합산했고, 통화 환산은 하지 않았습니다.

sql:
SELECT c.colors AS color, COUNT(DISTINCT l.format) AS legal_formats
FROM cards c
JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid = c.uuid AND l.status = 'Legal'
WHERE c.id BETWEEN 1 AND 20 AND c.colors IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY c.colors
answer: ID 1~20번 카드에서 흰색(W) 카드는 14개 포맷, 검정(B) 카드는 10개 포맷에서 합법입니다. 카드 색은 cards.colors 컬럼으로 해석했습니다. 테두리 색은 20장 모두 black이라 비교 기준이 될 수 없었습니다. 해당 포맷에서 'Legal'인 행이 하나라도 있으면 그 포맷을 센 것이고, Banned와 Restricted는 세지 않았습니다. 사용한 Card, Card Legality 용어는 아직 draft 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT p.Title, COUNT(*) AS related_count FROM posts p JOIN postLinks l ON l.PostId = p.Id WHERE p.Title LIKE '%principal component scores%' GROUP BY p.Id, p.Title HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM posts p2 JOIN postLinks l2 ON l2.PostId = p2.Id WHERE p2.Title LIKE '%principal component scores%' GROUP BY p2.Id))
answer: "How do I analyse principal component scores?" has the most related posts, with 3. The next one, "What are principal component scores?", has 2. I counted rows in postLinks where the post is the PostId, with no date filter, so the count covers the whole history. The query was not re-run in its final tie-aware form. I ran an equivalent ungrouped version that listed the two posts and their counts.

sql:
SELECT e.event_name,
 printf('%.2f', ROUND(COALESCE((SELECT SUM(x.cost) FROM expense x JOIN budget b ON b.budget_id=x.link_to_budget WHERE b.link_to_event=e.event_id AND lower(x.expense_description) LIKE '%water%'),0)*1.0/(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event=e.event_id),2)) AS water_per_attendee
FROM event e
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event=e.event_id);
answer:
The query returns 25 rows, one per event that has attendance records. Events with no water purchases show 0.00, and the two "Football game" events appear as separate rows. Examples: October Speaker 2.12, September Speaker 2.21, October Meeting 3.01, Yearly Kickoff 0.94.

Readings I chose:
- **Water purchases:** an expense counts as water if its description contains "water". Seven expense rows match, and each counts at its full cost even when it also lists cookies or chips.
- **Attendees:** the number of attendance rows for the event.
- **Linking expenses to events:** expenses reach an event through their budget line (expense → budget → event).
- **Output format:** the amount is rounded to two decimals and returned as text, so 0 appears as 0.00.

sql:
WITH j AS (SELECT DISTINCT f.name jname, c.type ctype, c.uuid FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid=c.uuid AND f.language='Japanese' WHERE c.watermark='boros')
SELECT jname AS japanese_name, ctype AS card_type, SUM((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rulings r WHERE r.uuid=j.uuid)) AS total_rulings FROM j GROUP BY jname, ctype;
answer: The query returns one row per (Japanese name, English card type) for cards with watermark 'boros' that have a Japanese foreign_data entry. Each row has the total ruling count across all of that card's printings, with 0 for cards that have none. For example, 光り輝く炎 (Sorcery) has 12 rulings and ボロスの印鑑 (Artifact) has 0. I read "English card type" as cards.type, the full type line such as "Creature — Human Soldier". I counted only printings that are both boros-watermarked and have a Japanese entry.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.height_cm > 0 THEN s.height_cm END), 1) AS avg_height_cm, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END), 1) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON p.id = s.publisher_id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'George Lucas';
answer: George Lucas's heroes (15 characters under the publisher 'George Lucas') average 187.2 cm in height and 83.0 kg in weight. I read "created by George Lucas" as heroes whose publisher is 'George Lucas'. The docs say a height or weight of 0 or NULL means unknown, so each average leaves out those values separately.

sql: select d.number from qualifying q join races r using(raceId) join drivers d using(driverId) where r.year=2017 and r.name='Italian Grand Prix' and q.q3 is not null and q.q3<>'' and q.q3=(select min(q2.q3) from qualifying q2 where q2.raceId=q.raceId and q2.q3 is not null and q2.q3<>'')
answer: 44 (Lewis Hamilton, Q3 time 1:35.554). Q3 times are stored as text in the same m:ss.mmm format, so I compared them as strings, and I ignored empty Q3 values. No other driver has the same time.

sql: SELECT id FROM cards WHERE borderColor = 'borderless' AND (cardKingdomId IS NULL OR cardKingdomFoilId IS NULL)
answer: The query returns the `id` of every borderless printing in `cards` where `cardKingdomId` (regular) or `cardKingdomFoilId` (foil) is NULL. I read "lacks a regular or foil listing" as missing at least one of the two, and I checked that the query returns 72 rows.

sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN a.element = 'h' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) AS hydrogen_fraction, m.label FROM atom a JOIN molecule m ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id WHERE m.molecule_id = 'TR006' GROUP BY m.molecule_id, m.label
answer: Hydrogen is about 0.3617 (36.2%) of the atoms in TR006, and the molecule's recorded label is '+', meaning carcinogenic. The fraction is hydrogen atoms (element 'h') divided by all atoms in the molecule, which works out to 17 of 47 (inferred from the ratio, not counted separately). The Atom and Molecule terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
WITH fl AS (
 SELECT l.loan_id, c.client_id, l.account_id, l.amount, l.duration, l.payments, l.status, c.birth_date
 FROM loan l JOIN disp d ON d.account_id=l.account_id AND d.type='OWNER'
 JOIN client c ON c.client_id=d.client_id AND c.gender='F'
), top AS (SELECT * FROM fl WHERE amount >= (SELECT MIN(amount) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT amount FROM fl ORDER BY amount DESC LIMIT 3))),
tx AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) n, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN type='PRIJEM' THEN amount END),0) dep FROM trans GROUP BY account_id)
SELECT t.client_id, t.amount AS loan_amount, t.duration AS duration_months,
 ROUND(t.payments*t.duration,2) AS total_payments,
 ROUND(t.payments*t.duration - t.amount,2) AS interest_paid,
 t.status AS loan_status, d.A2 AS district, d.A3 AS region,
 tx.n AS transaction_count, ROUND(tx.dep,2) AS total_deposits,
 CASE WHEN tx.dep > 2*t.amount THEN 'High Income' WHEN tx.dep > t.amount THEN 'Medium Income' ELSE 'Low Income' END AS income_category,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM loan l2 JOIN account a2 ON a2.account_id=l2.account_id JOIN district d2 ON d2.district_id=a2.district_id WHERE d2.A3=d.A3) AS region_loan_count,
 (SELECT ROUND(AVG(A11),2) FROM district WHERE A3=d.A3) AS region_avg_salary,
 CAST(strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',t.birth_date) - (strftime('%m-%d',t.birth_date)>'10-09') AS INTEGER) AS age
FROM top t JOIN account a ON a.account_id=t.account_id JOIN district d ON d.district_id=a.district_id
LEFT JOIN tx ON tx.account_id=t.account_id
ORDER BY t.amount DESC;
answer:
여성 고객의 대출 중 금액이 큰 3건(동액 없음)은 다음과 같습니다. 순서는 고객 id, 대출액, 기간, 총상환액, 이자, 상태, 지점 district, region, 거래 수, 총 입금액, 소득 구분, region 대출 수, region 평균 급여, 나이입니다.
- 10997: 566,640, 60개월, 566,640.00, 0.00, C, Hl.m. Praha, Prague, 200건, 447,173, Low Income, 84건, 12,541.00, 54세
- 2823: 541,200, 60개월, 541,200.00, 0.00, D, Karvina, north Moravia, 329건, 515,538, Low Income, 117건, 9,049.18, 79세
- 8506: 495,180, 60개월, 495,180.00, 0.00, C, Jesenik, north Moravia, 76건, 770,790, Medium Income, 117건, 9,049.18, 46세

적용한 해석은 세 가지입니다.
- 대출 고객은 해당 계좌의 OWNER 권한 고객으로 봤습니다.
- 총 입금액은 type이 PRIJEM(입금)인 거래 금액의 합계로 계산했고, 거래 수는 계좌의 전체 거래 건수입니다.
- 월 상환액에 기간을 곱한 값이 대출액과 같아서 세 건 모두 이자는 0.00입니다.

sql: select count(*) from (select o.UserId from (select UserId,min(Date) d from badges where Name='Organizer' group by UserId) o join users u on u.Id=o.UserId where u.Location like '%Germany%' and (select count(*) from badges b where b.UserId=o.UserId and b.Date<o.d and b.Name<>'Organizer')>=5)
answer: 11 users. I took "based in Germany" to mean Location contains 'Germany'. For anyone with several Organizer badges, I used the earliest one. I counted only non-Organizer badges earned strictly before that time, and required at least 5.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE LOWER(Diagnosis) LIKE '%psoriatic arthritis%'
answer: 2 patients have a diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis (IDs 3554252 and 4547222). The diagnosis text is spelled two ways ('Psoriatic Arthritis' and 'Psoriatic arthritis'), so I matched it case-insensitively. I counted every row in Patient, with no date or follow-up filter.

sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, CAST((strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',p.Birthday)) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09')<strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)) AS INTEGER) AS age FROM Patient p WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE GLU>=180 AND "T-CHO"<250) ORDER BY p.ID
answer: 13명이 조건에 해당합니다. 예를 들어 57266(M, 103세), 2371753(F, 93세), 3354706(F, 89세)입니다. 한 검사 기록에서 GLU≥180과 T-CHO<250을 동시에 만족하는 경우만 포함했습니다. 만 나이는 2026-10-09 기준으로 생일이 지났는지 반영해 계산했습니다. 생일이 비어 있는 환자는 이 조건에 해당하지 않았습니다.

sql: select substr(GSserved,1,instr(GSserved,'-')-1) as lowest_grade from schools where NCESDist='0632640' and GSserved like '%-%' order by case substr(GSserved,1,instr(GSserved,'-')-1) when 'P' then -2 when 'K' then 0 else cast(substr(GSserved,1,instr(GSserved,'-')-1) as int) end limit 1
answer: The lowest grade is K (kindergarten). I read "begins serving students" as the lowest grade in GSserved, the grade span actually enrolled, for schools in NCES district 0632640. One school has no grade span and was ignored. If you used GSoffered instead, one school offers P (preschool) and the answer would be P.

sql:
SELECT ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN y.Date LIKE '2013%' THEN y.Consumption END) - SUM(CASE WHEN y.Date LIKE '2012%' THEN y.Consumption END)) / SUM(CASE WHEN y.Date LIKE '2012%' THEN y.Consumption END), 4) AS relative_change
FROM yearmonth y
WHERE y.CustomerID IN (SELECT CustomerID FROM transactions_1k WHERE Date='2012-08-25' AND Price=634.8)
answer: The relative change is 5.8152, an increase of about 581.52%. The customer is CustomerID 6718, found as the one transaction on 2012-08-25 with Price = 634.8. I read "paid 634.8" as the Price column, since Amount × Price for that row is 17139.6 and nothing matches 634.8 that way. The 2013 total covers only months 201301 to 201311 because the data ends at 201311, so it is an 11-month total compared with a 12-month 2012 total. The Terms used are drafts, not certified.

sql:
WITH b AS (SELECT link_to_event ev, SUM(spent) sp, SUM(amount) am FROM budget GROUP BY 1),
x AS (SELECT b.link_to_event ev, COUNT(*) n FROM expense x JOIN budget b ON b.budget_id=x.link_to_budget GROUP BY 1)
SELECT e.event_name FROM event e LEFT JOIN b ON b.ev=e.event_id LEFT JOIN x ON x.ev=e.event_id
WHERE e.status='Closed' AND COALESCE(b.sp,0)<=COALESCE(b.am,0)
ORDER BY COALESCE(x.n,0) DESC, e.event_id LIMIT 1
answer: October Speaker. I read "closed" as event.status = 'Closed'. I read "purchases" as expense rows, counted per event through budget. Spending and budget are the sums of budget.spent and budget.amount for each event. Events with no budget rows count as 0 spent against 0 budget, so they stay in. October Speaker (recEVTik3MlqbvLFi) and November Speaker (reciRZdAqNIKuMC96) tied at 5 purchases each. The alphabetically first event ID is recEVTik3MlqbvLFi, so October Speaker is the answer.

sql:
select e.event_name, printf('%.2f', round(coalesce((select sum(x.cost) from expense x join budget b on b.budget_id=x.link_to_budget where b.link_to_event=e.event_id and lower(x.expense_description) like '%water%'),0)*1.0/(select count(distinct a.link_to_member) from attendance a where a.link_to_event=e.event_id),2)) as water_per_attendee
from event e where exists (select 1 from attendance a where a.link_to_event=e.event_id)
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 참석자가 있는 17개 행사를 확인했습니다. 같은 이름의 행사(Football game 2건)는 따로 표시됩니다. 물 구매가 있는 행사는 7곳이고, 나머지는 0.00입니다. 예를 들어 October Meeting은 3.01, September Speaker와 November Speaker는 각각 2.21입니다.

적용한 해석은 다음과 같습니다.
- 물 구매는 지출 설명(expense_description)에 'water'가 들어간 건입니다. 해당하는 설명은 "Water, Cookies", "Water, chips, cookies" 같은 4종류뿐입니다. 'bottled'라는 표현은 데이터에 없어서 이 건들을 생수 구매로 봤습니다.
- 물과 다른 품목을 함께 산 지출은 금액 전체를 물 비용으로 계산했습니다.
- 지출은 예산(budget)을 거쳐 행사에 연결했고, 행사 상태와 승인 여부는 따지지 않았습니다. 물 관련 지출은 모두 승인(approved=true)된 건입니다.
- 참석자 수는 참석 기록(attendance)에서 행사별로 중복 없이 센 회원 수입니다.
- 금액은 달러 기준으로 소수 둘째 자리까지 반올림했고, 문자열 형식('0.00')으로 출력됩니다.

sql: select c.colors, count(distinct l.format) as legal_formats from cards c join legalities l on l.uuid=c.uuid and l.status='Legal' where c.id between 1 and 20 group by c.colors
answer: ID 1~20 카드 중 흰색(W)은 14개 포맷, 검은색(B)은 10개 포맷에서 Legal입니다. 포맷 수는 해당 색 카드 중 하나라도 그 포맷에서 'Legal'이면 센 값(중복 제거)이고, Banned와 Restricted는 제외했습니다.

sql:
SELECT e.event_name, e.event_date, COALESCE(b.total,0) AS total_budgeted, COALESCE(a.cnt,0) AS members_attended
FROM event e
LEFT JOIN (SELECT link_to_event, SUM(amount) total FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event) b ON b.link_to_event=e.event_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT link_to_event, COUNT(DISTINCT link_to_member) cnt FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event) a ON a.link_to_event=e.event_id
ORDER BY e.event_name ASC, e.event_date ASC
answer: The query returns all 42 events with event name, event date, total budgeted and number of members who attended, sorted by name and then date. Total budgeted is the sum of budget line amounts for the event. Attendance is the count of distinct members in the attendance table. Events with no budget lines or no attendance rows show 0 (for example "Baseball game" shows 0 and 0). Many events show 0 attended or 0 budgeted because the data has no rows for them. The Event and Budget terms are draft, not certified.

sql: select count(distinct P.ID) from Patient P join Laboratory L on L.ID=P.ID where P.SEX='F' and L.WBC>3.5 and L.WBC<9.0 and (L.FG<=150 or L.FG>=450) and CAST(L.RNP AS REAL)>15
answer: 1 female patient matches. I counted distinct patients who have at least one lab record, on any date, meeting all three conditions. Normal WBC is 3.5 to 9.0 exclusive, and abnormal fibrinogen is 150 or below or 450 or above, both per the docs. RNP is stored as text, so I cast it to a number. 'negative' becomes 0 and RNP values of 16, 64 and 256 count as above 15, while 15 does not.

sql:
SELECT e.event_name
FROM event e
JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
WHERE e.event_id IN (
  SELECT b2.link_to_event FROM expense x
  JOIN budget b2 ON b2.budget_id = x.link_to_budget
  WHERE x.expense_description LIKE '%chip%')
GROUP BY e.event_id
HAVING MAX(b.amount) = (
  SELECT MAX(b3.amount) FROM budget b3
  WHERE b3.link_to_event IN (
    SELECT b4.link_to_event FROM expense x2
    JOIN budget b4 ON b4.budget_id = x2.link_to_budget
    WHERE x2.expense_description LIKE '%chip%'));
answer: October Speaker. Its largest single budget line is $155, and the next highest events are at $150. I counted an event as having spent on chips if any expense with "chip" in its description is linked to one of its budget lines. I compared events by the largest budget line across all their lines. Using only the chip-linked lines gives the same result.

sql: select m.first_name,m.last_name,round(sum(b.remaining),2) t from member m join (select distinct link_to_member mid, link_to_budget bid from expense where cost>50) e on e.mid=m.member_id join budget b on b.budget_id=e.bid group by m.member_id order by sum(b.remaining) desc,m.last_name,m.first_name
answer: Three members had an expense over $50: Phillip Cullen (107.50), Sacha Harrison (19.01) and Elijah Allen (4.75). Choices I made: "more than fifty dollars" means cost > 50. Each budget line is counted once per member, even if that member had several large expenses on it. The remaining amount is the budget table's `remaining` column, which already covers all expenses on the line, and negative values are included as they are.

sql: SELECT s.superhero_name, p.publisher_name FROM superhero s LEFT JOIN publisher p ON p.id = s.publisher_id WHERE s.eye_colour_id = s.hair_colour_id AND s.hair_colour_id = s.skin_colour_id AND s.eye_colour_id <> 1
answer: 4개 캐릭터가 해당합니다: Beast (Marvel Comics), Beast Boy (DC Comics), Hulk (Marvel Comics), Purple Man (Marvel Comics). 눈, 머리카락, 피부 색이 모두 같으면서 그 색이 알려진 경우만 골랐습니다. 'No Colour'(id 1)는 색을 모르는 값으로 보고 제외했습니다. 이 값까지 포함하면 결과가 늘어납니다. 출판사가 없는 캐릭터도 빠지지 않도록 LEFT JOIN을 썼으며, 이번 결과에는 출판사가 비어 있는 행이 없습니다. 사용한 용어(Superhero, Publisher, Colour)는 모두 draft 상태입니다.

sql: select sum(case k_symbol when 'UROK' then amount else -amount end) as net_interest from trans where account_id=(select account_id from disp where client_id=2823) and date between '1998-01-01' and '1998-12-31' and k_symbol in ('UROK','SANKC. UROK')
answer: 1998년 계좌 2335(고객 2823)의 순이자는 -505 CZK입니다. 이자 입금(UROK) 24건 합계 91, 페널티 이자(SANKC. UROK) 24건 합계 596을 차감한 값입니다. 고객 2823의 disp는 OWNER 1건(계좌 2335)이며, 계좌 단위로 모든 거래를 집계했습니다. 위키에는 금액 통화가 USD로 적혀 있으나, 질문에 따라 CZK로 보았습니다.

sql: select m.department, count(distinct m.major_id) as majors_offered, count(distinct mem.link_to_major) as majors_held, round(1.0*count(mem.member_id)/count(distinct m.major_id),2) as avg_members_per_major from major m left join member mem on mem.link_to_major=m.major_id where m.department in (select department from major where college='College of Humanities and Social Sciences') group by m.department order by m.department;
answer:
The query returns 11 departments with counts of majors offered and majors held, plus average members per major. Only 4 of them have any member majors:
- Languages, Philosophy and Communication Studies: 8 offered, 3 held, 0.38 members per major.
- Political Science: 3 offered, 2 held, 1.00.
- Liberal Arts Program: 1 offered, 1 held, 1.00.
- The other 8 departments have 0 majors held and 0.00.

I made three choices where the question was open:
- "Majors it offers" and "majors held" are given as counts, not name lists.
- The average is the number of member rows with a major in the department divided by the number of majors it offers. Members with no major (Randy Woodard) are excluded.
- A department counts as in the college if any of its majors is there. Every such department has all its majors in that college, so this didn't change any result.

sql: select round(avg(weight_kg),2) from superhero s join gender g on g.id=s.gender_id join alignment a on a.id=s.alignment_id where g.gender='Female' and a.alignment='Good' and weight_kg>0
answer: The average weight of female superheroes with a good alignment is 70.76 kg. I treated a weight of 0 as unknown, as well as NULL, and left both out of the average.

sql: SELECT d.code, q.q3 FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3<>'' AND q.q3=(SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying q2 WHERE q2.raceId=q.raceId AND q2.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q2.q3<>'')
answer: HAM set the fastest Q3 time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix: 1:35.554. No other driver matched it, so there is no tie. I took "fastest" as the lowest non-empty q3 value for that race. The times are stored as text in a fixed m:ss.mmm format, so the minimum compares correctly as text. The Driver, Qualifying Result and Race Terms the query relies on are still drafts and not certified.

sql: with t as (select e.type, count(distinct a.link_to_member) n from event e join attendance a on a.link_to_event=e.event_id where e.event_date>='2019-09-01' and e.event_date<'2020-06-01' group by e.type) select type,n from t where n=(select max(n) from t);
answer: Meeting and Registration tie, with 30 members each. I counted distinct members per event type, so a member who attended several events of one type counts once. The query keeps events dated 2019-09-01 through 2020-05-31, which covers every event in the table, and it does not filter on event status.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.date || '|' || r.text) AS ruling_count FROM rulings r JOIN cards c ON c.uuid = r.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Fireball'
answer: Fireball has 4 distinct official rulings, counted across all dates. The rulings table has 136 rows for Fireball because the same rulings are attached to each of its 36 printings. I counted each distinct date and text pair once, since a ruling applies to the card and not to a printing. If you want one row per printing, the figure is 136.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) FROM cards c JOIN sets s ON c.setCode = s.code JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE s.name = 'Coldsnap' AND f.language = 'Italian' AND f.text IS NOT NULL AND f.text <> ''
answer: 149 printings in the Coldsnap set have Italian rules text. I counted distinct card rows (printings) in the set named 'Coldsnap' that have an Italian foreign_data row with non-empty text. I chose non-empty text as the meaning of "has Italian rules text", because that column often holds empty strings. I did not check how many Italian rows have empty text, so I can't say how much that condition changes the count. The Terms used (Card, Card Foreign Data, Card Set) are drafts, not certified.

sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.SM IN ('negative','0'))
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID=p.ID)
AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID=p.ID AND e.Thrombosis>0)
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l."U-PRO" IN ('30','100','300','>=300','>=1000','+1(30)','+2(100)'))
answer: 2 patients. Reading used: normal anti-SM means at least one laboratory record with SM 'negative' or '0'. No thrombosis means the patient has examination records and none has Thrombosis above 0. Significant proteinuria means U-PRO of '30', '100', '300', '>=300', '>=1000', '+1(30)' or '+2(100)'. I did not count '-', 'TR', the bare digits '1' to '4', '%%' or '-15'. The Terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT p."SEX" AS sex, COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM "Patient" p WHERE p."SEX" IN ('F','M') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "Examination" e WHERE e."ID" = p."ID") GROUP BY p."SEX"
answer: Among patients with no Examination row under their ID, 962 are women (F) and 194 are men (M). I excluded 13 such patients whose SEX is blank, because the question asks only about women and men. If you want them counted, they would appear as a third row with an empty sex. The Patient term the query relies on is still a draft in the ontology, not certified.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN results.positionOrder <> 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_not_wins
FROM results AS results
JOIN drivers AS drivers ON results.driverId = drivers.driverId
JOIN races AS races ON results.raceId = races.raceId
WHERE drivers.forename = 'Lewis' AND drivers.surname = 'Hamilton' AND races.date >= '2010-01-01'
answer: 66.20% of Lewis Hamilton's race entries from 2010 onward (data runs through 2017) were not victories. Each results row counts as one entry, and a win is positionOrder = 1. Retirements count as non-wins. The Driver, Race and Race Result terms are draft, not certified.

sql:
WITH v AS (SELECT s.CDSCode, s.School, s.County, t.AvgScrRead r FROM schools s LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds=s.CDSCode WHERE s.Virtual='F'),
c AS (SELECT County, COUNT(*) n FROM v GROUP BY County),
top AS (SELECT * FROM c WHERE n >= (SELECT n FROM c ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 4)),
m AS (SELECT County, MAX(r) mr FROM v GROUP BY County)
SELECT top.County, top.n, COALESCE(v.School,'None') AS School
FROM top JOIN m ON m.County=top.County
LEFT JOIN v ON v.County=top.County AND m.mr IS NOT NULL AND v.r=m.mr
ORDER BY top.n DESC, top.County, School
answer: Top 5 counties by exclusively virtual schools (Virtual='F'): Los Angeles 12 (California Virtual Academy @ Los Angeles), San Joaquin 10 (California Connections Academy @ Ripon), San Diego 8 (None), Sacramento 5 (None), San Bernardino 5 (None). Sacramento and San Bernardino tie at 5, the fifth-highest count, so both are included. I counted all statuses (including closed schools) and treated a missing SAT row or null AvgScrRead as having no reported reading average. The School and SAT Score Record ontology terms are still drafts.

sql: SELECT atom.element FROM "atom" AS atom JOIN "molecule" AS molecule ON atom.molecule_id = molecule.molecule_id WHERE molecule.label = '-' GROUP BY atom.element HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MIN(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM "atom" a JOIN "molecule" m ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '-' GROUP BY a.element))

sql:
WITH latest AS (
SELECT player_api_id, defensive_work_rate,
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) rn
FROM Player_Attributes)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(p.height),2) AS avg_height_cm
FROM latest l JOIN Player p ON p.player_api_id=l.player_api_id
WHERE l.rn=1 AND l.defensive_work_rate IN ('high','low')
answer: 180.95 cm. I used each player's latest rating row (by date, then highest id) and counted only players whose current defensive work rate is 'high' or 'low'. Players whose latest value is dirty data (digits, 'o', 'ormal', NULL and similar) are excluded rather than counted as 'not medium'. The Player and Player Attributes terms are still drafts in the ontology.

sql: select r.year, count(*) as total_pit_stops from pitStops p join races r on r.raceId = p.raceId where r.year between 2002 and 2013 and r.raceId in (select s.raceId from driverStandings s join drivers d on d.driverId = s.driverId where d.nationality = 'Australian' and s.position < 20) group by r.year order by r.year
answer: Only 2011 to 2013 appear: 2011 has 1069 pit stops, 2012 has 905, and 2013 has 898. The database has no pit stop records before 2011, so 2002 to 2010 return no rows. I read "better than 20th" as standings position < 20 (strictly, so 20th itself is excluded). Australian means drivers.nationality = 'Australian'. Pit stops are counted for all drivers at each qualifying race.

sql:
SELECT L."T-BIL", L."Date", L."ID", P."SEX", P."Birthday"
FROM Laboratory L JOIN Patient P ON P.ID = L.ID
WHERE L."RNP" IS NOT NULL AND CAST(L."RNP" AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST("RNP" AS REAL)) FROM Laboratory WHERE "RNP" IS NOT NULL)
AND L."T-BIL" = (SELECT MAX(L2."T-BIL") FROM Laboratory L2 WHERE L2."RNP" IS NOT NULL AND CAST(L2."RNP" AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST("RNP" AS REAL)) FROM Laboratory WHERE "RNP" IS NOT NULL))
answer: One test matches: total bilirubin 0.4, test date 1989-07-18, patient ID 1650222, sex F, birthday 1947-03-17. I took "strongest anti-RNP result" as the highest numeric value of Laboratory.RNP (stored as text, so the query casts it to a number); that value is 256. Among the tests with that RNP value, the query keeps those with the highest T-BIL and lists each tied test. The Laboratory Test and Patient terms are still draft, not certified.

sql: select f.`County Name` as county, count(*) as school_count from frpm f join satscores s on s.cds=f.CDSCode where s.rtype='S' and f.`Academic Year`='2014-2015' and f.`Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)`>0.1 and s.NumGE1500>=1 group by f.`County Name` order by school_count desc, county
answer: The query returns one row per county, with the county name and its number of qualifying schools. Los Angeles is first with 305, then San Diego (86), Orange (62), San Bernardino (60) and Riverside (58). Ties are broken alphabetically. A school qualifies if its free-meal rate (K-12) is above 0.1 and its own SAT record shows NumGE1500 of at least 1. I used the 'Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)' column, which equals Free Meal Count divided by Enrollment. I counted only school-level SAT rows (rtype 'S') and excluded district rows. All frpm rows are 2014-2015, and the query filters on that year anyway.

sql: SELECT cardKingdomFoilId, cardKingdomId FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND cardKingdomFoilId IS NOT NULL AND cardKingdomId IS NOT NULL ORDER BY cardKingdomFoilId ASC, cardKingdomId ASC LIMIT 3;
answer: Result: (110505, 110335), (110506, 110336), (110507, 110337). I counted a card as a creature when `types` contains 'Creature', which includes Artifact Creature. The ids are stored as text, so I read "alphabetical order" as text ordering. All ids are 5 or 6 digits long, so numeric ordering could give different rows.

sql: select s.NCESSchool from frpm f join schools s on s.CDSCode=f.CDSCode where f.CDSCode in ('01751010130583','01612910137588','01611760134270') and f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)"=(select max(f2."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)") from frpm f2 where f2.CDSCode in ('01751010130583','01612910137588','01611760134270'))

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c WHERE c.name='Counterspell' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM foreign_data f WHERE f.uuid=c.uuid AND f.language='French') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM foreign_data f WHERE f.uuid=c.uuid AND f.language='Italian')
answer: 9. I counted Counterspell printings (rows in cards, one per set) that have both a French and an Italian row in foreign_data. The Card and Card Foreign Data terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT SUM(p.publisher_name='DC Comics') dc, SUM(p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics') m FROM superhero h JOIN publisher p ON p.id=h.publisher_id) SELECT CASE WHEN dc=m THEN 'Tie' WHEN m>dc THEN 'Marvel Comics' ELSE 'DC Comics' END AS publisher, ABS(m-dc) AS difference FROM c
answer: Marvel Comics has more superheroes: 387 against 224 for DC Comics, a difference of 163. The query returns the publisher name and the difference, and returns 'Tie' as the publisher if the counts are equal.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) FROM cards WHERE isPromo = 1 AND types LIKE '%Creature%' AND leadershipSkills LIKE '%''brawl'': True%'

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Examination e ON e.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND e.Diagnosis LIKE '%SJS%' AND e.Diagnosis NOT LIKE '%SJS susp%'
answer: 20 female patients. I counted distinct patients, not examination rows. I counted an examination diagnosis that mentions SjS (matched case-insensitively), whether alone or with other diseases. I left out entries where SjS is marked "susp" (suspected): 'SjS susp', 'RA, SjS susp' and 'Behcet, SjS susp'.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg)) AS avg_weight_kg
FROM superhero s
JOIN colour c ON s.skin_colour_id = c.id
JOIN alignment a ON s.alignment_id = a.id
WHERE c.colour = 'Green' AND a.alignment = 'Bad'
AND s.weight_kg IS NOT NULL AND s.weight_kg > 0
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp JOIN superpower p ON hp.power_id = p.id WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id AND p.power_name = 'Flight')
answer: 121 kg. Chosen reading: skin colour exactly 'Green' (not 'Green/Blue'), alignment 'Bad', has the 'Flight' power, and weight measured (NULL or 0 excluded). The ontology terms used are drafts, not certified.

sql: select round((max(milliseconds)-min(milliseconds))*100.0/max(milliseconds),2) from results r join races ra using(raceId) where ra.year=1988 and ra.name like '%Australian%' and r.milliseconds is not null
answer: 1.16%. I took the last full-distance finisher to be the slowest car with a recorded time. That is 4th place, 82 laps, 6,874,764 ms, against the winner's 6,794,676 ms. Cars that finished fewer laps have no elapsed time.

sql:
SELECT s.name, s.keyruneCode, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.translation IS NOT NULL AND t.translation<>'' THEN t.language END) AS language_count
FROM sets s LEFT JOIN set_translations t ON t.setCode = s.code
WHERE s.releaseDate >= '2020-01-01' AND s.releaseDate < '2021-01-01'
GROUP BY s.code, s.name, s.keyruneCode
ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.name
answer:
The query returns 34 sets released in 2020, each with its name, keyrune code and number of languages that have a translated name. Only 3 of them have any translation, and each has one language: Theros Beyond Death (THB), Ikoria: Lair of Behemoths (IKO) and Core Set 2021 (M21). The other 31 show 0.

I counted distinct languages whose `translation` is not null or empty. I used a LEFT JOIN so sets with no translations still appear with 0. Release date is limited to 2020-01-01 through 2020-12-31, and each set is grouped by set code. The `Card Set` and `Set Translation` terms in the ontology are still drafts.

sql: select distinct l.format, c.name from legalities l join cards c on c.uuid=l.uuid where l.status='Banned' and l.format=(select format from legalities where status='Banned' group by format order by count(*) desc limit 1) order by c.name
answer: Legacy has the most banned records (546 rows in legalities with status 'Banned'; next is duel with 488). The query returns the format and 102 distinct banned card names, one row per name. I counted records as legalities rows with status 'Banned' and found the names by joining to cards on uuid.

sql: SELECT c.watermark, COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) AS n FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid=c.uuid WHERE c.watermark IN ('azorius','boros','dimir','golgari','gruul','izzet','orzhov','rakdos','selesnya','simic') GROUP BY c.watermark ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1
answer: Golgari has the most, with 148 cards. Izzet and Dimir follow with 139 each, so there is no tie for first. I counted a card as printed in another language if it has at least one row in foreign_data, and I counted each card once.

sql:
WITH p AS (
 SELECT l.ID, MAX(CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)) m
 FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient pt ON pt.ID=l.ID
 WHERE pt.Admission='-' AND l.RNP GLOB '[0-9]*'
 AND l.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB<10)
 GROUP BY l.ID)
SELECT p.ID, pt.SEX, p.m AS max_rnp FROM p JOIN Patient pt ON pt.ID=p.ID
WHERE p.m=(SELECT MAX(m) FROM p)
answer: Patient 4915498 (female) has the highest anti-RNP level, 256, among outpatients (Admission = '-') who ever had HGB < 10. No other patient ties at that level. I cast the text RNP values to numbers, took each patient's maximum over all lab dates, and ignored 'negative'. The Laboratory Test and Patient terms in the ontology are still drafts.

sql: select c.Currency, count(*) as CustomerCount from customers c join (select CustomerID from yearmonth where Date between '201301' and '201311' and Consumption>0 group by CustomerID having count(distinct Date)=11) y on y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID group by c.Currency
answer: CZK: 61 customers, EUR: 4 customers. The transactions table only covers August 2012, so I used the monthly yearmonth table. I counted a month as fuel bought when Consumption > 0, so months with zero or negative consumption (refunds) don't count. A customer must have such a month for all 11 months from 201301 to 201311. If any recorded row counts, regardless of sign, CZK would be 62 and EUR would stay at 4.
